messages.content: Hi, I have a science project due Friday and I haven't started. It is about the water cycle.

That is still doable. You have a few days. Start by drawing the cycle on one page: evaporation, clouds, rain and rivers. Once the drawing is done, the writing comes much easier. Do you have chart paper at home?
Yes, my mother bought a big white sheet and some markers. I am Aarav, by the way.
Nice to meet you, Aarav. With a big sheet and markers you can make a bright poster. Draw the sun on the left, a sea at the bottom and clouds on top, then add arrows to show the water moving.
Okay. What should I write under the arrows?

Write one short line per arrow. Under the first arrow, "The sun heats the sea and water rises as vapour." Under the next, "Vapour cools and forms clouds." Keep each line to one sentence so your poster stays neat, Aarav.
My maths exam is on Monday and I keep forgetting formulas.

That happens to many students. Try writing each formula on a small card with one worked example on the back. Carry the cards around and read two or three at a time. Short, repeated looks work better than one long session.
Good idea. The ones I forget most are the area of a circle and the Pythagoras one.

Those two are easy to mix up, so give each its own card. For the circle, write pi times radius squared. For Pythagoras, write the two short sides squared add up to the longest side squared. Draw a tiny picture on each.
Which of the two should I practise first?

Start with the Pythagoras one, since it has more parts to remember than the circle. Do three practice questions on it tonight, then do the circle card tomorrow morning. Check your answers against the book, and good luck on Monday.
Our new English teacher is Mr Verma. He gave us a poem to memorise already.
That is a quick start. Poems are easier to learn than they seem if you take them a few lines at a time. Do you know yet how many lines it has?
It has sixteen lines. I am Meera and I am nervous about reciting in front of everyone.

Hello Meera. Sixteen lines is fine. Learn four lines each day and say them aloud while you walk or brush your teeth. Being nervous before reciting is normal, and saying it aloud many times makes the words feel natural.
What if I forget a line in the middle?
Take a slow breath and say the last line you remember again. Often the next line comes back. If it does not, pause and look at Mr Verma. Teachers usually help gently when a student is trying, Meera.
We are going on a school trip to the science museum next Thursday.
That sounds like fun. Museum trips are good because you can touch and try things. Do you know what you need to carry?
A packed lunch, a water bottle and a notebook. My friend Tom is bringing a camera.

That is a sensible list. A notebook is a good idea because you can write down things you want to remember. Tom's camera will be handy, though ask your teacher whether photos are allowed in every hall.
Can you remind me what Tom is bringing? I want to tell my mother.

Tom is bringing a camera. You are carrying a packed lunch, a water bottle and a notebook. You could tell your mother that, and say you will check with the teacher about photos, so there is no confusion on Thursday.
Results come out tomorrow and my stomach hurts just thinking about it.
That sounds stressful. Waiting for results is hard, and feeling it in your stomach is very common. Is there anything you can do tonight to keep busy and calm, like a walk or a favourite show?
I might help my mother cook. My name is Fatima, and my cousin Zara is also getting her results.
Cooking is a lovely way to keep your hands and mind busy, Fatima. It is nice that Zara is in the same situation too. You could message her after the results and share the news, whatever it is.
What should I say to Zara if she does badly?
Keep it simple and kind. You could say, "I am sorry, that is disappointing. I am here if you want to talk." Do not rush to fix it. Zara will probably just want someone to listen first, Fatima.
I forgot my homework notebook at school and the school is closed till morning.
That is annoying, but it can be fixed. Do the homework on loose sheets tonight and staple or paste them into the notebook tomorrow. Tell your teacher honestly what happened.
Okay. It is for Mrs Pillai, and she is quite strict.

Strict teachers usually respect honesty. Tomorrow, before class, go to Mrs Pillai, say you forgot the notebook, and show her the loose sheets with your name and date at the top. That shows you did the work.
Should I say sorry first or show her the sheets first?

Say a short sorry first, then show the sheets. Something like, "Mrs Pillai, I am sorry, I left my notebook at school, but I did the homework here." That way she hears the problem and sees the solution together.
Two of my classmates are fighting over who gets to be class monitor.
That can get heated. Being monitor feels like an honour, so both may feel hurt. Are you friends with them both?
Yes. Rohan and Kabir. They have not spoken for two days.

That is a long silence for friends. Maybe you could talk to each of them separately, listen to what bothers them, and then suggest that they speak to the teacher together. A fair method like drawing lots might settle things.
I think drawing lots is a good idea. Which of them should I talk to first?
It does not matter much, but be fair. Pick whichever you can reach first, and tell both Rohan and Kabir the same thing so neither feels you took a side. Suggesting lots to each of them should help.
I have to write an essay in my English exam. Any tips?

Plan before you write. Spend five minutes jotting three main points, then give each one a paragraph. Start with a clear opening line and end with a short conclusion. Keep your handwriting neat so the examiner can read it.
How long should the introduction be?
Two or three sentences are enough. Say what the topic is and what you will discuss. Do not tell the whole story there, since the details belong in the body paragraphs.
I want to write about the importance of reading. Could you suggest my three points?

Sure. First, reading builds vocabulary. Second, it helps you understand other people's lives and feelings. Third, it improves concentration, because you follow a long story. Those three points would make clear paragraphs for your essay on the importance of reading.
I got 62 percent in science and my father is not happy.
That is a decent score, though I understand your father hoped for more. How do you feel about it yourself?
A bit disappointed. I am Ishaan, and I studied hard for the chapter on electricity but still lost marks there.

Thanks for telling me, Ishaan. Losing marks in a chapter you studied hard feels unfair. It may help to look at your paper and see exactly where the marks went, whether in theory, diagrams or calculations.
Yes, I will ask my teacher to show me the paper.
That is a smart step. Ask her which questions on electricity cost you marks and why. Then practise those question types. Next time, Ishaan, your hard work on that chapter will show in the score.
Tomorrow is our class picnic to the lake. I am in charge of snacks for six people.
That is a nice job. Think of things that do not spoil in the heat and are easy to share, like fruit, biscuits and sandwiches. Do you know if anyone has an allergy?
Grace cannot eat peanuts. Everyone else is fine.
Thank you for checking. Then keep peanut snacks out entirely, including peanut biscuits, and read the labels on packets. Fruit, plain sandwiches and baked chips would be safe choices for the group.
Perfect. Is there something Grace can enjoy extra then?
You could bring a small box of grapes or sliced mango just for her, or for everyone to share. That way Grace has something she knows is safe and does not feel left out of the picnic.
I do my homework in front of the television and it takes forever.
That slows almost everyone down. Your mind keeps jumping between the screen and the page. Try a quiet corner with only your books and a glass of water. You may finish in half the time.
But my mother says I can watch after I finish. I am Lucy.

Then your mother's rule is a good reward. Lucy, you could even set a timer, such as thirty minutes for maths, a short break, then thirty minutes for reading. The television will feel nicer when the work is done.
During those thirty minutes of maths, what should I do if I get stuck on a question?

Skip it for now, finish the easier maths questions before the timer ends, and come back to it after your break. If it is still hard, circle it and ask your teacher or a classmate next day. Do not let one question steal your whole evening, Lucy.
My music teacher asked me to sing solo at the annual day and I said yes without thinking.
That is a big honour. Teachers pick students they believe in. Now that you said yes, it might help to choose a song soon so you can practise. Do you know which song it will be?
She said I can choose. Maybe a slow song, because I get nervous on fast ones. My name is Kabir.
A slow song is a good choice, Kabir. It gives you time to breathe between lines and keeps your voice steady. Pick one you really like, since you will sing it many times while practising.
Should I tell her about the slow song idea?
Yes, tell her. She can say whether it suits the stage and your voice. Mention that you feel steadier with slow songs, Kabir, and she may even help you shape it.
Do you think I should stay up all night before the chemistry exam?
I would not. A rested brain remembers far more than a tired one. If you stay up all night you may forget what you studied or make silly mistakes. Sleeping a proper night is a better plan.
But I have not finished the last two chapters.
Then use tonight wisely. Skim the key points of both chapters, mark anything unclear, and sleep at a normal time. Waking a little earlier for a quick look is better than studying until dawn.
Okay. Which chapters should I look at first? One is on acids and the other on metals.

Begin with acids, since you will probably need to remember the reactions and their products. Then take metals. Make a short list of the important points from each chapter so your morning revision is quick.
Good. So acids first and then metals. Can you suggest what to do in the morning?
Yes. After breakfast, read your short list for acids, then the one for metals, as planned. Do not start anything new. Drink some water and walk calmly to the exam hall.
We have a new girl in class who sits alone at lunch.
That could feel lonely for her. Starting at a new school is hard. Do you know her name?
It is Zara. She just moved from Pune.
That is a big change. You could invite her to sit with you and your friends tomorrow. A simple hello and a question about her old school can start a friendly chat.
What could I ask her about Pune?

You could ask what she liked best about her old school or what her favourite food was in Pune. Listen to her answers. Zara will feel that you are interested, and soon she may open up and ask you questions too.
My little brother cries every time he has to do his spelling homework.
That sounds hard for both of you. Spelling can feel boring when it is a long list. Maybe you could turn it into a game. How old is he?
He is seven. His name is Aarav and he likes drawing.
Then use his drawing. Ask Aarav to draw a picture for each word and write the word under it. Seeing the picture helps him remember the letters, and it feels like play instead of work.
That is clever. What about the words he cannot draw, like "because"?

For words like that, you can make a silly sentence together, such as "Big elephants can always understand small elephants." The first letters spell "because". Aarav might enjoy making up his own sentence too.
My result day plan is simple. Wake up, go to school, collect the report card, come home.
That is a clear plan. It might help to add one small treat, so the day has something to look forward to. Maybe a favourite snack afterwards?
Yes, my mother promised me jalebi if I pass. I am Tom, and I am a bit scared of maths.
Hello Tom. Jalebi is a good reason to smile, though you may deserve a treat for trying anyway. Maths can feel scary, but you have worked on it all year, so try to go in calmly.
What was the treat again? I want to remind my mother.
Your mother promised jalebi if you pass. You can gently remind her tonight, and maybe suggest a small treat for working hard, too, even if maths turns out a little lower than you wish, Tom.
Our school is starting a gardening club and I am thinking of joining.
That sounds good. Gardening teaches patience, and you get to be outside. Do you have any experience with plants?
Only a tulsi plant at home that my grandmother looks after. I help water it.
That is a start. Watering and noticing how a plant changes is the heart of gardening. Your grandmother can probably teach you a lot, too, about when to water and how much sun a plant needs.
I should ask her before I sign up. Do you think that makes sense?
It does. Ask your grandmother what she has learned about growing the tulsi. You will walk into the gardening club already knowing something real, and she will enjoy sharing it with you.
My friend Rohan copied from me in the last test. I did not say anything but I felt bad.
Feeling bad shows you care about fairness. It was not your choice that he copied, but it is good you are thinking about it. What would you like to do now?
I do not want to get him in trouble. But I do not want it to happen again.
You can speak to him privately. Tell him honestly that you felt uncomfortable and you would like him to study on his own. A calm, friendly talk usually works better than anger.
What exactly could I say?
Something like, "Rohan, I felt uneasy when you copied in the test. I am happy to study together before exams, but I will not share answers during one." That is honest and keeps the friendship.
I get very car sick. We have a three hour bus ride to the fort next week.
That sounds uncomfortable. Many people feel better sitting near the front and looking out at the road ahead. Fresh air from a window can also help. Have you told your teacher?
Not yet. I am Grace, and I am afraid of looking silly.
Hello Grace. Motion sickness is common and nothing to be embarrassed about. Telling your teacher quietly means she can give you a good seat and keep a bag handy.
Which seat should I ask for again?
Ask for a seat near the front, preferably by a window, so you can look at the road ahead. Grace, you can also eat a light breakfast that morning and avoid reading on the bus.
My teacher gave us a project on our family tree. I only know my grandparents.
That is a fine place to start. You can ask your parents about their brothers, sisters and cousins and add them. Family trees often grow when people start talking.
My mother's family is big. Her sister Neha lives in Delhi and her brother Sameer lives in Dubai.
Great, those are two branches already. Draw your mother with a line to Neha and Sameer. You can add their children underneath once you ask your mother what their names are.
Let me ask my mother. Oh, and who lives in Dubai again?
Your uncle Sameer lives in Dubai, and your aunt Neha lives in Delhi. You could mark each on your tree with a small note about where they live, so the project looks complete.
I think my maths teacher does not like me. She never picks me to answer.
That must feel bad. Sometimes teachers pick students who put up hands the most, and it is not personal. Do you often raise your hand?
Not really. I am shy. My name is Meera.
Thanks for telling me, Meera. Maybe try raising your hand once a class when you are sure of the answer. That small step can show her you want to take part, and she may start calling on you.
What if I get it wrong in front of everyone?
Everyone gets answers wrong sometimes, and a good teacher sees it as part of learning. If you are nervous, Meera, start with an easy question where you feel confident, and build from there.
Sports day is next week and I signed up for the 200 metre race.
That is exciting, and a 200 metre race needs both speed and stamina. Have you been practising on a track or somewhere else?
A little. My friend Ishaan runs with me every evening in the park.
That is a great way to train. Running with a friend keeps you going on lazy days. Remember to stretch before you run and drink water afterwards.
Should I run faster or longer in my practice?
For a 200 metre race, short fast runs are more useful. Try a few quick sprints with rests in between. Keep running with Ishaan, since he makes it more fun, and you will feel ready on the day.
My cousin Fatima passed her board exams with distinction! I want to do something nice for her.
That is wonderful news. A thoughtful gesture will mean a lot. What does Fatima enjoy?
She loves books, especially mysteries. I have about two hundred rupees to spend.
Then a mystery novel is perfect and would fit that budget. A second-hand book shop might give you even more choice. You could also write a short note inside to congratulate her.
Good thinking. What should the note say?

Keep it warm and personal, something like, "Dear Fatima, congratulations on your distinction. You worked so hard and you deserve it. Enjoy this mystery. You have earned some reading time." Sign it with your name.
I want to start getting to school early. Right now I run in just as the bell rings.
That is a good goal. Being early gives you time to settle and chat with friends. What makes you late right now?
I wake up late and then take forever to get ready. I am Kabir.
Hello Kabir. Try getting your bag, uniform and shoes ready the night before. That cuts the morning rush a lot. Going to bed a little earlier will help you wake up easily too.
Okay, so what should I pack the night before?

Pack your books for the next day's timetable, your homework, your water bottle and your tiffin if it can be kept fresh. Keep your uniform and shoes next to the bag, Kabir, so nothing is missing at dawn.
I am Rohan. Can you help me plan revision for my history exam? It covers the Mughal period.
Happy to help, Rohan. Break the Mughal period into rulers: Babur, Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb. Give each ruler one day and note major events and buildings.
I only have five days though.

Then group them. Day one, Babur and Humayun. Day two, Akbar alone, since he usually gets many questions. Day three, Jahangir and Shah Jahan. Day four, Aurangzeb. Keep day five for revising everything.
Okay. Is there a trick for remembering the buildings?
Link each building to its ruler with a small picture or a rhyme. Shah Jahan and the Taj Mahal is easy, and Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri. Try drawing a mini timeline with a tiny sketch for each one.
Good. Which day did you put Akbar on again?

Akbar has day two, all by himself, because he is likely to carry the most questions. On that day, Rohan, read about Fatehpur Sikri and his main policies, then test yourself without looking at your notes.
I need help packing for a three day school camp in the hills.
Sounds like an adventure. The hills can get cold at night, so bring a warm jacket, socks and a cap. Do you know where you will sleep, in tents or in a hostel?
Tents, I think. Our teacher said to bring a torch too.
Then pack the torch with spare batteries, and a thick blanket or sleeping bag if the school does not give them. Tents can feel chilly early in the morning.
Should I bring a book as well?
Yes, one small book is nice for quiet time. Keep it in a plastic bag in case it rains. Do not bring anything valuable that you would be upset to lose.
Right. My name is Lucy, and I will ask Mum about the blanket. Remind me what the torch needs?
Lucy, the torch needs spare batteries, so pack a couple in a small pouch. Check that it works the night before. Then ask your mum about the blanket and you will be ready.
I did not get picked for the school quiz team and I am sad.
I am sorry. It hurts when you really want something and it does not happen. Do you want to tell me how the selection was done?
There was a written test and I missed the cut by one mark. My name is Ishaan.
Missing by one mark is hard, Ishaan. It shows you were close, though, and it is a good sign for next time. Some teams also add substitutes when someone falls ill.
Can I ask the teacher to let me be a substitute?
Yes, you can. Be polite and say you would like to help the team if there is a place. It shows you are keen. The teacher will appreciate that you asked.
What should I say exactly?
Try something like, "Sir, I missed the team by one mark. If any substitute is needed, I would be happy to be considered. I will keep practising." That is honest and respectful, Ishaan.
Our principal has announced no phones in class from next month.
That is a big change for many students. Some will find it hard at first. How do you feel about it?
I think it is fair. But I use my phone to check the time and my bus timing.
That is a real use. A cheap wrist watch could solve the time. For the bus, you could note the usual time in your diary instead of checking each day.
My friend Meera uses her phone to talk to her mother after school.
Then Meera might ask the school office whether students can use the phone there after class. Many schools have a rule for calls, so a short chat is worth trying.
Okay, I will tell her. What exactly should I tell my friend to ask?
Tell Meera to ask the school office whether she can use their phone after class to call her mother. That way she can still reach her mother after school without breaking the new rule.
I want to thank my class teacher before she retires. Any ideas?
That is a lovely thought. A handwritten card from the class is always special. Do you know how long she has taught?
Thirty years. Her name is Mrs Iyer and she taught my mother as well.
Wow, that is a long time. Teaching your mother and now you is something to mention in your card. It shows how many lives she has touched, and Mrs Iyer will treasure it.
Maybe we could all write one line each.
That would be touching. Collect one line from each classmate on a large sheet and let everyone sign. Add a small decoration, like flowers, and give it to her on her last day.
What line should I write?
Think of a real memory, like a time she helped you. Something such as, "Mrs Iyer, you taught my mother and then me, and both of us remember your kindness." That would suit your card well.
My brother Kabir just got his tenth class result and he scored very high. Everyone at home is celebrating.
What lovely news. Congratulations to Kabir, and to your whole family on a happy day. How are you feeling about it yourself?
Happy for him but also a bit nervous because next year it is my turn. I am Zara.
That is an honest feeling, Zara. His result shows what steady work can do, but your path is your own. You do not have to match his score to do well.
Do you think I should ask him how he studied?
Yes, that is a good idea. Ask Kabir about his daily routine and which methods helped. Take the ideas that suit you and leave the rest, since everyone learns a little differently.
What should I ask first?
Start with, "How many hours did you study each day, and what did you do before exams?" Kabir will be glad to share, Zara, and his answer will give you a base for your own plan.
There is a cricket match between our class and the other section tomorrow.
That sounds exciting, and a friendly rivalry makes a match more fun. Are you playing in it yourself, or just going to watch from the side?
Playing. I am Aarav and I am the wicketkeeper.
That is an important role, Aarav. Keep your eyes on the ball and stay low. Have you kept wicket before?
Only in the street with my cousins. I am scared of dropping catches.
Everyone drops catches sometimes, even professionals. Focus on the next ball rather than the last one. Soft hands, which means catching with a little give, help the ball stay in.
Thanks. Remind me what position I play tomorrow?
You are the wicketkeeper, Aarav, so you stand behind the stumps. Watch the ball all the way into your gloves, and stay calm even if you miss one.
Is it better to study in the morning or at night?
It depends on you. Some people feel fresh in the morning, and others concentrate better at night. What time do you feel most awake?
I think evenings. But my father says mornings are better. I am Tom.
You can try both, Tom. Many students use the morning for hard subjects and the evening for lighter revision. Notice when you learn most with the least effort.
I find science hard and drawing easy.
Then give science your best time. If that is your evening, do science then and keep drawing for when you are tired. Match the work to your energy.
Okay, so what should I do with science if it is in the evening?
Since you find science hard, Tom, start the evening with it for forty minutes while you are alert. Then take a break and do drawing, which you find easy, to end the day happily.
A boy in my class has stopped talking to me and I do not know why.
That is confusing and upsetting. Has anything happened recently, like a small argument or a joke that went wrong?
Maybe I laughed when he dropped his tiffin last week. His name is Rohan.
That could be it. People often feel embarrassed when something like that happens in front of others, even if the laughing was not meant badly.
Should I apologise?
If you think that is the reason, a short sincere apology is a good step. Do not make it big. Just say you did not mean to hurt him.
What would I say to Rohan?
Find a quiet moment and say, "Rohan, I am sorry I laughed when your tiffin fell. That was unkind. I hope we can be friends again." Keep your tone gentle and let him answer in his own time.
Our class is voting on where to go for the end of year trip. The choices are a zoo, a fort and a beach.
Those are three good choices, and each offers something quite different to enjoy on the day. Which one do you like best yourself?
I like the fort, but my friend Grace wants the beach.
It is nice that you have different picks. Maybe you could tell Grace what you like about the fort, and ask her why she likes the beach. Voting should be friendly.
Fine. The fort has a good history and a museum.
Those are great reasons. You could mention them to the class before voting. Many students enjoy a place where there is something to see and learn, as well as a place to walk around.
Wait, who was it that wanted the beach? I forgot.
Grace wants the beach. You like the fort because of its history and museum. Whoever wins the vote, you two can still enjoy the day together, maybe sharing the fun of the beach or the fort.
I have to read a novel for English class but I find reading slow.
That is common. Reading speed grows with practice, and the right book matters. Do you know which novel it is?
It is Black Beauty. I am Fatima.
Hello Fatima. That is a story told by a horse, which many readers enjoy because it feels personal. It is also a gentle read, with short chapters.
How can I make it faster?
Read a little each day, even fifteen minutes, in a quiet place. Try not to stop at each hard word. Guess its meaning from the sentence and move on. Speed will come on its own.
What should I do about words I do not know?

Keep a small notebook and note the ones that appear again and again. Look them up at the end of the chapter, Fatima, so you do not break your flow. Reading Black Beauty that way will build your vocabulary too.
I told my teacher that my dog ate my homework. It was actually true but she did not believe me.
That sounds frustrating. It is a funny excuse, so teachers often hear it when it is untrue. How did she react?
She gave me a warning. My dog is called Bruno and he chewed the whole notebook.
A chewed notebook is real evidence, if you still have it. Bruno has put you in a hard spot, though. Bring what is left of the notebook and calmly show her.
I threw it away. Now what?
Then do the work again and ask politely to submit it a day late. You can explain what happened without arguing. Teachers tend to be fair when students stay honest and polite.
Okay. What should I keep away from Bruno from now on?
Keep your bag and notebooks on a high shelf or in a closed cupboard, away from Bruno's reach. A chew toy for him may help too, so your homework stays safe in future.
I want to throw a small party for my friend who did well in her exams.
What a nice idea. A party shows a friend that you are proud of her. Do you know what she likes to eat or to do for fun?
Her name is Meera. She loves chocolate cake and board games.
Then a simple party at home with chocolate cake and a few board games would be perfect. Meera would enjoy it. You could invite just a few close friends to keep it relaxed.
I will ask my mother to help with the cake.
That sounds good. You could also decorate with a banner saying "Congratulations Meera" made from coloured paper. Hand-made decorations often feel the most special.
Can you remind me what Meera loves, so I plan the party right?
Meera loves chocolate cake and board games. So the cake from your mother and a few games for everyone will be perfect. Add the paper banner and the party is ready.
I always get anxious when the teacher hands out the question paper.
Many students do. Your heart beats fast and everything feels blurry for a moment. Does it pass after a minute or two?
Yes, but I lose time. I am Ishaan.
Then try this, Ishaan. When you get the paper, close your eyes and take three slow breaths before you read anything. That small pause settles your mind so you can think clearly.
What should I do after breathing?
Read the whole paper once. Mark the questions you know well, and answer those first. Starting with easy ones builds confidence and takes the pressure off the harder ones.
Okay. What was the first thing again, before I read?
First, close your eyes and take three slow breaths. Then read the whole paper, Ishaan, and begin with the questions you know best. Practise this at home with an old question paper.
My science teacher, Mr Das, keeps saying I have talent but I never believe him.
It is kind of him to say that. Why do you think you find it hard to believe?
I only get average marks. I am Grace.
Marks do not show everything, Grace. A teacher sees how you ask questions, solve problems and think in class. Mr Das may notice things your marks do not show.
How can I find out what he sees in me?
Ask him directly after class. Say you would like to know where you are strong and where you can improve. Most teachers love a student who asks for feedback.
Good. What is my teacher's name again?
Your science teacher is Mr Das. You could ask him tomorrow, Grace, something like, "Sir, what do you think I do well, and what should I work on?"
My grandmother is coming to stay with us during my exams. She loves talking.
That could be lovely, or a little distracting, depending on the day. Exam time is tense for everyone. How do you feel about it?
I love her but I need quiet to study. I am Tom.
Then you can tell her kindly. Say you would love to chat in the evening, and that you need quiet in the afternoon to study. Grandparents usually understand when you are honest and warm.
Good idea. She also makes the best parathas.
Then you may have a good deal, Tom. Study hard in the afternoon, then enjoy a paratha and a chat with her in the evening as your reward.
What did I say she makes? I told my friend and forgot.
You said your grandmother makes the best parathas. You could tell your friend that you study quietly in the afternoon so that evening chats with her and those parathas feel like a treat.
I want to run for school captain but I am afraid of speaking in front of the whole school.
It is brave to want that. Speaking to a large group can feel scary. What part worries you most?
Forgetting what to say. My name is Kabir.
Hello Kabir. Write your speech and keep it short, about two minutes. Practise it aloud many times until it feels familiar. A few notes in your hand can help too.
What should the speech be about?
Talk about two or three things you would do as captain, such as keeping the playground clean or helping new students. Be real and simple, since students respond to honesty.
I like the idea about helping new students. How do I make sure I do not forget it on stage?

Since forgetting what to say is your big worry, Kabir, write "new students" in large letters on a small card. Tie it to a short story of your own first day. A story is much easier to remember than a list of promises.
My football coach wants me to play defence but I want to be a striker.
That is a common clash. Strikers score the goals, so they get the glory. What does your coach say about why?
He says I am fast and tall. I am Lucy.
Those are real defender qualities, Lucy. Speed helps you catch attackers and height helps win headers. A good defence also starts the attack by passing forward.
But I still want to score.
You can tell your coach honestly. Ask whether you can try striker in practice matches, while you keep playing defence in real games. Teams grow when players are open about what they want.
Okay, I will ask him. What qualities did he mention again?
He said you are fast and tall. Tell him you accept defence, and ask for a chance to try striker in practice. Lucy, show your best in both spots and he may change his mind.
I have a recitation tomorrow and I cannot remember the last stanza.
That is stressful, but you still have time tonight to fix it. Forgetting the last part is very common. Which poem is it?
It is about the sea. I am Aarav.
Hello Aarav. Try writing the last stanza out by hand two or three times, then say it aloud without looking. Writing helps the words stick.
It also helps if I say it before sleep, right?
Yes, that works for many people. Say it before you sleep, and again in the morning. Sleep helps the brain store what you learned.
Great. So what is the plan?
Write the last stanza out by hand a few times, say it aloud without looking, and repeat it before bed. In the morning, say it once more. Then you will be ready, Aarav.
I lost my money on the school trip bus. I had two hundred rupees.
Oh no, that is upsetting, especially on a day meant to be fun. Did you check all your pockets and your bag carefully?
Yes, twice. I am Meera, and I think it fell out near the seat.
Hello Meera. Tell your teacher right away. She can ask the driver to check under the seats, or ask the class politely whether anyone found it.
She asked, but no one has it.
I am sorry. That is a hard lesson. The money may not return, but you can still enjoy the trip. Maybe your teacher can lend you what you need for lunch.
Okay. Where did I think it fell?
You said it probably fell near your seat on the bus. Meera, you could ask the driver to check once more when the bus is empty, in case it slipped between the seats.
Our results are up on the school notice board today. I am scared to look.
That is a very human feeling, and many students feel the same on result day. Would you like to go and look together with a friend?
Yes. My friend Grace will go with me.
That is a good plan. Having Grace beside you will make it feel lighter, whatever the numbers show.
What if I fail?

Then it will be hard, but it will not be the end. You will have options such as extra classes or retaking the exam. Look first, then decide what to do. Right now you do not know the result, so try not to worry too much.
Ok. Who is coming with me again?
Grace is coming with you. Go together, take a slow breath at the board, and read your number calmly. If there is bad news, you will have a friend right there to talk to.
I want to join the school choir but my friends think it is uncool.
Their opinion matters, but so does yours. It is your time and your voice. Do you actually enjoy singing, and would you like being in the choir?
I love it. My name is Fatima.
Then that matters most, Fatima. Friends may tease at first, but people are often impressed when you do something you enjoy and do well.
What if they keep teasing me?
Then you can tell them calmly that you enjoy it and that you would like them to respect that. True friends usually come around.
Okay. I will join the choir. What should I sing at the audition?

Choose a short song you know well and can sing comfortably, Fatima. Since you love singing, pick one that makes you happy, and your voice will sound warmer. Once your friends hear you in the choir, they may stop calling it uncool.
Our teacher said the exam syllabus is unit one to five. But I only studied one to four.
That is fixable, as long as you start now. How many days do you have?
Four days. I am Zara.
Hello Zara. You have enough time to cover one unit well. Spend the first day on unit five, then use the remaining days to revise the others.
Is unit five long?
I cannot see your book, so I do not know. Flip through it and count the pages first. If it is long, split it into two days and spend the last two days revising units one to four.
Okay. Which unit was I behind on?
You are behind on unit five, Zara. Start with it today, because it is the new one. Then use your remaining days to go back over units one to four.
Our class is going to the zoo on Saturday, and I am so excited I cannot sleep.
That is lovely to hear. A zoo trip is a happy event. Is there an animal you most want to see?
Giraffes! I am Zara. And my best friend Lucy wants the tigers.
Good choices, Zara. Giraffes are calm and tall, and tigers are powerful. The zoo may keep them far apart, so you could plan your walk to see both.
Oh, we could split the day. Giraffes in the morning, tigers after lunch.
That is a clever plan. Ask your teacher if the group can move freely, or whether you must stay together. Either way, you could take photos or draw sketches for each animal.
I will draw. Hey, which animal did Lucy want to see?
Lucy wants to see the tigers, and you want the giraffes. If you split the day, you could draw your giraffe in the morning and Lucy could sketch a tiger after lunch.
Perfect. I will tell her we can do the tigers after lunch.
Yes, tell Lucy about your plan. She will be glad to know her tigers have a time reserved, and you will both enjoy the day more, Zara.
I passed my class ten board exams! I scored 81 percent.
Congratulations. That is a strong score and it comes from real effort. How does it feel?
Amazing. I am Aarav. My mother cried happy tears.
That is beautiful, Aarav. Parents often feel everything your hard work meant. Have you thought about how to celebrate?
We are going out for dosa tomorrow. Then I need to choose a stream for class eleven.
A dosa dinner is a good way to enjoy the moment. Choosing a stream is a big decision, so take your time and do not rush right after celebrating.
I like science and I like art. I cannot decide.
Many students feel torn like that. Talk to your teachers about what each stream needs, and consider what you enjoy doing for hours without getting tired.
Okay. Can you remind me what my score was, so I can tell my teacher?
You scored 81 percent in your board exams, Aarav. That gives you good choices in more than one stream. When you speak to your teacher, mention both science and art, and ask how each fits you.
Our English teacher gave us a surprise test today without telling us.
That can feel unfair, because there was no time to prepare. Most teachers use surprise tests to check what has stuck, not to trap you. How did it go for you?
I did badly. I am Meera.
I am sorry, Meera. Surprise tests are hard because you cannot prepare. One test usually does not decide your whole grade.
She said it will count for ten marks though.
That is worth taking seriously, but ten marks can be made up. Check your term plan and see how many tests are left. Doing well in those will balance it out.
Maybe I should ask her for a retest.
You can ask, politely. Many teachers will say no, but some will allow it if you explain that you were not prepared. At least she will know you care.
What was the subject of the test again? I want to mention it.
It was an English test, from your English teacher. Meera, when you speak to her, say that the surprise English test went badly and ask whether there is any way to improve your marks.
I think I will fail my physics exam tomorrow.
That is a heavy thought to carry the night before an exam. Worry often makes things look worse than they are. What makes you think you will fail?
I did not understand the chapter on light. My name is Rohan.
Thanks for telling me, Rohan. Light has some tricky ideas, like reflection and refraction. Is there a particular part you do not understand?
Mostly the diagrams with rays and mirrors.
Then use tonight to practise those. Draw each ray diagram twice, label the angles, and note the rules in a line or two. Diagrams usually carry easy marks once the pattern is clear.
Do you think I can still pass?
I cannot promise a result, but one chapter is rarely the whole paper. If you do the other chapters well, you have a fair chance. Do your best tonight and rest properly.
Okay. Which chapter was it again that I had trouble with?
It was the chapter on light, Rohan, especially the ray diagrams with mirrors. Practise those first tonight, and then go over the other chapters quickly so that you feel steady.
My best friend Grace is moving to another city next month.
That is sad news, and I am sorry. Losing a close friend to distance is hard at any age. How are you feeling about it right now?
Very low. We have been friends since class one.
A friendship that long is precious. It is natural to feel low. Do you know where she is moving?
Bangalore. I am Kabir, and I live in Jaipur.
Thank you, Kabir. Bangalore is far, but you can still stay close with calls and letters. Many friends stay close across cities.
Should I give her a gift before she leaves?
That would be a thoughtful touch. It does not need to cost much. A photo album of memories from your school years could mean a lot to her.
Good. Can you remind me what city she is going to?
Grace is moving to Bangalore. Since you are in Jaipur, Kabir, you could plan a call every Sunday. The photo album could go in her bag on her last day.
I have to give a talk in assembly tomorrow.
Good for you. Speaking at assembly is a real chance to be heard. A clear topic makes the talk much easier to prepare tonight. What is the topic?
Kindness. I am Ishaan.
Hello Ishaan. Kindness is a lovely topic because everyone has a story about it. You could talk about a time someone was kind to you.
I remember a bus conductor who helped me find my lost bag.
That is a real and warm story. Begin with it, and then say what it taught you about helping others.
How long should the talk be?
Two minutes is usually right for an assembly. That is roughly two hundred and fifty words. Practise it once or twice aloud with a timer so you know the length.
I will do that. What story did I want to start with?
You wanted to start with the bus conductor who helped you find your lost bag. Ishaan, tell it in a few short sentences, then say what it taught you about kindness.
My school basketball team lost in the finals. We were ahead until the last two minutes.
That must hurt. Losing a close game stays with you. How is the team feeling?
Sad. Our captain Tom is angry at himself for missing a shot.
That is hard for a captain to carry. One miss does not lose a game. A team wins or loses together, even if it does not feel that way right now.
How can I tell Tom that?
Be gentle and honest. Tell him everyone made some mistakes, and that the team got to the finals because of what he did too. Listening matters more than advice right now.
He might not listen.
He may be quiet for a while. Give him a day or two, and then find a calm moment to talk. Just being around shows you care.
Let me try. Who was the captain again?
Your captain is Tom, who missed the shot he is upset about. When you talk to him, say the team reached the finals because of him and everyone else working hard together.
Do you think a book club at school is a good idea? I would like to start one.
I think it is a lovely idea. A book club lets friends share stories and opinions. Do you have anyone in mind to join?
Four friends so far. I am Fatima.
Good start, Fatima. Four is a nice size for a first meeting. You could add more later. Will you pick the books together?
Yes. Maybe we could begin with Charlotte's Web.
That is a gentle story with a clear heart, and it is easy to talk about. You could ask each member what they think about Wilbur and Charlotte's friendship.
Where could we meet?
Ask your teacher if you can use the library or an empty classroom during lunch. A quiet place with a few chairs is enough. You could meet once a week.
Okay. What book did I say we might start with?
You said Charlotte's Web, Fatima. At the first meeting, each member could share a favourite moment from the first chapters, and then you can all choose the next book together.
I got a very low mark in my art project. I worked on it for two weeks.
That is disappointing, especially after so much effort. What did the teacher say about it?
She said it did not follow the theme. The theme was water and I painted a mountain.
I see. It sounds like the instructions got missed. That can happen when you are excited about an idea. It is a lesson about reading the theme carefully.
I feel silly. My name is Lucy.
You need not feel silly, Lucy. Your mountain may have been lovely. Often, the problem is the topic, not the skill. Learn from it and keep painting.
Maybe I can paint the same mountain again but with a lake in front.
That is a great idea. A mountain reflected in a lake would answer the theme and keep your work. You could show your teacher and ask if she would look again.
What did I paint again?
You painted a mountain, Lucy, and the theme was water. Adding a lake in front, with the mountain reflected in it, could connect your painting to the theme nicely.
A boy in the lower class keeps pushing me in the corridor.
I am sorry that is happening. That is not okay. Has it happened more than once?
Three times this week. His name is Kabir.
Thank you for telling me. Pushing is not acceptable. It would be wise to tell your class teacher or another teacher so the school can help.
I am scared he will get angry at me.
That is understandable. A teacher can speak to him without making you the centre of it. Try not to be alone in the corridor, and walk with friends in the meantime.
Okay. I am Aarav. What should I tell my teacher?
Say clearly what happened, when and where. For example, "Kabir has pushed me three times this week in the corridor." Keep it short and factual, Aarav, and ask for help.
We are planning our class excursion to a historical fort. I am Meera, and I am the group leader.
Congratulations on being the leader, Meera. That is a responsible job. What do you need to organise?
A list of names, permission slips and a first aid kit.
Those are the key things. Check names against the slips at the entrance of the bus, and keep the kit where you can reach it. Count heads whenever the group moves.
Good point. What if someone gets lost?
Agree on a meeting point at the start and tell everyone. If someone is missing, tell the teacher right away rather than searching alone. Stay calm.
That helps. Hold on, what are the three things I need to organise again?
You need a list of names, permission slips and a first aid kit. Meera, you could put them in one folder so nothing is missed on the morning of the trip.
My friend Ishaan failed one subject and he wants to hide from everyone.
That is a painful moment for him. Sometimes people want to hide when they feel ashamed. Have you spoken to him?
He is not answering my calls. I am Fatima.
Hello Fatima. Give him a little space but let him know you are there. A short message, like "I am here whenever you want to talk", can mean a lot.
And what do I do if he still does not reply?
Try again in a day or two. Maybe stop by his house if that is normal for you. You could also ask a mutual friend to check on him.
Ok. What about his parents?
Be polite and do not discuss his result unless they bring it up. Let Ishaan share things himself when he is ready, and support him quietly.
Who failed again? I want to message him.
Ishaan is the friend who failed one subject. You could send him a short, kind note tonight, Fatima, saying you are thinking of him and that there is no hurry to reply.
I have a big pile of homework and a cricket match tonight.
That is a tough clash, but it can be managed with a little planning. Both things matter to you. Which one has the tighter deadline?
The homework is due tomorrow, the match is tonight at six. I am Tom.
Then split it. Do the hardest homework in the afternoon before the match. After you come back, finish what remains. That way both get done.
What if I am too tired after the match?
Then do the harder parts before the match and keep only revision or reading for after. Even an hour of focused work in the afternoon makes a difference, Tom.
Okay, thanks. What time did I say the match was?
The match is tonight at six. Tom, aim to have your hardest homework finished by about four thirty, which gives you time to eat and rest before you play.
My teacher scolded me in front of the whole class and I felt humiliated.
That sounds painful. Being told off in public can make anyone feel small. What happened?
I was talking while she was teaching. I know I was wrong. My name is Grace.
It is good that you can admit that, Grace. You can still feel hurt even if you made a mistake. Both things can be true.
Should I talk to her about it?
You could, politely, after class. Say you are sorry for talking and that you would like it if she corrected you privately next time. Many teachers will listen.
That sounds hard but fair.
It is hard, but it shows maturity. You do not need to be perfect in the talk. Just be calm, honest and short.
Who was it that I was going to talk to again?
You plan to talk to your teacher, Grace, the one who scolded you in class. Wait for a calm moment and say sorry for talking, then ask her to correct you privately next time.
I need to prepare a seating plan for the class exam. Can you help me think about how?
A good seating plan keeps an exam fair and calm. Are you the teacher, or a student helping with the room?
I am a student monitor. I am Kabir. The teacher asked me to arrange 30 desks in five rows.
Thank you, Kabir. Five rows of six desks would be tidy. Leave enough space between desks so students cannot look at each other's papers.
What about my friends? They want to sit together.
For an exam, it is fairer to mix students up. Your teacher probably wants friends apart, and she may have a rule. Check with her before you place anyone.
Okay. How many rows did she say?
She asked for five rows. With thirty desks, that makes six desks in each row, Kabir. Leave a clear aisle between rows so the teacher can walk through easily.
I just opened my result online and the page says "pending." What does that mean?
It usually means your result is not ready or is under review. Do not panic. Many schools mark results as pending for small reasons.
Why would it be pending?
Possible reasons are a missing document, a late mark entry or a technical delay. I cannot see your school's system, so the best step is to ask the school office.
My name is Zara. Should I call the office?
Yes, Zara. A short polite call or visit will give you the real reason. Keep your roll number and your name ready.
OK. What word did the page show again?
It showed the word "pending." When you contact the office, Zara, mention that your online result page says pending and ask them what is needed to clear it.
My friend Rohan always borrows my pencils and never returns them.
That can be annoying, especially when pencils vanish one after another. It is usually a habit, not a bad intention. Have you told him how you feel?
Not yet. I am Aarav and I do not want to start a fight.
Hello Aarav. You can bring it up kindly. Say something like, "Could you please return my pencils? I run out." Most people do not realise it bothers you.
What if he laughs at me?
He may laugh at first because it feels awkward. Stay calm and repeat your request. If he still does not return them, you may say no to lending next time.
Right, I will try. What was it he borrows?
Rohan borrows your pencils and never returns them. When you talk to him, Aarav, be friendly and clear, and ask him to bring them back by the next day.
My father wants me to be an engineer but I want to be a teacher.
That is a big difference, and it must be hard to carry. Your own interest matters here. What draws you to teaching in the first place?
I like explaining things to my younger cousins. I am Meera.
That is a good sign, Meera. Teaching is a respected job, and enjoying explaining is a real strength. Have you told your father why?
Not exactly. He gets angry when I bring it up.
Try choosing a calm time, and begin with respect. You might say you understand why he wants you to have a secure job, and then share what you enjoy.
Should I mention my cousins?
Yes, Meera. Explaining things to your younger cousins is a real example. It shows your interest is not just a passing idea, and your father may see a different side of you when he hears it.
Our school is organising a charity sale. We can bring things to sell.
That is a good cause, and a charity sale is a happy way to help. Many students bring things they have made. What are you thinking of bringing?
Homemade cookies. My grandmother makes great ones.
Homemade cookies usually sell fast. Ask your grandmother if she can bake two or three kinds so there is some choice. Wrap them in small bags with a label.
Good idea. I am Lucy. What should I write on the label?
Write the name of the cookie, the price and the date it was baked. You might add "Made with love by Lucy and her grandmother" to make it personal.
Perfect. Who is baking them again?
Your grandmother is baking them, Lucy, and you will wrap and label them. That is a nice team, and it will make your stall feel special.
I came last in the school swimming race today.
That can sting, especially after you worked to get ready. A race is also a brave thing to enter. How did it feel to swim in front of everyone?
Embarrassing. I am Ishaan. My friend Tom came first.
Hello Ishaan. Finishing a race takes courage. Congratulations to Tom too. Last place today does not decide your future in swimming.
I want to improve. Where do I begin?
Begin with breathing and kicking, since those matter most for speed. A coach can show you simple drills. Swimming a little each week works better than a lot once in a while.
Maybe Tom can give me some tips.
That is a good thought. Tom may be glad to share what he does. Ask him politely and try one tip at a time.
What do I ask him first?
Ask Tom how he breathes while swimming and how he keeps his kick steady. Those two things are a good place to start, Ishaan, and he may even offer to swim with you.
I feel jealous of my classmate who always gets full marks.
That is a very human feeling, and many students have it quietly. It does not make you a bad person. Do you know why it bothers you so much?
I study just as hard but she still beats me. I am Fatima.
That can be frustrating, Fatima. Effort does not always show up as the same marks. Maybe you are strong in other ways.
I am good at drawing. Everyone says so.
That is a real gift. Marks are one way to measure learning, but there are many others. Try to enjoy your own strengths and learn from hers.
Could I ask her how she studies?
Yes, you can. Ask politely, and listen. She may share a method that works for her. You do not have to copy it, just see if anything helps.
What was I good at? I forgot what I said.
You said you are good at drawing, and that everyone says so. That is a lovely strength, Fatima. Be proud of it while you work on your marks too.
I am the one who forgot the permission slip for the school trip tomorrow.
Do not panic, because this can usually be fixed. Teachers see forgotten slips all the time. Is there still time to get it signed tonight by someone at home?
My father is out of town until late. I am Kabir.
Hello Kabir. Maybe your mother can sign it, or another guardian at home. If not, call your teacher or send a message through someone and explain.
Mother is home. I did not think of her.
Then ask her tonight. Read the slip together so she knows what it says. Put it right inside your school bag as soon as it is signed.
Good. Who should sign it again?
Your mother can sign, since your father is out of town, Kabir. Check that the slip allows either parent to sign. Then pack it first, before anything else, so you do not forget again.
Can you help me think of a name for our class magazine? We are a group of eight.
Happy to help. A good name is short and tells readers what to expect. What will the magazine have in it, stories, jokes, news from school?
A mix of all. Stories, jokes and sports news.
Then a name that feels like a mix could work, such as "The Mixed Bag" or "Class Notes". Those sound friendly and suit different sections.
I like "The Mixed Bag". Our teacher Mrs Pillai will read it first, so it has to sound sensible.
It does sound sensible and playful together. Mrs Pillai will probably smile at it. Put the name in clear large letters on the cover with the class and year underneath.
Actually, my friend Rohan suggested "Eight Voices" because there are eight of us.
That is a lovely idea too. It tells readers that every member has a voice. You might use "Eight Voices" as the name and "The Mixed Bag" for the jokes page.
Oh, I like that. So what would go on the jokes page?

Under the heading "The Mixed Bag", you could put the best jokes and riddles from all eight of you, perhaps one from each person. Rohan's "Eight Voices" stays on the cover. Show both to Mrs Pillai before printing.
My teacher said I can bring one page of notes to the geography exam.
That is helpful. It means you must choose carefully what to write. A single page can hold a lot if you organise it well.
What should I put on it?
Put the things that are hard to remember rather than what you already know, such as dates, definitions and map names. Skip long explanations. Short keywords are enough.
I am Ishaan. I always mix up the names of rivers and where they flow.
Then a small outline map would be perfect, Ishaan. Draw the main rivers in a few lines and write each river's name along it. A picture is faster to read than a list.
I also forget the capitals. Can I put them on the same page?
Yes, if there is space. Write them in a corner as a short column. Make sure you can read your own writing, though, because small cramped text is no help in a hurry.
Good. So the page has the river map and the capitals. Anything else?

Add a few dates or terms that you often forget. Ishaan, remember that a page of notes does not replace studying. Read the river map and the capitals a few times tonight, so you only need to glance at them in the exam.
I want to give my science teacher a small gift on Teachers Day.
That is a kind idea. A gift does not have to be big. What kind of person is she?
Mrs Rao is cheerful and loves plants. I am Zara.
Then a small plant would be a thoughtful gift, Zara. A little money plant or a succulent in a decorated pot is easy to keep. Add a card with a handwritten thank you.
Our school said no expensive gifts though.
Then keep it inexpensive. A cutting from a plant at home in a recycled jar, decorated with paint, would cost almost nothing and still feel personal.
That sounds nicer than buying one. What should I write on the card?

Something like, "Dear Mrs Rao, thank you for making science so interesting. I hope this little plant brightens your desk. With thanks, Zara." Keep it short and sincere, so she can read it in a moment.
The marks I needed to enter the science stream were higher than mine.
I am sorry to hear that. That is hard news after working so hard. How are you feeling?
Lost. My parents had planned for me to study science. I am Grace.
Hello Grace. It makes sense to feel lost when a plan changes. There may still be paths, such as a re-evaluation, a different school or a bridge course.
What is a re-evaluation?
It is a request to have your paper checked again, in case a mistake was made in adding or marking. Not every board allows it, so ask the school office what the process is.
Ok. I will go tomorrow. What else could I ask there?
Ask about deadlines, fees and what other streams or related courses are open to you. Write the questions down tonight so you do not forget anything in the room.
Good. What was the first thing you said I should ask about?

The first thing was the re-evaluation, Grace, where your paper is checked again for errors. Ask the office if your board allows it, what the deadline is and what it costs, and then move on to your other questions.
The homework today is to interview an elder and write about their school days.
That is a nice task. You may hear some surprising stories. Who are you thinking of interviewing?
My grandfather. He went to school in a village and walked six kilometres every day. I am Tom.
Walking six kilometres is a lot, Tom. That will make an interesting story. Prepare a few questions beforehand so the conversation flows.
What kind of questions?
Ask what his classroom looked like, what he did for lunch, who his favourite teacher was and what games he played. Open questions bring longer answers.
Okay. Should I write while he talks?
You could jot down key words and finish the details after. If he is comfortable, you could record the chat, but ask for his permission first.
Great. I think I will start with the walk to school.
That is a good opening. You might ask, "Dada, how did you walk to school and what did you see on the way?" Then follow up on whatever he mentions, since six kilometres every day offers many stories.
My friends are planning a sleepover and I am not sure my parents will allow it.
That is a common worry. Parents often want to know details first. Do you know who will host it?
Meera's house. Her mother will be there. I am Fatima.
That helps, Fatima. Parents usually feel better when an adult is home and they know the family. You can ask your parents calmly and offer to share Meera's mother's contact number.
What if they say no?
Listen to their reason. They may be worried about something specific that can be solved. If it is still a no, you can suggest a daytime visit instead.
Good idea. Can I tell them it is just a few girls?
Be honest and give the real details, including who is going and the hours. Trust grows when you share facts without being asked, and that makes a yes more likely.
Okay. Whose house was it again?
It is at Meera's house, and her mother will be home. Fatima, mention that clearly when you ask your parents, and offer to give them her mother's phone number.
Our school bus broke down on the way to the picnic spot.
That is a bother, but at least you are together. Is everyone safe? Is the driver fixing it?
Yes, everyone is safe. The driver is calling a mechanic. We are sitting under a tree. I am Aarav.
Good, Aarav. A shady tree is a nice place to wait. Maybe your teacher can organise a game or a song while you wait.
We are playing antakshari. My friend Lucy is leading.
That is a lovely way to pass the time. A breakdown can turn into a fun memory. Drink water and stay close to your teacher.
What should I tell my parents? They will worry.
Your teacher will probably contact them, but you can send a calm message too. Say the bus broke down, everyone is safe, and you are playing a game while waiting.
Okay. What game were we playing, so I can tell them?
You are playing antakshari, and Lucy is leading it. Aarav, tell your parents that, and that the driver has called a mechanic. That should reassure them.
Is it normal to feel sick before an exam?
Yes, many people feel nervous in their stomach before an exam. Nerves can do that. Is it happening to you now?
Yes. I am Meera, and my exam is in ten minutes.
Meera, take a few slow breaths in through the nose and out through the mouth. Sip some water if you can. Sit quietly and do not read new notes now.
It helped a bit.
Good. Walk into the hall slowly. Once the paper begins and you start writing, the worry usually fades because your mind has something to do.
Thank you. If I still feel bad, what do I do?

If you still feel bad in the hall, Meera, tell the invigilator quietly. They deal with this often and can let you sit comfortably or have some water. Do not hide it, since your health matters more than the paper.
I joined the school drama club but I got a tiny role with only one line.
A first role is a start. Even one line counts. How do you feel about it?
A little let down. My friend Kabir has the lead. I am Rohan.
That is a natural reaction, Rohan. But a small role done well gets noticed. Stage plays need every part to work, and one clear line can bring the house down.
My line is "The king is coming."
That is a strong line because it announces something big. Say it loudly and clearly, with a little excitement. The way you say it can make the audience sit up.
Okay. How should I practise it?

Say it in different ways, whispering, shouting and in an excited voice, and pick the one that suits the scene. Practise standing straight and looking at the audience, Rohan, so that "the king is coming" lands with real energy.
We have a school marathon next month, five kilometres.
That is a nice challenge, and five kilometres is a distance many beginners can reach with some practice. Have you ever run that far before?
Never. The most I have run is about two. I am Lucy.
Then you have a month to build up, Lucy. Add a little distance each week and mix running with short walks. Slow and steady is better than a hard push that leaves you sore.
How often should I run?
Three times a week is good, with rest days between. Run on grass or flat paths if you can. Wear comfortable shoes and drink enough water.
Okay. My friend Grace will run with me.
That is great. A running partner keeps you going. Agree on a time and stick to it, even when the weather is dull.
What distance should we aim for in the first week?
Since you have run about two kilometres before, Lucy, try two and a half in week one, with walking breaks if needed. Add a bit each week, and you and Grace should be at five by race day.
I cried in class today in front of everyone. I feel so embarrassed.
That sounds hard. Crying is natural, and most classmates understand even if it feels awkward now. What made you cry?
Our teacher read out the lowest marks in the class. Mine was one of them. I am Ishaan.
That must have been hard to sit through, Ishaan. It is understandable that you felt hurt. You did nothing wrong by crying.
What if they tease me tomorrow?
Some may say something, but most will forget soon. If anyone teases you, say calmly that it was a hard moment and walk away. If it continues, tell a trusted teacher.
Okay. Is it right to talk to my teacher about it?
Yes, Ishaan, you can, politely. Tell her how it felt when the marks were read aloud and ask if she could share them privately in future. Many teachers change when students speak up.
My mother has a parent teacher meeting tomorrow and I am nervous.
That is natural, since a meeting with teachers can feel like a test for the whole family. It helps to know what is worrying you. What are you worried about?
My maths marks are low. I am Kabir.
Hello Kabir. It might help to tell your mother before the meeting, so she is not surprised. Parents usually feel better when they hear things from you first.
What if she gets angry?
She may feel worried, but telling her yourself shows honesty. Tell her you want to improve and ask for her help in making a plan.
Maybe I could ask my teacher for extra practice.
That is a very good idea. Tell your mother you plan to ask about it. Showing you already have a plan will make her proud, and it will help the meeting go well.
What was I worried about again?
You were worried about your low maths marks, Kabir. Tell your mother tonight, and mention your plan to ask for extra practice. That way she walks into the meeting with good news as well.
I borrowed a book from the school library and I spilled tea on it.
Oh no, that is unfortunate, but accidents happen to everyone who borrows books. The first step is to see how bad it is. Is the book badly damaged?
A few pages are wet and wrinkled. I am scared to return it. My name is Meera.
Meera, the best step is to dry it gently. Open it, place paper towels between wet pages, and leave it flat, not in the sun. Then tell the librarian honestly.
Will I have to pay for it?
I do not know the rules of your library, so you will need to ask. Some schools only ask for a small fee, and many appreciate honesty more than a hidden problem.
Okay. I will go on Monday.
Good. Dry the book carefully before then. When you speak to the librarian, say what happened and that you are sorry.
Which pages were wet again?
A few pages are wet and wrinkled, Meera, but you did not say which ones. Look through the book tonight and note the page numbers, so you can show the librarian exactly where the tea spilled.
I want to try out for the school football team on Wednesday.
Good for you. A trial is a brave step and a fun way to meet other players. Knowing your best position helps you prepare. Do you have a position you like?
Midfield, I think. I am Tom.
Hello Tom. Midfielders run a lot and need good passing, so work on both. Some light running and passing practice before Wednesday will help.
I have a friend, Aarav, who plays in a club. Maybe he can practise with me.
That is a great idea. Aarav can pass back and forth with you and show you moves. Short, focused sessions are better than one long one.
Cool. What should I ask my friend to help me with first?
Ask Aarav to start with passing, since that matters most for a midfielder. Do a light session with him on Tuesday and rest that night, Tom, so your legs feel fresh for Wednesday's trial.
I got a call from my school saying my results have been revised and my total went up.
That is wonderful news, and I am happy for you. A call like that can change a whole day. How do you feel about it?
Shocked and happy. I think a teacher found a mistake in my English paper. I am Zara.
That is lucky, Zara, and a good reminder that people do check. How many marks were added?
Fifteen. My percentage went from 71 to 74.
A real improvement. Fifteen marks can open doors, and it is nice that the school corrected it so fast.
I want to tell my teacher thank you. Do you think that is okay?
Yes, that would be a kind thing to do. Teachers rarely hear thanks for such things, and it shows good manners.
What should I say about the marks?
You could say, "Thank you for finding the mistake in my English paper. The fifteen extra marks raised my percentage to 74, and I am very grateful." That is polite and clear, Zara.
I am organising a school trip with my teacher. We need ideas for a one day outing near our town.
That sounds exciting. What are you looking for, something educational or a fun outdoor day?
Both would be perfect. We have about forty students. I am Rohan.
Thanks, Rohan. A nature park or a local museum with a lawn would give you both. A farm visit could work too, with a short tour and games after.
A farm sounds interesting. Most of us live in the city.
That is a good reason to pick it. Students could see how crops grow and watch animals up close. Ask the farm whether it takes groups and what rules they have.
What if some students are scared of animals?
Plan quiet activities too, like a walk around the fields or planting seeds, so no one feels forced. Let the students choose what to join.
Good. How many students were we taking?
About forty students, Rohan. For a farm visit that size, you might split them into small groups of eight or ten, with a helper for each group, so everyone gets a chance to see the animals.
I have been getting too many silly mistakes in my maths tests.
That is frustrating, but fixable. What kind of mistakes are they, like wrong signs or copying numbers wrongly?
Both. I copy numbers wrong and I add instead of subtract. I am Kabir.
Hello Kabir. When you copy numbers, read them back once. For signs, circle the plus or minus before you start. These small habits catch many silly errors.
What if I run out of time?
Leave a few minutes at the end of the exam to check your work. If you are short on time, check the easiest questions first, where you are likely to be careful.
That is good. Can you remind me what two mistakes I make?

You copy numbers wrongly and you add instead of subtracting. For the first, read each number back after copying. For the second, circle the sign first. Both habits are quick, Kabir, and will cut mistakes.
A teacher at our school is leaving at the end of this month and many students are sad.
That is a big change. Who is the teacher, if you do not mind me asking?
Mr Fernandes. He teaches geography and is really funny. I am Lucy.
Hello Lucy. Funny teachers make lessons memorable, so it makes sense that students will miss him. Did he say why he is leaving?
He is moving abroad with his family.
That sounds like a big chapter for him. You could organise a small farewell with a card or a class photo to show how much he meant.
That is a nice idea. What should we put on the card?

A short message from each student works well. You could write, "Dear Mr Fernandes, thank you for making geography fun. We will miss your jokes and wish you the best abroad." Everyone can add a personal line.
My little sister starts school tomorrow and she is scared.
That is a big day for her, and for your family too. Many children feel nervous on the first morning. How old is she?
Five. Her name is Meera and I am Aarav.
Hello Aarav. Five is a young age to start. Reassure Meera that everyone is new and that teachers are kind. A small toy from home might comfort her.
Can she bring one?
Many schools allow a small comfort object in the first week, but check with the teacher. A family photo tucked in her bag might also help if toys are not allowed.
I will walk with her in the morning. What can I say?
Hold her hand and tell her about the fun parts of your own school, like playground games or colouring. Keep your voice cheerful, Aarav, and tell Meera you will wave at her at break time.
I do not understand the poem we have to analyse. It is by a poet I have never heard of.
That can be tricky. Many poems feel strange at first. Do you have the poem with you? Even a line or two could help.
It is about autumn. I am Grace. I do not get why the poet compares leaves to coins.
Hello Grace. Poets often compare things to show an idea. Leaves turn golden and fall like coins dropping, so it could mean both beauty and the passing of time.
Oh. So it could be about time passing?
Yes, that is possible. Autumn is often used to show change and endings. Read the poem once more and see if other lines support this.
Okay. What was the comparison again?
The poet compares the leaves to coins, Grace. Both are golden and both fall. Think about what coins mean, such as value or spending time, and see whether the poem's mood fits that idea.
My friend Ishaan is going through a rough time because his parents are separating.
That is very hard for him. It is kind that you want to help. How is he behaving?
He is quiet and does not play with us anymore. I am Fatima.
Hello Fatima. Quietness is a common way to cope. You do not need to fix anything. Just keep inviting him and let him join when he is ready.
Should I ask him about it?
It is gentler to let him bring it up. You can say, "I am here if you want to talk," and leave it there. Then do normal things together.
Okay. I will do that. Who is it that I should keep inviting?
You said it is Ishaan. Keep including him in games and lunch, Fatima, even if he says no sometimes. Just knowing the invitation is there can comfort him.
My school is publishing the merit list tomorrow. I am hoping to be in the top ten.
That is a good target and worth aiming for. It also means you have probably been working steadily. How do you feel about the list coming out tomorrow?
Nervous but hopeful. I have worked hard all year. I am Tom.
Hello Tom. Hard work over a full year counts for a lot, whatever the list says. Try to rest well tonight so you meet the morning calmly.
What if I am eleventh?
Then you would still have done very well. One place does not erase your work. Try to see the whole picture, not just the list.
True. My friend Grace is also hoping. Should I congratulate her if she makes it?
Yes, if she makes it, congratulate her warmly. If you both make it, celebrate together. If only one of you does, be kind to each other.
What would I say to Grace if I do not make it but she does?
You could say, "Well done, Grace, you deserve it." Be honest that you are a bit disappointed, if you feel that way, but be glad for her. It keeps the friendship strong whatever the list says.
Can you suggest a good timetable for the week before exams?
Of course. A good timetable depends on how many subjects you have and how strong you are in each one. Can you tell me which subjects you are taking?
Maths, science, English, social studies and Hindi. My name is Meera.
Thanks, Meera. Pick one main subject per day for deeper study, and use a short slot each day to glance at the others. Put the harder subjects early in the week.
Maths and science are hardest for me.
Then give maths the first day and science the second. English and Hindi need less cramming, so they can share a day. Keep the last day for social studies and a quick overall check.
Perfect. What day is science again?
Science is on the second day, right after maths on the first. Meera, keep the evenings light with ten minutes of review on the previous day's subject, so it stays fresh.
I think I am too shy to ask questions in class. My teacher says it is important.
Your teacher is right, and many students feel the same way. What makes it hard for you?
I am scared people will laugh. I am Rohan.
Hello Rohan. Most classmates are busy with their own doubts and are glad when someone asks. Questions usually help the whole class.
Maybe I can write my questions down first and read them out.
That is a smart idea. Having the words ready makes it easier to speak. You can also ask your teacher after class if class feels too big.
Which one first, class or after class?
Begin after class, Rohan, since it feels safer. Once you are used to asking one person, try reading one written question aloud in class.
Our school is sending me to a district chess tournament.
Congratulations, that is quite an honour, because the school chose you to represent it. It says a lot about your game. How long have you been playing chess?
Four years. I am Kabir and I play every Sunday with my uncle.
Four years of Sunday games is solid practice, Kabir. Your uncle must be proud. How do you feel about the tournament?
Excited and a bit scared. There will be older players.
That is normal. Treat every game as a chance to learn. Older players may be experienced, but chess has surprises. Think carefully, use your time wisely and stay calm.
Should I practise something special before the day?
Review the openings you play most and a few endgames. Kabir, play one or two practice games with your uncle in a timed format, so you get used to the clock.
Our school canteen is changing its menu to healthier food and nobody is happy.
That can be a surprise, and changes to food often upset students at first. Some of it may also be a good thing. What exactly are they removing from the menu?
Samosas and fried snacks. I am Zara. Everyone loves samosas.
