Hello Zara. Samosas are a favourite for many. Healthy menus often keep a treat once a week, so it may be worth asking if that is possible.
Who should I ask?
You could write a short polite note to the school or canteen manager, or speak to your class teacher. A group of students asking together may carry more weight.
My friend Lucy wants to start a petition.
That is a fair approach if it is polite and clear. Ask students to sign and list their reasons, like a once a week samosa day, and present it to the teacher.
Good. What did we want to ask for?

You want to keep samosas available, perhaps once a week, even if the menu turns healthier. Zara, you and Lucy could put that on the petition and ask the manager if the menu could include a few baked snacks too.
Sometimes I feel like I am not good at anything.
I am sorry you feel that way. It is a heavy feeling, and many people have it at some point. Has something happened recently?
I did not make the dance team and my marks are average. I am Grace.
Hello Grace. Two disappointments at once can make anyone doubt themselves. But missing one team and having average marks does not mean you are not good at anything.
I like baking. Is that a real skill?
Yes, baking is a real skill. It takes patience, planning and care. Many people find joy and friends through it.
Maybe I could bake something for the class.
That is a lovely idea. Sharing something you made can lift your spirits and show others what you can do. Pick a simple recipe that you are confident about.
Okay. What did I say I like?
You said you like baking, Grace. It is a real skill, and a tray of something you made yourself could be a nice way to feel proud and share it with your class.
I have three exams next week: English on Monday, science on Wednesday and Hindi on Friday.
That is a spread of days, which is good because you get time to breathe between papers. Which of the three worries you the most?
Science, definitely. I am Fatima.
Then use Monday evening, after English is over, to begin serious science revision, Fatima. You will have Tuesday as a full day for it, which is helpful.
Wait, I forgot, which day is Hindi?
Hindi is on Friday, the last of your three exams. After science on Wednesday, you can spend Thursday on a calm Hindi revision, and then walk in on Friday without rushing.
My friend Kabir texted that the results are out and I have not looked yet. I am afraid.
That feeling is common, and it is brave to say it. You do not have to look alone. Is there someone you can sit with while you check?
My older sister Neha is home. She will sit with me.
That is a good choice. Neha can support you whatever you see on the screen. Take a slow breath first, then open the page together.
Thanks. Who will sit with me again? I want to call her over.
Your older sister Neha will sit with you. Call her over, tell her you are ready and open the results together. Whatever they say, you will have her beside you.
I am going to a school trip to Jaipur next month. I have never been there.
That is exciting. Jaipur has forts, palaces and busy markets. Do you know what you will visit?
The Amber Fort and the City Palace, I think. My friend Tom said we also go to a bazaar.
Lovely choices. At the fort you can walk up the ramps and see the old halls. The bazaar will be colourful, so keep your money and phone safe while you walk.
What was the first place on the list that I mentioned?
You mentioned the Amber Fort first, then the City Palace. Tom told you about the bazaar too. Take a notebook to jot down what you see at the fort, since you will enjoy remembering it later.
Our class teacher announced that the winner of the best student award is going to be selected by votes.
That sounds fair and exciting, because every student gets a say in who is honoured. Votes also make the award feel earned. Do you have anyone in mind to vote for?
Yes, Zara. She helps everyone with their work. I am Rohan.
Zara sounds like a kind classmate, Rohan. Voting for someone who helps others is a good reason to choose them.
Wait. If I vote for her, can I tell her? Or is it a secret?
Votes are usually secret, so it is best not to say whom you voted for. You can tell Zara in general that you think she is helpful, though, and that will make her smile.
I want to read more books this year. Can you suggest how to start?
A good start is to read a little every day, even ten minutes. Pick short books or stories you find interesting. What kinds of stories do you like?
Adventure stories and some mysteries. My name is Grace.
Hello Grace. Then look for short adventure books and children's mysteries from your school library. A librarian can help you choose, and you can finish one quickly to feel proud.
What kind of story did I say I like again? I want to tell the librarian.
You like adventure stories and some mysteries. Tell the librarian that, Grace, and say you would like short books to begin with. She may suggest a few you will enjoy.
We got a project on recycling from our teacher. I do not know where to begin.
A good way to start is with what you see every day. Look at what your family throws away in a week. What did you find?
Plastic bottles, newspapers and vegetable peels. I am Meera.
Good, Meera. That already gives you three groups: plastic, paper and food waste. You could explain what happens to each when it is recycled or composted.
Which one should I do first in my project?

Start with the vegetable peels, since you can make compost at home and show photos. Then add newspapers and plastic bottles. Your project will have a clear order from kitchen waste to paper to plastic.
Yesterday I played badminton with my cousin Ishaan and I won for the first time!
That is great news. Beating a cousin feels extra special. How did the match go?
It was close, 21 to 19. He is older than me. I am Lucy.
Hello Lucy. Winning a close match against an older player says a lot about your focus. Did you do anything differently this time?
Yes. I stayed calm and did not rush. Who did I beat?
You beat your cousin Ishaan, who is older than you, by 21 points to 19. Staying calm clearly worked, Lucy, so try to use the same approach in your next game.
I feel very left out because my friends made a group and did not add me.
That must hurt. It is hard when friends seem to be doing things without you. Do you know why it happened?
I am not sure. Maybe they forgot. I am Kabir.
Hello Kabir. It is possible that it was a mistake. Before assuming anything, you could ask one of them kindly, without blaming.
What should I ask?
Something light, like, "Hey, I saw you made a group. Can I be part of it?" Keep your tone friendly, Kabir, so they can say yes easily.
Our teacher said we can each bring one snack for the trip but nothing that melts.
That narrows it down, but there are still plenty of options. Dry snacks like biscuits, nuts or fruit would all work. What do you like?
Nothing with nuts, I am allergic. I like banana chips. My name is Zara.
Thank you for telling me, Zara. Banana chips are a good pick since they do not melt and are easy to carry. Check the packet for nut traces if you have a serious allergy.
Good point. What did I say I was allergic to?
You said you are allergic to nuts. So banana chips are fine as long as the packet says no nut traces. Zara, you may also want to tell your teacher about it before the trip.
I just changed to a new school and I miss my old friends terribly.
That is a big change, and missing friends shows how much they mattered. How long has it been since you moved?
Two weeks. I am Tom. My old best friend is Ishaan.
Hello Tom. Two weeks is still early. You can stay in touch with Ishaan by phone or letters while you make new friends slowly.
What if I do not make any new friends?
You will likely make a few over time. Start with one person who seems friendly, such as a classmate near you. Ask for help with something small or share a snack.
Okay. Should I tell Ishaan about my new school?
Yes, tell him, Tom. Sharing stories about your new school keeps your friendship alive, and it may even help you notice the good things there.
Our teacher told us the science paper will have an essay question. I have never written one.
That is a new thing for many students. A science essay is simply a clear explanation. Do you know the topic?
It might be about pollution. I am Meera.
Hello Meera. For pollution, use a simple pattern: what it is, what causes it, what harm it does, and what we can do. Four short paragraphs would be enough.
Can you remind me the four parts again?
Of course. First, what pollution is. Second, its causes. Third, the harm it does. Fourth, what we can do about it. Practise writing it once tonight, Meera, and time yourself.
My history teacher, Mr Khan, tells the best stories. I can remember everything he teaches.
That is wonderful. Stories help us remember because we picture the events. What was the last one he told?
About Emperor Ashoka and the battle of Kalinga. I am Rohan.
That is a powerful story, Rohan. Ashoka saw the suffering after the battle and turned toward peace. It stays in the mind because it has a strong turning point.
Sorry, which teacher was it who tells these stories?
Your history teacher, Mr Khan. A good storyteller gives you the people and the feelings along with the facts. Rohan, you could try telling that Ashoka story to a friend, which is also good revision.
Hi, today is result day. I got 88 percent in my final exams.
Congratulations on a fantastic score. You must be so pleased. How did you hear the news?
The school sent it by message and my father read it out. I am Grace.
That must have been a lovely moment, Grace. Hearing it from your father makes it even more special.
He said he would take me for ice cream. What did I score again? My mother wants to know.
You scored 88 percent in your final exams, Grace. That is a strong result, and your mother will be very happy. Enjoy the ice cream with your father.
For homework I should write about my favourite festival. I am thinking of Diwali.
That is a good choice. Diwali has lights, sweets, family and stories. What do you like most about it?
The lamps and rangoli. My sister Neha and I make rangoli together. I am Aarav.
Hello Aarav. That is a lovely detail for your writing. Describing how you and Neha make the rangoli, with its colours and patterns, will make the piece personal.
Should I write about the lamps first or the rangoli first?
Start with the rangoli, since you make it with Neha and it is your own story. Then move to the lamps lit in the evening. The ending can be the family sitting together.
My friend and I had an argument about who is the better cricketer, Rohan or Kabir.
That sounds like a friendly debate. Cricket arguments can go on forever. Who do you pick?
Rohan. He bats well. My friend picks Kabir because he bowls well. I am Lucy.
Hello Lucy. Both have strengths, and neither is wrong. You could look at their match records in your school team, or simply agree that batting and bowling matter equally.
Maybe I should just say we can both be right.
That is a mature way to end it. You could say, "Rohan bats better and Kabir bowls better, so each is best at something." That keeps the friendship safe, Lucy.
Our bus leaves at six in the morning for the trip and I am worried I will oversleep.
That early start is hard. Set an alarm, and maybe a backup too. Is there someone at home who can wake you?
My mother will, but she also sleeps heavily. I am Ishaan.
Hello Ishaan. Then use two alarms in different places, such as one near your bed and one across the room. Pack your bag the night before so the morning is simple.
What time should I set the alarm?
Think about how long you need to get ready and reach the bus stop. If you need an hour, set the first alarm at four forty five, and a second at five. Go to bed early tonight.
Right. What time does the bus leave again?
The bus leaves at six in the morning, Ishaan. With your bag packed the night before, a five o'clock alarm will give you enough time to wash, eat and walk to the stop.
I have been chosen as the class representative. I am not sure what I have to do.
Congratulations, that is a responsible role. A class representative speaks for classmates and takes their ideas to teachers. Has your teacher explained the duties?
A little. I should collect suggestions and tell the teacher. My name is Fatima.
That is a good summary, Fatima. You might keep a small notebook for suggestions and share them once a week, so you stay organised.
Good idea. What was the job again?
You collect suggestions from your classmates and bring them to the teacher. Fatima, keep that notebook handy, and let classmates know when you plan to speak to the teacher, so they feel heard.
I am training for the school relay race. I run the third leg.
The third leg is an important part, because you receive the baton and keep the speed up. Do you practise handovers?
Not enough. I am Tom. I get the baton from Zara and give it to Aarav.
Hello Tom. Handovers win and lose relays. Practise with Zara and Aarav many times, so you know when to start running and where to put your hand.
Who do I receive from again?
You receive the baton from Zara and pass it to Aarav. Tom, ask both of them to practise handovers three or four times each day this week, until it feels smooth.
I told a lie to my teacher about being late and now I feel guilty.
Feeling guilty shows you have a good sense of right and wrong. What did you say to her?
I said the bus broke down. Actually I overslept. I am Meera.
Thank you for being honest with me, Meera. It is not too late to put it right. You could tell her the truth quietly and apologise.
Will she be angry?
She might be a little disappointed, but teachers often respect honesty even when it comes late. Telling her will probably make you feel lighter, Meera, and she will see your good character.
I am doing a project on birds and I need to find three facts about the peacock.
The peacock is a great topic. Facts can come from your school library, textbooks or a trusted nature book. Have you looked yet?
I know one. It is India's national bird. I am Kabir.
That is correct, Kabir. Another well-known fact is that the male has a long, colourful tail that he spreads out in a display. Check your library book for one more.
Can you remind me which fact I already have?
You already have the fact that the peacock is India's national bird. Add the tail display fact, and find a third in your library book. Then your three facts will be complete.
I failed my Hindi exam and I did not tell my parents.
That is a lot to carry alone. It is natural to feel afraid, but they will probably find out. Telling them yourself is better. How do you think they will react?
They will be upset. My name is Zara. My father is very strict.
Hello Zara. It could be hard, but parents often help more than you expect once the first shock passes. Choose a calm time and tell them you want help to improve.
Who should I tell first, my father or mother?
Since your father is strict, you might tell your mother first, Zara. She may help you find the right words, and then you can speak to both of them together.
Today at school there was a fire drill. Everyone had to leave the building quickly.
Fire drills are important. They teach everyone how to leave safely. How did it go at your school?
Quite well. We lined up and walked to the ground. I am Rohan and my class teacher counted us.
That is exactly how it should be, Rohan. Staying calm and in a line keeps everyone safe. A teacher counting the class makes sure no one is left behind.
Why did she count us?
Your class teacher counted you to be sure every student is outside. If someone is missing, the staff can act quickly. That is why the line and the count matter so much in a drill.
I finished reading my first long book today. It took me three weeks.
Well done. Finishing a long book is a real achievement, and three weeks of steady reading shows patience. Many readers never get that far. What was the book about?
A girl who lost her dog and goes on a journey to find him. I am Lucy.
That sounds like a heartwarming adventure, Lucy. Stories with a long search often make the ending feel even better. Did she find him?
Yes, she did. Can you help me start a review using what I told you about the story?

Begin with the story in one line: a girl lost her dog, went on a journey to find him, and found him in the end. Lucy, then say what you liked about the journey and how proud you felt finishing it in three weeks.
Tomorrow is the science fair and my model of a volcano is not working properly.
That is stressful the night before. Volcano models often fail because of the mix. What are you using for the eruption?
Baking soda and vinegar. I am Meera. Nothing happens when I pour the vinegar.
Hello Meera. Try putting the baking soda into a narrow container, add a little dish soap and a few drops of food colour, then pour in the vinegar quickly. The soap makes bubbly foam.
I do not have dish soap at home. Can I use something else?
A little liquid hand wash can work in a small amount. If you have neither, try more baking soda and pour the vinegar faster. Practise outside or on a tray so the mess stays easy to clean.
Okay, I will try with hand wash. What did I say was not working?

Your volcano gives no eruption when you pour in the vinegar. Meera, try the narrow container with baking soda, a bit of hand wash and quick pouring, and test it once tonight so you are sure before the fair.
Thanks. And if it still fails?

Then show the model anyway, Meera, and explain how the eruption should work. Judges often value your understanding as much as the effect, and you can show your tests with baking soda and vinegar as proof.
I have a viva exam tomorrow for chemistry. I have never had one before.
A viva is an oral exam, where the teacher asks you questions and you answer aloud. It can feel scary the first time. What topics will it cover?
Acids, bases and salts. My name is Rohan.
Thank you, Rohan. Practise saying definitions aloud, such as what an acid is and how to test one. Explaining it in your own words is the best preparation for an oral exam.
What if I do not know an answer?
Do not make something up. Say politely, "I am not sure, sir, but I think it may be this," and give your best guess. Teachers like to see honest thinking.
Right. Which topics were they again?
The topics are acids, bases and salts, Rohan. Take each one and say aloud what it is, one example and one test. Do that in front of a mirror, and you will be ready.
Should I wear anything special?
Wear your usual school uniform, neat and clean. For a viva, Rohan, speak slowly, look at the examiner, and keep your answers on acids, bases and salts short and clear.
Our school is taking us to a pottery workshop and I am excited. I have never made anything with clay.
That sounds like a creative day. Clay is soft and forgiving, so beginners usually enjoy it. What would you like to make?
Maybe a small bowl. I am Aarav.
Hello Aarav. A bowl is a great first project. The teacher will probably show you how to shape the sides evenly. Keep your hands slightly wet so the clay stays smooth.
My friend Grace wants to make a vase.
A vase is a bit harder because of the tall shape, but she can manage with help. You could cheer each other on during the session.
Maybe I will make a bowl for my grandmother.
That is a lovely gift. A handmade bowl carries a lot of care. You could paint it in her favourite colour once it dries.
What did Grace want to make?
Grace wants to make a vase, and you plan a bowl for your grandmother. Aarav, ask the teacher how long the clay needs to dry, since you will want to paint your bowl afterwards.
Can I tell you a story about my friends in parts? It is a bit long.
Of course. Go ahead and tell it however you like, and I will follow along.
Part one. Last week my friend Ishaan lost his lunch box and thought someone had taken it.
That sounds upsetting for him. Lost things always feel like a mystery. Did he look for it?
Part two. He asked everyone in class. I am Fatima and I helped him look. We even checked the staff room.
Good teamwork, Fatima. Searching together is a kind thing to do for a friend, and checking the staff room was thorough. What happened next?
Part three. It was in his own bag, under his sports shirt. He was so embarrassed.
That is a funny ending in a way, though I understand why he felt embarrassed. Everyone misplaces things. Hopefully you both laughed about it.
We did. Where did we finally find it?
You found Ishaan's lunch box in his own bag, under his sports shirt. You and Ishaan checked the whole class and even the staff room first, Fatima, so it makes a good story to laugh about later.
Tomorrow is the day for the class ten results and I cannot focus on anything.
That is a common feeling the night before results. Your mind is busy with what could happen. What have you tried to calm down?
Nothing really. I am Kabir. I keep refreshing the website even though results are not out.
Hello Kabir. Refreshing it will not change the result or speed it up. Try putting the phone in another room for an hour and doing something simple with your hands.
Like what?
A short walk, some cooking, a puzzle or helping at home would do. Anything that needs a little attention but is not stressful.
My brother has a carrom board. Maybe we can play.
That is a perfect distraction. A friendly game with your brother will pass the time and bring a few laughs. Keep the phone away while you play.
Okay. What did you say I should stop doing?
I suggested you stop refreshing the website, Kabir, since results are not out yet and it does not change anything. Play carrom with your brother instead, and check the website only tomorrow.
My coach asked me to be the vice captain of our school kabaddi team.
Congratulations, that is a mark of trust. Kabaddi needs courage and teamwork. How do you feel about the role?
Proud but a little scared. I am Lucy. The captain is Tom, and he is very good.
Hello Lucy. It is natural to feel that way. The vice captain supports the captain and steps in when needed. Working with Tom, you can learn from him as you go.
What should I do first?
Talk to Tom about how you can help. Ask what he expects, and offer to take care of small tasks like warm-ups or team talks. That builds trust early.
That sounds good. Should I also talk to my coach?
Yes, ask your coach what he wants from a vice captain. His expectations matter as much as Tom's. A short chat will remove most of your fears.
Who did I say the captain was again?
The captain is Tom, whom you describe as very good. Lucy, learn from how he leads the team, and let him know you are ready to support him in matches and in practice.
I need a birthday gift for my sister Anjali. She turns 16 on Saturday and loves drawing.
Sixteen is a nice one to mark. Since she loves drawing, a good sketchbook with thick paper and a set of soft pencils would be a lovely gift. Do you have a budget in mind?
Around 500 rupees. Maybe I should add something small too, like a card.
That fits well. Put the sketchbook and a pencil set in one bag, then write a short note inside the card about a drawing of hers you liked. A personal line means more than a long message.
Good idea. Her favourite is the sketch she made of our old neighbourhood tree.
Then mention the tree in the card. Something like, I still remember your tree drawing, keep making more. It shows you notice her work, and she will remember it for a long time.
Can you remind me what the budget was and how old she is turning?
You said around 500 rupees, and Anjali is turning 16 on Saturday. That is enough for a decent sketchbook and a small pencil set, with a little left over for the card.
My friend Sam keeps cancelling our plans at the last minute. It is the third time this month.
That would annoy me too. Three times in a month is a pattern, not bad luck. You could tell him calmly how it feels, without accusing him. Do you know why he keeps cancelling?
He says he is tired from work. But he still goes out with other people.
That stings, I can see why. Try saying it plainly, like, when you cancel on me, I feel left out. Then ask him what would make plans easier for him. Let him answer before you decide anything.
Okay. Should I talk to him on the phone or message him?
A phone call is better for this. Tone gets lost in text and he may read it as an attack. If you are nervous, jot down two or three points first so you stay calm.
Good. How do I bring up the other people without sounding jealous?

Mention it as a question, not a charge. You could say, I noticed you were out with others last week, so I wondered if our plans are just harder on weekdays. That gives Sam room to explain his tiredness honestly.
My cousin Vikram is getting married next month in Jaipur. I have no idea what to wear.
How lovely, a Jaipur wedding sounds colourful. Do you know if there are separate functions, like a mehndi or sangeet? Each often has its own dress style, so that helps decide.
There is a mehndi, a sangeet and the wedding itself. Three days.
Then plan three outfits. Something light and bright for the mehndi, something you can dance in for the sangeet, and a richer one for the wedding. You can reuse accessories to keep it simple.
Jaipur will be hot, right? I do not want to sweat all day.
Yes, it can be warm, so choose soft cotton or light silk. Pick lighter colours for the day events and carry a small fan or scarf. Comfortable footwear matters on a long day too.
Which of the three days should get the most comfortable outfit?
The sangeet, since that is where you will be dancing at Vikram's celebration. Choose a flared skirt or loose kurta set that moves easily, and shoes you can wear for hours.
My little brother Leo borrowed my headphones and broke them. He just says sorry and walks away.
That is frustrating, especially when the apology feels too quick. Did he offer to fix or replace them, or is it only the word sorry so far?
Only sorry. He is nine, so he has no money.
Right, so replacing them may not be fair. He could still help, like doing a chore for you or giving up a small treat until you can get repairs done. Have you told your parents?
Not yet. I do not want him to get into big trouble.
That is kind of you. You can speak to Leo first and ask him how he plans to make it right. If he stays vague, then a quiet word with your parents is reasonable.
Since he is so young, what small thing could he realistically do?
At nine, Leo could do your dusting chore for a week or give you his Saturday cartoon slot. Keep it small and clear, so he feels he has made up for the broken headphones in some way.
My grandparents are visiting us for two weeks. I love them, but I am worried the house will feel crowded.
It is nice that you love them and still feel a bit worried. Both can be true. Where will they sleep, and will you have any private space?
They will take my room. I will sleep in the living room.
That is generous, though it may feel odd. Ask for a shelf or a box for your daily things so you are not hunting for clothes. A small routine helps in a shared space.
Also I study in the evenings. The TV will be on a lot.
Tell your grandparents about it early, in a friendly way. Ask if the TV volume can stay low for two hours each evening, or find a quiet corner at a neighbour's, a library or a balcony.
Could I study in my own room instead, while they are out for a walk?
Yes, that is smart. When your grandparents go for their evening walk, your room is free, so you get a quiet hour at your own desk. Tell them the plan so they know to leave your things alone.
I had a small fight with my friend Hannah about a group project. She did not do her part.
That is irritating, especially if your marks depend on it. Did you already say something to her, or did the fight start from a heated moment?
It started in the corridor. I got loud and said she was lazy.
Calling her lazy probably made her defensive. Next time, try describing what happened instead, like, the slides are not done yet and the deadline is Friday. It is harder to argue with facts.
Should I apologise first? I still think she was wrong.
You can apologise only for how you spoke and still hold your point about the work. Something like, I am sorry I raised my voice, but I need your part by Thursday. That is honest and fair.
Good. Will it help to leave out the word I used in the corridor?
Yes. Do not say lazy again. Stick to the missing slides and the deadline. Hannah can then answer about the work instead of defending herself, and the talk stays calm.
My cousin Nisha is coming to stay for the summer holidays. She is a year younger than me.
That should be fun. Having a cousin around for the holidays means company for games and talks. What are you thinking of doing with her?
Maybe cycling in the mornings, and cooking something together on weekends.
Both are good ideas. Morning rides are cool and quiet, and cooking together is a nice way to talk. Pick one easy dish, like pasta or sandwiches, so nobody feels the pressure to be perfect.
She is vegetarian and I am not. Will that be a problem?
Not at all. Make a vegetarian dish you both enjoy, like paneer rolls or vegetable pasta. You can cook your own extras separately later. The important thing is that Nisha feels welcome in the kitchen.
Great. So what should we make on the first weekend?
Paneer rolls would be a good start. They are easy and vegetarian, so Nisha can eat everything, and you can add an egg or chicken filling on your own roll if you like.
Priya forgot my birthday yesterday. We have been friends for eight years.
Oh, that must have hurt, especially after eight years. Did she say anything, or has she not noticed yet?
She has not said anything. Maybe she is busy with exams.
That could be the reason. People often lose track of dates during exam weeks. You might wait a day or two, then tell her gently that you felt a little sad.
I do not want to make her feel guilty though.
You can keep it light, like, I know exams are heavy, but I missed hearing from you on my birthday. That tells the truth without blaming her. Most good friends respond with a warm apology.
Okay. How long should I wait before I say it?
Wait until her exams end, if they finish this week. Priya will have a clear head then, and you can mention the birthday kindly. After eight years of friendship, one honest chat should be fine.
I am planning a surprise party for my dad's 50th. Where do I even start?
What a nice plan. Start with three things: the date, the guest list and the place. Is your father someone who enjoys a crowd, or would a small group of close people suit him better?
Small group. Maybe fifteen people. He likes quiet dinners.
Then a home dinner or a small private room at a restaurant could work. Ask your mother to invite the guests quietly so he does not hear. Decide who brings what, so the work is shared.
My uncle Omar can keep a secret, so I will ask him to help.
Good choice. Uncle Omar can bring your dad out of the house for an hour while you set up. Just give him an easy reason to give, like a short errand or tea at a nearby place.
Perfect. What should Omar tell Dad to get him out?
Omar could say he needs help choosing a gift or a phone plan, something your father enjoys advising on. Keep it believable and short, so Omar is back with him just as your guests arrive.
We are going to my aunt's house on Sunday. She always asks me about my marks and I hate it.
That can be tiring. Many relatives ask about marks because they do not know what else to say. Do you want to avoid the topic, or just have a good answer ready?
A good answer ready. I did not do very well last term.
Then keep it short and true. Something like, it was a hard term, and I am working on it. Then add a question about her, like asking how her garden is doing. People love sharing their own news.
What if she keeps pushing?
Smile and say, I would like to talk about something else today, maybe my plan to improve. You are allowed to set a gentle limit. If it continues, your parents can help change the subject.
Can I tell my mother before Sunday so she helps out?
Yes, tell her before the visit. She can steer your aunt away from marks when you arrive on Sunday, and you will not feel alone if the question comes up.
My older sister Diya and I share a room. She leaves her clothes everywhere and it drives me mad.
Sharing a room is hard when habits differ. Have you ever talked to her about it, or is it building up quietly?
Building up. I just sigh and pick them up.
Sighing may not tell her much. Choose a calm moment and say what bothers you, like, clothes on the floor make the room feel messy and I need my side clear. Then suggest a small fix.
Like what kind of fix?
A basket for her clothes would do it, or one hook on her side of the wall. Make it easy for her to follow. You could also agree on a quick tidy before bedtime each night.
I think the basket is better. Should I buy it myself?
If it is cheap, buying the basket yourself is a friendly gesture, and Diya may feel less lectured. Give it to her with a smile and say it is for her side of the room.
I have to give a short speech at my best friend Ethan's wedding. I am terrified.
Congratulations on being asked. Being nervous is normal, and it usually means you care. How long should the speech be, and do you know what you want to say?
About three minutes. I know a funny story from college, but I am unsure if it is okay.
A funny story can work well if it is kind and does not embarrass him or his family. Ask yourself whether Ethan would laugh at it or wince. Keep the ending warm and positive.
It is about him sleeping through an exam and still passing.
That sounds harmless and sweet. Tell it in a few sentences, then link it to what makes him a good friend, like how he stays calm. End with good wishes for the couple.
Where should I put that story, at the start or the end?
Put the exam story near the start, so you open with a laugh and settle your nerves. Then move to what you admire in Ethan, and finish with your good wishes for the couple.
My friend Omar is moving to another city next week. I do not know how to say goodbye.
That is a big change. Saying goodbye can feel awkward. What do you two usually enjoy doing together? A last meetup around that could feel natural.
We play cricket every Sunday in the lane behind our building.
Then make this Sunday special. Gather a few friends for one last match in the lane, and maybe take a group photo afterwards. Simple and familiar is often the best goodbye.
Should I give him something?
A small gift is a nice touch. Perhaps a framed photo from the match, or a note with a favourite memory. Choose something he can keep easily while he is unpacking in a new city.
The photo idea is nice. Can I connect it with what we play?
Yes. Take the group photo during your last cricket match, with the bat and ball in front, and write the date on the back. Omar will remember those Sundays in the lane every time he sees it.
My brother and I argued over the TV remote again. Mum shouted at both of us.
Remote arguments are common between siblings, even if they feel big in the moment. How old are you both, and what were you each trying to watch?
I am 14, he is 11. I wanted a cricket match, he wanted cartoons.
A simple schedule might help. For example, he picks first for an hour, then you pick. Or the match is on during its time and cartoons come after. Fair rules reduce shouting.
He will say he was there first.
Then agree that whoever is watching a show gets to finish it, and the other chooses next. Say it calmly when you are both in a good mood, not in the middle of a fight.
What if the match runs longer than his cartoons would?
Then the cartoons wait, but he gets the next slot without argument. Tell your younger brother he can pick the first show after the cricket match ends, so the long match feels fair to him.
My cousin Sam and I used to be close but we barely talk now. He lives abroad.
Distance can do that, even when people still care. Do you miss him, or are you just noticing the gap now?
I miss him. I just do not know what to message after so long.
Keep it simple and honest. Something like, I was thinking about you today and wondered how you are. You do not need a big apology for the silence. A warm hello is enough.
What if he replies slowly because of the time difference?
That is likely, so do not read too much into it. Choose a time that suits both places, and send voice notes if typing feels stiff. Over time, a regular check-in can rebuild the habit.
Should I mention anything from when we were kids?
Yes, a shared memory is a great opener. Mention something funny you and Sam did as children, and ask if he remembers it. That bridges the years quickly and warmly.
It is my son's seventh birthday on Friday. He wants a space-themed party. Any cheap ideas?
A space theme is great and can be done on a small budget. Think paper stars, dark blue sheets for the wall and silver foil planets. Will it be at home?
Yes, at home, with about eight kids.
Then you can make a rocket cake from a simple sponge, and a moon rock treasure hunt using crumpled foil balls hidden around the house. Kids this age enjoy games more than fancy decor.
What about the return gifts?
Small glow-in-the-dark stickers or a star-shaped pencil in a paper bag work well and cost little. Let each child pick a planet sticker as they leave, so everyone feels included.
Nice. With eight kids, how many gift bags do I need?
Eight guests means eight bags, plus one spare in case a cousin turns up. Your birthday boy gets the party itself, so you do not need a bag for him, just a star pencil for his desk.
My uncle Vikram always makes jokes about my weight at family dinners. Everyone laughs but I do not.
I am sorry, that is hurtful, and you do not have to laugh along. Has anyone ever told him it bothers you?
No. I am afraid it will make things awkward.
A private word is the gentlest way. Choose a quiet moment and say, I know you mean it as a joke, but comments about my body upset me. Please stop. Most relatives change when they understand.
What if he says I am too sensitive?
You can stay calm and repeat it, like, maybe so, but I would still like you to stop. You do not need to win the argument. Your feelings are a good enough reason to ask.
Should I tell my parents about him first?
That can help. If your parents know about Uncle Vikram's jokes, they can back you up at the next dinner. You can still talk to him privately yourself, since a direct word is often what works.
I want to invite my new classmate Nisha over, but my old friend Hannah might feel left out.
It is thoughtful of you to think about both. Do Nisha and Hannah know each other at all?
Not really. Hannah is a bit shy.
Then you could invite them together. Choose a simple activity like baking or a board game, so they have something to do besides making conversation. Shy people relax when there is a task.
What if they do not get along?
Then you have not lost anything. You will still have time with each of them separately later. Do not push them, just include both and let the friendship grow naturally if it is going to.
Which game would work best for a shy person?
Pick something with simple rules and teamwork, like a card game or a word puzzle. Hannah can join without speaking much at first, and Nisha will see how kind your shy friend is.
My sister's wedding is in two months and my mother is stressing about everything. How can I help?
It is kind of you to ask. Wedding planning is a lot for one person. Has your mother mentioned which tasks worry her most?
Mostly the guest list and the catering.
Offer to take one of them completely. For example, you could manage the guest list in a simple notebook or sheet, with names, phone numbers and who has replied. That takes a big load off.
I can do that. What about the catering?
You can sit with her to make a shortlist of caterers, check what each includes, and ask relatives for recommendations. Let her make the final decision so she feels in control, but you do the legwork.
Maybe I should start the guest list tonight, then. Where do I begin?

Start with the names your mother already has in mind, and add your sister's friends and your father's relatives. Put each phone number beside the name, and mark who is coming. Share the finished list with your mother, who can then focus on the caterers.
My roommate Priya and I keep arguing about the dishes. We both think the other does less.
That kind of quarrel is very common. It often grows because nobody has tracked who does what. Do you have any system now?
No, we just wash when we notice.
Then try a simple schedule. Alternate days, or one of you cooks and the other cleans. Put it on the fridge so it is clear and neither of you has to guess or keep score.
She says her days are busier than mine.
That may be true on some days. You could agree that on very busy days the other person covers, and then they swap back. A fair rule that allows for swaps usually ends the arguing.
Good. How do I bring up the schedule without starting another fight?

Choose a calm time, not right after a dirty-dishes moment. Say you want to stop arguing and suggest the fridge chart. Let Priya change a day or two, since having a say makes her more likely to follow it.
My twin brother Ethan got a better score than me in maths. I feel bad even though I am happy for him.
It is human to feel both together. Being happy for him and sad for yourself do not cancel each other. Is this the first time he has scored higher?
No, it happens a lot in maths. I do better in English.
Then you each have a strength. It might help to stop comparing and ask Ethan for tips on maths, since he is good at it. You could offer to help him with English in return.
Do you think he would actually help?
Most siblings enjoy being asked. Say it simply, like, can you show me how you solved question five? Twins often learn well together, and it may bring you closer rather than make you rivals.
Okay. And what could I offer him in return, exactly?
Since English is your strong subject, offer to read his essays and point out where a sentence could be clearer. Ethan could get better marks in writing, and you both gain from the swap.
I forgot my friend Leo's birthday and he is upset. What should I do?
Forgetting happens, but it is good that you want to fix it. Start with an honest apology. Have you talked to him yet?
Only a quick sorry in the corridor.
A corridor sorry may not feel like enough for him. Write or say a longer one, like, I am really sorry I forgot, it matters to me, and I want to make it up to you.
How can I make it up to him?
Plan a small celebration of his own. Take him for a snack he likes, or make a card with a few funny memories. It shows effort, and that matters more than an expensive gift.
He loves samosas. Is that enough for a make-up treat?
Yes, samosas are a good start, because they show you remember what he likes. Take Leo to his favourite stall, give him the card, and tell him you are sorry again while you eat together.
My mother wants me to call my aunt every Sunday but I find it boring. What do I say for twenty minutes?
Many people feel that. A call goes easier with a few topics ready. What does your aunt like talking about?
Her garden and her cat, mostly.
Perfect, those are easy starters. Ask what is blooming this week or what her cat did lately. People love talking about what they care about, and you will not need to fill the time yourself.
What if I run out of things to say?
Share one small thing from your own week, like a funny moment at school or a new dish you tried. Even a short call is fine. Ten warm minutes is better than twenty forced ones.
I could ask about her cat first. What is a good question?
Ask what the cat has been up to lately, or where it likes to nap in her garden. Your aunt will probably tell a story, and that can fill many minutes without effort.
Hannah and I want to start a tiny book club, just the two of us. Any tips?
Lovely idea. Pick one short book you both want to read, decide a weekly meeting day, and keep the talk loose. Two people can chat for hours about a story. Do you already have a book in mind?
I was thinking of a mystery. She likes those, I prefer fantasy.
Then take turns choosing. Hannah picks the first book, a mystery, and you pick the second, a fantasy. That way each of you gets to share something you love, and nobody feels outvoted.
Okay. I keep mixing us up, though. Which of us likes mysteries again?
Hannah is the mystery fan, and you prefer fantasy. So Hannah picks the first book, a mystery, and your fantasy choice comes next. Ask her what she thought of your pick afterwards.
What can I cook for my husband's birthday? He is not fussy but likes spicy food.
Something with a little heat and a festive feel would be nice. How many people are you cooking for, and do you want a full meal or a special dish?
Just the two of us, plus our daughter. Dinner at home.
Then a pot of chicken biryani or, if you prefer vegetarian, a paneer tikka masala with jeera rice. Both are spicy and feel like a treat. Add a simple dessert like kheer so it feels special.
Biryani sounds right. Can I make it a day before?
Yes, you can prepare the masala and marinate the chicken the day before. Cook the rice and assemble on the day, so it smells fresh. Kheer can also be made earlier and chilled.
My sister Priya is two years older than me and always bosses me around.
That can be wearing. Older siblings sometimes act like a second parent without noticing. Does she boss you about big things, or small daily stuff?
Small things, like what I wear or when I should study.
Then you could tell her kindly, I know you mean well, but I want to decide those things myself. If she hears it calmly, she may ease off. If not, ask your parents to remind her.
I will try that. She is leaving for college next month actually.

That changes things a little. Priya may be worried about leaving you, which can make the bossing stronger now. A warm talk before she goes, with her advice welcome only when you ask, might help you both.
My neighbour's kids kicked their ball into our flower pots again. My mother is furious.
Broken pots are upsetting, especially if it keeps happening. Has anyone spoken to the neighbours yet?
Not yet. Mum wants to shout from the balcony.
Shouting could turn a small thing into a bigger fight. A calm word at their door works better. She could say the pots were damaged and ask if the children could play farther away.
Okay, I will suggest it. What if they say kids will be kids?
Your mother can agree and still ask for a solution, like a play spot at the far end of the lane. Calm and firm usually works. Staying friendly with neighbours matters for years ahead.
I am attending a wedding alone and know almost nobody there. It is my colleague's.
That can feel awkward but it is manageable. Weddings usually have lots of moving parts, so people mix easily. Do you know at least the couple?
I only know the groom, from work. I will say hi and probably sit in a corner.
Say hi to him, then look for other colleagues, since they will be there too. If you stay in a corner, you will feel more alone. Sit at a table with friendly faces and ask how they know the couple.
That is a good question to ask. Anything else?
Compliment something, like the decorations or the food, and listen to the answer. People enjoy telling their stories. Leave when you feel ready, after wishing the groom well and eating something.
My cousins are coming over this weekend. There will be six of us kids at home. What games can we play?
Six is a good number for lots of games. How old are you all? Games depend on whether the group is young or mixed.
Between 8 and 15.
Then try something everyone can join: hide and seek in the evening, a team treasure hunt with clues, or a quiz with teams. The older ones can write clues and the little ones can search.
The treasure hunt sounds fun. How should we set it up?

Write five or six clues on paper, each leading to the next hiding place. Put a small prize at the end, like sweets to share. Make two teams so there is a friendly race, and let the oldest cousin judge.
My dad snores so loudly that my mother has moved to the guest room. Should I be worried?

It is understandable to be concerned. Loud snoring is common, and many couples sleep apart for rest. I cannot tell what causes it, but a doctor can check if it seems heavy. Is your mother upset about it?
A bit tired, but she jokes about it. Dad is embarrassed.
Then be gentle with both. Tell your father it is not a big shame. If he is willing, a visit to a doctor is a sensible step, since that is the right person to look at it properly.
Okay. I will bring it up softly when he is relaxed.
That is the right way. Choose a calm moment, maybe over tea, and say you care about him and want everyone to sleep well. Avoid teasing, since he already feels embarrassed.
I had a great evening with my friend Anjali yesterday but now I feel strange, like I talked too much.
That feeling is common after a happy evening. Did Anjali seem bored, or is it more a worry in your own head?
She laughed and asked questions. I just think I went on about my job.
If she was laughing and asking questions, she was probably interested. People are usually kinder to us than we are to ourselves. Next time, you could ask about her job to even things out.
Right. Her new job is pretty interesting, actually.
Then ask Anjali about it next time. A simple, how is the new job going, shows you care, and it gives her a chance to share. Friendships feel balanced when both people get their turn.
Do you think a 12-year-old would like a book as a birthday present from me? She is my niece Diya.
Many twelve-year-olds enjoy books if the subject fits their taste. What does Diya usually like to do in her free time?
She loves animals and is always watching nature shows.

Then a book about animals would be a good match. Look for a colourful one with true stories about rescued wildlife or one about a day in the life of animals. Photos help keep a twelve-year-old interested.
I will check a bookshop. Should I add anything to go with it?
A bookmark with an animal picture would be sweet, and a handwritten note inside the cover. Diya will see you chose it just for her love of animals, which makes the gift feel personal.
My two friends, Leo and Omar, are not talking to each other and both keep telling me their side.
That is an uncomfortable spot to be in, with both friends giving you their story. Do you know what started the quarrel?
Leo says Omar did not invite him to a football game. Omar says he did, but Leo never replied.
It sounds like a misunderstanding. Try not to take sides. Instead of passing messages between them, suggest that Leo and Omar speak to each other directly, so nothing gets twisted on the way.
What if they both refuse?

Then give it a little time, and stay friendly with both. You could invite them to something casual separately. If you keep repeating each side, you may end up in the middle of it, so stay neutral about the football game itself.
I got invited to a friend's destination wedding in Goa, but the trip is costly. I am torn.
It is a fair worry. Weddings can be expensive when travel is involved. I cannot give financial advice, but I can help you think it through. How close are you to your friend?
Very close. We were roommates for three years.
Closeness matters, and you could also ask yourself what you would feel later if you missed it. Some people go for fewer days to keep it manageable, or join just for the main ceremony.
The ceremony is on the second day. I could go for that only.

That could be a sensible compromise. Going just for the second day in Goa lets you be there for the main moment, and you can send a heartfelt note to your old roommate for the rest of the celebrations.
My brother Vikram and I are planning a surprise for our parents' anniversary. He keeps changing the plan.
Planning with a sibling can be tricky when ideas keep moving. What was the original plan?
A dinner at their favourite restaurant. Now he wants a trip to a hill station.
A trip is a bigger plan and needs more time and money. You could agree that dinner happens on the day and the trip comes later as a second gift. That way both ideas survive.
That is clever. I will tell him it is dinner on the day, then the hill station later.
Good, it keeps the peace. Settle the restaurant booking first, so the anniversary is safe, and then you and Vikram can start planning the hill station trip calmly without any pressure on the date.
My mother-in-law is visiting for a month. I want things to go well but I am nervous.
A month is a long visit, so it is wise to prepare. Have you two had a good relationship until now?
It is okay. She is a bit particular about how the kitchen is run.
Then ask her early what she likes in the kitchen and maybe give her a corner that is hers. People feel respected when they have a say. You can keep your own routine for everything else.
I like that idea. She loves making pickles.
Then invite her to make pickles with you and give her a shelf for the jars. It gives her a reason to feel at home, and you might learn her recipe too, which can bring you closer.
Priya and I are going to a concert together on Saturday. I am worried about crowds.
Concerts can be loud and busy, so it makes sense to plan. Is it indoors or outdoors, and do you know when you would arrive?
Indoors, in a big hall. We planned to get there an hour early.
An hour early is a good idea. You will find a better spot and get in before the rush. Agree a meeting point with Priya in case you lose each other, and keep your phone charged.
Good. Where should we agree to meet, though?
Pick a landmark that is easy to describe, like the main entrance pillar or the snack counter near the front. Tell Priya before you go so you both know exactly where to meet if you get separated.
My best friend Sam is turning 30 and says he does not want any fuss. But I think he secretly would like something.
Some people say that and still enjoy a small gesture. Do you have a sense of what he would like, even if he will not ask?
He likes quiet time, music, and good tea.
Then a small afternoon with a few friends, nice tea, and a playlist of his favourite songs could be perfect. Keep it relaxed, with no big surprise or speech, so it fits what he said.
That is exactly his style. Maybe I will gift him a tea set.
A tea set would suit him well, since he likes good tea. Pair it with a handwritten note for his thirtieth, and you will honour his wish for no fuss while still showing you care.
I snapped at my mother this morning when she asked me about my exam results again. Now I feel awful.
It sounds like you were stressed, and you feel bad about it. That shows you care. Do you want to talk to her, or are you not ready?
I want to apologise but I also want her to stop asking so much.
You can do both. Say you are sorry for snapping, and then explain that the questions make you anxious. Ask if you can share news when you are ready, instead of her asking each day.
What if she says she is only worried?
Then you can say you understand and thank her for caring. Offer to give her an update on a set day, like Sunday evening, so she knows she will hear about your exam results without having to ask.
My cousin Anjali just got a job in Pune and I want to throw her a small party. Who should I invite?
That is a thoughtful idea. Think of the people she is closest to, so the group stays relaxed. Who does she usually spend time with?
Mostly our cousins and two school friends. About ten people.
Ten is a nice size for a home party. Ask the school friends and cousins, keep the food simple, and write a card that everyone signs. She can take it to Pune as a keepsake.
I love the card idea. Should it be a surprise?
A surprise can be sweet, but check with her parents so she is free that evening. Keep the card hidden until the end, then give it to Anjali with a toast to her new job in Pune.
We always argue when the whole family goes on a trip. Last time it was over which route to take.
Family trips can bring out small fights, especially in a car with many people. Who usually decides the route?
My dad, but my uncle always disagrees.
One way is to agree on the route before you leave and let one person navigate. Then there is a clear plan, and the rest of you can relax. Decide who has the final say, politely, in advance.
I will suggest it. Should my uncle navigate then, to keep him happy?

That is a thoughtful compromise. If your uncle navigates and your father drives, both feel useful. Just agree beforehand that the route chosen at the start stays unless there is a real problem like a closed road.
My friend Ethan keeps borrowing money and forgetting to return it. It is small amounts, but it adds up.
That is a tricky one. Small amounts can still feel unfair. Have you reminded him before?
Once, as a joke. He laughed and said he would pay soon. That was a month ago.
A joke may not have registered as a real reminder. Next time, say it plainly and kindly, like, I noticed the money from last month is still pending, can you return it this week?
What about future requests?

You can say you are not comfortable lending right now. That is allowed, and you do not need a long reason. Good friends respect a clear no, and it protects the friendship from more small resentments with Ethan.
I am the bridesmaid for my cousin Nisha. She wants us all to wear the same pink dress, but I do not like pink.
Being a bridesmaid often means some compromise. It is her day, but your comfort matters too. Have you told her how you feel?
Not yet. I do not want to cause drama.

Try asking if a slightly different shade or style is possible, instead of saying you dislike pink. For example, a dusty rose may feel different. Offer to match the fabric or style so the group still looks together.
That is a gentle way. What if she insists on the exact pink?
Then decide whether it is worth a disagreement. It is one day, and Nisha will treasure having her bridesmaids match. You can wear it with gold jewellery that you like, to make it feel more yours.
I want to make a card for my grandmother's 80th birthday. What should I write?
Eighty is a lovely milestone. A few warm lines in your own words are best. What is one thing you love about spending time with her?
She tells me stories about her village and teaches me old songs.
Then mention that. You could write, thank you for the stories about your village and the old songs you taught me. They are the best part of my visits. Happy 80th birthday, Nani.
I like it. I might add a drawing of her village.
A drawing will make it even more special. Even simple sketches of the fields or the well she describes will show her you listened closely to her stories, which is a lovely gift for your grandmother.
My little sister Anjali wants to sleep in my bed every night since she saw a scary movie. I need my space.
It is kind that you care but it is also fair that you need space. How old is Anjali, and was the movie very scary?
She is seven. It was a ghost story at a friend's house.
At seven, scary images can stay in the mind for days. You could compromise, like she can stay on your floor with a blanket for a few nights, and then go back to her own bed. Tell your parents too.
Good idea. Maybe a night light for her room would help.

A night light is a lovely, simple idea. Show Anjali that her room is safe by checking it together before bed, and keep the door slightly open. Within a few nights, she will likely feel ready for her own bed again.
I borrowed my friend Omar's bicycle and scratched it. I have not told him yet and I am dreading it.
Scratches feel big when you are the one who caused them, but telling him soon is the better path. How bad is the scratch?
Not huge, but visible, on the side of the frame.
Then tell him today, plainly, before he finds it. Say, I scratched your bicycle and I am sorry, and offer to help fix it or pay for a touch-up paint. Honesty will matter more than the scratch.
Okay. I will go to his house after dinner.

Good plan. Take the bicycle with you so he can see the scratch himself, and let him react. Omar will probably appreciate that you came yourself and told him the truth instead of waiting for him to notice.
My cousin Leo and I are the same age and our parents keep comparing us. It is exhausting.
That sounds draining. Comparisons can make cousins feel like rivals even when they get along. How do you and Leo feel about each other?
We are good friends. He hates it too.

Then you already have an ally. You and Leo could joke about it privately, and even agree to answer comparisons with something kind about each other. That quietly shows your parents the habit is not needed.
Nice. We could say something nice about each other every time.
Yes, and it may work well. If your parents compare, you praise Leo and he praises you. After a few tries, the adults may notice that two cousins who support each other do not need ranking.
Guess what, my cousin Diya is finally visiting from Dubai next week!
That is exciting news, a visit from Dubai is a big event. How long has it been since you last saw her in person?
Almost three years. She was twelve then, so she must be taller than me now.
Three years is a long gap, and children change a lot between twelve and fifteen. You will probably have plenty to talk about. Are you planning anything for her arrival?
Mum is making her favourite, rajma chawal. And I want to take her to the old bookshop near our house.
Both are sweet touches. Rajma chawal says welcome without a single word, and the bookshop will help you two settle into easy chat. Does she like reading?
Yes, mostly comics. We used to swap them all the time.
Then the bookshop is perfect. You could each pick one comic for the other as a welcome gift and keep the old swapping habit alive. That would make her feel she is truly back.
Wait, what dish is Mum cooking again? I want to tell Diya to skip lunch.
Rajma chawal, her favourite. Tell Diya to arrive hungry. After lunch you can take her to the bookshop and choose your comics together.
I have a problem. My friend Leo told me a secret, and now my other friend Sam is asking me about it.
That is a tricky spot. A secret told in trust is worth protecting. Does Sam know there is a secret, or is he guessing?
He saw Leo upset and thinks I know why.
Then you can be honest without sharing details. Say that Leo told you something private and it is his to share. That is truthful and does not reveal anything. Most people respect that.
What if Sam gets annoyed with me?
He might be a bit annoyed at first, but he will likely understand later. You could add that you would keep his secrets safe too. That shows him why you are careful.
Should I tell Leo that Sam is asking?
It is a good idea. Leo should know others noticed he was upset, and he can decide what to share with Sam. It also shows him you protected his secret.
Okay. I will tell Leo tonight. Is it wrong to feel relieved I did not say anything?
No, it is not wrong at all. Relief is natural when you keep a promise under pressure. You did the right thing for Leo, and Sam may even trust you more later.
My daughter Hannah is turning ten and wants a sleepover. I have never hosted one.
A sleepover is a lovely way to celebrate ten. How many girls does she want to invite?
Five, so six including her.
That is a manageable number. Plan simple things: a movie, snacks, a few games and sleeping bags in one room. Let the parents know the pick-up time in the morning so there are no surprises.
What if someone gets homesick in the night?
It happens often at that age. Keep a phone nearby so she can call her parents, and let her sit with you for a while with some warm milk. Most children settle again quickly.
What kind of snacks would work for the movie?
Popcorn, fruit slices, mini sandwiches and a bowl of chips are enough. Check with each family about allergies first. A hot chocolate before bed makes the evening feel special.
Good. Can you tell me again how many girls will sleep over besides Hannah?
Five guests besides Hannah, so six girls in total. Make six beds or sleeping bags, and keep one spare for a friend who might change her mind at the last minute.
I want to gift something to my cousin Nisha for her wedding. Cash is boring.
A thoughtful gift is a nice idea. What do you know about their plans, like where they will live?
They are renting a small flat in Bengaluru.
A small flat means space is limited, so something useful and compact would be good. For example, a nice set of cups and plates, a framed photo of the two families, or a good lamp.
I like the framed photo. We have a great picture from her engagement.
That is a lovely choice, since it carries a memory. Get a simple frame in a colour that fits a small flat, like warm wood or white. A short note on the back adds a personal touch.
What should I write on the note?
Keep it simple and warm, like, dear Nisha, wishing you both a home full of laughter. Then sign it with your name and the date of the engagement photo.
Nice. Remind me, which city are they moving to?
Bengaluru. They are renting a small flat there, so a framed engagement photo is a good fit, since it takes little space and gives the new home something personal.
Me and my brother had a huge fight about who gets the bigger room. My parents said we must decide ourselves.
That is a big decision to make together. What reasons does each of you give?
I am older, so I think I deserve it. He says he has more things.
Both are real reasons. A fair way might be to look at what the room is used for. If he needs space for his things and you need it for studying, maybe you can agree on a trade.
What kind of trade?
For example, he takes the bigger room, and you get the better desk, a lock for your drawer, or the room with the better light for study. Each of you gets something important.
He might say that is not fair. He is a bit stubborn.
Then suggest a trial. Try the arrangement for a month and then talk again. People accept a change more easily when it is not forever.
Okay, good idea. But what was his reason again, so I can respond properly?
He said he has more things, so he needs more space. Respect that point, and then explain that you need a good study spot. A month's trial lets both of you test it.
We are cooking for twenty relatives this weekend. My grandmother wants everything homemade.
That is a big cooking job, but also a lovely tradition. Who will be helping in the kitchen?
Me, my mother, and my aunt. Grandmother will direct.
Then divide the work early. One person makes the main dish, one handles the sides and rice, and one does the sweets. Grandmother can check the taste and tell stories while you work.
Can we prepare some things the night before?
Yes, definitely. Chop vegetables, soak lentils, make the dough and prepare the masala paste the night before. Keep them covered in the fridge. Saturday will be much calmer.
What about dessert? Grandmother likes her gulab jamun.
Gulab jamun can also be made a day early, since the syrup soaks in better overnight. Reheat gently before serving. Your grandmother will be proud to see her favourite on the table.
Right. And how many relatives did I say are coming?
Twenty relatives. Plan food for about twenty-two, to be safe, and make a double batch of gulab jamun so your grandmother's favourite does not run out.
I made a new friend at the gym today. Her name is Priya. Is it weird to ask her for coffee?
Not weird at all. Friendly invitations are common, and coffee is a low-pressure way to chat. Did you two talk a lot?
Yes, we chatted for about fifteen minutes between sets.
Then a coffee invite sounds natural. You could say, I enjoyed talking today, would you like to get coffee after our workout sometime? Keep it casual, so she can say yes or no easily.
What if she says no?
Then smile and say no problem, and keep chatting at the gym as before. A no to coffee is not a no to friendship. People may be busy or prefer to keep gym time just for exercise.
Good. Should I invite her after the workout or ask in advance?
Asking Priya at the end of a session works well, since you are already together and relaxed. If it is too sudden, ask her for the next time you see each other, so she has a day to think.
My brother Ethan is getting on my nerves. He keeps coming into my room without knocking.
That is annoying when you want privacy. Have you told him you want him to knock?
I have, but he forgets or does it on purpose. He is twelve and thinks it is funny.
At twelve, testing limits is common. A sign on your door that says knock first could help. If he keeps ignoring it, tell your parents so they can back the rule.
I could add a small lock too, but Mum might not like it.
It is worth asking her, and explaining that you want a calm space for homework. Parents often agree if you give a clear reason. A knock rule is also a gentler first step.
Ok. What should the sign say?
Keep it short and a little funny, like, Please knock. This room belongs to someone who is studying. If it makes Ethan smile, he may follow the rule more willingly than if it sounds angry.
One more thing, how old did I say he is?
Twelve. At twelve, Ethan will likely respond better to a rule that sounds fair and slightly playful, so the sign and a calm word with your parents should work.
My grandfather turns 75 next month. We want to do something meaningful, not just a cake.
Seventy-five is a lovely milestone, and a meaningful plan is a great idea. What does your grandfather enjoy doing or talking about?
He loves old Hindi songs and he used to be a teacher.
Then you could organise a small gathering where family members sing his favourite songs. You could also ask former students to send short messages, which would mean a lot to a teacher.
The messages idea is great. How do we find his old students?
Ask your grandfather's old friends or neighbours, or any school contacts he still has. A short note can be passed on by relatives. Even three or four messages will be a precious surprise.
We could make them into a little book.
Yes, print the notes on plain paper, add old photos if you have them, and tie everything into a simple booklet. He can read it again whenever he wants.
Great. What else did I say he loves, besides teaching?
Old Hindi songs. At the gathering, play or sing his favourite songs, and hand him the booklet from his students at the end, so he gets both his music and his teaching memories.
My friends are all getting married and I feel left behind. I am 28 and single.
That feeling is more common than people admit. Many friends feel it when weddings come one after another. Are you feeling pressure from others, or mostly from yourself?
Both. My aunts keep asking when it is my turn.
Those questions are tiring, even when people mean well. You can answer lightly, like, when it happens, you will be the first to know. Then change the topic. You do not owe anyone a timeline.
I try, but it still hurts sometimes.
It is fine that it hurts. Be kind to yourself on those days. Spend time on things you enjoy, and keep up with friends who do not ask about it. Your life is full already, even without a wedding.
I do enjoy painting. I joined a class last month.
That is a wonderful step. A class gives you new people, a skill and something of your own to look forward to each week. Does the painting class feel good so far?
Yes. Actually, can you remind me what age I said I was?
You said you are 28. That is still young, with a new painting class and lots of time ahead, so the questions from your aunts do not need to decide how you feel.
My cousins Anjali and Vikram are twins and they keep fighting at family gatherings.
That sounds noisy. Do they fight over the same things each time, or does it change?
Usually it is about who got the bigger slice of something or who sits where.
Then small rules might help, like one person cuts and the other picks first. Seating can rotate. These fights are often about feeling treated fairly, not about the food or seat.
I am older than both of them. Should I step in?
A little, but gently. You could be the referee for the cutting rule so it feels like a game. If you scold them, they may turn on you, so keep the tone light and fair.
Okay. The cutting rule is clever. Who picks first?
Let Vikram cut and Anjali pick first the first time, then swap the next time. Say it out loud so both know it is the family rule, and everyone can see it is fair.
Nice, I will try it at Sunday's lunch. Which twin cuts first?
Vikram cuts, and Anjali picks first. Next gathering they swap, so Anjali cuts and Vikram picks. At Sunday's lunch, remind them that fairness is the point of the rule.
My friend Hannah is going through a hard time. Her dog died last week.
I am sorry to hear that. Losing a pet is a real loss, and it can feel very heavy. Have you been in touch with her?
I sent a message but I do not know what else to do.
Small things matter. Visit her if she is open to it, bring her favourite snack, and let her talk about the dog if she wants. You do not need to fix anything, only be there.
What should I avoid saying?
Avoid saying things like, it was only a dog, or you can get another one. Say, I am sorry, I know how much you loved him, and listen. If she is quiet, sit with her.
She named him Bruno. Should I mention his name?
Yes, using his name is kind. It shows you remember how special he was. You could say, I was thinking about Bruno today, and ask if she wants to share a favourite memory of him.
My cousin Omar said something rude about my mother at a family function. I am still angry.
That would upset me too. Family comments about parents can cut deep. Do you know why he said it, or was it out of nowhere?
He was joking, I think, about her cooking. But it was in front of everyone.
A joke in public can feel like an insult, even if he did not mean harm. It may help to speak to him privately and say how it landed. Does your mother know?
She laughed it off, but I could see she was hurt.
Then you noticed what others missed, which shows how much you care for her. When you talk to Omar, mention that your mother was hurt and that jokes about family are tough in front of an audience.
Should I do it by phone or in person?
In person is better if it is easy, since tone matters. If not, a call is fine. Avoid writing it, as a long message can look like an attack.
Alright. What did he joke about again?
Your mother's cooking. When you speak to Omar, say that a joke about her cooking, in front of everyone, hurt her feelings, and ask him to be more careful next time.
I always feel lonely on my birthday. Everyone sends messages but nobody calls or visits.
That sounds hard. Messages can feel thin when you want real company. Have you ever asked friends to meet you on your birthday?
No, I usually wait for them to suggest something.
Waiting can make the day feel empty. This time, you could invite two or three friends for a simple meal or walk. Say plainly that you would like their company, so they know it matters.
I am a bit shy about asking.
That is okay. A short message might help, like, I would love to see you on my birthday, are you free for dinner on Saturday? It is polite, clear, and easy to say yes to.
What if people are busy?
Then pick another day close to your birthday. The celebration does not have to fall on the exact date. Even a late dinner with two good friends would still feel special.
Good point. What was that short message you suggested?

It was, I would love to see you on my birthday, are you free for dinner on Saturday? Change the day if Saturday does not suit them. It stays polite and clear, and it tells your friends their company matters to you.
My parents are visiting my aunt in Chennai and I am staying home alone for a week. I am 17.
That is a good chance to show you are responsible. Do you have any plans for the week?
Studying mostly, but I might invite a friend over.
A friend can make the week more pleasant. Check with your parents first, and agree on a few simple house rules, like keeping the house tidy and not having late nights.
They already said it is okay for one friend. Maybe Sam.
Then it is settled. Let Sam know the rules, like keeping the music low for the neighbours and locking up at night. Sharing the cooking can make it fun.
What should I cook for the week?
Choose easy dishes like khichdi, dal with rice, vegetable pulao and scrambled eggs. Cook once, then eat twice. Your mother may have frozen things in the freezer too, so ask before she leaves.
Thanks. Where are my parents going again?
To Chennai, to visit your aunt. They will be away a week, so plan your cooking and study times, and tell Sam which days he is welcome.
Our new puppy is mine, but my younger brother thinks he is his. We keep arguing over him.
A puppy can cause big feelings. Who actually brought him home, and what did your parents say?
We picked him together. Dad said we both share him.
Then a shared plan helps. Make a schedule for feeding, walking and playing, so each of you has your own jobs and your own time. Jobs also teach responsibility.
He is too young to walk him alone, though.
Then you can walk him together. Your brother can hold the lead for part of the walk while you stay close. It helps him feel the puppy is partly his, which may ease the arguments.
Good. What should we name him? We have not agreed on that either.
Make a short list, with each of you adding two names. Then vote, or pick randomly from a bowl. Whichever name wins, tell each other it is fair, since both of you agreed to the method.
Alright. What did Dad say about the puppy?
Dad said you both share him. Remind your brother of that when you make the walking schedule, and also when you pick the name, so the puppy truly feels like a shared pet.
I am so nervous. I am meeting my online friend Priya for the first time tomorrow.
It is exciting and nerve-racking at once. A few safety steps help. Have you told someone at home where you are going?
Not yet. I was going to tell my brother.
Good, tell your brother the time and place. Meet in a busy public spot, like a cafe in the daytime, and keep your phone charged. Message him when you arrive and when you leave.
Okay. What if we have nothing to talk about?
You have been talking online, so you already share interests. Ask about what she is looking forward to, and mention something from your chats. Silence for a moment is normal and fine.
We both love sketching. Maybe I should bring my sketchbook.
That is a great idea. Bring it and, if the moment feels right, share a few drawings. Sketching gives you both something to look at and talk about.
Today my neighbour Mrs. Rao and my mother had a disagreement about parking. Both are upset.
Parking disagreements are very common in apartment blocks, and they usually blow over. Do you know exactly what happened this morning?
Mrs. Rao's car blocked ours in the morning, and Mum shouted at her.
That is stressful for both. A calm talk later might help, perhaps over tea. Your mother could say she was in a hurry and felt frustrated, and ask if they can agree on the spots.
Mum is stubborn and might not want to talk.
You could gently remind her that Mrs. Rao has been a good neighbour for years. A small gesture, like taking her a plate of sweets, can break the ice without saying much.
That is nice. We have laddoos from yesterday.
Laddoos are perfect. Your mother could take a few over and say she is sorry for the shouting, then mention the parking spots. Mrs. Rao will likely meet her halfway.
Can I ask for advice? I am organising my own wedding and my mother and future mother-in-law disagree on everything.
