Congratulations on your wedding. That is a stressful stage with many opinions. What are the main things they disagree on?
The menu and the number of guests, mostly.
Those are big ones. It may help to sit with your partner first and decide what the two of you want. Then you can share your choices kindly with both mothers, so they feel included but not in charge.
My partner is Vikram. He wants a smaller wedding.
Then you and Vikram are already aligned on the guest list. Tell both mothers that you want a smaller celebration, and ask each for her top five guests. That gives them a role in the decision.
And the menu?
Offer a taste session with both families, and let each mother suggest one dish she feels strongly about. You get a mixed menu, they both feel heard, and the choice still belongs to you and Vikram.
My cousin Nisha sent me a very long message about her problems, and I do not know how to reply.
It is kind that she trusts you. Do you know what she needs, advice or just someone to listen?
I think she just wants to vent. She has been stressed about her job.
Then start by saying you read it and you are sorry she is stressed. You do not have to solve everything. Ask one gentle question, like what has been the hardest part this week.
What if I say the wrong thing?
Warmth matters more than perfect words. Say what is true, like, that sounds exhausting, I am here for you. If you are unsure, offer a call so she can talk freely.
A call sounds better. Maybe on Sunday morning?
A Sunday morning call sounds calm. Tell Nisha you have read her message and that you would like to hear more on the phone, so she knows you care and you are not brushing her off.
My father forgot my mother's birthday, and she is hurt. I want to help fix it.
That is a tender situation, and it is kind of you to step in. Has he realised yet?
Yes, he feels terrible. He asked me what to do.
A sincere apology matters most. He can tell her what he feels, without excuses, and then plan a small gesture, like a favourite dinner or a walk together. A little effort goes a long way.
She loves jasmine flowers. Could that help?
Then jasmine flowers are a lovely start. He could bring a string of them with a handwritten note saying sorry and that she matters. It is simple, personal, and fits her taste.
That is sweet. Should we also cook?
Yes, you could cook her favourite dish together, with your father taking part. Seeing him make an effort in the kitchen would show her that he cares more than any expensive gift.
Okay. What flower should he buy again?
Jasmine, since your mother loves it. A fresh string of jasmine with his note beside the plate will show that he remembered what matters to her, even if he forgot the date.
I want to plan a small birthday lunch for my friend Anjali. She is vegetarian and her husband is not.
That is easy to manage with a buffet-style lunch where everyone picks what they like. How many people will be coming to the lunch?
About eight. Mostly family.
Then offer a few vegetarian dishes as the main spread, such as paneer curry, dal and pulao, and add one non-vegetarian dish on a separate table for her husband and others. Label everything clearly.
Good idea. Should the cake be eggless?
Yes, an eggless cake means Anjali can eat it with everyone. It also keeps the table simple. Many bakeries make good eggless cakes, and nobody will notice any difference.
Perfect. What flavour do you suggest?
Chocolate is a safe crowd-pleaser, and butterscotch or mango works well if the season is right. If you remember what Anjali likes, choose that, since it is her birthday.
I have not spoken to my school friend Ethan in two years. I want to get back in touch but feel shy.
It is brave to want to reconnect. A short, warm message is usually well received. What was your friendship like back then?
We were inseparable. We used to cycle to school together.
Then mention that. You could write, I was thinking about our cycle rides to school and wondered how you are. It is friendly, specific, and gives him an easy way to reply with a memory.
What if he does not reply?
Try not to take it hard. People get busy, and messages sometimes slip by. You could wait a week and send a gentle follow-up. If there is still silence, you will know you tried.
Okay. I will send it tonight. How do I start the message?
Start with a warm greeting and his name, like, Hi Ethan, it has been a while. Then add the line about your cycle rides to school, and ask how he has been.
Let me tell you about my weekend. We drove to my mother's village near Mysuru.
That sounds like a refreshing trip. Was it a long drive, and did the whole family go?
Four hours. Me, my parents, and my little cousin Diya, who is six.
A six-year-old in the car for four hours must have been lively. Did Diya keep herself busy, or did you all have to find ways to entertain her?
She sang the same song about twenty times, then fell asleep. In the village she chased the hens all afternoon.
That sounds like pure joy. Village afternoons are a treat for children who live in cities. Did the hens survive her enthusiasm?
Ha, yes. Now she wants to go back and name every hen.
Naming them is a fine plan. Maybe you can write their names in a small notebook before the next visit, so Diya has a project to look forward to.
What was she doing to the hens, again? I want to tell Mum properly.
She was chasing them all afternoon. You can tell your mother that Diya is already planning to go back and name every hen she chased.
Question: is it rude to leave a group chat when my friends keep arguing in it?
It is not rude. Leaving a chat that stresses you is a fair choice, though how you do it matters. Are these friends you want to stay close to?
Yes, mostly. Just the group chat is noisy and sometimes mean.

Then you could mute it first, so you stop seeing every message but stay in. If the arguments keep upsetting you, you can leave and tell one or two friends privately that you will still meet in person.
Muting sounds easy. I will mute it for a week.
A week is a good test. You may find the arguments fade, or you may find you do not miss the noise. Either way, you keep your friendships and protect your peace.
After the week, if I leave, who should I tell?
Tell the one or two friends you are closest to, in a short private message saying it was getting too noisy for you. Keep it friendly so nobody thinks you are leaving the friendship.
Today is my birthday and nobody at home remembered. I am pretty down.
I am sorry, that must feel lonely. Happy birthday to you anyway. Have you told anyone that it is your birthday?
No, I did not want to ask for a wish.
I understand, but a gentle reminder is not begging. You could say, by the way, it is my birthday today, and see how they react. Family often forgets in a busy morning and feels bad later.
Okay, I might tell my mum at dinner.
That sounds like a good moment, when everyone is together. Say it lightly and let her respond. In the meantime, do something small for yourself, like a favourite snack or a walk.
I will get a jalebi on my way home. I do love jalebi.
A jalebi on your birthday is a lovely treat. Enjoy it slowly, and maybe share one with your mum at dinner when you tell her. It is a gentle way to open the conversation.
I have just been asked to be the best man at my brother's wedding.
Congratulations, being asked to be best man is a real honour for you. How are you feeling about taking on the role?
Proud, but nervous. His name is Omar and we have never been that close.
That is honest, and it is a chance to grow closer. Ask Omar what he wants from you on the day. Knowing his hopes will help you plan your role, and the conversation itself will bring you closer.
Good idea. Should I plan a small bachelor outing for him?
A small outing is a nice gesture if Omar would enjoy it. Ask him what he likes, like a cricket match or a good meal with a few friends. Keep it relaxed and not too late the night before.
He loves cricket. A match with cousins could work.
Then a friendly cricket game with the cousins is a perfect fit. Pick a weekend a few weeks before the wedding so Omar is not tired, and finish with a meal together.
I said something mean to my best friend Priya during a fight and now she is not replying to my messages.
That sounds painful. It is good that you want to repair it. Do you remember what you said?
I told her she only thinks about herself.
That is a hard thing to hear. A sincere apology can help. Say that you are sorry for the words, that they were unfair, and that you value her. Avoid adding but or explaining why you were angry.
Should I keep messaging her until she replies?
No, one clear message is enough. Repeating it can feel like pressure. Give her a day or two, since she may need time to cool down. Then, if she stays silent, try a short call or meet in person.
Alright. What did I say to her that I should take back?
You told her she only thinks about herself. In your apology, say clearly that this was unfair and that you do not truly believe it. Priya needs to hear that you regret those exact words.
Yesterday was fun. Me and my brother built a model plane together.
That sounds like a good day. Did you follow a kit, or design it on your own?
A kit, but it had five hundred tiny pieces. It took six hours.
Six hours is real patience. Did you two share the work smoothly, or were there some disagreements over the pieces?
A few. He wanted to glue everything fast, I wanted to wait for it to dry. We compromised.
A good compromise too, since rushing with glue can ruin a model. It sounds like you work well together when you both give a bit. Where does the plane sit now?
On the bookshelf. We will paint it on Sunday.
A painting day sounds fun. Plan your colours before Sunday so you are not arguing over them, and let each of you paint one wing, so the plane feels like both of yours.
I am going to the cinema with Sam and Hannah tonight, but Hannah wants a horror film and I get scared easily.
That is a common clash between friends who like different films. Have you told Hannah that you get scared easily?
Not yet. I do not want to ruin the fun.
You would not ruin it by being honest. You could suggest a film that is exciting but not too scary, like an adventure or a thriller with humour. That way everyone enjoys it.
Sam likes comedies, so maybe we pick one that is funny and a bit spooky.
A spooky comedy is a smart middle path. It gives Hannah some thrills, makes Sam laugh, and keeps you from being too scared. Ask them both if they are open to it.
Good, I will suggest that. Who wanted the horror film again?
Hannah did. When you suggest the spooky comedy, tell Hannah it still has some scares for her, and mention that Sam will like the jokes. She is more likely to say yes then.
My cousin Anjali is two years younger than me and she has started copying everything I do. It is a bit much.
That can feel odd, but it often means she looks up to you. Does she copy your clothes, your hobbies, or both?
Both. She even picked the same college course as me.
That is a big copy, but choices like that can also come from trust. You could talk to her kindly, saying you are flattered and that you want her to find her own path too.
I do not want to hurt her feelings.
Then say something positive first, like, I am happy you like what I like, and I would love to see what you discover on your own. She may take it as a compliment.
Good. Which subject did she copy again? I want to mention it.

You said she picked the same college course as you, though you did not name the subject. You can say that you are happy she shares your interest, and add that she might enjoy adding electives or hobbies that are only hers.
What do you do when your family argues about politics at the dinner table?
That is hard on the people trying to eat. It often helps to change the subject kindly or set a rule, like no heated topics at meals. Is this happening in your home?
Yes, my uncle and my dad. It starts every Sunday.
Then someone neutral, like your mother or you, could suggest a rule. For example, say, can we keep Sunday lunch for good news and food? Say it with a smile so it does not sound like a scold.
Maybe I should start by asking everyone to share one good thing from the week.
That is a great idea. It gives the table a positive direction, and it makes people listen to each other. Start with your own good thing, so it feels easy to follow.
I will try next Sunday. Who starts the arguments?
You said it is your uncle and your dad. They both feel strongly, so ask each of them to share a good thing first, which can calm them before any topic comes up.
My friend Diya is turning 21 and wants a rooftop party. We have a small group, around twelve.
A rooftop party sounds lovely. Is it at someone's home, and will it be in the evening?
At her building, in the evening. We plan to string some lights.
Fairy lights would look beautiful. Check the weather and have a backup plan, like an indoor space nearby. A few cushions and a speaker for music will make it cosy.
What about food? We do not want to cook too much.
Keep it simple with finger food, like sandwiches, samosas and fruit skewers, and order a cake. Ask each friend to bring one dish so the workload is shared.
Good. The weather, what if it rains?
If it rains, move the party to the building's common room or someone's living room, and hang the lights there. Tell the twelve guests the plan in advance so Diya's evening does not get ruined.
I need to tell my friend Leo that I cannot attend his housewarming. I feel guilty.
It is kind of you to worry about his feelings. Why can you not come?
I have a family function the same evening. It is my aunt's anniversary.
That is a good reason, and Leo will probably understand. Tell him soon, so he is not waiting. You could say you are sorry to miss it, and that you would love to visit another day.
Should I bring something later?
A small housewarming gift is a nice touch, like a plant or a set of coasters. When you visit, tell him you were sad to miss the party and enjoy a tour of the new home.
My sister Diya and I just had a screaming match about whose turn it was to do the laundry.
That sounds very loud, and probably upsetting for both of you. Are things calm between you now, or still tense?
Still tense. We are not speaking.
Silence after a shouting match is common. When you are both calmer, one of you could start with, I am sorry we shouted. Then agree on a system so the laundry does not cause another fight.
What kind of system?
A simple rota works well. You do it on Mondays and Thursdays, she does Tuesdays and Fridays, and the weekend is shared. Write it on a note and stick it where you both see it.
I will say sorry first. It was my turn actually, so I was in the wrong.
That is mature of you. Admitting that the turn was yours will help Diya relax and apologise too, and the rota will make sure it does not happen again.
I am getting married in December and I am worried the weather will be too cold for an outdoor ceremony.
Congratulations on the wedding. December can be properly chilly depending on where you live, so it is wise to plan ahead. Where will the wedding be held?
In Shimla, at my family's old house with a garden.

Shimla in December will be cold, so plan for warmth. Heaters, shawls for guests, and hot tea or soup between ceremonies would make everyone more comfortable. You might hold the main rituals in the afternoon sun.
Good thinking. Maybe we offer blankets in the colours of the wedding.
That is a lovely idea. Matching blankets look warm and pretty in photos, and guests can take them home as keepsakes. Keep a few extras for older relatives.
What was the place again? I should tell the photographer.
Shimla, at your family's old house with a garden. Tell the photographer about the cold and the afternoon sun, so they can plan the portraits and keep the blankets in the photos.
Vikram, my cousin, is staying with us for a month for his exam preparation.
That is a big commitment for both of you. How is it going so far?
Pretty good, though he studies until midnight and I hear him pacing.
Late study nights can be tough on whoever shares the house. Have you talked to him about it, or are you just putting up with it?
I have not said anything. He is stressed, so I do not want to add pressure.
That is considerate. You could still ask for a small change, like pacing in the hall instead of the room, or using a soft rug. Frame it as a way to help him focus.
Good idea. I might offer him my desk lamp, too.
A desk lamp is a kind gesture, and good light makes long evenings at the desk more pleasant. Vikram will feel supported, and you can both sleep better during his exam month.
Can you help me think of a fun idea for a friends' reunion? We have not met in five years.
That sounds really special after five years apart. How many friends are involved, and where do you plan to meet up?
Eight of us. Most are in Delhi, but two will fly in from other cities.
Then a long lunch at someone's home in Delhi would be easy. Ask everyone to bring an old photo from school or college, and make a small display. It sparks stories and laughter.
Love it. Maybe we also do a quiz about our old teachers.
A quiz about your teachers is great fun. Have each friend write three questions, and keep the prizes silly, like a sweet or a funny certificate. The team spirit will bring old memories back.
Wonderful. How many of us did I say are coming?
Eight, with two travelling in from other cities. With eight people, two teams of four for the teacher quiz would be perfect.
My sister Nisha is taking a job in another country. I am happy but also sad.
Both feelings make sense. When someone close moves far away, it is a big change. How are you handling it?
Mostly I act cheerful, but at night I feel empty.
It is okay to feel that, and you do not have to hide it. You could tell Nisha how much you will miss her. It might make the time together before she leaves more precious.
She leaves in three weeks. What should we do together?
Plan a few simple things, like a day trip, a favourite meal, or a long evening of old photos. Choose activities that let you talk, because those are the memories you will hold on to.
I think a day trip to the lake near our town. She loves it there.
That sounds perfect. A day at the lake with Nisha, with a picnic and plenty of talk, is a lovely way to spend time before she goes. Bring a camera for a few photos.
I got annoyed with my friend Ethan because he kept looking at his phone while I was telling him something important.
That is frustrating. Did you tell him how you felt, or did you let it go?
I let it go but I am still upset.
Then it may help to bring it up gently. You could say, when I was telling you about my news, I felt you were not listening. Most people do not realise they are doing it.
What if he gets defensive?
Stay calm and explain that you are not angry, you just want his attention for important talks. If he reacts, give it a moment. Often people apologise once the first sting is gone.
Right. Should I do it face to face?
Yes, face to face is better, away from his phone. Choose a quiet time and tell Ethan that it matters to you that he listens when you share something big.
I am turning 40 next week and I do not feel like celebrating.
That is okay. Not everyone wants a big celebration. Is there a reason you do not feel like it, or just no interest?
I feel I have not achieved enough. My friends are further ahead.
Those feelings are very common around milestone birthdays. Comparing yourself to others rarely gives a fair picture. You have your own path and things you have done that count.
Maybe. My daughter Diya says she wants to bake me a cake.
That sounds sweet. A cake from your daughter is a celebration of you, and it does not need a crowd. You can accept it simply and enjoy it with the people who love you.
I think I will. She is nine, so it will probably be lopsided.
Lopsided is best. A lopsided cake from nine-year-old Diya will mean more than a perfect shop one, because it will carry her effort and her love for you.
Mum wants me to marry someone from our community, but I have met someone else.
That is a delicate situation. It sounds like you care about both your mother and this person. Does your mother know about them?
No, I have been afraid to tell her.
That is understandable. Choose a calm moment, perhaps when she is relaxed, and begin with what you value about her. Then share that you have met someone who matters to you.
What if she gets upset?
She may be upset or shocked at first. Give her time to react. Stay respectful and say you want her to know them. Over time, many parents soften when they meet the person.
His name is Sam. Should I introduce him soon?
Wait until your mother has had time to hear the news and think. Then suggest a small, easy meeting, like tea at home, so she and Sam can meet without pressure.
I found out my friend Hannah has been talking about me behind my back. I am hurt.
That is painful to hear, especially when it comes from someone you trust as a friend. How did you find out about it?
Anjali told me. She heard Hannah say I am too bossy.
That is hard to hear. Before reacting, it may help to remember that you heard it second hand. You could ask Hannah directly, in a calm way, if there is something bothering her about you.
I am afraid I will cry or shout.
Then it is fine to take a day to settle your feelings first. When you talk, begin with, I heard something that hurt, and I would like to understand. That invites honesty rather than a fight.
Okay. Who told me about it again?
Anjali. She heard Hannah say you are too bossy, so you could say that you heard it from a friend, without blaming Anjali, and ask Hannah to explain what she meant.
The wedding invitations for my sister's wedding are due to go out and nobody can agree on the wording.
That is a very common sticking point in wedding planning, and it can be solved. What are the different suggestions people are making?
My father wants it formal and traditional. My sister wants something light and modern.
A middle path may work, like a traditional opening line with a warm, simple message below. For example, begin with the family's blessing, and then say, we would love to celebrate with you.
That could work. Dad will like the blessing line.
Then your father feels honoured and your sister gets a friendly tone. Keep the details clear, with date, place and time, and a short line for replies.
What was my sister's preference again?
She wants something light and modern. In the draft, keep her friendly line, and add your father's blessing at the top, so both of them recognise their ideas in the card.
My brother Leo is getting a scholarship to study abroad and I am proud but my parents seem to forget about me.
It is wonderful that Leo got it, and your feelings are valid too. Have you told your parents how it feels?
No. I do not want to seem jealous.
Wanting attention is not jealousy, it is a need. Choose a quiet moment and say, I am very happy for Leo, but I would like some time with you too. Your parents may not realise.
I could ask Mum to go out for a coffee with me.
That is a lovely idea. A one-on-one coffee with your mother gives you the space to share your own news and feelings, and she will likely be glad you asked.
Good. What did I say my brother is getting?
A scholarship to study abroad. When you talk to your mother over coffee, say you are proud of Leo's scholarship, and then share something of your own, so she remembers to celebrate you.
Tomorrow I am meeting my cousins from Lucknow at the railway station. Any tips for a long wait?
Trains often run late, so check the status before you leave home. Carry water, a snack and something to read. How many cousins are you picking up?
Three of them: Nisha, Omar and little Ethan. Ethan is only five.
Then bring a small treat or a colouring book for Ethan, since a five-year-old gets restless on platforms. Nisha and Omar will probably be tired too, so keep the ride home short and simple.
We are taking an auto home. Will we all fit with the luggage?
Three cousins with bags will be tight in one auto. Ask for two autos, or a larger cab if the station has one. Let the adults share, and put Ethan next to a window so he can look outside.
Good point. Maybe my dad can come and bring the car.
That would solve it. With your dad's car, the luggage goes in the boot and the cousins sit together. Tell him the train time and ask him to park near the exit, to make loading quick.
Hold on, who was the little one again, and how old?
Ethan, who is five. Keep a colouring book or a small snack ready in the car for him, so he stays calm while the older cousins, Nisha and Omar, catch up with you.
I want to cheer up my friend Anjali. She failed her driving test yesterday.
That is disappointing for her, but very common. Many people need more than one attempt. Do you know how she is feeling?
She says she is fine, but she was very quiet at lunch.
Quiet usually means she is hurting a little. You could invite her for something relaxed, like a walk or ice cream, and let her talk if she wants. No need to force it.
Should I mention the test or avoid it?
Let her decide. You can say, I am here if you want to talk about yesterday. If she brings it up, listen. If not, enjoy the walk and let her feel normal again.
That makes sense. She loves mango ice cream.
Then mango ice cream is a great plan. Choose a quiet place and invite her this week. Choosing her favourite flavour will tell her you thought about her specifically.
Great. Also, when is she retaking the test? I should wish her luck.
I do not know, since you have not mentioned the date. Ask Anjali over ice cream when she will retake it, and promise to send her a good luck message that morning.
My twin sons turn eight on Sunday and want different things. One wants a cricket party, the other wants a baking party.
That is a fun challenge. Do they want separate parties, or can they be combined?
Combined, I think, with the same friends.
Then you could do two parts. Start with a short cricket game in the garden, then move indoors to decorate cupcakes. Both boys get their favourite, and the children enjoy a variety.
Nice. What if it rains?
Then play indoor cricket with a soft ball in the hall or the biggest room. Move furniture aside and set simple rules, like no hitting above the knee. The baking part will not need any change.
What about the names? I want a banner for each of them. They are Leo and Ethan.
A banner with both names is lovely. Use two colours so each boy feels it is partly his, like blue for Leo and green for Ethan, and hang them side by side above the cupcake table.
One more thing, which twin wanted baking? I will give him the first cupcake.
You said one wants cricket and the other wants baking, but you did not tell me which boy is which. Ask Leo and Ethan which one chose baking, and give that boy the first cupcake.
My sister Hannah and her fiance are doing a very small wedding, just twenty people. Some relatives are upset not to be invited.
That is a tough position. Small weddings are a valid choice, but they can hurt feelings. What does Hannah say about it?
She says it is about being calm, not about excluding anyone.
That is a good reason. She and her fiance could explain it kindly, saying they wanted something quiet and personal. Perhaps they can add a get-together for the wider family a few weeks later.
A reception later could work. Dad suggested the same.
Then your father already likes the idea. A relaxed lunch or tea for relatives after the wedding lets everyone share the joy without crowding the ceremony.
Where could we hold it? Our home is small.
A rented hall, a community room or even a restaurant's private area could work. If the weather is good, a garden or terrace would be pleasant too. Ask relatives to bring a dish to share.
Good ideas. How many people did I say will be at the wedding itself?
Twenty. Those twenty guests are for Hannah's small wedding, and the later reception can be for everyone else. Keep the invitations friendly so the wider family feels welcome too.
I am so frustrated. My roommate Omar keeps eating my food without asking.
That is irritating, especially if you plan your meals and shop for them yourself. How often does it happen?
Almost every day. Yesterday he finished my paneer.
That is a lot. A calm conversation is best. Say you do not mind sharing sometimes, but you would like him to ask first. If you can, set a clear rule, like a labelled shelf for your food.
I do not want to seem petty over some food.
It is not petty. Food costs money and effort. A fair request about respect is reasonable. You can say it kindly, and offer to share on days when you cook extra.
That is a fair deal. I can make extra on Sundays.
Then Sunday sharing is a good compromise. Tell Omar that Sunday extras are for both of you, and everything else on your shelf is yours. A clear rule avoids future arguments.
Okay. What did he finish yesterday? I want to mention it.
He finished your paneer. Mention it calmly as an example, and say you would have happily shared if he had asked, and that Sunday extras are the way to share from now on.
I am visiting my grandmother in a care home tomorrow. She sometimes forgets who I am.
That must be hard for you. Visiting her is a kind thing to do. Do you know how she has been lately?
Her memory comes and goes. Last time she thought I was my mother.
That can feel sad. It might help to stay calm and warm, and gently say your name and that you are glad to see her. Do not correct her harshly. Familiar things often comfort her.
What should I bring? She likes sweets.
Soft sweets she enjoys, like peda or barfi, are a nice idea, if the home allows it. You could also bring a photo album and look at old pictures together. Photos can bring up happy memories.
I have an album of her wedding. Would that be too sad?
It may bring her joy, as it is from happy days. Watch her face while you look. If she seems upset, switch to a lighter topic or a song. Let her lead the way.
I think she will like that. What sweet should I bring?
Peda or barfi, as we said, since she likes sweets. Bring a small box along with the wedding album, so you have something to share while you look at the photos together.
My younger sister Priya wants to come with me everywhere. She is five years younger, and I am 17 and want to go out with friends.
That is a normal tension between siblings of different ages. How does Priya react when you say no?
She cries, and then Mum tells me to take her along.
That is hard. You could make a deal, like taking Priya out for something fun on weekends, so she has something to look forward to. Then your evenings with friends are easier to protect.
What can we do together that she would enjoy?
At twelve, she might like a park trip, a movie, or making something at home like bracelets. Let her pick, so she feels respected, and keep it just the two of you.
She loves making bracelets. I might buy some beads.
That is a thoughtful idea. A box of colourful beads and thread would make Saturday special, and Priya will see that you want time with her too.
Good. How old is Priya, again?
Priya is twelve, five years younger than you. A bead bracelet afternoon is just right at that age, and it may make her feel less left out when you go out with friends.
Do you think it is okay to tell a friend that her new haircut does not suit her?
It depends on how you say it and whether she is asking. Is she asking for your opinion, or are you thinking of volunteering it?
She asked. Her name is Nisha. I think it is too short for her face.
Then be honest but kind. You could say you liked her longer hair more, but that she can still carry the new cut well. Hair grows back, and she may feel better hearing a calm view.
She seems very happy with it though.
If she is happy, then your opinion matters less. You can say, if you love it, I love it too. Honesty is useful when it helps, but it need not spoil her good mood.
True. Maybe I will just compliment her smile instead.
That is a sweet choice. Telling Nisha she looks glad and bright is honest and kind. She asked about the haircut, so you can add that the cut looks bold and you love how happy she is with it.
Remind me what I thought was wrong with the haircut?
You thought it was too short for her face. You do not have to say that now, since Nisha is happy, but if she asks again you can say you preferred it a little longer.
I am helping my mother plan my aunt's 60th birthday. Aunt Diya likes quiet but my mother wants a big party.
That is a classic clash between what the family wants and what the person herself would enjoy. What kind of party would Aunt Diya enjoy most?
Probably a small gathering with a few close friends and a nice meal.
Then maybe the best way is to focus on her happiness. You could suggest to your mother that a small party feels more personal. Perhaps a second, bigger event could follow if relatives insist.
My mother may argue that sixty is a big number.
She is right that it is a big number, and you can agree. But you can say that a big birthday can still be warm and quiet. Respect for Aunt Diya's character is the best tribute.
That is a gentle argument. I might say that too.
Then say it kindly, and offer to handle the details for the small party so your mother feels useful. People give in more easily when they have a role in the plan.
Remind me who likes quiet and who wants the big party?
Aunt Diya likes quiet, and your mother wants the big party. A small meal with close friends honours Diya's taste, while a role in the planning keeps your mother happy.
My friend asked me to help with her wedding photographs. I am only a hobby photographer. Should I say yes?
It is kind of her to ask, and a nice compliment. Is she asking you to be the main photographer, or just help?
Just to take candid shots alongside a professional.
Then it is a great fit. Candid shots from a friend capture moments a professional might miss. Ask her what she would love captured, like family hugs or small funny moments.
What equipment do I need?

Your own camera is fine if it works well in low light. Bring spare batteries and memory cards, and wear comfortable shoes, since you will be on your feet for hours. Charge everything the night before.
I have a decent camera. Her wedding is in the evening, so low light is a worry.
Evening events are tricky. Talk to the professional about the lighting, and practise indoors at dusk. Shooting near lamps and keeping your hands steady will help a lot.
Okay. Where was I supposed to take shots, again, in relation to the professional?
Alongside the professional, as the candid photographer. Stay near the guests for the funny, quiet moments, and leave the main posed shots of the couple to the professional.
I have been arguing with my father about my career. He wants me to study engineering, I want to study music.
That is a big disagreement and a serious choice. How long have you been discussing it?
For months. He says music is not a stable career.

That is a common worry for parents. It may help to show him a plan, like what music course you want to take, what jobs it can lead to, and how you will manage. A calm plan speaks louder than a quarrel.
I do have ideas. I want to teach and perform.
Then write them down with details. Teaching and performing can give steady work. Share your plan at a quiet moment and ask him to read it before he responds.
What if he still says no?
Then give him time. People sometimes need weeks to adjust. You could also ask a teacher or mentor you both respect to talk with him. I cannot say how it will end, but a calm approach helps.
Right. Which subject did he want me to study, again?
Engineering. When you share your music plan, acknowledge that he wants you to have a secure future, and show how teaching and performing could give you that too.
My little cousin Leo is staying with us this week and he does not eat vegetables. Mum is stressed.
Fussy eating is very common in young children, and it usually passes with patience. How old is Leo, and what does he like to eat?
He is six.
At six, many children refuse vegetables. Try making them fun, like cutting them into shapes, or hiding grated carrot in a paratha. Eat together and let him see you enjoying them.
He likes parathas, so that might work. What else?
Let him help in the kitchen. Children often try food they helped make. He could wash tomatoes or mix the dough. Do not force him to eat, as pressure can make him refuse more.
Good. He will love helping Mum with the dough.
Then let him roll a small paratha of his own with grated carrot inside. Praise his work and let him eat it with a little butter. It may be the first vegetable he tries this week.
What age did I say he is? I want to explain it to Mum.
Six. Tell your mother that at six, Leo is old enough to help with the dough and young enough to be fussy, so a little patience and a carrot paratha should help.
We have never travelled just the two of us, but Priya and I are planning a trip to Rishikesh.
That sounds like a fun adventure, and travelling as a pair for the first time is exciting. How long is the trip going to be?
Three days. We are going by train from Delhi.
Three days is a good length. Book your tickets and a place to stay early. Share the plan with your families, including addresses and phone numbers, so everyone feels at ease.
We are also thinking of river rafting. I am a little scared.

Rafting is usually done with trained guides and life jackets. Pick a registered operator and follow the instructions carefully. It is fine to be nervous, and you can choose a gentler stretch of the river.
Good. What if Priya and I disagree during the trip?
Small disagreements happen. Agree before you go that you will say what you want plainly and that either of you can ask for a break. Splitting up for an hour can also help.
Okay. Remind me where we are going and how we are travelling?
You are going to Rishikesh for three days, travelling by train from Delhi. Book the train and your stay early, and tell both families the plan before you and Priya leave.
Do you have ideas for what to say in a birthday message for a friend I have not talked to for a while?
Yes. Warm and short works best. How long has it been, and what was your friendship like?
About a year. We used to study together for exams. His name is Ethan.
Then something like, happy birthday, Ethan. I still remember our late-night study sessions and I hope your year is full of good things. Warm, short and specific.
That is nice. Should I ask how he is?
Yes, add a line like, it would be nice to catch up sometime. It opens the door without pressure. If he replies, you can continue naturally.
I think I will also send him a picture from our study days.
A picture is a lovely touch, as long as it is a friendly one. It will bring back good memories and give him something simple to reply to.
Which memory did I say I would mention?
The late-night study sessions you had with Ethan. Mention those in the birthday message, add the picture if you have one, and say you would like to catch up sometime.
My cousin Sam wants to borrow my laptop for a month, but I need it for college work.
It is fair to be careful with something you need. Why does Sam need a laptop?
His own broke and he has an online course.
That is a real need, and you want to help. You could say you cannot lend yours for a month, but you could share it for a few hours each day. Or suggest a repair shop or a library computer.
A few hours might work. I use it mainly at night.
Then Sam could use it during the day while you are at college, and return it before evening. Agree on the timing, and ask him to keep your files untouched.
Good. I should make a separate account for him.
That is smart. A separate account keeps your college files safe and gives Sam his own space for the course. Set a simple password and tell him the rules.
When is it that I use the laptop the most?
At night, you said. So Sam can have it during the day and you take it back before evening, which keeps your college work safe and still lets him finish his course.
Dad and I disagreed about what time I should be home on Saturday. He says nine, I say ten.
Curfew talks are common in many homes. How old are you, and what is the plan on Saturday?
I am 16. I am going to a friend's birthday dinner at a restaurant.
Dinners can run late, so an hour of flexibility is reasonable to ask for. Tell your father where you will be, who is with you and how you will get home. Parents often agree when they feel informed.
What if he still says nine?
Then try offering a middle point, like nine-thirty, with a message when you leave the restaurant. Showing that you can keep a promise this time will help you win more freedom next time.
My friend Hannah moved to Canada last year and we only talk once a month. It feels strange.
Distance changes how friends stay in touch. Does the monthly call feel like enough, or do you miss more?
I miss more. But she is busy and the time difference is awkward.

Then you could add small, light contact between calls, like sending a photo of something funny, or a short voice note. These tiny messages keep the friendship warm without needing a long conversation.
A voice note sounds nice. She would hear my voice at least.
Exactly, and she can listen when it suits her, whatever the time difference between you and Canada. Tell her about your day in a minute or two, and ask her to send one back.
Mum's birthday is on Thursday and I have only 300 rupees. I want to give her something nice.
A thoughtful gift does not need to cost much, and three hundred rupees can go a long way. What does your mother enjoy?
She loves flowers and writing in her diary.
Then a small bunch of her favourite flowers and a pretty pen for her diary would fit nicely and stay in budget. You could also write a short note to tuck inside the diary.
Great, I will buy the pen and a few marigolds. What was my budget again?
Three hundred rupees. A pen and a small bunch of marigolds should fit within that, and your handwritten note costs nothing but will be the best part of the gift on Thursday.
My uncle is coming from Kolkata and sleeping in the study. Is there anything I should do to make it comfortable?
That is a thoughtful question. Think of a clean bed, a fresh towel and a quiet space. Is there a bed in the study, or will you set one up?
A fold-out bed. It is a bit squeaky.
Then put a thick sheet or mattress topper on it, and check it before he arrives. A small lamp and a glass of water near the bed will make him feel welcome, and leave a clear shelf for his things.
Good. Where is he coming from again? I want to ask about the train.
Kolkata. Ask him which train he is taking and when it arrives, so someone can meet him. Long journeys are tiring, so offer him hot tea and keep the first evening free for rest.
I might be late to my cousin's wedding because of work. I feel bad. It is on Friday.
It is hard to balance work and family events, and it is kind that you care. How late do you think you might be?
About an hour. The ceremony is at six, I finish at five, and the hall is far from my office.
That could work. Plan your clothes ahead and carry them to work, so you can change quickly. Let your cousin know about the timing, so she is not surprised. She will probably understand.
Right. Her name is Diya. I will message her today.
Good. When you message Diya, say you will arrive about an hour after the ceremony begins and that you cannot wait to celebrate with her. A friendly note will ease any worry on her side.
My brother Vikram has started giving me advice about everything. He is only a year older.
That can be irritating, especially when it is not asked for. Is he usually right, or does it just feel bossy?
Sometimes right. But he talks like he is the boss.
You could tell him you value his help but would like him to ask first. Something like, I will ask when I need advice, thanks. If you say it kindly, he may notice and soften.
What if he gets offended?
A little offence at first is possible. Reassure Vikram that you respect his opinion and just want to make some choices yourself. In a week or two, he will probably adjust.
My cousin Nisha and I are planning a surprise for our grandmother's 80th birthday.
What a lovely plan for such a big milestone. What kind of surprise do you and Nisha have in mind for her?
We want to gather all the cousins and sing her favourite old song. She loves it.
That will mean a lot to her. Have everyone learn the song in advance, hide in another room, and walk in together when she comes out. Record it so she can enjoy it again.
Good. I will ask Nisha to organise the hiding. What should I bring?
Bring a small bouquet or a sweet she likes, and the lyrics printed in a large font for the cousins who forget the words. Let Nisha handle the hiding, as you agreed, so you can lead the singing.
I feel jealous of my friend Leo because he got a promotion at work and I did not.
It is human to feel that, even when you are happy for a friend. Did he get it in the same team as you?
Yes, we work together. He joined after me.
That can sting. Try to see the feeling without acting on it. You can congratulate him sincerely and also ask your manager what skills to build for the next chance.
I do not know if I can ask my manager. I am nervous.

A short, calm request works. You could say, I would like to grow here, what should I focus on? Managers usually respect that. Do it after congratulating Leo, so you also feel good about how you handled his news.
Mum and my aunt are not speaking because of a misunderstanding over a family recipe.
Family fallouts over small things can last a long time. Do you know what happened?
Aunt shared Mum's pickle recipe at a function without asking. Mum felt hurt.
Recipes can be very personal, so Mum's reaction is understandable. Your aunt may not have realised it mattered. A gentle conversation, where each explains how she felt, might clear it up.
I could suggest they make the pickle together. Mum loves making it.
That is a kind idea. Making the pickle together lets your mother share her recipe on her own terms, and your aunt can say sorry in a friendly setting. It turns the pickle into a bridge.
Sam is coming over to celebrate my birthday and I want to bake a cake, but I have never baked.
That is a sweet plan. A simple cake is a good first try. What flavour do you want?
Chocolate. I have a recipe with eggs, flour and cocoa.
That is a good base. Read the recipe through before you start, measure everything first, and do not open the oven too early. Let it cool fully before adding any topping.
I might just dust sugar on top instead of icing. Who is coming over again?
Sam is coming. Sugar on top is a neat, easy finish. Light a candle and enjoy the cake with Sam, even if the first bake looks a little rough.
My dad wants to wear his old wedding sherwani to my wedding, but it does not fit anymore.
That is a sweet idea, and shows how much the day means to him. How different is the fit?
It is quite tight around the middle. It is from thirty years ago.
A tailor can often adjust an old sherwani, by letting out seams if there is extra fabric. Take it to one early and ask what is possible. If not, a new matching one is an option.
Good thinking. Maybe he can keep the old one for the photos.

That is a lovely idea. If the tailor cannot let it out, your dad can wear a new sherwani for the ceremony and pose with the old one in a photograph. It will honour his own wedding, thirty years ago, and yours too.
My parents are arguing a lot lately and I do not know how to feel.
I am sorry, that sounds uncomfortable to live with. Is it loud arguing, or more tense silence?
Both. Mostly about money and my grandmother's health.
Those are heavy worries, and many families argue when stressed. It is not your job to fix it. You could tell a trusted adult, like an aunt, how you feel, and take time for things you enjoy.
I talk to my aunt Anjali a lot. She is calm.
That sounds helpful. Your Aunt Anjali can listen and might gently talk with your parents. Keep telling her how you feel, and spend some time outside the house when the tension is high.
My twin sister Priya and I are going to different colleges this year. We have never been apart.
That is a big change for twins who have always been together. How are the two of you feeling about it?
I am excited and scared. She is mostly sad.
That is a natural mix. You could plan regular calls and a visit every month, so you both know the bond stays. You might also share small daily things, like photos of your lunch or your classes.
We could pick a fixed time for a call each Sunday.
A fixed Sunday call gives both of you something to look forward to and makes distance feel smaller. Tell Priya the plan before you leave, so she feels less sad about going to a different college.
My friend Omar texted me at 2 a.m. saying he is feeling very low. I am not sure what to do.
It is good that you noticed his message and took it seriously. Did he say what is wrong?
He did not. He just said everything feels heavy.

Reply warmly, and tell him you are glad he told you. Ask if he wants to talk and whether he is safe. If he mentions harming himself, call his family or a crisis helpline right away. Otherwise, stay with him and listen.
He said he just needs to talk. I will call him in the morning.
A morning call is kind, and a message tonight telling Omar that you will ring him can help him wait. If he stays low for several days, gently suggest he talk to his family or a counsellor.
I got angry with my younger brother for spilling juice on my notes. I yelled and he cried.
That is upsetting for both of you. Notes are important, and so is your brother. How are you feeling now?
Guilty. He is only seven and it was an accident.
Then a quick apology will mean a lot to him. Tell him you were upset but should not have yelled, and that you know it was an accident. A hug can work wonders at seven.
I will. Maybe I can also help him pour juice next time.
That is a kind thought. At seven he may still spill, so helping him pour is a good habit, and you and your brother will have a small routine that makes accidents less likely.
My grandson turned one and I want to give him something that will last. What do you suggest?
How lovely. A gift that lasts could be a small keepsake, like a silver spoon or a framed first-birthday photo. What do you think would suit your family?
We are a traditional family. A silver bowl maybe, with his name.
A silver bowl with his name is a classic gift and he can use it later. Ask the jeweller to engrave his name and the date, and wrap it with a short blessing in your own words.
That is perfect. How old is he now, so I get the engraving right?
He is one, since you said he just turned one. So the engraving can carry his name and the date of his first birthday, which will be a treasured detail for him later.
I just found out that my cousin Ethan and I are both going to the same college. We did not know.
What a nice surprise, and a good coincidence. Starting college with a cousin there will be fun. Do you two get along well?
Very well. We used to play together as kids. He is the funniest person I know.
Then you have a friendly face ready at college. You can travel together, share notes and look out for each other during the first weeks, when everything feels new.
I might ask him to be my study partner. He studies maths and I do too.
That sounds like a good plan. Studying maths with Ethan can be fun and effective, since you already get along and you can explain things to each other in your own words.
Leo and I are fighting about a video game console that we share. He plays it all weekend and I barely get a turn.
Sharing a console can get unfair quickly when one person is always faster on the controller. Have you two ever set any time slots?
No, whoever grabs the controller first plays. Leo is always faster.

Then try fixed slots, like Saturday morning for him and Saturday afternoon for you, and swap the next weekend. A written timetable stops the race to the controller, and it is hard to argue with a plan you both agreed on.
He might say Saturday morning is the best slot. What can I say to that?
Suggest swapping the best slot every week, so Leo gets Saturday morning one weekend and you get it the next. That is fair, and he cannot say the early slot is always his.
I need ideas for my son's tiffin tomorrow. He is seven and gets bored easily.

Try food he can pick up with his fingers, like small vegetable parathas rolled up with a little cheese inside. Add cucumber and carrot sticks and a few raisins on the side. Different shapes keep a child interested.
He does not like cheese, but he loves potato. His name is Aarav by the way.

Then make Aarav a potato roll. Mash boiled potato with salt, a pinch of cumin and chopped coriander, spread it in a soft chapati and roll it tight. Cut it into thick pieces so they look like little wheels.
How do I stop the roll from going soggy by lunch?
Let the potato filling cool fully before you spread it, and keep it fairly dry. Wrap the rolls in paper or a clean cloth, not in a hot closed box. Aarav's rolls will stay soft and not wet.
Diwali is next week and I am hosting my family for the first time. I am scared.
That is a big step, and it is normal to feel nervous. Start by choosing one main meal and two sweets, not ten dishes. Clean the house a little each day so the last day is calm.
My mother-in-law is coming and she is very particular about sweets.

Then make one sweet really well instead of many average ones. Besan laddoo or coconut barfi are simple and hard to spoil. You could also ask her to bring her own special sweet, which makes her feel respected.
Good idea. I will ask her for her kaju katli. Should I make the laddoo a day before?

Yes, laddoo keeps well, so make it two days before if you like. Roast the besan slowly until it smells nutty, and let it cool before shaping. Your mother-in-law's kaju katli can arrive fresh on Diwali day.
Can you tell me how to make plain rice that is not sticky?
Wash the rice in cold water until the water looks almost clear. Use about one and a half cups of water for one cup of basmati rice. Cook it on low heat with the lid on, and do not stir.
I used a pressure cooker last time and it turned to mush.
A cooker cooks fast, so it is easy to overdo. For basmati, wait for just two whistles, switch off the flame, and let the pressure drop by itself. Also soak the rice for twenty minutes first.
Okay, and what if I want to make the rice for biryani?

For biryani, boil the soaked basmati in plenty of salted water until it is about three-quarters cooked, then drain it. It will finish cooking in the layers later. That way the grains stay long and separate, not mushy like last time in your cooker.
Yusuf here. My friend Sofia is coming for dinner Saturday. She is vegetarian.

That is easy to plan for. A good menu is dal, a dry vegetable like aloo gobi, rice or rotis, and a simple raita. Finish with something sweet like kheer. Nothing needs meat to feel like a proper dinner.
She also does not eat onion or garlic on some days, I forgot to ask which.
It is kind to ask her before Saturday, just a short message is enough. Meanwhile, keep the menu flexible. Dal can be tempered with cumin and ginger, and many dishes work well without onion or garlic.
I asked. She said no onion or garlic on Saturday. Any tip for the dal?
For Sofia's dal, use cumin, ginger, a green chilli and a pinch of asafoetida in the tempering. Add a little tomato and lemon at the end for flavour. She will not miss the onion or garlic.
What should I cook when I come home tired and have almost nothing in the fridge?
Khichdi is the best answer. Rice, moong dal, a little turmeric and salt in one pot, and it is ready in twenty minutes. Eat it with ghee and a spoon of curd or pickle.
I only have eggs, one onion and some bread today though.
Then make a quick egg bhurji. Fry the chopped onion, add salt and a pinch of chilli, then pour in the beaten eggs and stir until set. Toast the bread and eat it together.
Nice. Can I add the leftover rice into the eggs instead of using bread?

Yes, that makes a simple egg fried rice. Fry the onion, scramble the eggs, then add the cold leftover rice and mix on high heat for two minutes. Cold rice works better than fresh, so your leftover rice is perfect.
Ben here. Our Christmas dinner is at my place this year. Where do I begin?
Begin with the guest list and the main dish. Once you know how many people are coming, choose one main, two sides and one dessert. Write the plan on paper so you can shop in one trip.
There will be eight of us, and my sister Chloe is bringing the dessert.
Good, that takes one job off you. With eight people, a roast chicken or a big pot of biryani would both work. Tell Chloe early what else is on the table so her dessert fits the meal.
I will do roast chicken. What should I ask Chloe to bring besides the dessert?
Ask Chloe to bring a drink or a salad, since you already have the chicken and the sides to manage. A big bowl of fruit juice punch is easy to carry and serve to all eight guests.
My daughter Riya says her tiffin smells funny by lunchtime. What am I doing wrong?
Smells usually come from food packed hot and shut in a closed box. Let the food cool a few minutes before you close the lid. Also wash the box well with a little lemon or baking soda once a week.
I do pack her curd rice. It is always warm because I pack it in the morning.
That is the cause. Curd rice should go in cold, and warm curd turns sour quickly. Mix the rice and curd at night, keep it in the fridge, and pack it right before she leaves.
Okay. What can I add so it tastes better but does not spoil?

Add grated carrot, chopped cucumber and a few pomegranate seeds just before packing. A tempering of mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil is fine too if it is cooled first. Riya will enjoy it more and it will stay fresh.
I will try that tomorrow. Can I give her a small piece of pickle on the side?
A little pickle is fine and many children like it with curd rice. Pack it in a tiny separate container so it does not leak into the rice. Riya can add it herself when she eats.
Daniel here. I want to learn to make a good Sunday breakfast. Any simple idea?

Try masala omelette with toast, or soft idlis with chutney if you have batter. For a first try, the omelette is quicker. Chop an onion, a tomato and a green chilli, mix with the eggs and cook on a medium pan.
I like the omelette idea. How many eggs for two people?
Use two eggs per person, so four in total. Make two separate omelettes rather than one big one, because they are easier to flip. Add a little salt and pepper and a pinch of coriander.
What if my wife Sofia does not like chilli?
Then skip the chilli in her omelette and add a little black pepper or grated cheese instead. Make Sofia's first so it has no spice on the pan, and then make yours with the green chilli.
Pongal is on Sunday. Can you explain what we cook for it? I am new to this.

The main dish is sweet pongal, made from new rice, moong dal, jaggery, ghee and cardamom. It is cooked in a pot outdoors, and when the milk boils over, people shout 'Pongalo Pongal'. A savoury ven pongal is also common.
Why does the pot boil over on purpose?
The overflowing milk is a sign of good luck and plenty for the year. People watch the pot closely and cheer when it spills. It is a way of thanking the sun and the harvest.
I do not have a garden. Can I cook it in my kitchen?
Yes, many families cook it on the stove at home. Use a big pot so there is room for the milk to rise. You can still say 'Pongalo Pongal' when it boils over, even in an apartment kitchen.
I want to make gulab jamun but mine always turn hard. Why?
Hard gulab jamun usually means the dough was kneaded too much or too tightly. Mix the milk powder and flour lightly, only until it comes together. The dough should feel soft, not stiff.
I also fry them on high heat.
That is another problem. High heat browns the outside before the inside cooks, and it makes them hard. Fry them on low heat, turning often, until they are an even golden brown.
And what about the syrup? Should it be hot when I put them in?

The syrup should be warm, not boiling hot, and not cold either. If it is too hot, the jamuns can shrink; if it is cold, they will not soak well. Since you fry on low heat now, put them in warm syrup straight away.
My cousin Manav is visiting for a week and I do not know what to feed him each day.

Plan the first two days with simple home food, then something special on the weekend. A mix of dal-rice, vegetable curry, a rice dish and one outside treat keeps it varied. Ask him what he missed from home.
He is from Pune and misses misal pav.
Then misal pav is a lovely welcome. You can make the spicy sprouts curry on the first evening and serve it with bread. Buy the farsan to sprinkle on top, since it is hard to make at home.
Great, I will do that on his second night. What about breakfast?

For Manav's breakfast, try poha one day, upma another, and parathas with curd on the weekend. These are quick and filling. Since misal pav is on his second night, keep that morning light so he enjoys the dinner.
What is the easiest chutney to make with a mixer?
Coconut chutney. Blend grated coconut, a green chilli, a small piece of ginger, roasted chana dal and salt with a little water. It takes five minutes and goes with idli, dosa or vada.
I do not have chana dal. I have peanuts.
Peanuts work well too. Dry roast a handful until they smell good, rub off the skins, and blend them with the coconut. The chutney will be a little thicker and richer.
Should I add curd to it?

A spoon of curd is nice if you want it creamy and mild, but add it after blending. Then temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves on top. With your peanut version it will taste a bit like a Sunday breakfast chutney.
Chloe told me she hates cooking dal. Is dal really that hard?

Not at all. It only seems hard because people leave it on too high a flame or forget the tempering. Boil washed dal with turmeric and salt until soft, then add fried cumin, garlic and chilli at the end.
She says hers always comes out watery or too thick.
That is a water problem. Use about three cups of water for one cup of toor dal as a start. If it is too thick, add hot water and boil again; if it is too thin, simmer without a lid for a few minutes.
I will tell her. Which dal is the easiest for a beginner like her?
Moong dal is the easiest because it cooks quickly and does not need soaking. Yellow moong takes about fifteen minutes. If Chloe wants a gentler start, that is a better choice than toor dal.
Eid is tomorrow and I still have not planned the food. Help.
No panic. Pick one star dish, such as biryani, and a sweet like sheer khurma. Then add a simple raita and salad. Marinate the meat tonight so tomorrow is easy.
I am Yusuf, and I will have about ten guests. Do I make the sheer khurma tonight?
Yes, Yusuf, make it tonight. It tastes even better after resting, and it will free your morning for the biryani. Keep it in the fridge and warm it slowly before serving.
Okay. How much biryani for ten people?

For ten people, plan about one kilo of rice and a bit over a kilo of meat. If some guests are children, you will have some left, which is good on Eid. Cook it in a big heavy pot so the layers cook evenly.
That helps. What time should I start the biryani tomorrow?

Start about three hours before the guests arrive. Cooking the biryani takes around one and a half hours, and then it needs half an hour to rest. That leaves you a little time to freshen up for your guests.
I want to bake a cake for my friend Pooja's birthday but I have never baked before.

A simple vanilla sponge is a good first cake. You need flour, sugar, eggs, butter, baking powder and milk. Mix them well, pour into a greased tin and bake at a medium heat until a stick comes out clean.
I do not have an oven. Only a pressure cooker.
You can still bake in a cooker. Remove the rubber ring and whistle, put a layer of salt or sand at the bottom, place a stand on it, and set your tin on top. Cook on low flame for about forty minutes.
Does the cake smell like salt?

No, the salt stays at the bottom and does not touch the cake. The tin sits on a stand above it. Pooja's cake will taste of vanilla and butter, as long as the tin is covered with foil or a plate to keep it dry.
What is a healthy tiffin for an office worker who is tired of sandwiches?
Try a vegetable pulao with a small box of curd. Or a roti roll with paneer and cabbage, which is filling and neat to eat. Add a fruit for dessert.
I like the roti roll. My name is Arjun and I leave at seven so I need something quick.
Arjun, make the filling the night before. Fry crumbled paneer with onion, cabbage and a little spice, then store it in the fridge. In the morning, just warm a roti, fill it and roll it in foil.
Will the roll get cold by lunch?
It will, but it still tastes fine cold, because the paneer filling is dry. If you have a microwave at work, warm it for thirty seconds. Otherwise your roti roll is just as good at room temperature.
My friend Kavya just told me she is going vegan. I want to cook for her but I do not know how.
It is thoughtful of you to ask. Vegan means no meat, eggs, milk, curd, ghee or honey. A lot of Indian food already fits, like chana masala, dal made with oil, and vegetable pulao.
So no ghee or paneer?
Right, no ghee, paneer, butter or curd. Use oil or coconut milk for richness instead. Tofu or chickpeas can take the place of paneer in a curry.
Will chana masala work for her dinner?
Yes, chana masala is a great pick for Kavya. Just cook it in oil, not ghee, and check that the bread or rice is also plain. A salad with lemon dressing will round it off nicely.
Tell me how to make a simple tomato soup for a cold evening.

Chop four ripe tomatoes, one onion and a small piece of ginger. Cook them in a little oil with a cup of water until soft, then blend. Add salt, pepper and a pinch of sugar and simmer for five minutes.
Can I skip the onion? My brother Ben cannot eat it.
Yes, skip it. Use a little extra ginger and a clove of garlic if Ben can eat that. The soup will taste a bit sharper but still good. Add a spoon of butter or cream at the end to make it smooth.
He cannot eat garlic either, I just remembered.
Then use only ginger and a bit of black pepper, and add a small carrot while cooking. The carrot gives sweetness and body to Ben's soup, so it will taste full even without the onion and garlic.
I have unexpected guests coming in an hour. What can I cook fast?
Make something quick like vegetable upma or poha, plus tea. Both take fifteen minutes and use things most kitchens have. You can also fry some papad to serve on the side.
I have poha and potatoes. How do I make it taste like I tried?

Fry cumin, mustard seeds, curry leaves, and diced potato first, then add the washed poha. Finish with lemon juice, sev or peanuts on top and fresh coriander. Those finishing touches make it look like a planned dish.
I only have lemon, no peanuts or sev.
That is enough. Squeeze the lemon over the poha at the very end, and add the coriander if you have it. A plate of hot, fresh poha with potato and lemon is a lovely snack for unexpected guests.
What can I make for Holi for kids who cannot eat very spicy things?
Gujiya is the classic Holi sweet, with a coconut and sugar filling, and children usually love it. You can also make thandai without nuts, or simple sweet puris. Keep all the savoury snacks mild.
My niece Riya is five. Is gujiya hard to make?
It takes patience more than skill. Make a stiff dough, roll small circles, put the filling in, seal the edges and fry. For a five-year-old, a mould helps, and Riya may enjoy pressing the edges.
I do not have a mould. How do I seal them?

Wet the edge of the circle with a little water, fold it over and press with a fork. You can also twist the edge with your fingers for a rope design. Riya will like using the fork, and the marks keep the filling inside.
Daniel wants to host a movie night. What snacks are easy to make for six people?
Make popcorn in a pot, a tray of nachos or bhel, and some sandwiches cut in small squares. All are easy to eat in the dark and need no plates. Keep drinks in a jug on the side.
Is bhel easy? How do I make it?
Bhel is very easy. Mix puffed rice, chopped onion, tomato, boiled potato, sev and a little green and sweet chutney right before you serve, or it gets soft. Ready-made chutney from the shop is fine.
Okay I will do bhel and popcorn. Can I prepare the bhel for Daniel's party in the afternoon?
Chop the vegetables and keep the chutneys ready in the afternoon, but mix everything only just before serving. If you mix the bhel early, the puffed rice goes soft and loses its crunch.
I burnt the bottom of my dal pot. How do I clean it?
Fill the pot with water and a spoon of baking soda, and boil it for ten minutes. Leave it to cool for an hour, and then scrub gently. The burnt layer usually lifts off easily.
I do not have baking soda. I have lemon and salt.
Then boil water with a few lemon slices in the pot, and let it sit. After that, sprinkle salt and scrub with the cut lemon. It works slower than baking soda, but it does lift the black marks.
Was it my fault the dal burnt? I left it for a few minutes.

It happens to everyone, so do not be hard on yourself. Dal sticks fast when the flame is high or the water is low. Next time keep the flame low and stir the dal pot every few minutes while you are doing other work.
Sofia asked me what 'Pongal' means and I did not know how to explain it.

Pongal means 'to boil over' in Tamil. It is the name of both the harvest festival in mid January and the sweet rice dish cooked on that day. The festival thanks the sun, the rain and the farm animals.
How many days is it celebrated?
It is celebrated for four days. The first day is Bhogi, the second is Thai Pongal, the third is Mattu Pongal for the cows and bulls, and the fourth is Kaanum Pongal, when families visit each other.
Which one should I tell Sofia is the main day?
Tell Sofia that the second day, Thai Pongal, is the main one. That is the day families cook the pot of pongal outdoors and let it boil over, and it is also the day the festival is named after.
Is it okay to eat curd rice at night? My grandmother says no.

Many families in India avoid curd at night, and it comes from old habit. There is no strict rule, and plenty of people eat curd rice for dinner without trouble. Do what feels right for you and your family.
My grandmother's name is Lakshmi and she says the cold is bad for the throat.
Many grandmothers say that, and it is worth respecting her wish when you are at her house. You can also have your curd rice at lunch, when she is happy and you still enjoy it.
What can I eat at night instead when I visit Lakshmi?
At Lakshmi's house, light foods like khichdi, warm dal with rice or soft rotis with a vegetable fit well. They are easy on the stomach and she will be glad you ate what she cooked.
Pooja is coming to stay for the weekend. What breakfast can I make that feels special?
Make masala dosa on Saturday and sweet french toast on Sunday. If dosa batter is too much work, try stuffed parathas with curd and pickle. Fresh fruit and tea or coffee finish the table well.
She told me she loves anything with potatoes.
Then stuffed aloo paratha is the answer for Saturday. Mix boiled potato with salt, chilli, cumin and coriander, stuff it in the dough and cook with a little butter. Serve with curd and a pickle.
Sunday too? She leaves in the afternoon.
For Sunday, make a quick potato hash with onions and a fried egg on top, or aloo sandwiches. Pooja will get her potatoes both days, and the Sunday breakfast is light enough before she travels.
I went to the vegetable market this morning and it was so crowded.
Morning markets are always busy, especially on weekends. Did you find what you wanted? Fresh vegetables usually sell out early, so going early is smart even if it is crowded.
Yes. I bought spinach, brinjal and a big pumpkin. The pumpkin was cheap so I could not say no.
A big pumpkin is useful. You can make a sweet and sour curry, a soup, and even a halwa from it. The spinach should be cooked soon, since it wilts in a day or two.
What can I do with the brinjal tonight?

Make a simple bharta tonight. Roast the brinjal on the flame until the skin is black, peel it, mash it and cook it with onion, tomato and spices. That leaves the pumpkin for tomorrow and the spinach for lunch.
Okay. And what was the one I should cook first?
Cook the spinach first, because it spoils fastest. Make a quick dal palak or a spinach sabzi with garlic. Then the brinjal bharta can be tonight's dinner and the pumpkin can wait a day or two.
Can you teach me how to make good chai? Mine tastes like hot water with milk.
Boil water with crushed ginger and a spoon of tea leaves for a couple of minutes first. Then add milk and sugar and let it boil up until it turns a deep colour. Strain it into cups.
How much tea leaves for two cups?
For two cups, use about two small spoons of tea leaves and a cup and a half of water, plus a cup of milk. You can add a little more tea if you like it strong.
I forgot to say, my friend Manav likes his chai with cardamom.

Then crush two cardamom pods and add them with the ginger, when the water starts to boil. The smell fills the kitchen. Manav will like it, and if he prefers only cardamom, make his cup in a small separate pan without the ginger.
I am cooking for the first time for my girlfriend Pooja. Dinner on Friday. Nervous!
It is sweet that you are cooking for her. Choose a dish you have made before, so you feel calm. Something like pasta, or fried rice with an omelette, is easy and always warm and comforting.
I can make pasta. Should I try a new sauce?
Not on the big day. Practise any new sauce on Wednesday or Thursday. For Friday, make the sauce you know well, and add one small extra such as garlic bread or a simple salad.
Good point. I will make the white sauce pasta. What do I do about the table?

Keep it simple. Clean the table, put two plates, a candle or small lamp if you like, and keep the music soft. Add the salad in a bowl in the middle. Pooja will care more about the effort than any fancy setting.
Thanks. Should I tell her what I am making or keep it a surprise?

Either is fine. If you want to be safe, ask Pooja if she likes white sauce pasta, because some people prefer red sauce. If she does, you can tell her the plan or keep the garlic bread as the surprise.
My mother is visiting from Kerala. She wants to cook lunch in my flat.
What a nice visit. Give her the kitchen and let her cook the way she likes. You can help by chopping vegetables or washing rice, which is also a good way to learn her recipes.
Her name is Meenakshi. She is making fish curry, but my flat does not have a chimney.

Then open the kitchen window and turn on any fan that you have. Keep the kitchen door closed so the smell does not spread. After cooking, light a little incense or boil water with cloves to freshen the air for Meenakshi's next dish.
I am a bit shy to tell her about the smell. How do I say it kindly?
Say it gently, like 'Amma, let us keep the window open so the smell goes out quickly.' Make it about helping the kitchen, not about her cooking. Meenakshi will understand.
Okay. I will ask her to teach me the fish curry too.
That is a lovely idea. Ask Meenakshi to show you each step, and write down the quantities as she goes, because many mothers cook by feel. Then you can make her fish curry yourself later.
I want to learn to make a good sambar. Where do I begin?

Start with toor dal. Boil it with turmeric until soft and mash it. Then cook tamarind water with chopped vegetables, sambar powder and salt, and mix in the dal. Temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Which vegetables are best? I only know drumstick.
Drumstick is a classic. Also try pumpkin, brinjal, carrot, small onions and tomato. A mix of three or four vegetables makes the sambar richer than only one kind.
My friend Kavya says add a bit of jaggery. Is that right?
Yes, a small piece of jaggery balances the sourness of the tamarind. Use only a little, about half a teaspoon. Kavya's tip is common in many homes, and it makes the sambar taste rounder.
We are going on a picnic on Sunday. Nine of us. What food travels well?
Pick food that tastes fine cold. Lemon rice, puri with potato sabzi, sandwiches, boiled eggs and fruit all travel well. Avoid anything with too much gravy, which spills.
Chloe said she will bring a cake. Is that okay to carry?
A cake travels better if it stays in its tin and is kept flat, away from the sun. A simple loaf cake is best, and a frosted one will melt. Ask Chloe to pack it in a firm box.
Okay. And how much puri for nine people?
Plan about five puris per person, so around forty-five. Make a few extra in case someone wants more, since people eat more outdoors. The sabzi should be dry, not runny, so it does not spill.
I will tell Chloe to put the cake box on top. Anything else to remember?
Pack water, napkins, a knife for the cake and a bag for rubbish. Also carry a mat to sit on. With nine people and Chloe's cake, a few extra paper plates will come in handy.
What is the difference between jeera rice and plain rice?
Jeera rice is basic rice with cumin seeds fried in ghee or oil, then mixed in. It has a light smell and goes well with dal or curry. Plain rice has no tempering at all.
How do I make it in the pot?
Heat a spoon of ghee, add a teaspoon of cumin seeds and let them crackle. Add washed rice, stir for a minute, then pour in water and salt. Cover and cook on low flame until done.
Oh, and my friend Daniel is allergic to ghee. What can I use?
Use any plain oil, such as sunflower or coconut oil, for Daniel. The cumin will still crackle and smell good. Since he is allergic, make sure no ghee touches his pot or spoon.
My kids want something crunchy after school. I do not want to buy packets.
Make roasted chana, popcorn or baked masala makhana. All three are quick and use few things. Mix with a pinch of salt and chaat masala for flavour.
My son Arjun hates makhana. He says it is like air.

Fair enough, some children feel that way. Roasted chana or peanut chikki may suit Arjun better, since they have a stronger crunch. Or you can cut bread into triangles and toast them with butter and masala.
He likes the bread idea. Is there a way to make it a bit healthy?
Use brown or whole wheat bread, and toast it in the oven or in a pan with just a few drops of oil. Sprinkle some sesame seeds on top. Arjun will enjoy the crunch and not notice the change.
I tried a new restaurant dish last night, a creamy paneer curry, and I want to make it at home.
Paneer butter masala is a common one. You cook tomato, onion, ginger and garlic, blend them smooth, then simmer with butter, cream and a little spice. Add soft paneer cubes at the end.
It was orange and a little sweet.

That sounds right. The orange colour comes from tomato and a little Kashmiri chilli powder, and the sweetness is from a pinch of sugar or honey and the cream. Start with one tomato more than the onion.
I am Sofia, by the way, and I cannot find cashews. Is it okay without?
Yes, Sofia. Cashews just make the sauce thicker and smoother, but cream does that job too. You can also soak a few melon seeds or use a spoon of ground almonds if you have them at home.
My roti keeps coming out hard and I do not know why.
