The dough might be too dry or kneaded too little. Use warm water, knead for several minutes and let the dough rest for twenty minutes under a damp cloth. Soft dough makes soft roti.
I do rest it, but only for five minutes.
Try twenty minutes. The rest lets the flour soak up water and relax, so it rolls out easily. Also cook the roti on a hot pan and press it with a cloth until it puffs.
Should I put oil in the dough?
A teaspoon of oil in the dough helps, yes. Add it after you mix the flour and water, and knead again. Along with a twenty-minute rest instead of five, it should make your roti much softer.
Yusuf here. My sister's wedding is next month and I have to arrange sweets for guests.
Congratulations to your family. For a wedding, a mix of two or three sweets suits most people. Choose one milk sweet, one dry sweet and one fried sweet so there is something for every taste.
Her name is Zainab. She loves rasgulla.
Then rasgulla should be on the list. It is a good, light sweet that most people like. You can pair it with a dry sweet like kaju barfi and a warm jalebi.
I will ask the caterer. How many pieces per person should I order?

Plan for two or three pieces of each sweet per guest, and a little extra for children and for tea. Ask the caterer for a rough number too. Zainab's rasgulla may go fast, so order a bit more of that one.
I want to teach my younger brother Ben how to cook. He is twelve.
Twelve is a good age to start. Begin with easy things where he can see quick results, like scrambled eggs, a sandwich or instant noodles. Always stay near him around the stove.
He wants to make something with fire. Is it too soon?
A gas flame is fine if you are right beside him. Show him how to turn the knob, hold the pan handle, and keep long sleeves away. Start with a small pan of eggs and a low flame.
Okay, I will show him eggs first. What do I teach him before turning the stove on?
Teach Ben to wash his hands, tie back loose hair or clothes, keep a dry cloth handy and place the pan firmly. Tell him to never leave the pan alone. Then let him crack the eggs himself.
And what should I do if the oil catches fire?
Never use water on an oil fire. Cover the pan with a lid and turn off the flame, then leave the lid on until it cools. Tell Ben this rule before his first egg so he knows it well.
Any breakfast idea for leftover chapatis?
Make chapati upma. Tear the chapatis into small bits, fry onion, mustard seeds and chilli, add the bits with a little salt and turmeric and toss well. It takes ten minutes.
I like that. My husband Manav likes sweet more than spicy though.
Then make a sweet version for him. Tear the chapati, warm it in a pan with a spoon of ghee, sugar and a pinch of cardamom. Some people call it chapati laddoo when it is shaped into balls.
Will the sweet one taste good for Manav's tiffin as well?
Yes, it keeps well for a few hours. Shape the sweet chapati mix into small balls so it is easy to eat at his desk. Wrap them in paper and they will not get soggy for his lunch.
My in-laws are visiting for Diwali and I want them to feel welcome.

Start with a clean room and fresh bedsheets, and keep water and a small snack on the table. At meals, ask what they like, and serve their favourites first. Small things like these make guests feel at home.
My father-in-law is diabetic. What sweets can I offer him?

I am not a doctor, so please ask your family or his doctor what he can eat. You could keep a plate of fruit or roasted nuts on the table next to the sweets, so there is something for him to enjoy as well.
That is a nice idea. His name is Raghav, and he likes pomegranate.
Then cut a bowl of pomegranate for Raghav and keep it near him at tea time. He will see that you remembered. It also gives him something to have while others enjoy their sweets.
Chloe and I want to bake cookies this weekend but I forgot what we need.

For simple cookies you need flour, butter, sugar, an egg and a pinch of baking powder. You can add chocolate chips or a little cinnamon if you like. Mix, shape small balls and bake until the edges turn golden.
What temperature and how long?
Bake at about 180 degrees for ten to twelve minutes. Take them out when the edges are golden even if the middle still looks soft, because they firm up as they cool.
Chloe prefers crunchy ones. How do I make them crispier?

For crunchier cookies, flatten the dough balls before baking and bake a couple of minutes longer. Use a little less butter if the dough feels too oily. Let Chloe's batch cool fully on the tray so they dry out.
I am trying to eat less oily food. Any tips for cooking at home?
Use a non-stick pan so you need less oil, and measure it with a spoon, not by pouring. Steam, boil or roast vegetables instead of deep frying. Add flavour with spices, lemon and herbs.
I love puris and pakoras though. Is that wrong?
Not wrong at all. Enjoy them as an occasional treat, not every day. You can make them a little lighter by draining them on paper and using fresh, hot oil that is not smoking.
Okay. My friend Pooja says an air fryer is good for pakoras?

An air fryer can make pakoras with less oil, though they will be drier than deep fried ones. Spray the batter lightly with oil first. If Pooja has one, try it at her place before you buy one yourself.
Kavya is packing tiffin for her husband and always runs out of ideas. Can you give her a week's plan?

A simple week works well. Monday: roti and mixed vegetable. Tuesday: lemon rice and curd. Wednesday: paratha and pickle. Thursday: dal rice. Friday: pulao and raita. Repeat in a different order next week.
He likes variety. What can she change on Wednesday so it is less boring?
Make it a stuffed paratha, like aloo or paneer, with a small box of curd and a salad. A different filling each week keeps it interesting without extra effort.
She likes that. Can she add a sweet to the box?
A small sweet is a nice surprise. A piece of jaggery or a single laddoo travels well, or some dry fruits and dates. Kavya can tuck it in a separate corner so it does not mix with the paratha.
Daniel invited me for Christmas lunch and I am Hindu. Should I bring something?
It is polite to bring a small gift, and Daniel will probably love it. Something like sweets, fruit or a flower plant works well. Ask him if he needs help with the food too.
What if he does not eat sweets? I am not sure.
Then bring something else, like a plant or a box of dry fruits and nuts. You can also just message him and ask what he would like. It takes a minute and avoids guessing.
Good idea. I will bring a plant. What should I wear, just normal?
A neat, comfortable outfit is fine for Daniel's lunch. Christmas is a cheerful day, so something bright is nice. You do not need anything special, because he invited you to enjoy it with him.
Idli batter at home sounds like fun, so I am going to try it. How long does it take?
You need rice and urad dal soaked for about six hours, ground to a smooth batter, then left to ferment overnight. In total it takes around a day. In a cold place it can take longer.
My kitchen is cold right now. How do I help it ferment?
Keep the batter in a warm place, like inside a switched-off oven with the light on or near a warm stove. Wrap the pot in a cloth. It should rise and look bubbly.
I am Riya and I do not have a grinder, only a mixer. Will that work?
Yes, Riya, a mixer works if you grind in small batches with a little cold water. Grind the dal until it is fluffy and the rice a bit rougher. The batter can then rest in your warm spot overnight.
Tell me a quick way to cut an onion without crying.
Chill the onion in the fridge for fifteen minutes first, and use a sharp knife. A sharp knife breaks fewer cells, so less gas reaches your eyes. Cut the root end last.
I did that and still cried.
Then try cutting near the open window or a running exhaust fan to blow the gas away. Some people wear glasses, which also helps. It will always bother some people a little.
Let me tell you, my brother Manav does not cry at all. Why?

Some people are less sensitive, or they cut very fast, so less gas reaches them. It does not mean they cut better. So you are not doing anything wrong, and the fridge trick and window can still help you.
Sofia and Arjun are bringing their baby over tomorrow. What should I cook?

Make food that is mild and soft, since a baby will be there and the parents may eat quickly. Khichdi, dal rice, steamed vegetables and a simple fruit bowl are all good. Keep spice separate for the adults.
The baby is only eight months old, so she eats only mashed food.
Then keep a small portion of plain khichdi aside before adding spice, and mash it with a fork. Ask Sofia whether the baby has any foods she should avoid. Let the parents decide what to give her.
Good thought. I will ask her. Should I buy a high chair?
No need to buy one for a single visit. Ask Sofia if she is bringing a seat or a stroller. If not, a cushion on a sturdy chair or the parents' lap will do for the baby for the visit.
Last night I made biryani for the first time. It was a mess.
Do not worry, almost everyone's first biryani is difficult. It has many steps. What went wrong, was it too dry, too wet, or the rice broke?
The rice was mushy at the bottom and raw at the top.
That means the water was uneven. Boil the rice only three-quarters, drain it well, then layer it over the masala. Seal the pot with dough or foil and cook on very low heat for twenty minutes.
I did not seal it. Is that why?
Yes, that is likely why the top stayed raw. Steam escaped without sealing, so the top layer did not cook. Seal the lid next time. And the mushy bottom came from too much water.
I am making a shopping list for the week. Can you help me plan?
Sure. Start by deciding the dinners for the week, then list what each needs. Add basics like rice, flour, oil, milk and eggs. Check what is already in your kitchen so you do not buy things twice.
We are four people. I plan dal, rajma, paneer curry and fish. My daughter is Riya and she is fussy.

Then add something for Riya on the side each day, like curd, a plain roti or a fruit she likes. That way she is never hungry even when she dislikes the main dish. For the list, add onions, tomatoes, ginger, garlic and green chillies.
She likes banana and cucumber. Do I need to buy those daily?
Bananas and cucumbers last a few days, so buy them twice a week. Buy a small bunch of bananas, because they ripen fast. For Riya's cucumber, pick firm ones and keep them in the fridge.
Should I buy the fish at the start of the week?
Fish is best fresh, so cook it on the first or second day. If you buy it on the first day, plan the fish dinner for that evening and keep the rajma and dal for later in the week.
Good. Can you remind me what I said about Riya?
You said Riya is fussy, and that she likes banana and cucumber. So keep some of both ready for her side plate on the days when the main dish is rajma or fish.
I will tell you what happened at my cousin's wedding and you tell me what you think. First, the cook did not turn up.
That sounds stressful. A wedding without a cook is a big problem. Did the family find someone else, or did the guests have to wait?
My uncles ran to the kitchen themselves. My uncle Raju started making rice.

That must have been a lively scene. Rice is a good first step because it is hard to ruin. It is brave of Raju to step in, and having several relatives help could actually make the cooking feel like a family effort.
It got worse. He burnt the first batch and the smell went all over the hall.
Oh no, a burnt smell can spread fast. I hope someone opened the doors. It is a stressful moment, but a burnt first batch is also a classic wedding story that families laugh about later.
They made more rice and everyone ate it. People said it was the best wedding food.

What a lovely ending. Hungry guests, a team of relatives and a second try made the meal memorable. Raju's burnt first batch will probably be remembered as part of the story, which will be told at every family gathering.
Yes! Now tell me, what was the name of the uncle who made the rice?
It was your uncle Raju. He started making the rice when the cook did not turn up, and he burnt the first batch before the second one worked.
Do you know an easy dessert I can make this afternoon?
Yes, a fruit custard bowl is easy. Mix cold custard with chopped bananas, apples and grapes. Another option is a layered trifle with biscuits, jam and cream. Both are quick and are served cold.
I like the fruit idea. I am Daniel and I have six guests tonight.
Then make a big bowl for Daniel's six guests. Use about a litre of milk custard, and add two apples, two bananas and a handful of grapes. Chill it for at least two hours so it sets well.
Do I add the bananas now or later?
Add the bananas just before serving. They turn brown and soft if they sit in the custard for hours. Cut the apples and grapes earlier and keep them in the fridge.
Okay. How many bowls should I set out for the six guests?
Set out eight small bowls: six for your guests, one for you and one spare. That is easy and makes sure no one waits. You can serve the custard from one big bowl at the table.
I am making rangoli for the first time this Diwali. Any tips?
Start with a simple design, like a flower with a circle in the middle. Draw it lightly in chalk first, then fill with coloured powder or flower petals. Work from the centre outwards.
I am Kavya and my mother used to do it every year. I only watched.
Then you have seen more than you think. Try to recall her designs and start with one she made often. It is also a sweet way to carry on her tradition. Do not worry if lines are not perfect.
She always did a lotus. Is that hard?
A lotus is not hard if you build it in layers. Draw a small circle, then pointed petals around it, then a second ring of petals in between. Kavya, use two colours so the petals stand out clearly.
What if it rains? We live on the ground floor.
If rain is a risk, make your lotus in the doorway, under cover, or use flower petals, which look fine even slightly wet. You could also make it on a large plate and place it at the entrance.
Good. Which design did I say my mother always did?
You said she always did a lotus. So the lotus is a lovely choice for your first rangoli, and the layered petals will help you get it right.
My neighbour Mrs Nair invited us for dinner and I want to take something small. Any idea?
A box of homemade or good bakery sweets is a safe and kind gift. Fruit or flowers also work. Choose something that she can enjoy later, so she does not need to serve it at dinner.
I do not know what she likes. I only know that she lives with her husband and they have a dog.
Then a basket of fruit or a small box of sweets suits most people. If you are unsure, you can ask her kindly what she prefers. For the dog, do not bring food unless you know it is allowed.
Right. Do you think I should bring flowers also?
Flowers are a nice touch, but one gift is enough. If you take sweets, add a small bunch of flowers only if it is easy to carry. Mrs Nair will be pleased either way.
I will take sweets. What should I talk about at dinner?
Ask about their dog and how long they have lived in the area, and talk about food. Compliment the dishes. Most hosts like it, and Mr Nair may enjoy telling stories about the dog.
Tonight I want to cook something that smells amazing. Ideas?
Try a tomato rice with whole spices, or a simple garlic and cumin tempering on dal. Biryani or fried onions give the strongest smell. Roasting spices also makes the kitchen smell good.
Fried onion sounds great. How do I fry them without burning?
Slice the onions evenly and fry them in oil on medium heat. Stir often, and add a pinch of salt to draw out the water. When they turn golden brown, take them out right away.
They go dark quickly when I turn away. What do I do?
Lower the flame and do not walk away. Onions go from golden to burnt in a minute. Take them off the pan a little before they look ready, because they keep cooking in the hot oil.
Okay. Will fried onion go with dal?
Yes, a spoon of fried onion on top of dal adds a sweet and savoury smell. Mix a little into the tempering with cumin too. Your dal tonight will smell lovely with the golden onions.
Manav's school tiffin keeps coming back full. He is nine. What do I do?
Ask him what he does not like about it. It could be that the food is cold, hard to eat, or that he has no time. Children often skip lunch to play. A short chat can help find the cause.
I asked. He says he has only ten minutes for lunch.

Then pack food that is quick to eat: small pieces, nothing that needs cutting or peeling. Rolls, mini idlis, cut fruit and small sandwiches are easier. Also remind him that eating comes first, then play.
What if he does not eat even then?
Try a lighter tiffin and give him a bigger snack after school. Talk to his teacher, who may remind him to eat. Manav may just need some time to settle into the routine with only ten minutes.
I will talk to the teacher. What can I add to the box that is fun?
Add a small surprise, like a note, a star-shaped sandwich or a few cut fruits in a pattern. A little note for Manav saying 'eat first, then play' can also be a nice way to remind him.
Can you give me a very short recipe for lemon rice?
Cook rice and let it cool. Heat oil, add mustard seeds, chana dal, peanuts, curry leaves and turmeric. Mix in the rice with salt and lemon juice. It takes about ten minutes after the rice is cooked.
I have no peanuts. Is there another crunchy thing?
Use cashew pieces, or roasted sesame seeds, or even fried papad crushed on top. Any of them add crunch. Chana dal itself also gives some crunch when it is fried well.
I will try cashew. My name is Yusuf, I like it sour.
Then add the lemon juice of one and a half lemons for a cup of rice, Yusuf. Add it after switching off the flame so it stays fresh and sour. You can also add a bit more before serving.
Okay, should the rice be hot or cold when I mix?
Slightly warm or room temperature is best. If rice is very hot, it turns sticky and the lemon loses its taste. Cool rice from yesterday also works well for the cashew lemon rice you plan.
I just moved into a new flat. What basic things do I need in my kitchen?
A pressure cooker, a kadhai, a tawa, a couple of pots, a knife and board, a ladle and some spoons will do. Add steel boxes for spices and a few storage containers. You can add more as you cook.
I have little space. What is the one thing I must not skip?
A pressure cooker. It cooks rice, dal and vegetables fast and saves gas. If you can only buy one thing, buy a medium size one, which suits one or two people.
I live alone. My name is Ben. Is a three litre cooker right for me?
Yes, Ben, a three litre cooker is a good size for one person, and even for two. You can cook dal, rice and a vegetable in it, and it takes little space on the shelf.
Good. And which two pans should I buy after that?
After the three litre cooker, buy a kadhai for curries and frying, and a flat tawa for rotis and dosas. With those three things, you can cook most Indian meals as a person living alone.
Which is healthier, brown rice or white rice?
Brown rice has more fibre because the outer layer is kept. White rice is lighter and easier to cook. Both are fine as part of a normal meal, and what you eat with the rice matters too.
I like the white rice taste better.
That is fine. You can eat white rice and add dal, vegetables and curd to balance the meal. Taste matters, because you will cook what you enjoy and keep eating it.
My friend Pooja eats red rice. What is that?
Red rice is another type of whole grain rice, often from Kerala or Tamil Nadu, and it has a nutty taste. It takes longer to cook than white rice. Pooja may have grown up eating it.
Does it taste like brown rice?
It is close, but a bit more earthy and slightly chewy. If you want to taste Pooja's red rice, ask her to share a small bowl, and then decide if you like it more than white rice.
It is raining and I want something hot and crunchy. What do I make?
Pakoras are the classic rainy day snack. Mix besan with a little water, salt, chilli and ajwain to get a thick batter. Dip sliced onion, potato or spinach in it and fry until golden.
I have onions, potatoes and bread.
Then make onion and potato pakoras, and bread pakoras too. Dip bread slices in the batter after putting a thin potato filling between two slices. Fry them on medium heat so they cook through.
My friend Chloe is coming over. She has never had bread pakora.
She is in for a treat. Serve Chloe's bread pakora hot with green chutney or ketchup, and cut each into triangles so she can try both. Add some chai and you have the perfect rainy afternoon.
How do I make the green chutney quickly?
Blend a handful of coriander and mint, a green chilli, a small piece of ginger, salt and lemon juice with a spoon of water. It takes two minutes and goes well with Chloe's bread pakora.
I always skip breakfast. Is there something very quick I can eat?
Try a banana with peanut butter on toast, or a glass of milk with oats. Overnight oats are good: mix oats and milk in a jar at night, and eat them in the morning with fruit.
I do not have time even for toast.
Then keep boiled eggs or a handful of nuts and a fruit in your bag. They need no cooking and can be eaten on the way. Even a banana on the go is better than nothing.
I am Arjun and I take the bus. Can I eat in the bus?
Yes, Arjun, a banana or a handful of nuts is easy to eat in the bus. Avoid messy things like curd or gravy. Carry a napkin and a water bottle with you.
Which one stays fresh longer, a banana or an egg?
A banana stays fine for the whole morning in a bag, but it can bruise. A boiled egg is best eaten within a few hours, and should stay cool. For your bus ride, the banana is safer.
What is the story behind Holi? My kids keep asking.
Holi remembers the story of Prahlad, a boy who loved Vishnu, and his aunt Holika. She tried to burn him, but she was the one who burned. It is told as the win of good over evil.
My son Arjun asked why we throw colours then.
The colours come from the playful stories of Krishna and Radha, and from the spring season. People throw colours to celebrate the end of winter, forgive each other and meet with joy.
My daughter wants to know why the bonfire comes first.
The bonfire on the night before is called Holika Dahan. People light it to remember how Holika burned while Prahlad stayed safe. The next morning is when families play with colours.
Can you say that story one more time in short, for my son Arjun?

A boy named Prahlad believed in God. His aunt Holika tried to burn him in a fire, but she burned and he stayed safe. That is why people light a bonfire, and why Arjun and the family play with colours next day.
I always add too much salt. How do I fix a dish that is too salty?
Add a peeled raw potato and boil it for a few minutes, or add a little more water, tomato or curd. A spoon of sugar or lemon juice can balance the taste a bit. Next time add salt in small amounts.
It is the dal I made for my friends tonight. I am Pooja.
Then for Pooja's dal, add hot water and bring it to a boil again, and add a squeeze of lemon. If it is still salty, stir in a small amount of cooked rice or a spoon of curd. Taste after each step.
Should I tell my friends the dal was too salty?
You do not need to announce it. Serve the dal with plenty of rice and curd, which balance the salt. If anyone asks, you can say you were learning, and Pooja's friends will understand.
Okay. Thanks. What was that trick with the potato?
Boil a peeled raw potato in the dal for ten minutes. It soaks up a little salt, so you can take it out before serving. It is not perfect, but for your salty dal it will help a bit.
Chloe and I are planning a surprise birthday party for her brother Ben. We have a very small budget.
Keep it simple: a few friends at home, a homemade cake, and snacks you can cook, like sandwiches and pakoras. Decorate with balloons and paper. The surprise matters more than the cost.
Where should we hide everyone?

Hide the guests in a room and ask them to stay silent until Ben comes in. Switch off the lights, and when he opens the door, everyone jumps out. You can also ask a friend to keep Ben busy till the guests arrive.
Chloe says he gets scared easily. Is that okay?
If Ben is easily scared, use a gentler surprise. Put the guests in the living room with lights on, and have them call his name when he walks in. A soft welcome is kinder than a loud jump.
Good idea. What snacks can we make that are not expensive?

Make sandwiches, popcorn, a big pot of pulao and a simple cake. These are cheap and feed many. A fruit punch in a big jug is also cheap, and Ben will enjoy the party his sister and friends worked for.
What was the plan for the surprise again?
Keep the guests in the living room with the lights on, and when Ben walks in, they call out his name softly. Since Ben gets scared easily, there is no loud jump.
Can you explain how to make kheer for the first time?
Boil a litre of milk in a heavy pot, add a handful of washed rice and cook on low heat, stirring now and then. When the rice is soft and the milk is thick, add sugar and cardamom.
How long does it take?
It takes about forty minutes on low heat. Do not rush it with a high flame, because the milk can burn at the bottom. Stirring often keeps it smooth.
My mother-in-law Sushila likes it with dry fruits.
Then add chopped almonds, cashews and raisins at the end. You can fry them lightly in a spoon of ghee first for more flavour. Sushila will enjoy it with the nuts on top.
Can I make it a day before she comes?

Yes, kheer tastes good the next day and thickens in the fridge. Add a little warm milk when reheating it. Make Sushila's kheer a day ahead, and add the dry fruits just before serving to keep them crisp.
Daniel is vegetarian but his wife Sofia is not. How do I cook for both when they come over?
Plan a meal where most dishes are vegetarian and one dish has meat. Rice, dal, a vegetable and roti suit both. Add a chicken curry for Sofia, cooked in a separate pot.
Is it okay to use the same spoon?
No, use separate spoons and pots for the meat dish. Daniel is vegetarian, so any meat touching his food would upset him. Keep the serving spoons and plates separate.
Good. What dessert can they both eat?
Kheer, fruit salad or ice cream are fine for both. Check that the dessert has no egg or gelatin if Daniel avoids them. A simple kheer is safe and traditional.
Great. Will I need extra rice, since the chicken is a side?
Yes, a little extra rice is good, since Sofia will pair the chicken with it, and Daniel will have the dal and vegetable with his. Make a bit more rice than usual.
Arjun and I went to the fish market today for the first time.
How was it? Fish markets are loud and smelly but full of fresh things. Did you buy anything?
We bought two big pomfrets. The seller said they were caught this morning.
Good. To check freshness, the eyes should be bright, the gills red and the flesh firm. Clean and cook them the same day if you can.
He told us to fry them with turmeric and salt. Is that enough?
Yes, that is the simplest way. Rub turmeric, salt and a bit of chilli on the cleaned fish, rest it for ten minutes and shallow fry until crisp on both sides. Serve with lemon and rice.
We will do that. Remind me, who did I go to the market with?
You went with Arjun, and you came home with two fresh pomfrets. Fried with turmeric and salt, they will make a good first meal from your first fish market visit.
My mixer jar is leaking a bit. Can I still use it?
A small leak can be a rubber ring that is worn or not seated well. Check the ring under the blade, wash it and fit it back firmly. If it is cracked, buy a new ring, which is cheap.
It was fine yesterday and today it leaks.
Then it probably moved while washing. Remove the ring, dry it, and press it back into its groove. Tighten the jar on the base and try with a little water first.
Okay. It was the ring, I fixed it. By the way, my name is Kavya and I make chutney every day.
Good, Kavya. If you use the mixer daily, wash the ring and blade well each time and let them dry. That prevents smell and keeps the ring in good shape for months.
What do I serve for a simple lunch for my father's friends? There will be five elderly men.
Keep it light and easy to eat: soft rotis, dal, a mild vegetable, rice, curd and a small sweet. Avoid very spicy or hard foods. Serve warm and sit them comfortably.
My father's name is Mohan and he likes plain food.
Then keep Mohan's lunch simple, with little oil and mild spice. Make a plain dal, lauki sabzi, and soft phulkas. Offer pickle on the side so friends can choose.
Should I serve the food or let them help themselves?
For elderly guests, it is kinder to serve them at the table and refill the plates. Ask Mohan how his friends like it. Keep a jug of water and a glass for each person on the table.
What sweet can I offer that is soft?
Kheer or suji halwa is soft and warm and easy to eat. Serve a small bowl for each person. Mohan and his friends will enjoy it after the plain meal.
Pooja gave me a recipe for mango kulfi but I lost the paper. Can you help?
Sure. Boil a litre of milk until it reduces by a third, then add sugar and cardamom. Cool it, blend with ripe mango pulp, pour into moulds and freeze for six hours.
Do I need condensed milk?
It is not necessary. It saves time, since you do not need to boil the milk for long. If you use it, add less sugar. Otherwise, the slow boiled milk gives a richer flavour.
I have a few cups. Can I freeze it in those?

Yes, small cups are fine. Pour in the mixture, cover with foil, insert a stick when partly frozen and freeze fully. To remove, dip the cup in warm water for a few seconds. Pooja's kulfi will come out whole.
My spice box is a mess. I never know which is which.

Try labelling each small tin with its name and putting the most used ones, like turmeric, cumin, chilli powder and coriander powder, at the front. A round steel box with seven small bowls works well for daily use.
I have turmeric, cumin, mustard, chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala and hing. That is only seven.

Then a seven-bowl box is perfect for you. Put turmeric, cumin and chilli powder in the bowls that are easiest to reach, since you use them most. Keep the rest of the stock in larger jars outside the box.
My friend Riya says spices lose smell if kept near the stove. Is that true?
Yes, heat and steam make spices lose flavour faster. Keep your box in a drawer or shelf close to the stove, but not right above the flame. Riya's tip is a good one, especially for ground spices.
Which of the seven goes bad first?
Garam masala and ground coriander usually lose smell first, because they are blended or ground. Whole mustard and cumin last longer. So check your garam masala first, and smell it before you add it.
Yusuf here. It is Ramzan and I want to organise an iftar at home for my neighbours.

What a kind idea. Keep the meal simple: dates, fruit, a cold drink, pakoras or samosas, and one main dish like biryani or haleem. Serve the first sweet thing at sunset and the main food a little later.
There will be about twelve people. Some are not Muslim, so I want to explain things.
A short welcome is enough. Say what iftar means, that it is the meal that ends the day's fast, and that the fast opens with dates and water. Guests usually enjoy hearing the story behind the food.
Should I ask my neighbours about food they cannot eat?
Yes, ask when you invite them. Some people are vegetarian or avoid certain foods, and it is easy to plan once you know. Mention in the invitation that you will have a vegetarian dish too.
I will do that. Two of them are Jain, so no onion or garlic. Can I make samosas for them?
Yes, Yusuf. Make a separate batch of samosas with potato, peas, cumin and ginger, without onion or garlic. Keep that batch aside and label it, so your Jain neighbours know it is theirs.
Easy way to make paneer at home?
Boil a litre of full cream milk, then add two spoons of lemon juice or vinegar. The milk will split into curds. Strain through a thin cloth, rinse, and press with a heavy plate for half an hour.
What do I do with the leftover water?
That water is called whey and it is useful. Use it to knead dough, cook rice or make soup. It adds a little protein and softness. You can also drink it with salt.
My sister Pooja wants to know if it works with toned milk.
It works, but you get less paneer and it is softer. Full cream milk gives a better result. Tell Pooja to use full cream the first time, and try toned milk later.
What will she make with it?
She might make palak paneer, paneer bhurji or a simple tikka. Fresh paneer is soft, so it suits bhurji very well. Pooja can also eat a few cubes with a pinch of salt and pepper.
It is so hot that I do not want to cook at all. What can I eat?
Cold foods are best: curd rice, cucumber raita, fruit salad, or a chilled buttermilk with roasted cumin. You can also soak poha and have it as a salad with onion, tomato and lemon.
I like the poha idea. My friend Chloe says add pomegranate. Is that good?
Yes, pomegranate adds sweetness and a nice crunch. Add a spoon of it on top just before eating. Chloe's idea also makes the poha look pretty.
What do I do about drinks? I get tired of water.
Try jaljeera, nimbu pani with a pinch of salt, or coconut water. Add mint leaves and ice to a jug of lemon water. Chloe's pomegranate can also be added to a glass of water for a light flavour.
What was the thing Chloe suggested again?
Chloe suggested adding pomegranate to the poha salad. It gives sweetness and crunch, and you can also drop a few seeds in a glass of water.
I would like to host a Sunday lunch for my colleagues. Eight people.
A relaxed menu is best: one rice dish, a dal, two vegetables, roti, raita and a sweet. Cook the sweet and dal the day before, so Sunday is only rice, vegetables and rotis.
What if one colleague is vegan?
Then make most dishes vegan, using oil instead of ghee and skipping curd in the main dishes. Serve the raita in a separate bowl. Your vegan guest can then eat almost everything.
Her name is Kavya. Can she eat the sweet?
Only if it has no milk or ghee. Kheer and halwa both have milk or ghee, so make a coconut milk payasam or a fruit salad instead. Kavya will be happy to have a dessert made for her too.
I will make coconut milk payasam for her. Should I add jaggery or sugar?

Jaggery tastes richer and goes well with coconut milk, though it can darken the colour. Sugar keeps it clear. For Kavya's payasam, jaggery is nice, and add it after the milk is off the heat so it does not split.
Does banana bread need eggs? My sister Riya cannot have them.
A banana bread can be made without eggs. Mash very ripe bananas well, and they will act as the binder. Add flour, a little oil, sugar, baking soda and a pinch of salt, then bake until golden.
How many bananas?
Use three ripe bananas for a standard loaf tin. The riper they are, the sweeter and softer the bread will be. Mash them until almost smooth.
Can I add walnuts?
Yes, chop a handful of walnuts and fold them in at the end. They give a nice crunch. If you are serving it to Riya, check first whether she is fine with nuts.
She is. Should I add chocolate also?
You can, a small handful of chocolate chips is plenty. Add them after the walnuts and stir once or twice. Riya's egg-free banana bread will taste like a treat with chocolate and walnuts.
My daughter Chloe will only eat plain rice and curd. How do I get her to try more?
Do not force it. Put a very small amount of a new food on her plate, next to the rice, and let her see you eating it. Children often need to see a food many times before they try it.
She is four. She likes the colour yellow.
Then use that. Make yellow foods like pumpkin curry, yellow dal, corn or banana. Call them fun names. A bright plate can make a four-year-old curious.
She likes a game called 'tasting detective'. Could I use that?
That is a great fit. Let Chloe be the detective and describe each bite: crunchy, soft, sweet or salty. A small sticker for each new food tasted can add to the fun.
Good. What can I mix into her curd rice?
Try stirring in a little mashed banana, grated carrot or a few pomegranate seeds. Start with a tiny bit so Chloe can still enjoy the rice she likes, and slowly add more as the detective game goes on.
Tonight I plan to make dal and rice. I am bored of it though.
Make it special by tempering the dal differently. Fry garlic and red chilli in ghee and pour it on top. Or cook the dal with spinach for dal palak. A new tempering can change the whole taste.
I have spinach and tomatoes. I'm Manav.
Then make dal palak, Manav. Boil the dal with turmeric and tomato, add chopped spinach in the last five minutes, and finish with a garlic and cumin tempering. The green colour looks fresh.
Can I add the spinach at the beginning?
You can, but it will lose its bright colour and become dull. Adding it at the end keeps the colour and the taste fresh. For your dal palak, cook the spinach only five minutes.
Okay. Do I serve it with plain rice or something else?
Plain rice is a good partner, and a spoon of ghee on top makes it richer. You could also serve a fried papad and a bit of pickle. With Manav's dal palak, that is a full, simple dinner.
Which is better for tiffin, a steel box or a plastic one?
Steel boxes last longer, do not hold smells and are safe with hot food. Plastic is lighter and cheaper. For hot food, steel is the better choice. For dry snacks, plastic is fine.
My nephew Arjun drops everything. Plastic might be better?
Steel does not break, so even if Arjun drops it, it will dent but still work. Plastic can crack. Pick a steel box with a tight lid and a rubber seal, which is strong and spill proof.
Does steel keep food warm?
A single layer steel box does not keep food hot for long. A double walled steel box or an insulated bag keeps it warm for a few hours. For Arjun's school day, a bag helps.
I will take the double walled box then. How do I wash it?
Wash it with warm soapy water and a soft sponge, and dry well, especially the lid. Do not put a double walled box in boiling water. Arjun's box will last for years if you take care of the seal.
I am planning to give sweets to neighbours this Diwali. What do I make?
Easy and neat to give: coconut barfi, besan laddoo or dry fruit chikki. All of them keep for days, so you can make them ahead. Wrap in small boxes with a ribbon.
I have ten families to give. My name is Daniel.
For ten families, make one big batch of laddoo, around forty pieces, four for each family. Daniel, you can also add a few pieces of a second sweet, so each box has two kinds.
What if I do not have time?
Buy one sweet from a good shop and make one at home. A mix works well, and your homemade one will feel special. You can also give dry fruits in a neat box.
Will the laddoo be okay for a week?
Yes, besan laddoo stays fresh for about a week to ten days in a closed box at room temperature. Make Daniel's batch three or four days before Diwali and they will be at their best.
I feel sad today. Can food help? What do I make?

I am sorry you feel sad. Comfort food can help a little. Something warm and familiar, like khichdi, a hot bowl of dal rice, or a cup of chai, can feel like a hug. Cooking itself can also calm your mind.
My grandmother used to make me sweet rice when I was sad.
Then make that for yourself. Cooking something she made can feel like having her near. Cook rice with milk, sugar and a pinch of cardamom, just like she did.
Her name was Radha. She added saffron.
Then add a few strands of saffron, soaked in warm milk, to Radha's sweet rice. The smell and the colour will bring back the memory. Eat it slowly, and let yourself remember her.
Thank you. Whose recipe is it, again?
It is your grandmother Radha's. She made it with milk, sugar, cardamom and saffron. It is a sweet way to remember her when you feel low.
Mother's Day is near and I would like to cook for my mother. She does everything for us.
That is thoughtful. Plan her favourite meal and let her rest while you cook. Set the table, add a flower and serve her first. The cleaning up can be part of your gift too.
Her favourite is vegetable pulao and raita. My name is Sofia.
Sofia, a vegetable pulao is a good choice for a first try. Fry whole spices and onions, add rice and vegetables and cook with water. Make the raita with curd, cucumber and roasted cumin.
How long should I soak the rice?
Soak basmati rice for twenty to thirty minutes, then drain well. This helps the grains cook long and separate, and the pulao is less likely to turn mushy.
What should I tell her while she waits?
Just tell her to sit and rest, and that dinner is a surprise. Sofia, let her sit with tea or a book. When the pulao and raita arrive, she will know how much you care.
Christmas is coming and I want to bake a plum cake. Where do I start?

A plum cake needs dry fruits soaked in orange juice with a little spice and orange peel. Soak raisins, dates and cashews a few days before. Then make a batter of flour, butter, sugar and eggs and bake slowly.
How many days before should I soak the fruit?
Soak them at least three days, and up to a week for a rich cake. Keep the jar closed and shake it each day. The fruit gets soft and sweet.
I will soak them for five days. My name is Ben and I have never done this.
Five days is a good choice, Ben. Keep the jar in a cool place, and give it a shake each day. When you bake, line the tin with paper and use a low heat so the cake does not burn.
How long will the cake bake?
It will bake around an hour to an hour and a quarter at a low heat. Check with a thin stick after fifty minutes. Ben's cake is ready when the stick comes out clean.
Can you help me say no to guests who want more food when I have run out?
Say it kindly and honestly, like 'I am so sorry, everything has been eaten. Would you like some fruit or a cup of tea?' Offering something else shows that you care. No one will mind.
But I feel bad. My aunt Meera always asks for seconds.
Then keep a small extra dish ready, like some rice and curd or a few rotis, for people who want more. Aunt Meera will feel welcome, and you will not feel bad.
Good idea. How much extra should I plan for ten guests?
Plan about one extra portion for every five guests, so two extra portions for ten guests. That way even Meera's second helping is covered, and there is something for the late ones too.
What was my aunt's name?
Your aunt is Meera, and she always asks for seconds. Keep a small extra dish of rice and curd ready for her.
I love street food but my mother says it is unsafe. I am Arjun and I am seventeen.
Street food can be delicious. It is wise to choose stalls that look clean, are busy with customers and cook the food fresh and hot in front of you. Avoid food that has been sitting out for hours.
I want pani puri. Is it okay?

Pani puri is popular, but the water is a worry if it is not clean. Pick a stall that uses bottled or boiled water, with a clean ladle and gloves. If unsure, skip it and eat something that is fried hot.
Could I make pani puri at home so my mother is happy?
Yes, you can. Buy ready puris, make spicy water with mint, coriander, tamarind and spices, and fill with boiled potato and chickpeas. You and your mother can make it together.
Great, what do I put inside?
Fill each puri with a little mashed boiled potato and a few boiled chickpeas, then pour the spiced water in. Arjun's homemade version will be fresh, clean, and your mother can even have one too.
My grandfather Mohan drinks tea six times a day. Is that too much?
I cannot give medical advice, but many people drink a few cups of tea daily. If you are worried, you can ask his doctor. It also helps to make his tea lighter, with less sugar.
He puts three spoons of sugar. How do I make him drink less?
Do not change it all at once. Reduce the sugar slowly, half a spoon at a time, every few days. He may not even notice. Add cardamom or ginger for flavour instead.
He is stubborn. He may notice.
Then involve him. Tell him you are trying a new tea with ginger and cardamom and ask for his opinion. Mohan will feel respected and may like it. Do not hide what you are doing.
Okay. I will make him cardamom tea this evening.
That is a kind plan. Crush two cardamom pods and boil them with the tea leaves, and add a little less sugar than usual. If Mohan likes the smell, he will be more open to it.
Which sweets are made for Eid?
Common ones are sheer khurma, made with vermicelli, milk and dates, and kheer. Many families also make seviyan, shahi tukda and baklava. It differs from home to home and country to country.
My friend Yusuf's mother makes sheer khurma. What does it taste like?
It is creamy, sweet and rich, with the soft texture of vermicelli. Nuts, dates and a little cardamom add flavour. It is served warm or cold, in small bowls, after the Eid meal.
Can I make it for him?
Yes, but it is nice to ask Yusuf first if he would like it. A homemade sheer khurma is a thoughtful gift. Do not worry if it is different from his mother's, as every family has its own way.
Yes. What do I need for it again?
For Yusuf's sheer khurma, you need milk, fine vermicelli, ghee, dates, sugar, cardamom and nuts like almonds and pistachios. Fry the vermicelli in ghee first, then simmer it in milk until it is soft.
I want to buy good mangoes. How do I choose?
Smell the stem end. A ripe mango has a sweet smell. It should feel slightly soft when pressed gently, and be heavy for its size. Avoid ones with black patches or wrinkles.
My friend Pooja likes the Alphonso kind. I have heard it is expensive.

Alphonso mangoes are sweet and often costly, especially at the start of the season. Prices drop as the season goes on. If you are on a budget, wait until later or try other varieties like Kesar or Langra.
Is it alright to buy them raw and ripen at home?
Yes. Keep raw mangoes in a paper bag or a box with newspaper for a few days. Check them each day, and eat them once they smell sweet and feel soft. That is a good way to get ripe mangoes for Pooja.
What was the kind Pooja likes?
Pooja likes the Alphonso. If it is too costly, Kesar is a good second choice, and it is sweet and usually less expensive.
I need a simple recipe for chicken curry. I am Daniel and I have never cooked meat.

Wash and cut chicken into pieces. Fry onions, ginger and garlic, add tomato and spices, then the chicken and a little water. Cook it covered until the chicken is fully cooked and no pink remains inside.
How long does it take?
Usually thirty to forty minutes on medium heat for bone-in pieces. Check one thick piece by cutting it open. The meat should be white and firm all the way through, with clear juices.
What about washing the chicken? I heard it is not good.

It is better not to wash raw chicken under the tap, because the water can splash germs around your kitchen. Cook it well and the heat will kill them. Wash your hands, knife and board after touching it.
Okay. Any last tip for my first time?
Yes, Daniel. Keep the flame at medium, do not rush and use a timer. Cook the chicken fully, and taste the gravy before the end to fix the salt.
I broke a glass in the kitchen and I am afraid to pick up the pieces. What do I do?
First, keep children and pets out of the room and wear shoes. Pick up large pieces carefully and put them in a thick paper. Then use a broom and dustpan for small pieces.
There are tiny pieces everywhere. How do I get them?
Press a slice of bread or a damp paper towel gently on the floor to pick up small shards. You can also use tape. Then go over it with a flashlight to see any shiny bits.
I am Riya and I live alone. Do I throw the glass in the bin?
Yes, Riya, but wrap it in thick paper or a cardboard box and write 'glass' on it. This keeps whoever handles the rubbish safe. Do not put it in a thin bag.
What did I say my name was?
Your name is Riya, and you live alone. Wrap the broken glass in thick paper and mark it, so the person handling the rubbish stays safe.
We are planning a picnic by the lake. Daniel and I will make sandwiches for twelve people.
A good plan. Make a mix of fillings so everyone finds something: cucumber and cheese, potato with chutney, and egg for those who eat it. Cut sandwiches into triangles and wrap them in foil.
How many bread slices do we need?
For twelve people, count two sandwiches each, so twenty-four sandwiches, which means forty-eight slices. Buy one extra loaf in case. Daniel can butter while you fill.
Should we make them in the morning?
Yes, make them in the morning of the picnic so they stay fresh. Keep them in a cool bag, and add a layer of lettuce so the bread does not get wet. Daniel can pack them in the box.
How many sandwiches did we say, again?
Two each for twelve people, so twenty-four sandwiches, using forty-eight slices of bread. You and Daniel can buy one extra loaf just in case.
I bought a cake from a bakery for my sister's birthday and it is dry. What can I do?
Brush each slice lightly with sugar syrup or milk to soften it. Serve with ice cream or whipped cream, which add moisture. A fresh strawberry or mango topping also helps.
Her name is Pooja and she loves ice cream. Which one goes well?
Vanilla ice cream goes with almost any cake and will balance the dryness. If the cake is chocolate, a scoop of vanilla or coffee ice cream is lovely. Pooja will enjoy the combination.
It is a chocolate cake. Should I warm it?

Yes, warm each slice for about fifteen seconds in a microwave if you have one. It will soften and the chocolate smells better. Then add a scoop of vanilla ice cream, and Pooja's dry cake will be a hit.
My mother fasts on Mondays and I want to cook something she can eat. I am Kavya.
What kind of fast does she keep? Many fasts allow fruit, milk, sabudana, potato, and rock salt. Ask her what is allowed, so you cook what she can eat.
She eats sabudana, potatoes, peanuts and fruit.
Then make sabudana khichdi. Soak the sabudana for a few hours, fry cumin, peanuts and potato in ghee, add the sabudana and rock salt, and cook until the pearls turn clear. Serve with curd.
My sabudana always sticks. Why?
It usually means it was soaked in too much water, or not drained well. Wash it, soak it in just enough water to cover it, and keep it for four to six hours. The pearls should be separate and soft.
Okay. And what did she say she eats?
Kavya, your mother eats sabudana, potatoes, peanuts and fruit during the fast. So the khichdi with potato and peanuts is a perfect dish for her Monday.
Weekend plan: pancakes for the kids. Can you give me a quick recipe?
Mix one cup of flour, a spoon of sugar, a pinch of salt and a teaspoon of baking powder. Add one egg, a cup of milk and a spoon of melted butter. Whisk lightly and cook on a hot pan.
My kids are Riya and Manav. Riya wants round ones, Manav wants animal shapes.
For Riya, pour the batter in a small circle and it will make a round pancake. For Manav, use a spoon or a squeeze bottle to draw a simple shape, like a cat or a fish, on the pan.
How do I know when to flip?
Flip when you see small bubbles on the top and the edges look dry, usually after about two minutes. Use a thin spatula and turn it fast. Manav's animal shapes cook quicker, so watch them closely.
I want to cook a surprise dinner for my parents' anniversary. They like south Indian food.
Lovely. A menu of masala dosa, sambar, two chutneys and a sweet like payasam would feel special. Make the batter two days earlier and the payasam the day before.
That is a lot. I am Yusuf and I have only cooked eggs.
Then simplify, Yusuf. Buy ready batter, and make just the sambar, chutney and a simple sweet. Plain dosas are easier than masala ones. That way you can skip the potato filling.
Can I buy the sambar too?
Yes, a good ready sambar is fine for a first time. Add fresh curry leaves and a spoon of ghee to make it taste homemade. Your parents will care about the effort and the surprise.
Okay. And which parts did I decide to make myself?
You will make the chutney and a simple sweet yourself, and buy the batter and the sambar. Yusuf, make the chutney the day before, so the anniversary day is calm.
My new neighbour just moved in next door. I want to welcome her with food.
That is a warm gesture. A small plate of something homemade, like sweets, a cake or a snack, works well. Keep it simple and wrap it neatly. Add a short note with your name and flat number.
Her name is Chloe and she is from London. I do not know if she likes spicy food.
Then keep it mild. A small box of coconut barfi or a slice of homemade cake would be a safe choice. You can offer a spicier dish later, once you know what Chloe enjoys.
I will make a cake. Should I knock and give it, or leave it at the door?
Knock and give it with a smile, so she knows who you are. Keep it short, since she may be busy unpacking. If she does not answer, leave it with a note for Chloe.
What should I write on the note?
Write something short, like 'Welcome to the building! I am in flat 4B. Please knock if you need anything.' Add your name and your number if you are comfortable with it. Chloe will feel welcome.
Good. Which flat did I say I live in?
You said flat 4B. Put that on the note, so Chloe knows exactly where you live and can find you easily when she needs help.
Let me tell you about my day in parts. First, I woke up late.
Oh dear, a late start can make the whole day feel rushed. Did you miss anything important because of it, or did you manage to catch up?
I missed the bus, so I took an auto. The driver, a man called Salim, was very chatty.
A chatty auto driver can make a ride fun or tiring. What did Salim talk about? Sometimes they know the best street food places and the best shortcuts too.
He told me about a tiffin place near my office that makes the best parathas.
That is a useful tip. Local tiffin places often serve fresh home style food at fair prices. Parathas are great for lunch, and it is nice that a stranger shared it with you.
I went there at lunch and it was true. The aloo paratha was huge.
I am glad it was good. A big aloo paratha with curd and pickle is a proper meal. A bad start can end well, and that was thanks to Salim.
Yes. What did Salim tell me about?
Salim told you about a tiffin place near your office that makes the best parathas. You tried the aloo paratha at lunch and found it huge and tasty.
How do I make masala chai for a crowd? About fifteen cups.
Boil six cups of water with a big piece of crushed ginger, four cardamom pods and a few spoons of tea leaves. Add six cups of milk and sugar, boil until deep brown, and strain.
I do not have a very big pot.
Then make it in two batches, one after the other, or use a large pressure cooker pot without the lid. Keep the first batch hot in a flask while you make the second one.
Do I have a flask? Yes, my aunt gave me a steel one. Her name is Nirmala.
Then Nirmala's flask is just right. Pour the hot chai in, close it, and it will stay hot for hours. Rinse the flask with hot water first so it keeps the heat better.
How much sugar for fifteen cups?
Use about fifteen spoons for a medium sweet chai, which is one level spoon per cup. Add a little less at first, taste, and add more. Guests can add extra sugar from a bowl too.
Great. What did I say about the flask?
You said your aunt Nirmala gave you a steel flask. Use it to keep the first batch hot while the second batch is brewing.
Diwali shopping is stressing me out. I have a long list.
That sounds like a lot. Break the list into groups: food, decoration, gifts and clothes. Do one group a day instead of everything at once. Cross off each item as you buy it.
Food is the hardest. I am Pooja and I am hosting twenty people.

For twenty people, keep the menu simple. Make a few sweets ahead, order the main dish from a caterer or cook one big dish like pulao, and get snacks from a shop. You do not need to do everything yourself.
Can I really buy some things ready-made? My mother-in-law will judge me.
Yes, you can. Many families do it. Make one dish yourself, like her favourite sweet, and buy the rest. Pooja, a calm host is better than a tired one, and most guests care about the warmth.
Which of the sweets can I make ahead?
Laddoo, barfi and chikki all keep for days, so you can make them a week before. Fried items like gujiya are best made two days earlier. Do not make milk sweets too early.
And what is the number of guests I said?
You said twenty guests. So plan about four or five pieces of sweets for each person, and make sure you have enough plates and cups for twenty, plus a few extra.
What is a tiffin that is still tasty at room temperature? My husband eats lunch late.
Choose dry dishes that taste fine cold: stuffed parathas, lemon rice, vegetable pulao or roti rolls. Avoid gravy and fried crisp things, which go soft. Add pickle and fruit.
He likes rice. His name is Daniel and he works in a hospital, so he often misses lunch time.
Then lemon rice or tamarind rice suits Daniel, since both taste better after sitting. They also do not spoil quickly because of the lemon and tamarind. Add some peanuts and curry leaves.
Can I add boiled egg to it?
Yes, but eggs should stay cool, so pack a boiled egg in a separate box and use an insulated bag. If lunch can be hours late, it is safer to skip the egg and give nuts instead.
Good point. What nuts go well with rice?
Roasted peanuts, cashews or almonds are all fine. A small handful in a separate bag keeps them crisp. Daniel can sprinkle them over his lemon rice when he sits down to eat.
So what was the rice we decided on?
We decided on lemon rice for Daniel, or tamarind rice as another choice. Pack the nuts separately so they stay crunchy for his late lunch.
My little son Manav is afraid of Holi colours. How can I help?
Let him watch from a safe place first. Show him the colours in small plates and let him touch them with a finger. Many children need time, so do not push him.
He is five. He will play only if his friend Arjun is with him.
Then invite Arjun to your house and let the two boys play together. Start with a little colour on a cheek, or use water and flower petals instead of powder.
Is it safe to use colour on children?
Use soft, skin-safe colours or homemade ones made from flowers, turmeric or beetroot. Put oil on the skin and hair beforehand, and keep colours away from the eyes and mouth. Watch Manav closely.
I like the flower idea. How do I make colour at home?
Dry rose petals and grind them for pink. Mix turmeric with gram flour for yellow, and use ground neem or mint leaves for green. These are gentle on Manav and Arjun's skin.
Which friend does he want with him?
Manav wants his friend Arjun with him. So invite Arjun first, and let the boys start with petals and gentle colours before anything stronger.
Do you have a recipe for soft, fluffy idlis? Mine are hard.
Idlis turn hard when the batter is too thick, not fermented enough or steamed for too long. The batter should flow like thick pancake batter. Steam for ten to twelve minutes only.
I used ready batter from the shop.
Ready batter can be thick. Mix in a little water until it falls easily from a spoon. Add a pinch of salt, and let it rest at room temperature for an hour before steaming.
I did not rest it. I took it straight from the fridge. I am Kavya.
That is the reason, Kavya. Cold batter does not rise well. Take it out of the fridge at least one hour before and do not stir too much, so the air stays in.
What if I do not have an idli stand?
Use small steel bowls or cups, greased with oil, in a pressure cooker or a wide pot. Pour the batter in and steam without the whistle. Your idlis will turn out soft if the batter rests first.
What was my mistake again?
You used ready batter straight from the fridge without resting it. The cold batter did not rise, so the idlis were hard. Let your next batch rest for an hour first.
I am going to a wedding and I am confused about how much to eat. There are so many dishes.
Weddings often have long menus. A good way is to take small portions of what looks best, and go back for more if you like. You do not need to try everything.
There will be a live dosa counter and a chaat counter. I am Ben.
Then begin with the dosa while it is hot, Ben, and go to the chaat after the main meal, or before if the queue is short. Keep sweets for the end.
I am nervous about eating in a big crowd in a nice dress.
That is common. Choose foods that are easy to eat while standing, like dosa, chaat or small snacks. Avoid anything with a lot of gravy. Keep a napkin in hand and eat slowly.
What if I spill something?
Do not worry, it happens to many people. Dab the stain with a damp napkin, do not rub. Keep a small stain remover pen or a few tissues in your bag for Ben's evening.
What counters did I say they had?
You said there would be a live dosa counter and a chaat counter. Ben, take the dosa when it is hot and the chaat after, and leave space for sweets.
I need to prepare a big dinner and I have only two burners. How do I manage?

Plan dishes that can be made ahead and reheated, like dal, curries and sweets. On the day, use the two burners for rice and rotis, and keep the rest warm. Use the oven or a microwave for reheating too.
I have a rice cooker. Can I use it for more?
Yes, a rice cooker is helpful. Cook rice or pulao in it, and it will free one burner. Some models can also steam vegetables or cook dal.
I am Arjun and I have no help in the kitchen.
Then do most of the work the day before, Arjun. Chop vegetables, make the curries and the dessert, and store them in the fridge. On the day, you only warm things and make rotis.
Should I make rotis ahead too?
You can make rotis a few hours ahead and keep them in a closed box wrapped in a cloth. Heat them on the tawa for a few seconds before serving. That saves time for your two burners.
And what did I say I could use to free a burner?
You said you have a rice cooker. Use it to cook rice or pulao, and it will free one of your two burners for the curry or rotis.
We are celebrating Pongal with my husband's family, who are from Tamil Nadu. I am from Punjab and do not know the traditions.
It is lovely that you are joining in. Ask your mother-in-law what you can help with. Usually families draw a kolam at the door, cook pongal in a new pot and offer it to the sun.
What is a kolam? Is it like rangoli?
Yes, it is similar. A kolam is a pattern drawn with rice flour at the doorstep. It is often made fresh each morning, and during Pongal it is large and colourful.
I am Sofia and I want to try it. Can I?
Yes, Sofia. Ask your mother-in-law to show you a simple pattern first, like a row of dots joined by lines. Practise once on paper before the real doorstep.
What else will I see on that day?
You will see new clothes, sugarcane stalks, turmeric plants tied to the pot, and the pongal pot boiling over while everyone shouts 'Pongalo Pongal'. There is music, sweets and family meals.
Which place is my husband's family from?
Your husband's family is from Tamil Nadu, while you are from Punjab. That makes your first Pongal a lovely mix, and Sofia, you can share a Punjabi sweet too.
My monthly grocery bill is too high. Any tips for buying food smartly?
Plan meals for the week and buy only what you need. Buy grains and pulses in bulk, buy vegetables that are in season, and avoid buying when hungry. Carry a list and stick to it.
We waste a lot of vegetables. They go bad in the fridge.
Keep older vegetables in front, wash and dry greens before storing them, and use soft vegetables first. Soups, parathas and pulaos are good ways to use leftovers.
I am Riya and I live with two friends. We never agree on what to cook.
Then make a rota, Riya. Each person plans and cooks one or two days a week. Keep a shared list on the fridge for things that run out. It reduces arguments and waste.
What if one of them eats a lot more?
Talk about it kindly and agree on a simple rule, like splitting the bill equally for staples and each paying for their own special items. A shared list helps everyone see what is used.
Remind me, what did I say about the vegetables?
You said you waste a lot of vegetables because they go bad in the fridge. Use the soft ones first, and make soup or pulao so you and your friends use up the leftovers.
Daniel is coming over for Christmas and he asked me to teach him a simple Indian dish.
A good first dish is jeera rice with a simple dal. Both are easy, need few ingredients, and are filling. Start with the dal, since it teaches tempering.
I am Chloe. How should I teach him? He cooks only pasta.
Show him each step once, then let him try. Start with chopping, then boiling the dal and finally the tempering. He will learn fast, as he already knows how to boil and season.
Which spices should I show him?
Show him turmeric, cumin, mustard seeds, red chilli powder and salt. Let Daniel smell each one. Five spices are enough for a first lesson.
What if he burns the tempering?
Burnt tempering is common, and it only takes a few seconds. Tell him to keep the flame low and add the cumin to hot, not smoking, oil. If it burns, start again, since it can taste bitter.
Which dish was he going to learn?
Daniel will learn dal and jeera rice, his first Indian dish. Chloe, start with the dal and tempering, then add the rice when he feels confident.
My son Ben asked how milk becomes curd. I did not know how to answer.
Milk has tiny helpful bacteria in curd. When you add a spoon of old curd to warm milk, those bacteria grow and turn the milk sugar into a sour taste, and the milk thickens into curd.
He is eight. Can I say it more simply?
Say that a spoon of curd has tiny living helpers. Put them in warm milk and they work all night, making it thick and sour. In the morning, the milk has become curd.
He wants to try it. How warm should the milk be?
The milk should be warm, like bath water, not hot. If you can keep a finger in it for a few seconds, it is right. Too hot will kill the helpers.
Where do we keep it overnight?
Keep the bowl covered in a warm, quiet place, like a shelf or inside a closed cupboard. In winter, wrap it in a cloth. Ben will see the curd set in six to eight hours.
What is my son's name, so I can say it to him when he sees it?
Your son's name is Ben. You can say, 'Ben, look, the tiny helpers made curd for us!' when you open the bowl in the morning.
I have a mango and some milk. Any quick dessert?
Make a mango milkshake: blend the mango, cold milk and a little sugar. Or chop the mango, mix with chilled cream and serve as mango fool. Both take five minutes.
I prefer something I can eat with a spoon. My name is Yusuf.
Then make mango fool, Yusuf. Whip some cream or thick curd with a spoon of sugar, fold in mashed mango, and chill. Serve it in small glasses with a few mango pieces on top.
I have no cream. Only milk and a bit of curd.
Hang the curd in a cloth for an hour to make it thick, then mix with sugar and mango. It will taste like a light mango yoghurt. A little cardamom adds a nice smell.
What if I do not have an hour?
Then mix the curd with milk powder if you have it, or just use plain thick curd as it is. Add the mango and sugar, and stir. It will be a bit lighter, but still good.
What fruit did I say I had?
You said you have a mango. Use it with the curd and a spoon of sugar, Yusuf, and your quick dessert will be ready in minutes.
The people downstairs complained about the smell of my cooking. I feel awful.
I am sorry, that is an upsetting thing to hear. Smells travel in flats, and most people do not mean to be rude. A friendly talk can often fix it.
I cook with lots of fish and garlic. My name is Pooja.
Strong smells can bother some neighbours. Try cooking with the window open, using the exhaust fan and keeping the door closed. Covering pots with a lid also helps keep smells in.
Should I apologise to them?
A friendly word is enough. You could say, 'Sorry if my cooking smelled strong, I will keep the window open and use the fan.' Pooja, that shows you care, and most people soften after that.
What if they still complain?
Offer to share a dish with them. People often feel better when they taste the food. If the problem continues, a simple chat with the building committee can help find a fair way to handle it.
What did they complain about again?
They complained about the smell of your cooking, especially the fish and garlic. Pooja, keep the fan on and the lids closed, and talk kindly with them.
Which snacks should I pack for my daughter's school trip? She is ten.
For a school trip, pack light, dry food that does not spoil: sandwiches, biscuits, cut fruit, a small box of nuts, and a bottle of water. Avoid anything that melts or leaks.
Her name is Riya. She likes cheese.
Then make a cheese sandwich for Riya, and add a few cheese cubes. Keep them in a small box with a cold pack, since cheese does not like heat for many hours.
It is a long trip. They leave at six and come back at six.
For twelve hours, send two small meals and a few snacks. A roti roll for lunch, a fruit and some nuts for the afternoon, and biscuits for the bus. Add extra water.
Should I send sweets?
A small sweet is fine, like a laddoo or a few dates. Skip chocolate because it melts. Riya will enjoy it as a treat on the bus on the way back.
What did I say she likes?
You said Riya likes cheese. So the cheese sandwich and cheese cubes are a good pick for her long trip.
Dinner with my boss at a restaurant is coming up and I am nervous about ordering.
Choose food that is easy to eat and not too messy, such as rice with dal or a simple curry, not very spicy dishes. Avoid anything you have to eat with your hands unless others do so too.
I am Arjun and I am vegetarian. My boss eats everything.
Then check the vegetarian section and order something familiar, like paneer curry with naan, or a vegetable biryani. You do not need to explain more. A polite, calm order is enough.
What if he orders for the table?
If your boss orders, you can say 'I am vegetarian, so I will skip the meat, thank you.' Most people understand. Arjun, there is no need to feel awkward about it.
What do I talk about while eating?
Ask about his work, his weekend or favourite food, and listen. Avoid heavy topics like office problems. People enjoy talking about themselves, and a light chat will make the meal easier.
What did I say about my food?
You said you are vegetarian, and your boss eats everything. Arjun, order a vegetarian dish, such as paneer curry or a vegetable biryani, and enjoy the meal.
There is a lot of leftover dal and rice from yesterday. What can I make?
Mix them to make khichdi, or make dal paratha: knead the dal into wheat dough with a little salt and cook like paratha. You can also fry the rice with onion and a little of the dal.
I like the paratha idea. How much dal in the dough?
Use about half a cup of thick dal for two cups of flour, and add water only if needed. The dough should be soft but not sticky. Add cumin and chopped coriander for flavour.
My brother Manav does not like dal. Will he notice?
He may not, because the dal blends into the dough and the paratha tastes like a spiced roti. Serve it with curd and pickle. Manav will probably just enjoy it.
And for the leftover rice?
Make a quick fried rice with onion, capsicum and a spoon of soy sauce, or a curd rice for the evening. Cold rice fries better than fresh rice.
Which of the two ideas was for my brother?
The dal paratha was the idea for Manav. He may not notice the dal in the dough, and the paratha with curd and pickle is a nice way to use it.
I want to give homemade sweets as a gift. What stays fresh and looks good?
Barfi cut into diamonds, laddoos in paper cups and coconut sweets all look neat and keep for a few days. Pack them in a clean box with parchment paper between layers.
Which one is the easiest? I am a beginner. My name is Chloe.
Coconut barfi is easy, Chloe. Cook desiccated coconut with milk and sugar until it thickens, add cardamom, set it in a greased plate and cut it into squares when cool.
How long does it take to set?
It sets in about an hour at room temperature, or thirty minutes in the fridge. Cut it when it is firm but not fully hard, so the edges stay clean.
Can I colour it?
Yes, add a drop of food colour to half the mixture for two layers, pink and white. Spread the first layer, let it cool slightly, then add the second. It will look lovely in the box.
What was the sweet I was going to make?
You are going to make coconut barfi, Chloe. It is easy for a beginner, and cutting it in squares and packing it neatly will make it a good gift.
I live in a hostel and can only use an electric kettle. Can I make real food?

Yes, a kettle can do more than tea. You can make instant oats, soaked poha, instant noodles and even soup, all with poured hot water. Keep the kettle clean and use only water for it, as the rules usually say.
I am Manav and I get hungry at night. What is the fastest thing?
Poha is the fastest. Wash a cup of thick poha, pour hot water from the kettle on it for two minutes, drain, then add salt, lemon, peanuts and chopped onion. It needs no flame at all.
I do not have peanuts. I have biscuits and bananas.
Then have a banana smashed with a few crushed biscuits and a little milk or curd. It is filling and sweet. Manav, keep a pack of roasted chana too, for the nights you want something salty.
Actually, I changed my mind. I will make the poha tonight and the banana thing tomorrow.
Good plan, Manav. Tonight, soak the poha with hot water, add salt and lemon, and enjoy it warm. Keep the bananas and biscuits aside for tomorrow, when you want something sweet.
It is raining. I want a hot soup. What can I make in ten minutes?

Try a quick sweet corn soup. Boil corn kernels with water, a pinch of pepper and salt, thicken with a spoon of cornflour mixed in cold water, and simmer for a few minutes. Add a beaten egg if you like.
I do not have corn. I have carrots and peas.
Then make a mixed vegetable soup. Chop the carrots small, boil with the peas and a little ginger, then mash a few pieces to thicken. Season with salt and pepper.
I have bread too. My name is Ben. Could I put bread in it?
Yes, Ben, toast the bread and cut it into small squares, then drop the croutons into the hot soup just before eating. They give crunch and make the soup a full meal.
Okay. How about a spice?
A little cumin powder and black pepper are nice in vegetable soup. You can also add a squeeze of lemon at the end. Ben's carrot and pea soup will feel warm and sharp on a rainy day.
What vegetables am I using?
You are using carrots and peas, with a little ginger, and toasted bread squares on top. That makes a warm bowl for the rain, Ben.
How do I boil an egg so the yolk is soft but not runny?
Place the egg in boiling water and cook for about seven minutes, then put it in cold water right away. The white will be set and the yolk soft and creamy. Peel it under water.
Mine always crack when they go in the water.
Lower the egg gently with a spoon instead of dropping it. You can also start with a room temperature egg. A tiny pinch of salt in the water can help if one does crack.
What if I want a hard boiled egg for my sister Kavya's tiffin?
For Kavya's tiffin, cook it for ten to twelve minutes, then cool it in cold water. A firm yolk is better for the tiffin, because a soft one can spill. Pack it in a small box.
Should I peel it in the morning or at night?
Peel it in the morning, just before packing, or leave the shell on until she eats. An egg in its shell stays fresher. If you peel the night before, keep it in a closed box in the fridge.
Which sister did I say it is for?
It is for your sister Kavya. Cook the egg ten to twelve minutes and keep the shell on until the morning, then pack it in a small box for her tiffin.
I am thinking of starting a small home bakery. Where should I begin?
Begin with two or three things you bake well, like cookies, brownies and a simple cake. Test them on friends and family first. Ask what they like and how much they would pay for it.
My cakes are good. My name is Sofia. How do I tell people?
Start by telling friends, neighbours and relatives, and share photos of your cakes. Orders often start through word of mouth. Add your name and phone number on the boxes.
I do not know about rules for selling food at home.

Rules differ from place to place, so check with your local food authority about a licence and hygiene rules before you sell. Sofia, your local municipal office can tell you where to ask. I cannot give legal advice.
Okay. In the meantime, what can I do?
Keep baking, keep notes about costs and timing, and take good photos. Ask friends to try your cakes and give honest comments. This builds your skill while you check the rules.
I want to understand what Christmas dinner is like in a Christian family in Kerala.
Many Kerala Christian families eat appam with stew, chicken or duck roast, beef fry, fish curry and rice. There is plum cake and wine cake for dessert. Dishes differ from family to family.
Chloe is my friend and she says her mother makes appam. What is that?
Appam is a soft, bowl-shaped pancake made from rice batter and coconut milk, with a thin crisp edge and a fluffy middle. It is eaten with vegetable or meat stew.
What goes into the stew?
A mild coconut milk stew with potatoes, carrots, onions, green chillies, ginger and whole spices like cinnamon and cloves. It is not spicy, and the soft appam soaks it up well.
I would like to try making it. Is the batter hard?

It needs fermenting, like dosa batter, but it is not hard. You grind soaked rice with cooked rice and coconut, add yeast or toddy and leave overnight. Ask Chloe's mother for her recipe, as families have their own.
Whose mother makes the appam?
Chloe's mother makes the appam. Since you would like to try, ask Chloe to share her mother's recipe, because that will be the best one to start with.
Why does my dosa stick to the tawa?
Usually the tawa is not hot enough, or not seasoned. Heat it well, wipe with a halved onion dipped in oil, and sprinkle a little water. When the water sizzles and dries, it is ready for batter.
I use a non-stick one.
Then it may be too hot or the coating is worn. Keep medium heat, and use only a little oil. If the coating is scratched, dosa may stick, and it might be time for a new pan.
My brother Yusuf says use cast iron instead.

Cast iron makes crisp dosas when properly seasoned. It takes practice and needs oil, but lasts for years. Yusuf's advice is right if you like crisp edges, and you can keep the non-stick pan for omelettes.
Okay. Should I try the cast iron then?
Try it if you enjoy the process. Season it with oil, heat it well and wipe with onion. Make the first dosa as a test, because the first one is always the trial.
Which pan did I say I use now?
You use a non-stick tawa now. Yusuf suggested cast iron, which gives crisp dosas but needs seasoning. Keep the non-stick one if it works for your omelettes.
My plan for tonight was paneer curry, but I just found out my guest, Pooja, does not eat paneer.
No problem, there are lots of other choices. You could make a mixed vegetable curry, chickpea curry or a mushroom masala using the same gravy. The sauce will still be good.
I have mushrooms. Is it too late to change?
Not at all. Use the same onion tomato gravy, and add the mushrooms instead of paneer. Mushrooms cook in ten minutes, so it will be ready on time. Do not wash them for long, just wipe them.
Does Pooja eat mushrooms? I did not ask.
A quick message will tell you. Many people are fine with mushrooms, but some dislike the texture. If she says no, make chickpea or mixed vegetable curry instead.
