She said yes, mushrooms are fine! Anything else I should change?

Check that the rice and rotis are plain, and that no paneer is left on the serving spoon. Since Pooja does not eat paneer, keep the dessert free of it too. Mushroom masala with rice will make a good dinner.
We have two guests, one is a child. I do not know what to serve for the child.
Offer plain foods children usually accept: rice and dal, a small roti with butter, or a simple pasta. Add fruit and a glass of milk or juice. Avoid very spicy food.
The child is Riya, she is six and shy.
Then do not make a fuss over her. Give Riya a small plate with a few simple items and let her eat slowly. A shy child feels better with a familiar food and a quiet seat.
What can I do to make her feel comfortable?
Give her a small job, like putting napkins on the table, or show her a toy or a book. Children relax when they have something to do. Do not force her to speak.
Good. What was the girl's name?
Her name is Riya, and she is six and shy. Offer her simple food and a small job, and she will relax.
My mother asked me to buy vegetables for the week. I have never done it.

Start with basics: onions, potatoes, tomatoes, and a few green vegetables like beans, spinach and gourds. Choose firm, bright vegetables and avoid ones with soft spots. Ask the seller for a fair price.
Her list says lauki, bhindi and capsicum. I am Arjun.
Arjun, pick lauki that is firm and light green with smooth skin. For bhindi, choose small ones that snap easily when bent. Capsicum should be shiny and firm with no wrinkles.
How much of each should I buy?
For a small family, about half a kilo of each is usually enough for a few meals. Ask your mother how many people are eating. If vegetables are cheap, you can buy a little more.
The seller gave me a very high price for the bhindi.
Ask at one or two other stalls before buying. Prices differ, and it is fine to say politely that you will check elsewhere. Your mother will be happy that you were careful with her money, Arjun.
Is it okay if the tiffin I send for my husband is the same two items every day?
It is fine if he likes them, but variety helps. You do not need to change everything. Change the vegetable, the filling in the roti or add a different side, and it will feel new.
He likes roti and aloo. His name is Manav.
Then rotate the aloo dish: jeera aloo one day, aloo gobi, dum aloo, and aloo in tomato gravy. Manav will get his favourite food in many styles.
What about the roti? Can I vary that?
Yes, make plain roti, methi paratha, paneer paratha or missi roti on other days. Mix a spoon of besan or chopped greens into the dough for variety.
Which one should I try first?
Try methi paratha first, because it goes well with jeera aloo and keeps soft for hours. Manav will notice the new smell, and the potato he likes will still be there.
And what did you say about his favourite?
Manav likes roti and aloo, so you keep those and only change the style of the aloo dish and the type of roti. That way he gets variety without losing his favourite.
My daughter Sofia gets a certificate at school on Friday. How should we celebrate at home?
A small family dinner of her favourite dish is lovely. Add a small cake or sweet and tell her you are proud. Keep it simple, so the focus stays on her.
She loves noodles and chocolate.
Then make vegetable noodles for dinner and a simple chocolate pudding or brownie for dessert. Let Sofia help to stir or decorate, which makes the evening more special.
Her grandmother Lakshmi wants to come too.
Then invite Lakshmi for dinner, and ask her to bring a small gift or a blessing. Seeing her grandmother there will make Sofia feel even more proud.
Can we make the pudding the night before?
Yes, chocolate pudding sets well in the fridge overnight. Make it on Thursday evening, cover it, and take it out half an hour before dessert. That leaves Friday for noodles and welcoming Lakshmi.
I always feel I cook too slowly. How do I speed up?
Prepare before you start: chop all the vegetables, measure spices and keep everything near the stove. Cooking is much faster once the work before it is done. Cook two things at once on two burners.
I am Kavya. I take an hour just to cut onions and tomatoes.
That sounds slow, so a sharper knife may help, and a proper chopping board. Practise a steady rhythm, not speed. You can also chop vegetables for two days at once and store them.
Is that safe? Will they stay fresh?
Chopped onions and tomatoes keep for a day in the fridge in a closed box. For two days, chop only the onions. Kavya, add the tomato fresh, or use a puree.
Okay. What do I do first tomorrow?
Start by sharpening your knife or checking that it is sharp, then chop the onions for two days. Tomorrow's cooking will go faster, and you can compare the time you save.
We are having a family lunch and my uncle Raju only eats plain boiled food. Everyone else wants spicy.
You can cook both without much extra work. Make the main dish spicy, but keep a small portion aside before adding spices. Cook it plain with a little salt for Raju.
What about the rice and dal?
Dal and rice can stay plain for everyone, and the spicy tempering and pickle can be added at the table. That way each person decides how much spice to add.
That helps. Is there something I can add to Raju's plate to make it more tasty?
A little ghee and a squeeze of lemon will make plain boiled vegetables and rice taste nicer. A spoon of curd on the side also adds flavour, without chilli.
Okay, so I keep a plain portion for him?
Yes, keep a small plain portion for Raju before adding spice. Add ghee and lemon for taste, and let the others add pickle and chilli at the table.
I am taking the night train to Jaipur on Friday with my cousin Neha. Any tips?
That sounds like a fun trip. Carry a light shawl because train coaches get cold at night, and keep your phone charged before you board. Do you have a lower berth or an upper one?
Upper berth, and I am a bit worried about climbing up. Also Neha snores.
The upper berth is fine once you learn the trick: use the little ladder, put your bag at the foot end, and climb slowly. For the snoring, earplugs are cheap and work well. Pack a pair for yourself.
Good idea. What should I eat on the train?

Take simple food that does not spill, like parathas, dry fruit and a few bananas. Buy tea from the vendor instead of carrying a flask. Wash your hands before eating, since you will be touching rails and doors.
Okay. Remind me, who snores again and what do I need to buy for it?
Neha is the one who snores, and you wanted earplugs for it. Buy two pairs so you have a spare, and keep them in the pocket of your bag where you can reach them in the dark.
My grandmother lives in Pune and I visit her next weekend. I want to take her something nice.
That is a kind thought. Something she can use every day is often best, like a soft shawl, a good tea, or a framed photo of the family. What does she enjoy doing most?
She loves gardening and her tulsi plant is her pride. Her name is Kamala Aaji.
Then a nice pair of gardening gloves or a small copper watering can would suit Kamala Aaji very well. You could also bring a pot with a new herb for her to grow beside the tulsi.
I like the watering can. Can I get one that is not too heavy for her?

Yes, look for a small one that holds about one litre, with a long thin spout. Full, it will still be light enough for Kamala Aaji to lift with one hand, so she can water her tulsi without bending much.
I missed my bus to college this morning and I am so annoyed.
I am sorry, that is a rough start to the day. Is there another bus soon, or will you need a different way to get there? Try not to rush too much, since that is when people trip.
Another bus comes in 20 minutes. But my first class has a quiz and Mr. Verma is strict.

Then wait for the next bus and send Mr. Verma a short, polite message now saying you missed your bus and will be a little late. Teachers usually respect honesty, and you can ask if you may still take the quiz.
I sent it. He said I can take it after class.
That is a good result. Sit calmly on the bus and look over your notes instead of worrying. Next time, leave ten minutes earlier, and you can avoid this whole problem.
Yes. By the way, what was the name of my teacher again? I want to thank him.
His name is Mr. Verma, the one with the quiz. A simple thank you after class is enough, something like, Thank you for letting me take the quiz later, sir.
Packing for a three day trip to Goa with friends. I always overpack. Help!

Start with a rule: one bag only. Lay out three outfits, one light jacket for evenings, swimwear, sandals and a toiletry pouch. If something does not fit that list, leave it behind. Does the trip include any special plan?
A beach day, a fort visit, and a dinner at a fancy place.
Then add one nicer outfit for the dinner and a hat for the fort, since it will be sunny. Wear your heaviest shoes on the travel day instead of packing them, so they do not take space in the bag.
My friend Farhan wants me to carry his sunscreen too.
That is fine, it is small. Put it in a zip bag so it cannot leak onto your clothes, and keep it near the top so you can reach it at the beach.
Wait, which friend wanted me to carry what? I forgot already.
Farhan asked you to carry his sunscreen. Pack it in the zip bag at the top of your luggage, and you can hand it to him when you reach the beach.
I got lost in the old part of the city today. All the lanes look the same.
That happens to almost everyone in an old city. Stay calm and stand somewhere safe, like near a shop. Do you know the name of a landmark nearby, such as a temple or a market?
There is a big sweet shop called Ganesh Sweets on the corner.

Good, that is easy to use. Ask the shopkeeper for directions to your destination, and ask him to repeat it slowly. Shopkeepers in a lane know it better than any map, so he can probably point you right.
He told me to take a left, then a right at the temple. It worked!
Well done. Next time, note one or two landmarks as you walk in, so finding your way back is easier. Even a photo of a shop sign will help.
Yes. What was the shop that helped me called?
It was Ganesh Sweets, on the corner. You could even buy a few laddoos there next time as a thank you for the directions.
Any ideas for a quiet weekend? I am tired from exam week.
You earned a calm weekend. Sleep late, cook something simple, take a slow walk and read something that is not a textbook. What kind of things help you relax?
Music and long walks. Also my sister Mia is visiting on Sunday.
That works nicely. You can do your long walk on Saturday with music, and keep Sunday for Mia. Maybe make her favourite snack, so the day feels like a treat for both of you.
She loves paneer sandwiches. I can make those.
Perfect. Toast the bread on a pan with a little butter, and add mint chutney inside. They are quick, so you will not feel tired after cooking.
Great. And which day did I say she is coming?
You said Mia is visiting on Sunday. So Saturday is your quiet day for the walk, and Sunday is for the paneer sandwiches and time with her.
We planned a picnic on Saturday but the forecast says rain. Should we cancel?
Not yet. Rain forecasts often change, and you can plan for both. Is the picnic outdoors in a park, or could it move to someone's house or a covered spot?
A park near the lake. Eight of us are going, organised by Rahul.
Then ask Rahul to check the morning of the picnic. If it is only a drizzle, take a big tarp and umbrellas. If it is heavy rain, move to someone's home and eat there instead.
Rahul says Tara's house has a big balcony. We can go there.
That is a great backup. The balcony keeps you dry and the food can be shared easily. Tell everyone the new place early so no one goes to the lake by mistake.
Okay. Who was organising the original picnic again?
Rahul is organising it. Since the plan has changed to Tara's balcony, he is the best person to send the new address to the group.
My first solo trip is next month, to Udaipur. I am nervous.

Nerves are normal, and a first solo trip is a big step. Udaipur is a gentle city for visitors. Plan your stay first, then a few things to see each day, and tell a family member your schedule. How long will you stay?
Four days. I booked a small guesthouse near the lake run by a man called Mr. Sethi.
Good, small guesthouses are often helpful. Ask Mr. Sethi for his favourite sights and where to eat safely. Locals give the best tips, and he can also call you a trusted auto when you need one.
Nice. Should I plan every hour?

No, it is better to plan only the main thing each day, like the palace on day one and a boat ride on day two. Leave free time for walking and resting, because solo trips are more fun with some surprises.
What was the guesthouse owner's name again? I want to message him.
His name is Mr. Sethi. In your message, say your arrival date, how long you plan to stay, and ask if he can arrange a pickup from the station.
We are going camping this weekend, my first time. Where do I start?
Camping is a great adventure. Start with a simple list: tent, sleeping bag, torch, water, food and a small first aid kit. Who is going with you, and where is the campsite?
My cousins Rahul and Mia, and the site is near a lake outside Pune.
Then plan to arrive before dark, so you can pitch the tent while there is light. Choose flat ground away from the water edge. Rahul and Mia can help hold the poles and tie the ropes.
We are cooking on a small stove. What should we make?
Something easy and warm, like khichdi or noodles, with chai. Keep the food simple and wash up properly afterwards. Store leftovers in a sealed box, so animals are not drawn to the tent.
Rahul says we should carry a guitar. Is that too much?
If someone can carry it safely, a guitar is lovely around a fire. Pack it in a soft case and keep it away from damp ground. It might be the best part of the night.
Okay. One more thing: who is going with me, and where?
Your cousins Rahul and Mia are going with you, to a campsite near a lake outside Pune. Share the packing list with them so each of you carries a part.
Nani is coming from Hyderabad tomorrow and I want her to feel welcome.
What a sweet thought. A clean room, fresh sheets and her favourite foods will help. Does she have any special needs, like a firm bed or a quiet place?
She likes a firm mattress and she gets cold at night. She also loves mogra flowers.
Then put a thin mattress or folded blanket under her sheet to make the bed firmer, and keep an extra blanket nearby. A few mogra flowers in a small glass beside her bed would be a lovely touch.
I can get the flowers from the market. What about food?
Ask your mother what Nani eats and what she misses. Many grandparents enjoy home cooked food and light dinners. A cup of warm milk or tea at bedtime may help her sleep after the journey.
Mom says she likes sabudana khichdi. I will help make it.
That is a fine welcome meal. Soak the sabudana overnight and cook it with peanuts and potatoes in the morning, so it is fresh when she arrives. She will be delighted that you helped.
What did I say she likes besides food?
You said Nani loves mogra flowers. Buy a few from the market tomorrow morning and put them in a glass beside her bed, along with the extra blanket for cold nights.
Is it okay to eat strong smelling food on a train? My mom packed fish curry for me.
Strong smells can bother others in a closed coach, so it is kinder to avoid it. Is there somewhere else you can eat, like the corridor at a quiet time, or can you save it?
The trip is ten hours and I do not have anything else. My cousin Sana travels with me.
Then eat it at a time when fewer people are around, and keep the container tightly closed. Wash your hands and throw the waste in the bin. You and Sana could also buy a simple snack at a station.
Sana says we should eat when the train stops at a big station.
That is a good plan. You can step down on the platform and eat quickly, away from the coach, before the train leaves. Do not wander far from the door, and keep your eye on the clock.
Good. But what if the train starts early?
Keep your container sealed and hop back on at once if you hear the horn or a whistle. Sana can watch the train while you finish. If it is too tight, eat only half and save the rest for later.
Okay. Who is travelling with me, and what are we eating?
Your cousin Sana is travelling with you, and the food is the fish curry your mother packed. Eat it at the big station stop, and wash your hands before you board again.
I have exams, a cousin's wedding, and a trip all in the same month. How do I manage?
A calendar will help. Write each date down and see where they overlap. Then decide what cannot move. Which dates are fixed?
The exams are on the 5th to the 12th. The wedding is on the 20th. The trip is flexible.
Then study hard until the 12th and avoid other plans. After the exams, you can enjoy the wedding on the 20th. Postpone the trip to the end of the month or the next month, since it is flexible.
My friend Tara wants to go on the trip right after exams, on the 14th.
That could work, because you will be free and relaxed after the exams. You need to be back in time for the wedding, so a three or four day trip, returning by the 18th, is possible.
What if I get tired from exams and the trip?
Then keep the trip short and calm, with plenty of rest. Tell Tara that you want a slow trip, not a busy one. You can also rest in the days before the wedding to recover.
Okay. When did I say my exams end, and what is on the 20th?
Your exams end on the 12th, and the wedding is on the 20th. If Tara goes on the 14th, you will have time to enjoy a short trip and still be back well before the wedding.
I want to start taking the bus to college instead of my parents driving me. How do I plan it?
A good step towards independence. First find the route and the time the bus takes. Where is your college and where do you live?
I live in Dwarka and my college is in Rohini. The college starts at nine.
Then check the bus numbers that go from Dwarka to Rohini, and the first bus of the morning. It may need a change. Try the journey once on a weekend to see how long it takes.
I tried it on Sunday. It took ninety minutes with one change.
That is long, but doable. Leave home two hours before nine so a delay will not make you late. Carry a book or music to make the ride pleasant.
Can I use a pass to save money?
Many bus services offer student passes. Ask at the bus depot or your college office, and carry your college ID. Check the rules directly, since I do not know the current details for your city.
Okay. What was the plan about leaving time again, and which two areas?
You live in Dwarka and your college is in Rohini. Leave home two hours before the nine o'clock start, so the ninety minute ride and the change have a little extra time.
Packing a bag for my first night at a friend's house. What do I bring?
Bring a change of clothes, your toothbrush, your nightwear, a towel if needed, and your phone charger. A small gift for her family is a nice thought too. Whose house is it?
Emma's. Her parents are very welcoming. This is my first sleepover.
A first sleepover is exciting. Pack a small bag, and add a book or a favourite pillow if you cannot sleep without it. Tell your parents the address and Emma's mother's phone number.
What if I feel homesick at night?
That is quite normal. Keep your phone nearby so you can message home, and tell Emma if you feel sad. Many people feel better after a few quiet minutes, and lights out chat helps too.
Should I take sweets for Emma's parents?
Yes, a small box of sweets or fruit shows thanks. Hand it over politely when you arrive, and say thank you to her parents again in the morning for having you.
I will do that. Can you remind me whose house it is and what I am giving?
It is Emma's house, and you are giving a small box of sweets to her parents. Say thank you when you arrive and again in the morning.
I lost my way to my friend's new flat. All the buildings look the same.
Housing colonies can be confusing. Stop and call her, or ask the security guard at the gate. Do you remember the name of the building or the block number?
Block C, third floor. Her name is Olivia, and her building has a green gate.
Then tell the guard that you are looking for Block C, the one with the green gate. Block letters are usually painted on the wall. Once you find it, take the lift to the third floor.
I found Block C but there are two lifts and I do not know which one works.
Try the one with a light on the panel, or take the stairs if it is only three floors. When you reach the third floor, look for Olivia's door number, which she should have told you.
She did, it is 304. Can you put the whole address together for me so I can save it?
Sure. Olivia's flat is number 304, on the third floor of Block C, the building with the green gate. Save that in a note on your phone, so next time you can show it to the guard straight away.
We are planning a family holiday to Kerala and everyone wants something different.
That is common with families. Make a list of what each person wants and see what fits. Who wants what?
Dad wants backwaters, Mom wants temples, my brother wants a beach, and I want to see elephants.

Kerala can offer all four. Many places have backwaters and temples close together, and there are beaches near Kovalam. Some sanctuaries and temple festivals have elephants. Try a route that moves from one to the next.
That sounds perfect! Can we do it in a week?
Yes, a week is enough if you plan by days. Spend two days on backwaters, one on temples, two near a beach and two in an area known for elephants. Do not pack too much into one day.
Dad says he will book the houseboat first. Is that wise?
Yes, that is wise. Houseboats get booked early in the holiday season, and the backwaters were the one thing your dad asked for, so fixing his part first will make him happy.
Would a taxi driver mind if I asked him to turn down the music?
No, it is fine if you ask politely. Say, Excuse me, could you lower the volume a little? Most drivers are happy to oblige. Is it too loud for you?
Yes, I have a headache. We are going from the airport to my hotel.
Then tell him your head hurts, and ask him politely. It also helps to say thank you afterwards. If he does not want to, you can put on earphones or close your eyes.
He turned it down. Now he is chatting and is quite friendly.
That is nice. Drivers know the city well, so you can ask him about places to eat or see. Keep the chat polite, and do not share private details like your room number.
We are almost at the hotel. What should I say to him at the end, given how the ride started?
Thank him for turning the music down when you mentioned your headache, and for being good company after that. You can also thank him for the tip about the restaurant by the sea.
My seat on the train is next to a window that will not close and it is raining.
That sounds uncomfortable. Tell the coach attendant or the ticket checker, and ask to change seats if there is a free one. Do you have any waterproof cover with you?
Only a jacket. The attendant says there is a free seat in the next coach.
Then move there and take your bags with you. Shake the rain off your jacket on the way. A dry seat will make the rest of the journey far more pleasant.
Done. But now the new seat is by a family with a crying baby.
Babies cry when they are tired or uncomfortable, and the parents are likely worried too. A smile or a kind word can ease things. If you need quiet, wear earphones and rest.
I offered the mother some water and the baby stopped crying. Now the rain has stopped. Should I go back to my old seat?
No need. The window by your old seat would not close, so it may still be wet and cold. Your new seat is dry, and the mother and baby are calm now, so stay where you are.
My grandmother taught me to make chapati today. Mine looked like a map of India.
That is a very good start. Everyone's first chapatis have strange shapes. Did she say anything that helped you?
She said to press the dough ball flat with my palm first, and roll from the centre outwards.
That is exactly right. Rolling from the centre and turning the dough after each roll keeps it round. A light dusting of flour stops it from sticking. Keep practising and the shape will come.
She also told me to rest the dough for half an hour.
Yes, resting makes the dough soft, so it rolls easily and puffs well on the pan. Cover it with a damp cloth so it does not dry out.
I will make them again on Sunday with her. Which tip should I try first?
Try the one she gave first, pressing the ball flat with your palm and rolling from the centre outwards. Rest the dough for half an hour beforehand, and your Sunday chapatis should be rounder.
I think I am scared of buses now. One braked hard last week and I fell.
I am sorry you fell. It makes sense to feel nervous after that. Were you hurt, and are you all right now?
Just a bruise on my knee. But I flinch every time the bus stops.
That is a normal reaction, and it usually fades. Try standing near a pole or sitting near the front, and hold on firmly before the bus stops. Feeling prepared helps your body relax.
I think sitting is better. Maybe I will pick the seat behind the driver.
That is a good choice. The seat behind the driver is usually easy to reach and gives you a rail to hold. Over a few rides, the fear should get smaller, and you will trust yourself again.
Today I stood near the pole like you said and held on before the stop. It went well.
That is a good sign. Holding the pole before the stop is the habit that protects you from another fall, like the one that bruised your knee. Keep doing it and the flinching will fade.
We reached the hill station but it is foggy and we cannot see anything.
That can be disappointing, but fog is part of hill stations. Does the forecast say it will clear?
Our driver says it may clear by noon. My brother Farhan is grumpy about it.
Then take a warm breakfast and some tea first. Fog can look mysterious in photos, and a short walk nearby can be fun. By noon, you may get a clear view, so Farhan may feel better.
Good. Farhan wants to go to the viewpoint right now.
A viewpoint in thick fog will only show white, so it is better to wait until noon. You can tell Farhan to rest first and promise a visit when the driver says it is clear.
He agreed. What should we do until then?
Play cards, have a long breakfast, or explore a nearby shop or cafe. Farhan may enjoy a hot snack like pakoras, and by noon you will all be ready for the viewpoint.
I packed too much and my suitcase will not close. Help!
Take everything out and look again. Remove anything you can buy or borrow at your destination. Roll your clothes tightly instead of folding, as it saves space. What is taking the most room?
My shoes and a big jacket. I am going to Shimla for a week.
Wear the jacket and the heaviest shoes on the travel day. Pack only one extra pair of light shoes. In Shimla, the jacket will be useful anyway, so wearing it costs you nothing.
Good idea. I wore the jacket and now the suitcase closes!
That worked well. Before you leave, check the weight if you are flying, and keep your documents and charger in a small bag you can reach. Enjoy Shimla.
Since it will be cold in Shimla, should I keep anything else out of the suitcase, apart from the jacket I am wearing?

Keep a cap and gloves in the small bag with your documents and charger, so you can reach them when you step out in Shimla. Since you are already wearing the big jacket, the suitcase will still close easily.
My friend Sana asked me to join her for a pottery class on Sunday. I have never tried it.
That sounds like a fun first. Pottery is calm and a little messy. What made Sana choose it?
She says it helps her relax after the week. I am nervous that I will be bad at it.
Nobody expects a first pot to be perfect. The teacher will show you step by step, and most people laugh at their first attempts. Wear old clothes and short nails, since clay gets everywhere.
Okay, I will go. Should I bring anything?
Usually the studio gives you everything, but check with Sana. Bring a towel and a bag for dirty clothes. You might also wear an apron if you have one.
I will tell Sana yes. What did you say about my first pot?
You do not have to make it perfect. Nobody does on a first try, so go with Sana, enjoy the clay, and laugh at the lopsided parts.
Our family got separated at the temple during the festival. It is so crowded.
Try to stay calm and avoid pushing through the crowd. Move to the side near a wall or a stall. Do you have a phone with you, and do you know where the others were heading?
My phone has no signal. We were heading to the main hall. My sister Tara has the same problem.
Then stay near the main hall's entrance and wait for her. People who are separated usually go to the place they planned to go. Ask a volunteer or police officer to help with an announcement.
I asked a volunteer. He said to wait by the flag post.
Good. Stay by the flag post and keep your eyes open. Tara may also ask a volunteer, and they may bring her to you. Do not walk about looking for her.
Tara just came! She was at the main hall entrance for half an hour.
I am glad you found each other. For the next festival, fix a meeting spot first, like the flag post, so Tara and your family will always know where to go if you get separated.
I invited ten people to my birthday but only four said yes. I feel sad.
That can hurt, and it is okay to feel sad. People are often busy and may not mean anything by it. Who said yes?
My close friends Neha, Jack, Farhan and Mia. The others have other plans.
Then you will have a small, warm party with people who care about you. Four friends can have a lot of fun together, with more time to chat. Plan something simple like a game and cake.
True. Maybe we can go bowling and then eat pizza.
That sounds fun, and bowling works well for a group of five. Check if the place needs advance booking, and tell Neha, Jack, Farhan and Mia the time so they can plan.
I will book a lane. How many people should I book for?
Book for five, since it is you plus Neha, Jack, Farhan and Mia. If one of the others changes their mind later, the alley can usually add one more person.
We always go to the same beach every holiday. I want to propose a change.
A fresh place can be exciting. What are you thinking of, and how will your family feel about it?
Maybe a jungle resort. My dad loves the beach, though, and my sister Olivia too.
Then you could suggest a trade: the jungle this year and the beach next year. Explain what you like about the jungle, like animals and bird watching, so your family sees why it is fun.
I think Olivia might like the animals. She loves birds.
Then tell her first, and let her help you persuade your dad. A jungle resort will give Olivia a lot to see. Once she agrees, your dad is more likely to give it a chance.
Good plan. What should I say to her tonight, given what I told you she loves?
Good. Tell Olivia about the birds you might see, and ask her to speak to your dad with you. If she is excited, the jungle trip has a much better chance.
I booked a hotel online but now I see the photos do not match the real place.
That is disappointing. Look at the booking details and the cancellation rules first. Did you pay in advance?
Yes, I paid, but the booking says free cancellation until tonight.
Then you can cancel before the deadline and book somewhere else. Take screenshots of the booking and the cancellation message. Read reviews of the new place carefully before you pay.
I cancelled and found another hotel with good reviews.
Good move. When you reach the new hotel, check the room before you unpack. If anything is wrong, tell the reception right away, so they can fix it or give you another room.
For the new hotel, what should I check first when I reach there?

Check that the room is clean, the door locks properly and the bathroom works. Compare it with the photos you saw online, since the first hotel did not match. Ask for another room at once if something is wrong.
I am going to visit my sister Neha at her hostel. She asked me to bring some homemade food.
That is a caring gesture. Pick food that stays fresh on a long journey, such as dry snacks, ladoos or theplas. How long is the trip?
Six hours by train. She loves her mother's besan ladoo.
Besan ladoos travel well and stay fresh for days. Pack them in a tight steel or plastic box, and put it in the middle of your bag so it does not get squashed.
Mom also wants to send pickle. Is that okay?
Yes, but double seal the jar with plastic wrap under the lid and put it inside another bag. A leak would be messy. Keep the ladoos and pickle apart from your clothes.
Okay. Will Neha be able to share with her friends?
Yes, hostel friends love homemade food. Pack a little extra of the besan ladoo so Neha can share some and still have enough for herself.
I got on a bus without a ticket by mistake because the conductor never came.
That can happen on a crowded bus. The best step is to be honest. Look for the conductor and tell him you have not bought a ticket yet. Is the bus still moving?
Yes. I got off already but I feel guilty about the fare.
It is good that you feel that way. If you take the same route again, tell the conductor straight away and pay. You can also pay a little extra next time, if it makes you feel better.
I will pay tomorrow. The same bus passes at eight.
Then board the eight o'clock bus and say, Yesterday I could not buy a ticket, so I will pay now. The conductor will probably appreciate your honesty and not make a fuss.
I paid today and the conductor smiled. Should I tell my friend about it?
You can, if you like. Telling your friend about paying the fare from yesterday's ride shows how honesty feels. It might also remind your friend to check for the conductor on busy buses.
I sat next to a lovely old couple on the flight today. They told me about their travels.
That sounds like a nice surprise, and a good way to pass a flight. Where had they travelled in all those years?
They have visited forty countries. The lady, Mrs. Dsouza, said her favourite was Japan.
Forty countries is amazing. Did Mrs. Dsouza say why she loved Japan most? People who travel a lot often have good reasons.
She said the people were polite and the food was fresh, and the trains were always on time.
That is a lovely summary. If you ever go to Japan, you will have Mrs. Dsouza's story to remember. It might be worth writing down what she said in your travel notes.
I want to visit Japan someday because of what she said. What should I do first?

Start by learning a few Japanese phrases and reading about the things Mrs. Dsouza loved, like the polite people, the fresh food and the trains that always ran on time. Having a goal and a rough date makes a dream easier to reach.
My mother says I should pack a small sewing kit for the hostel. Is it needed?
It is very useful. A small kit with a needle, thread in a few colours and some safety pins will save you when a button comes off. Do you know how to sew a button?
No, not really. My roommate may know.
Then ask her to show you, or watch a short video before you go. Sewing a button takes only a few minutes to learn. Keep the kit in your drawer so you can find it fast.
I will practise on an old shirt. Mom says Aunt Sana taught her this way.
That is a good way. Using an old shirt means you can make mistakes without worry. Aunt Sana's method sounds sensible, and soon you will fix buttons quickly.
Which colours of thread should I take? And who did Mom say taught her to sew this way?

Aunt Sana taught your mother this way, by practising on an old shirt. For thread, take black, white, navy and one bright colour like red, since these match most clothes. Keep a few spare buttons in the kit too.
I am babysitting my cousin Aryan this weekend. He is four and very energetic.
That will be a busy but fun weekend. Plan a few simple activities so he does not get bored. What does Aryan like?
Cars, drawing and water play. He also hates vegetables.
Then you can make a road for his cars with chalk outside, give him paper to draw, and let him splash in a tub of water with cups. For vegetables, cut them into fun shapes or serve them with a dip.
Good ideas. He might refuse to nap, though.
Many four year olds do. Keep the afternoon calm with a story or soft music, and let him rest his body even if he does not sleep. A quiet hour helps both of you.
I will try. What did you suggest for the vegetables again?
Cut them into fun shapes or serve them with a dip, so Aryan finds them playful. Cucumber stars with a mild curd dip may tempt a boy who hates vegetables.
I miss my grandfather. He passed away last year and today is his birthday.
I am sorry. Missing someone on their birthday is natural. Remembering him is a way of keeping him close. What was he like?
He used to hum old film songs while he gardened. He grew roses.
That is a beautiful picture. You could plant a rose in his memory, or hum one of his songs while you water the plants. Small rituals like that can bring comfort.
I think I will buy a rose plant this evening.
That sounds meaningful. Choose a colour he liked, and plant it where you can see it often. Each time it blooms, you may think of his roses and the old film songs he hummed in the garden.
Wrong exit at the metro station today, and now I am on the other side of the city.
Do not worry. Metro stations are well signposted. Look for the map on the platform and find your line. Where do you need to go?
To a coaching class near Lajpat Nagar. I have a test at four.
Then check the map for the line to Lajpat Nagar, and note where you need to change. Ask the station staff if you are unsure. You have time if you move now, so there is no need to panic.
The staff said to change at the next station and take the pink line.
Good. Follow the signs for the pink line at the change station. Check the final stop on the train board, so you board the right direction, and you should reach Lajpat Nagar for your test.
I reached Lajpat Nagar in time! How early should I leave next time?
Leave about twenty minutes earlier than you think you need. A test at four in Lajpat Nagar is easier to reach calmly if you allow time for wrong exits or a missed change at the station.
My friends and I want to see a late film, but my mother wants me home by nine.
It helps to talk to her calmly. Explain what you are planning, and ask what she is worried about. What time does the film end?
Half past ten. I would need to be home by eleven.
Then tell her the end time and who is going with you, and offer to send a message when the film ends. A safe plan, like going with friends and being dropped home, can make her more comfortable.
Mom said yes if Rahul's father drops me home.
That is a fair compromise. Check with Rahul that his father can do it, and thank him. Send your mother a message when you leave the cinema, as promised.
I am going now. What should I send my mother?
Send a short message when the film ends, as you promised. Something like, Film is over, Rahul's father is dropping me home. It keeps her calm, and she will trust you more next time.
My grandfather in the village has invited all his grandchildren for the harvest festival.
That is a lovely invitation. Harvest festivals are full of food, music and family. How many cousins are going?
About twelve. Mia and Emma are my favourites. We will sleep on the terrace.
That will be a great memory. Sleeping on a terrace under the stars with Mia and Emma sounds wonderful. Bring a light blanket and mosquito repellent, since evenings can be cool and buzzy.
Good thinking. Dada also wants us to help with the harvest early in the morning. Can I still sleep on the terrace with my favourite cousins?

Yes, just sleep a little earlier. Sleeping on the terrace with Mia and Emma means you will wake with the sunrise anyway. Wear old clothes and a hat for the harvest, and ask Dada to show you how to sort the crop.
My visa interview is next week and I am anxious.
That is normal, as it is an important day. Prepare your documents in a folder and read the instructions again. Where is the interview?
At the embassy in Mumbai. I am travelling from Nagpur the day before.
Then book your train early and a stay close to the embassy, so you are not rushing. Keep the interview letter and identity papers in your hand bag, not in a suitcase.
My brother Aditya is coming with me for support.
That will help you feel calmer. Aditya can wait outside while you attend, and you can share a meal afterwards. Sleep well the night before, so you are fresh for Mumbai.
What if I forget something in the interview?
Stay calm, take a breath and answer honestly. If you do not remember a detail, say so. Keep your papers organised in a folder, and Aditya can help you check it all the night before you leave Nagpur.
We are taking a boat across the river to visit a fair on the other bank. I have never been on a boat.
That sounds exciting. Boat rides are usually calm, and the boatman will tell you where to sit. Is it a small boat or a larger ferry?
A small wooden boat. About ten people sit in it. My uncle Rahul is coming along.
Then sit in the middle and keep still, especially when the boat starts and stops. Hold the side if it rocks. Life jackets are good if the boatman has them, so ask Uncle Rahul to check.
What if my slippers fall into the river?
Keep them on your feet or hold them in a bag on your lap. Wet slippers are easy to dry, but a lost one is a bother. Wear shoes with straps if you can.
We reached the fair! There is a big wheel and lots of food stalls. I do not know where to start.
Begin with the big wheel while you have energy, then walk slowly past the stalls and pick one snack. Stay close to Uncle Rahul in the crowd, and decide on a place to meet if you separate.
Okay. And how are we getting back, and with whom?
You are going back across the river in the same kind of small boat, and Uncle Rahul is with you. Agree on a time to return so the boatman is ready for the evening crossing.
My friend Aditya wants me to help him move into a new room on Saturday.
That is a kind way to spend a Saturday. Moving takes many hands. What time does he want you, and how far is the new room?
He wants me by nine. It is a shared flat on the third floor and there is no lift.
Then wear comfortable clothes and sports shoes, and drink water before you start. Carry smaller boxes upstairs and let others handle the heavy furniture. Taking short breaks will save your back.
He says he will buy lunch for everyone who helps. Four of us are going.
Good, lunch is a fair thank you. Ask him which dish he is planning, in case someone has a food rule. After lunch you can help arrange the room, so he feels settled by evening.
We finished by two. His room looks nice, but he has nowhere to keep his books.
A simple fix is a set of stacked crates or a plank on bricks. Both are cheap and quick. Or you could ask the shop where he buys furniture for a small shelf.
Maybe I can gift him a shelf. Who was I helping again, and on which floor?
You helped Aditya move into his shared flat on the third floor. A small shelf would be a useful housewarming gift, and his books would finally have a place to go.
I promised my little brother I would take him to the park after school, but a classmate asked me for help with maths.
It is good that you want to keep both promises. Is the help urgent, or can your classmate wait a bit?
He has a test tomorrow. My brother's name is Tara, no wait, it is my sister Tara. She is eight.
No problem, mixing up a detail happens. So Tara is eight, and your classmate has a test tomorrow. You could help him for half an hour first, then take Tara to the park for the rest of the time.
I told Tara and she is fine to wait, as long as we get ice cream.
That is a fair deal. Help your classmate first, and then take Tara to the park. Finish on time, since she is looking forward to the treat and you promised her the time.
Done. We went to the park and she ate a big ice cream. Did I manage to keep both promises?

Yes, you did. You helped your classmate before his test tomorrow, and then you took Tara to the park with the ice cream you promised her. A quick good luck message to your classmate would be a nice finish.
Our train to Mysore is delayed by two hours. My little brother Aarav is already cranky.
Two hours is long with a child. Find a seat away from the crowd, and let him walk a little so he can burn off energy. Do you have any snacks or something to play with?
Only biscuits. He wants a game.
Try simple games that need no phone: spot the colours, a word chain, or counting how many red bags pass by. Ask Aarav to be the judge, because children love having a job.
Counting red bags worked. He is laughing now.
That is lovely to hear. When he gets tired of it, switch to yellow or blue. Aarav will probably also sleep well once the train finally starts moving.
I take the same bus every day and I never talk to anyone. Should I?
You do not have to, but a small hello can make the ride nicer. Start with a smile or a nod to someone you see often. Do you see the same faces each morning?
Yes, there is an old uncle who always sits by the window and reads a newspaper.
He sounds like an easy person to greet. Try saying good morning once, and see how he reacts. If he wants to chat, he will; if not, a nod is still friendly.
I said good morning today and he smiled and asked my name. Now what do I say tomorrow?
Tomorrow you could ask what he is reading in his newspaper, since he always has one by the window. Keep it light and short. If he asks about you, tell him a little, and the habit will grow naturally.
What should I put in a small bag for a day trip with my school friends?
Keep it light: a water bottle, a snack, a cap or umbrella, a small towel, a phone charger, and a little cash. Wear comfortable shoes. Where are you going?
A waterfall near Lonavala. My friend Sana is bringing the lunch.
Then you can skip the heavy food and bring only snacks. Take a spare t-shirt in a plastic bag, since you may get wet near the falls, and wear shoes with good grip because rocks get slippery.
Good point. Should I bring extra food in case Sana forgets?
A small packet of nuts or a couple of fruits is enough as a backup. Since Sana is bringing the lunch, you do not need a full meal. Just something to keep you going if the plan runs late.
My grandfather turns seventy next week and we are going to his village for the day.
What a lovely occasion. Seventy years is worth celebrating. Do you know what your grandfather likes, so you can make the day feel special for him?
He loves old songs and jalebi. His name is Dada Mohan.
Then play a few of his favourite old songs during tea and bring a box of fresh jalebi. If the cousins can come, ask each one to say a short sentence about a happy memory with Dada Mohan.
I love that. Maybe I can also write him a card.

A card is a wonderful gift. Write one memory in your own words, like a day he taught you something. Give it to Dada Mohan with the jalebi on his seventieth birthday, and he will probably keep it for years.
I am at a bus station and I cannot find my platform. Everything is in a rush.
Take a breath and move to the side so you are not in anyone's way. Look for the enquiry counter or a board with bus numbers. Which bus are you trying to catch?
The 5:30 bus to Nashik. I think it is platform nine.
Then walk towards the numbered signs and look for nine. If you cannot see it, ask a conductor in a uniform. Show him your ticket, so he can read the details and point you correctly.
Found it! It was platform eleven actually. I would have waited at nine!
I am glad you checked. Platform eleven for Nashik, then. Sit near the front so you can see the driver's board, and keep your bag on your lap until you board.
I have nothing planned this Sunday and I feel bored already.
A blank Sunday can be good. Pick one small thing to look forward to, like a long breakfast or a bike ride. What do you enjoy that you rarely have time for?
Painting. I have not touched my paints since last year.
Then make Sunday your painting day. Set up near a window, put on soft music and paint anything, even a cup on the table. It does not need to be perfect, just enjoyable.
I will paint the mango tree outside my window. My dad calls it his tree.

That is a lovely subject, especially since it matters to your dad. As you have not painted since last year, start with quick pencil lines, then fill in the greens. You could give him the painting of his tree as a gift.
Plan changed again. My friend Emma cannot come to the movie on Friday.
That is disappointing, but plans do shift. Do you want to keep Friday and go with others, or move the movie to a day when Emma is free?
I would prefer to wait for her. She picked the film.
That is thoughtful. Message her and ask which days suit her, then offer two options. Since she picked the film, the outing will mean more to her if she is there.
She says Sunday afternoon works. Can you help me tell the group?
Sure. You could write: Hi all, Emma cannot make Friday, so we are moving the movie to Sunday afternoon. Please tell me if that works for you. Keep it short and friendly.
I need to book a ticket for my mother to visit her sister in Kochi, but I have never done it before.
Start by deciding the date and whether she prefers a train or a bus. For a long trip, a train is usually more comfortable. Does your mother have a favourite way to travel?
She likes trains because she can sleep. She goes in a window seat, always.
Then look for a train with a sleeper or air-conditioned seat, and choose a window berth when booking. Check the departure time too, so she does not have to leave at midnight.
Okay. Also, remind me, which city is my aunt in?
Your mother's sister lives in Kochi, so that is the city you are booking to. Keep your mother's name exactly as it appears on her identity card when you fill in the ticket.
We are deciding between the hills and the sea for the school holidays.
Both are lovely. The hills are cool and good for walks. The sea is good for swimming and sand games. Who is going, and what does everyone like?
Me, my parents and my sister Olivia. Olivia hates cold weather.
Then the sea might suit you better. Olivia will be comfortable in the warmth, and your parents can relax on the beach. You can still do a little walking along the shore or a short coastal trek.
Good. Mum says we can pick a quiet beach. Any ideas on what to do there?

Collect shells in the morning, build a sandcastle, and watch the sunset in the evening. The warm sea air will suit Olivia, so ask her to choose one activity each day. She will enjoy the trip more if she gets a say.
Is it rude to talk on the phone in a train compartment?
It can be, if you talk loudly or for a long time. Others may want to rest or read. A short call is fine if you keep your voice low. Is something happening?
A man next to me is talking loudly to his boss for an hour.
That must be tiring. You can politely say, Excuse me, could you please speak a little softer? Most people do not realise how loud they are, and a calm request usually works.
I asked him and he said sorry. What if he gets loud again with his boss later?
Then give him one more quiet, friendly reminder. If his call with his boss gets loud again after that, you can ask the ticket checker about another seat, or put on earphones and enjoy the view.
The bus is full and an elderly lady is standing near me. What do I do?
Offer her your seat with a smile. You can say, Please sit here, aunty, I am happy to stand. Most elders appreciate it even if they refuse at first.
I offered. She said thank you and sat. Her name is Mrs. Pillai and she is going to the market.
That was kind. Since the bus is crowded, hold the rail firmly and keep your bag in front. You could ask Mrs. Pillai if she needs help carrying anything when she gets off.
She does have two heavy bags! Should I help her?
Yes, ask her first, and carry the bags only as far as the bus stop. Say, Mrs. Pillai, may I help you with these? That way she is comfortable and you stay safe.
Do I really need to pack a first aid kit for a weekend in the mountains?
A small one is a good idea. Include plasters, antiseptic wipes, and any medicines you normally take. You will not need much, but it is useful if someone gets a blister. Where are you going?
Manali, with my friends Jack and Tara.
Then also carry warm layers, sturdy shoes and a rain jacket. Mountain weather changes fast. Share the load with Jack and Tara so one person does not carry everything.
Tara says she will bring the kit. Is that fine?
Yes, that is a good split. Still, keep a few plasters in your own bag in case you get separated. Jack could carry the snacks, and you can take care of the water bottles.
Aditya here. I am travelling to Bhopal alone for a job interview tomorrow.
Good luck, Aditya. Travelling a day before is smart. Do you have your documents and a place to stay tonight?
Yes, I booked a small hotel near the station. The interview is at ten in the morning at a company called Sunrise Textiles.
That is a good spot. Check how far the office is from the hotel tonight, and plan to leave early. A short walk or a quick auto ride means you arrive calm and not rushed.
The hotel says it is fifteen minutes by auto. Should I iron my clothes now?
Yes, do that tonight so the morning is easy. Lay out your shirt, your file and your shoes. Then sleep early, because a rested mind helps more than last minute revision.
One more thing. I am nervous about the first question.
Many interviews start with Tell me about yourself. Prepare three short lines: your studies, one thing you are proud of, and why Sunrise Textiles interests you. Say them aloud once before bed.
Okay. What was the name of the company again? I want to read about it tonight.
It is Sunrise Textiles. Read their website for what they make and where they work, and write down one or two questions to ask at the end. That shows real interest.
We visit my grandparents in Lucknow every summer. This year I want to do something different.
That is a nice idea. Visits can feel the same each year, so a small change can make it special. What did you usually do there?
Eat a lot, play cards with my cousins and sleep in the afternoon.
Then try one new thing, like asking your grandparents to teach you a family recipe, or to tell stories from when they were young. Both will give you something to remember.
My nani makes the best kheer. She never writes the recipe.
Then ask her if you can cook it together this summer, and write each step as she goes. Measure with spoons and cups, because she probably uses her own eye for amounts.
Good plan. My cousin Farhan can help me taste test.
Farhan will be happy to do that job. After the first try, share a bowl with your nani and ask what she would change. She will enjoy teaching you.
Wait, whose kheer did I say I wanted to learn?
Your nani's kheer, the one she never writes down. Cook it with her in Lucknow this summer, and Farhan can be the taste tester.
My phone died and I do not know how to get to my friend's house. I am in a new town.
Try not to panic. First, find a safe public place with people, like a shop or a petrol pump. Do you remember anything about the address, even a landmark?
Her house is near a big school called St. Mary's. Her name is Sana.
That helps. Ask a shopkeeper or a rickshaw driver where St. Mary's School is, and head that way. Once you are near the school, ask again for the street, since people nearby usually know it.
I found the school. Now how do I find her house?
Ask the guard at the school gate. Say you are looking for Sana's house nearby, and give her family name if you know it. If you can borrow a phone, call her to guide you the last few steps.
A shopkeeper let me call her. She is coming to meet me!

That is a happy ending. Wait right where you are near St. Mary's School until Sana arrives, so she does not miss you. When you get to her house, charge your phone and keep a charger in your bag from now on.
I want to do something fun on Saturday but I have only a small budget.
There are lots of cheap, fun ideas. A picnic in a park, a visit to a free museum or a long cycle ride all cost little. What do you like to do?
I like being outside. And my friend Jack has a football.
Then call Jack and play a game in the park. Bring water, and ask a few more friends. Teams make it more fun, and it costs nothing apart from a snack.
Great. Should I make a fixed time, or just see who turns up?
Fix a time and a place, because it avoids confusion. Say, Five o'clock at the park gate. People who can come will arrive, and those who cannot will tell you in advance.
I told everyone. Five people said yes.
That is a good number for a game. With Jack's football and five friends, you can do two teams or take turns. Bring a few extra bottles of water, since it will be warm.
Wait, who has the football again?
Jack has the football. Remind him the day before so he remembers to bring it, and maybe he can pump it up too.
I just got on the wrong train. How bad is this?
Stay calm, it is fixable. Do not jump off while it is moving. Check the next stop on the route board or ask the ticket checker. Where were you meant to go?
Pune. I think this train is going to Mumbai.
Then get down at the first station where the train stops. Ask the staff about a train back towards the junction. The ticket checker can tell you what to do about your ticket, too.
The checker said I can get down at Lonavala and take another train back.
That sounds sensible. Once you reach Lonavala, check the board for trains to Pune and sit at the platform until it arrives. Tell your family so they know you are safe and might be late.
I called my mother. She was not angry.
I am glad. Mistakes like this happen, and you handled it well. Now just wait at Lonavala for the Pune train, drink some water and keep your bag close.
One more thing: where was I going originally, and where did the wrong train take me?
You were going to Pune, but the train was heading towards Mumbai. You are getting off at Lonavala and taking a train back to Pune from there.
I forgot to pack my charger and now I am at the station. What should I do?
Check if the station has a shop nearby that sells chargers. Otherwise, you can ask a fellow passenger if you can charge briefly. Do you have time before the train?
Yes, about forty minutes. There is a small shop outside.
Then go quickly and buy a basic one. Check that it fits your phone before you pay. Come back inside early so you are not rushing when the train comes.
I bought it. Another thing, I think I forgot my towel too.
A towel is not a disaster. You can buy a small one at your destination, or borrow one from whoever you are staying with. Do not run around now, since you have the main thing sorted.
True. My cousin Rahul will lend me one.
Perfect, then you are all set. Just text Rahul the train time so he can pick you up and bring the towel along. Keep the new charger in your front pocket so you will not leave it behind.
Everyone in our group has a different idea for the holiday. It is making me tired.
That happens often with groups. One way is to write each idea down and let everyone vote. That way no one feels ignored. How many ideas do you have?
Three. Beach, mountains, or staying home and doing a movie marathon. Neha wants the mountains.
Then list those three and ask each person to give a first and second choice. Count the votes. If mountains win, Neha will be pleased, and others can still pick the activities.
Fine. Mia wants the beach, so I guess it will be a tie.
If it is a tie, try a mix: the mountains for the weekend and a beach day later. Or let the person who has not won before pick. Being fair matters more than the exact place.
Good, I will propose a mix. What did I say Neha wanted?
You said Neha wanted the mountains, while Mia wanted the beach. A mix could keep both happy, with mountains first and a beach day when school is out.
I took the wrong bus today and ended up very far from home.
That sounds stressful. First, are you safe, and do you know where you are? Look for a bus stop sign, a shop name, or a landmark.
I am at a stop called Rajiv Chowk. It is dark and I am a little scared.
Stand under a light near other people or a shop. Call someone at home and tell them the stop name, Rajiv Chowk. Ask the conductor of the next bus how to reach home, or let your family pick you up.
Dad is coming. He says it will take twenty minutes.
Good. Stay in the lit area and keep your phone in your hand. When your dad arrives, you can tell him what happened and plan the right route for next time.
Okay. Where was I standing when I called him?
You were at the Rajiv Chowk bus stop. If your dad cannot find the spot, tell him to look for the lit area near the shop where you are waiting.
Let me tell you what happened on my way to school. Our auto driver, Raju bhaiya, stopped suddenly.
Oh no, what happened? Was he all right, and were you safe in the back? Tell me more when you are ready.
A small puppy ran across the road. Raju bhaiya braked just in time and we all lurched forward.
That was quick thinking from him. A sudden stop can scare everyone, but it is good he saw the puppy. Did the puppy get away safely?
Yes. He sat on the roadside and shook. Raju bhaiya got down and gave him some water from his bottle.
What a gentle thing to do. It sounds like Raju bhaiya is a kind man. Maybe the puppy will remember him and wait near that corner next time.
My grandfather is coming to stay with us for a month. I have never lived with him before.
That will be a new experience for everyone. It can be lovely to hear his stories. What do you know about what he likes?
He wakes up at five, drinks black tea and listens to the radio. He is quite quiet.
Then you might find mornings peaceful. You could make his tea some days, or sit with him while the radio plays. Quiet people often open up slowly, in their own time.
I tried. I made tea today and he said it needed less sugar.
That is a normal beginning. Next time, use one spoon less sugar and tell him you listened. He may soften when he sees you took his words seriously.
He did smile a little. Should I ask him about his village tomorrow?
Yes, try it over tea, when the radio is low. Ask something simple like what he did as a boy in the village. Let him talk, and do not worry about silences.
I will. Can you remind me what he said about the tea?
He said it needed less sugar. So use one spoon less and bring it before the news on the radio, and see whether he approves.
I think I lost my wallet on the bus. I have just noticed.
That is upsetting. Try to stay calm and check your bag and pockets once more. When did you last remember having it, and which bus was it?
I paid for my ticket with it about an hour ago on bus 42.
Then contact the bus depot or the conductor of route 42 and describe the wallet. Also check with the police station near your stop, since honest people often hand wallets in.
I called the depot. They said someone found one and will keep it until six.
That is good news. Take an identity card with you when you collect it, so you can prove it is yours. Check everything inside once you have it back.
I will go at five. Thank you. What bus was it again, in case they ask?
It was bus 42. When you reach the depot, say you paid your ticket on that bus about an hour before you noticed it was missing, and describe the wallet's colour.
Rahul invited me to his farm for the weekend. I have never been to a farm.
That sounds like a great change from city life. You will probably wake up early and see lots of green. Do you know what the farm grows?
Mostly sugarcane and a few mango trees. He also has two buffaloes.
Then wear old clothes and sturdy shoes, since farms get muddy. Ask Rahul to show you how the buffaloes are fed, and if it is mango season, you are in for a treat.
Is it okay if I ask silly questions about the buffaloes? I know nothing about them.
Of course. Farmers are usually proud of their work and happy to explain. Ask how sugarcane grows or how the buffaloes are milked. Rahul will enjoy showing you around.
I take the local train every day and today someone stepped on my foot and did not apologise.
Ouch, that is annoying. Crowded trains make people careless. Is your foot all right? A little pain should fade, but check if it swells.
It is fine, just sore. I was more irritated than hurt.
That is understandable. It is hard to stay patient when every day is a crush. Try to board earlier or step to the less crowded end, if you can. A little space makes the ride calmer.
Maybe I will try the ladies coach near the front. My friend Mia takes it.

That is a good idea, as it is often less crowded, so there is less chance of someone stepping on your sore foot again. You can also travel with Mia and chat on the way, which makes the journey feel shorter.
Our school trip is to a fort in Rajasthan. I want to take good photographs.
A fort has great colours and shapes. Go early or late in the day, since the light is softer then. Is it your phone or a camera?
A phone. Mine is old, so the pictures look dull.
Then clean the lens with a soft cloth, and tap on the screen to focus on the part you like. Shoot a doorway or a window, with some people in the frame to show the size of the fort.
I like that idea. What about the sky? It will be very bright.
A bright sky can wash out the picture. Try standing so the sun is behind you or to the side. Tap on the bright part to darken it, and take a few shots, because you can pick the best later.
I will try. What was the first thing you told me to do with the phone?
First, clean the lens with a soft cloth. A smudged lens is the most common reason for dull photos from the fort, especially on an old phone.
Tara and I planned a cycling trip but now she has a cold.
Poor Tara. A cold can drain energy, so it is wise to rest first. Is the trip fixed for a certain date?
This Sunday, but we can shift it by a week.
Then postpone it. Cycling with a blocked nose is no fun, and she will recover faster with rest. Use the free Sunday for a quiet activity, or visit her if she is up to it.
Okay. I will call her today. What can I say to cheer her up?
You could say, Tara, rest well and beat this cold, the cycles are not going anywhere. We will ride next Sunday instead. Keep it light and warm, so she knows there is no pressure at all.
There is a bus strike tomorrow and I have an exam at nine.
That is a real worry. Think of other ways to reach the exam hall: a friend with a bike, a shared auto, or a relative who can drive. Who lives close to you?
My classmate Aditya lives two streets away and he has a scooter.
Ask Aditya tonight if he can give you a ride, and offer to share the fuel cost. Leave an hour earlier than usual, because roads may be busy on the strike day.
He said yes! He will pick me up at seven thirty.
That is a relief. Keep your admit card and pens ready tonight, so you are not hunting for them in the morning. Sleep early so you feel fresh for the exam.
Right. And who is picking me up, and when?
Aditya is picking you up on his scooter at seven thirty. Be at your gate five minutes before, so you start the day without any hurry.
What is the best way to pack shoes in a suitcase?
Put each pair in a cloth bag or a plastic cover, so the dirt does not touch your clothes. Place them along the edge of the suitcase, soles facing the wall, and tuck socks inside to save space.
Smart. Can I put snacks inside the shoes as well?
Small, sealed snacks are fine, but I would avoid anything that crumbles or smells strong. The shoes are warm and enclosed, which can spoil food. A separate small pouch is safer.
I see. My mom packed a jar of pickle for my aunt, though.

Do not put the jar inside the shoes like the snacks. Wrap it in a towel or a few clothes, and put it in the centre of the bag where it is cushioned. Seal it in a plastic bag too, so your aunt gets the pickle and your clothes stay clean.
My cousin Olivia is visiting from abroad and I want to show her around Delhi.
What a nice plan. Delhi has so much to see. Does Olivia like history, food, or shopping? That will help you choose the places.
She likes history and she loves street food. She stays four days.
Then on day one visit the Red Fort and old Delhi lanes, where she can try chaat. Another day you could see Humayun's Tomb and walk in the gardens. Leave one day open to rest.
She asked if the street food is spicy.
Some of it is, but you can ask the vendor to make it mild. Tell Olivia to start with something simple like aloo tikki, and to carry bottled water. Take it slowly, so her stomach adjusts.
I am afraid of flying, and I have a flight on Monday.
Many people feel this way, and you are not alone. It can help to know that flying is very safe. Is this your first flight, or have you flown before?
My second. The first time my ears hurt a lot.
Chewing gum or sucking a sweet during take off and landing can help your ears. Yawning also works. Sit near the wing if you can, since that spot feels smoother.
Nice tips. Anything for the nervous feeling?
Breathe in slowly for four counts and out for four. Listen to calm music or watch a film. Remember that the bumps you feel are only air, and the crew is trained for them.
Thank you. What did you say would help my ears?
Chew gum or suck a sweet during take off and landing, and yawn if your ears feel blocked. Since your ears hurt last time, keep a few sweets in your pocket on Monday.
I am organising a surprise trip for my parents' anniversary. Where do I start?
What a loving idea. Start with the budget and the dates, then pick a place they would enjoy, not just one you like. Do they prefer quiet places or busy ones?
Quiet. They love lakes and old temples. The anniversary is on the twelfth of December.
Then look at a lake town with a temple nearby, such as Pushkar or Udaipur in winter, when the weather is pleasant. Book a stay a few weeks ahead so you get a good room.
I like Pushkar. How do I keep it a secret?
Tell them only that you are planning a family weekend, and keep the details to yourself. Ask your sibling or a cousin to help with packing, so they do not guess from the bags.
My brother Aditya can help. Should he know the place?
Yes, one trusted helper is useful, and Aditya can handle small tasks like tickets while you manage the stay. Ask him to keep the name Pushkar between you two.
Perfect. Remind me, which place did I choose and which date is it?
You chose Pushkar for the lake and temples, and the anniversary is on the twelfth of December. Plan the trip so you arrive a day early and the room is ready.
I am taking my grandmother on a train for the first time in years. She is a bit scared.
That is a caring thing to do. A calm start will help her. Do you know how she feels about crowds and stairs?
She walks slowly and gets dizzy in crowds. Her name is Savitri Ajji.
Then reach the station early, and book a lower berth so she does not have to climb. Ask a porter to help with bags, so you can hold Savitri Ajji's arm and walk slowly.
Good. Should I take food from home for her?
Yes, simple food she is used to will feel comforting, like khichdi in a container or soft rotis. Carry a bottle of water too, and keep her medicines in your hand bag.
She also hates loud noise. The train is noisy.
Choose a seat away from the door, where it is quieter, and give her the window so she can look outside. A soft chat with her can also take her mind off the noise.
We reached! She even liked the window. What was I supposed to do with her bag again?
You were going to ask a porter to carry the bags so you could hold Savitri Ajji's arm. Do that again when you reach the station at the other end, and walk slowly with her.
My little sister Mia wandered off at the mela and we cannot find her.
Stay calm and act quickly. Tell the nearest police officer or the mela help desk straight away, and give them her name, age and what she is wearing. How old is Mia?
She is six. She is wearing a yellow frock and has two ponytails.
Tell that to the help desk and ask them to announce it on the loudspeaker. One of you should stay at the spot where you last saw her, while the other searches nearby.
My dad is at the desk. I will wait at the ice cream stall where we lost her.
Good plan. Stay near the stall, because Mia may walk back towards a place she remembers. Look at the height of children around you, and call her name now and then.
She is here! She was watching the puppet show.
I am so glad. Hug her and tell her gently to hold your hand in crowds. Let the help desk know she is found, so they stop searching.
Will do. Which stall did I say I was waiting at?
You were waiting at the ice cream stall where you lost Mia. Maybe buy her one now, and walk back to the help desk together to tell them she is safe.
I want to host a small get together at home on Saturday evening. About six friends.
That sounds fun. Keep the food simple and easy to share, and make a little space for chatting. What snacks do you have in mind?
Maybe pakoras and chai. My friend Sana will bring a cake.
Pakoras and chai are a lovely pair, especially if it is cool outside. Make the batter early, then fry just before they arrive. Sana's cake will be a nice end to the evening.
Do I need games or music?
A little of both is nice but keep it simple. A soft playlist in the background and one easy game, like charades, is plenty. Friends mostly come for the company.
Okay. One of my friends, Jack, is vegetarian, and Farhan is allergic to peanuts.
Then make your pakoras with onion or potato, which suits Jack, and avoid peanut oil. Read the cake label as well, and ask Sana whether it has any nuts for Farhan.
Good thinking. Who is allergic to what?
Farhan is allergic to peanuts, so use a different oil and check Sana's cake. Jack is vegetarian, so the onion and potato pakoras will work for him.
I want to record my grandfather's stories before I forget them. How do I begin?
A wonderful idea. Sit with him in a quiet room, switch on a voice recorder on your phone and ask open questions. What would you like to hear first?
His childhood in Amritsar. He was born there before the move.
Then ask him to describe his house, his school and what he did on holidays. Ask for names and small details, like what the street smelled of. Do not interrupt too much.
He gets tired quickly though. He is eighty.
Keep each session short, perhaps twenty minutes, with tea in between. Do it over several days. If he drifts to another story, let him, because those are often the best ones.
Could I write them down afterwards?
Yes, listen to each recording and write a short summary in your own words. Keep his exact words for special lines. Later you can make a small booklet for the family.
I will start tomorrow. Where did he grow up, so I can prepare questions?
He grew up in Amritsar, where he was born. Prepare questions about his house, school and festivals there, and write them on a small card to keep beside the recorder.
I am learning to travel by bus alone. My parents are worried.
It is a good skill, and being a little careful is wise. Start with a route you know well. Where do you need to go?
To my music class at Shanti Nagar. It is twenty minutes.
Then take the bus there with a parent once, noting the stops, and then try alone. Keep your phone charged and share your live location with your parents, so they feel at ease.
What if I miss my stop?
Do not panic. Get off at the next stop, and cross carefully to catch a bus back. You can also ask the conductor to tell you when Shanti Nagar arrives, before you sit.
Good, I will do that. My mom wants me to message her when I reach.
That is a fair request, and an easy one. Send a short text like, Reached class safely. It builds trust, and soon your parents will worry less and let you go on your own more often.
Do you remember where my class is?
Your music class is at Shanti Nagar, about twenty minutes by bus. Ask the conductor to call out the stop, so you do not miss it.
I have to pack for a month at my hostel in another city. How do I decide what to take?
Think in groups: clothes, study things, daily needs and a few comfort items. Start with what you use every day and add extras only if they fit. Is it a cold or a warm city?
Warm, but it rains a lot. Pune in July.
Then take light cotton clothes, two pairs of quick drying shoes, a sturdy umbrella and a raincoat. Pack a small bag of plastic covers to keep your books dry.
What about bedding?
Check what the hostel gives first. If not, a thin sheet and a pillow cover are enough for a warm city. Do not carry a big quilt, since you can buy a blanket there if you need one.
I will ask the warden. My roommate is Neha, I think.
Then message Neha before you go and decide who brings the kettle or the extra lamp. Sharing a few items saves bags and money for both of you.
Great. Which city did I say, and what month?
You said Pune in July, so the rain is the main thing to prepare for. Pack the umbrella and raincoat on top of your bag so you can reach them quickly when you arrive.
Our family is driving to the hills tomorrow and my brother gets car sick.
That is common, and a few small steps can help. Seat him by a window, and keep the car cool. Does he feel sick on every long ride?
Mostly on curvy roads. His name is Rahul and he is ten.
Then let Rahul look at the road ahead, not a book or a screen. Stop for a short break every hour for fresh air, and offer dry snacks like biscuits instead of oily food.
Can he chew something on the way?
Ginger candy or a fennel seed can be soothing for many children. Do not give anything unusual if he has not tried it, so offer only what he already likes.
We will try the ginger candy. We also plan to stop at a dhaba for lunch.
A dhaba stop is a good break. Let Rahul get down, stretch and walk a little before eating. Keep his meal light, and do not rush back into the car immediately.
Good. Who was getting car sick, and which seat should he take?
Rahul, your ten year old brother, gets car sick. Give him a window seat and keep the air cool, so he can look at the road ahead.
We are stuck between visiting my uncle in Chennai or going to a hill station.
Both sound nice. It might help to weigh what each one gives you: family time with your uncle, or rest and cool air. What do you need most right now?
I need rest. But my uncle Faisal always feels hurt when we skip him.
That is a real concern. You could do a short stay in Chennai first, then go to the hills for rest, or visit your uncle for a long weekend and keep the hill station for another time.
What if I call him and explain?
That is kind and honest. Tell Uncle Faisal that you need rest this time but promise a proper visit soon. Most relatives understand if they are told with warmth and given a date.
I will call him tonight. Should I say a date?
Yes, giving a rough month makes the promise feel real. Say, Uncle Faisal, we will come to Chennai in March for a few days. Then put it in your calendar so it truly happens.
Good. Who is the uncle I should call?
Your Uncle Faisal in Chennai. Call him tonight, explain that you need rest now, and promise the March visit so he knows he is not being skipped.
I booked two tickets for a morning train, one for me and one for my friend Emma.
Nice, that should make the journey more fun. Do you have your seat numbers and the train time written somewhere safe?
Yes. But Emma just texted that she has to stay back for a work meeting.
