That is a pity. If the ticket is still valid, you can ask the railway office about cancelling it or changing the name. Check the rules for refunds soon, because they depend on how close the departure is.
Could I give her ticket to my cousin instead?

Often the name can be changed only at a counter, with an identity card and some paperwork, and a few hours of notice. Check with the station for Emma's ticket. If it works, your cousin can take her seat.
The bus conductor shouted at me today because I did not have change.
That sounds unpleasant. Carrying small notes is the best habit for buses, but a shout was not nice either. Did it upset you much?
A bit. Everyone looked at me.
It happens to many people, and others forget it fast. Next time, keep a few ten rupee notes in a separate pocket. If it happens again, you can say politely, Sorry, I only have a large note.
Good. I will keep coins in my bag now, so the conductor has no reason to shout again.

A small coin pouch is a great idea, along with a few ten rupee notes. Keep it where you can reach it without opening the whole bag. Then you can pay the conductor quickly, and there will be nothing to shout about.
My grandma wants me to stay overnight at her flat but I have never done it.
That could be a sweet memory for both of you. Is there something about it that makes you hesitate?
I think I will be bored. She does not have a television, only her radio and knitting.
You might surprise yourself. Ask her to teach you to knit, or let her tell you stories from when she was your age. Bring a book and a card game too, so you have choices.
The knitting sounds fun. Maybe I can make a scarf for my brother.
That is a lovely gift, and learning from your grandma makes it more special. Start with a simple pattern and a thick wool, so the scarf grows quickly. Your brother will treasure it.
I took a shortcut through a park and now I cannot see the exit.
Stay where you are for a moment and look around for a path, a signboard or a person. Parks usually have gates on several sides. Is it still light outside?
Yes, but it is getting dim. I can hear traffic on my left.
Then walk towards the sound, since roads usually run along park edges. Stay on the main path and avoid empty corners. Once you reach the road, you can find a gate or a shop.
I found the road! It was just behind a hedge.
Good, you used the traffic noise well. Walk along the road to the nearest gate and avoid shortcuts through dark places next time, especially when the light is fading.
My weekend is full of chores, but I really want to see my friend Tara.
Chores can make a weekend feel short. Can you do some together, or finish the big ones early so you get a free afternoon?
I could finish the cleaning by Saturday noon. Then I am free.
Then ask Tara if she can meet after lunch. You could grab chai near your home or take a walk. Having a fixed time makes you finish the chores faster.
She said yes, three o'clock at the tea stall. I am so happy.
That is great. Make a small list of the chores now and tick them off in the morning, so you reach the tea stall on time and enjoy the time with Tara without stress.
My trip to my aunt's village is on Friday but my exam got shifted to Saturday morning.
That is awkward. Since the exam matters most, it is wise to rethink the trip. Can you travel after the exam, or is Friday the only day your family can go?
My parents can go only on Friday. My aunt has a function that evening.
Then maybe your parents go on Friday and you join on Saturday afternoon after the exam, by bus or train. You may miss the function, but you can revise properly and still spend time with your aunt.
I think that works. Aunt Neha will understand, I hope.
She probably will, since it is about your exam. Call her and explain, and say you will arrive on Saturday after the paper. Aunt Neha will likely be proud that you put studies first.
What should I carry in my hand bag for a long flight?
Keep your documents, phone, charger, a book, a light snack, a bottle you can fill after security, and a thin jacket. Planes get cold. Do you have anything for your ears or neck?
A neck pillow. And I want to take my medicines.
Keep your medicines in your hand bag, not in checked luggage, with the original labels. That way they are with you if the suitcase is delayed. Also carry your doctor's note if you have one.
Okay. My checked bag is already full. Can I move the neck pillow to my hand bag?
Yes, you can clip it on the outside of the hand bag or wear it through the airport. It takes little space, and you will be happy to have it when you try to sleep on the plane.
I have two days in Jaipur. Where should I go first, the fort or the market?
Go to the fort first, early in the morning, when it is cool and less crowded. The market is better in the afternoon or evening when it is lively. How do you plan to get around?
By auto. I also want to eat something special.
Then ask your driver for a good dal baati or ghewar place, and have lunch after the fort. Fix the fare before you start, and keep small notes ready so payment is simple.
I will do the fort and the market on the first day. The second day is free. Any ideas?

Take an auto again to the observatory and the palace in the old city. If you want gifts, go back to the market in the evening, and try ghewar if you did not have it on the first day. Do not rush, since both places are big.
For Diwali holidays, I want to see my cousins but my mother says it is too far.
It is nice that you want to be with family. Perhaps there is a middle way. Where do the cousins live, and how long does it take?
In Hyderabad. About ten hours by bus.
That is a long ride, so a night bus might be comfortable if your mother agrees. Or your cousins might come to you for a couple of days. Why not ask your mother which option she prefers?
My cousin Farhan said they can come to us. Mom will like that.
That sounds easy for everyone. You can plan a small lamp decoration together and some sweets. Having Farhan and the others at home will make your Diwali joyful.
I am travelling to a city where I know no one. What if I feel lonely?
That feeling is natural. Plan small things that bring you into contact with people, like a walk in a park or a cafe. Why are you going there?
For a course. It is three months. I leave in a week.
Three months is a good time to make friends. Join the class group, say hello to neighbours, and find one regular spot, like a tea shop. Calling home on a fixed time each day will also help.
I will try. I think I will find a tea shop first.

Good start. Visit the same tea shop at the same hour for a few days, and the owner will soon greet you by name. Over your three months on the course, that friendly face can make the new city feel like home.
Guess what, I won a small prize in the school quiz! My teacher gave me a book.
Congratulations, that is wonderful news. All your studying paid off, and a book is a great prize. What is the book about?
It is about a boy who travels by train across India. I have not started yet.
That sounds like a fun one, and it is perfect for a train ride of your own. Read a few pages each night, and see if the places he visits match any you know.
My dad said we can read it together on our trip to Kolkata.
What a nice plan. Reading a book about train travel while on a train will make it feel real. You and your dad can take turns reading aloud and spot the places he mentions.
I dropped my train ticket somewhere on the platform and the guard is asking for it.
Check your pockets, bag and the place where you were standing. If it is gone, go to the ticket checker and explain honestly. Do you have a digital copy or a booking message?
Yes, I have a message with the booking number on my phone.
Show it to the guard along with your identity card. A booking message with the name and number usually proves you paid. Stay polite and answer any questions he asks.
He accepted it. I will keep the message open from now on.
A good habit. Also take a screenshot of the booking in case the phone has no signal. Keep your ID with you as well, since the guard will want to see it again.
I want to try the night bus to Bangalore. Is it comfortable?
It can be, if you pick a decent seat or sleeper and carry a few things. Take a light blanket, earplugs and a small bottle of water. Have you chosen a bus operator?
Not yet. My friend Olivia says to pick one with good reviews, and a seat near the middle.
Olivia gives good advice. The middle of the bus has less bumping than the back, and reviews tell you about cleanliness and timing. Check the pickup point too, so you do not have to travel far.
The pickup is a bit far from my home. Should I still go?

Think about getting there safely at night. If the pickup is far, pick another operator or ask a family member to drop you. Safety matters more than a slightly cheaper seat, and Olivia would likely agree.
I always get a window seat and I always fall asleep and miss my station. How do I stop that?
Set an alarm on your phone for ten minutes before the station, and put the phone in your hand, not in the bag. You can also ask the person beside you to nudge you. Which station do you get off at?
Kalyan. It is about an hour from where I board.

Then set the alarm for fifty minutes after you board and keep the volume high. You might also vibrate the phone against your leg. Sitting upright and holding a book can keep you from sinking too deep into sleep.
My friend Tara sometimes travels with me. She could wake me.
That works well, as long as she knows your stop. Tell her Kalyan clearly before you board, and still keep your own alarm as a backup, in case she dozes off as well.
Ha, true. What if she is not there one day?
Then rely on the alarm and ask a neighbour passenger. Most people are happy to help, and a quick, Please tell me when we reach Kalyan, is all it takes.
I forgot my grandmother's birthday yesterday. I feel terrible.
It is kind that you care so much. A late greeting is still welcome. Call her today and say sorry warmly. Would she be upset, do you think?
No, she is gentle. But she waited for my call, I think.
Then be honest and sweet. Say, Ajji, I am sorry I was late. Happy birthday. Tell her something you love about her, and ask how she spent the day. She will care more about your voice than the date.
I called. She laughed and said she knew I would call sometime.
What a gentle response. To make it up, you could send her a small card or plan a visit soon, so the birthday has a proper celebration after all.
I will visit next Sunday. Should I take a cake?

A small cake would be a lovely surprise, since you missed the actual day. Choose a flavour Ajji likes, and bring candles so you can sing to her. She laughed off the late call, so she will love a proper celebration.
Can you help me make a packing plan for a three day wedding in another city?
Of course. Weddings need several outfits, so start with those. How many events are there, and are any of them formal?
Four events: a mehendi, a sangeet, the wedding and a reception. The wedding is the most formal.
Then pack one outfit per event, plus a simple spare. Add matching accessories in a small pouch, comfortable shoes for dancing, and a safety pin kit. Iron or steam the main outfit before you leave.
My cousin Sana is in the same room. We could share some things.
That helps a lot. Share the iron, the hair dryer and the sewing kit with Sana, so each of you carries less. Decide who brings what before you pack, so you do not double up.
We agreed that I bring the safety pins and she brings the dryer. Anything else?
Take a small bag for gifts and the invitation card. And remember the pins, since you promised those to Sana. A pair of flat slippers will save your feet after hours of dancing.
I think we are on the wrong road. My uncle is driving and he refuses to ask for directions.
That can be frustrating. A gentle approach helps. Do you have any idea where you are heading, and how long you have been driving?
We are going to a temple near Nashik. We have driven for about forty minutes and nothing looks familiar.
Suggest a short stop for tea, and ask at the shop in a friendly way. You could say, Uncle, shall we check with the chaiwala? People often agree if it sounds like a break and not a criticism.
He stopped. The shopkeeper said we missed a turn about five kilometres back.
Good, now you know. It is better to turn around than to keep guessing. Thank the shopkeeper, and ask him which landmark marks the right turn so you do not miss it again.
He said look for a petrol pump with a blue roof.
Then watch for the petrol pump with the blue roof on your way back, and turn there. Tell your uncle too, so both of you can spot it, and the temple near Nashik will be close.
I have a free Saturday, and I need to choose between a trek and a movie.
A trek can give you fresh air and exercise, while a movie is easy and comfortable. How do you feel today, and what is the weather like?
Sunny and I feel restless. My friend Jack suggested the trek.
Restless usually means you need movement. The trek sounds right, and going with Jack will make it more fun. Wear good shoes and carry water and a small snack.
What if I get tired halfway?
Then rest and go at your own pace. Choose an easy trail for a first time, and tell Jack to keep the speed gentle. Turning back is fine, because the point is to enjoy it.
Okay, I will go. If it rains, then what?
Then take the movie plan as the backup. A rainy trek can be slippery, so with Jack you can switch to a film in the afternoon and still enjoy the day.
I have promised two friends I will visit them on the same day. Now I am stuck.
That happens when plans overlap. The best step is to be honest early. Are the two friends in the same city, and how long is each visit?
Same city, but different sides. Farhan wants lunch and Olivia wants me for the evening.
Then it can work, because lunch and evening are different times. Have lunch with Farhan, leave a little early, and travel across for Olivia. Check the distance so you do not arrive tired and late.
The trip takes an hour. Is that too much?
An hour is fine if you plan for it. Tell Olivia you may be slightly late, or ask if she can meet you halfway. Either way, tell both of them your plan in advance.
I will tell Farhan I must leave by three. Does that sound okay?
Yes, saying three o'clock to Farhan is clear and polite. That leaves you time for the hour of travel before the evening with Olivia, and nobody feels hurried.
How can I stay safe on a late evening bus?
Sit near the front, close to the driver or conductor, and stay aware of who is around you. Keep your phone charged and tell someone your stop. Are you travelling alone?
Yes, I get back from tuition at eight. The bus is usually half empty.
Then sit near other passengers, preferably other women or families, and keep your bag on your lap. Share your live location with a parent, and ask them to meet you at the stop when possible.
My dad can come to the stop if I call him from the bus.
That is an excellent plan. Call him when you are two stops away, so he is waiting when you get down. Wait to stand until the bus has nearly stopped, and walk to him straight.
Good. And if the bus is empty at that time?
If the bus is nearly empty, sit near the driver and keep your dad on the phone until you get off. You can also ask the conductor to tell you when your stop comes.
We are going to the zoo with my five year old nephew. What should I take?
Take water, simple snacks, a hat, sunscreen and wet wipes. A small stroller or a carrier helps if he gets tired. What does he love most?
Elephants. His name is Aryan, and he talks about elephants all day.
Then go to the elephant enclosure first, while Aryan has the most energy. Let him watch as long as he likes. Bring a small notebook where he can draw them, since children enjoy that.
He might ask a lot of questions about them.
That is wonderful. If you do not know an answer, say, Let us find out together. You can read the sign near the enclosure, or ask the keeper, and Aryan will feel proud.
Good. We will do the elephants first, then lunch. What if he wants to stay there the whole day?
Gently tell Aryan there are other animals to meet and that you can come back to the elephants before leaving. Let him wave goodbye to them first, and he should be willing to move on.
Holidays in my village are near and there is no network there at all.
A break from the phone can be a gift. Download music, books and games before you leave, and tell friends that you may be hard to reach. What will you do there?
Help my grandfather on the farm, and play with my cousins by the river.
That sounds peaceful. Wear clothes you do not mind getting dirty, and ask your grandfather to teach you something new, like planting or watering. You might enjoy the work more than you expect.
I think I will. What should I tell my friend Emma, who messages daily, about where I will be?

Send Emma a short message now, saying you will be in your village with no network, helping your grandfather on the farm. Tell her you will reply when you are back, and she will enjoy the river stories later.
I want to learn to read maps better. I always follow the phone and feel lost without it.
A good skill, and it is easy to practise. Start by looking at a paper or printed map of your own area and finding your house, school and the main roads. Do you have such a map?
No, but I can print one. I live near the big park in Indiranagar.
Then print the map, mark the park and your home, and trace routes to places you know. Notice the main roads and landmarks, such as the park, since those are easier to remember than street names.
I did that. Now I can see how the park connects to the market.
That is a real step forward. Next time you go out, walk from the park to the market and check the map as you go. Soon you will build a picture of Indiranagar in your head.
What should I do if the paper map confuses me?
Turn it so north points the same way you are facing, and find one landmark you know, like the park. Then work out the rest from there, one turn at a time.
My train leaves at six in the morning and I am terrible at waking up. Advice?
Prepare as much as possible the night before: pack the bag, lay out clothes and keep the ticket by the door. Then set two alarms. How far is the station from your home?
About thirty minutes by auto. My dad usually drives me but he is out of town.
Then book an auto the evening before, and ask the driver to come at a fixed time. Give him your phone number so he can call if you are late. Sleep early, because a tired mind snoozes more.
Good idea. I found a driver called Babu. He said he will come at five.
Great. Five o'clock gives you a safe buffer. Put Babu's number in your phone, and send him a reminder message at bedtime so he does not forget about the early pick up.
What if he does not turn up?
Keep a backup: ask a neighbour or a friend who lives nearby, or find the number of a second auto stand. Wake up with enough time to try both before the train leaves.
Okay. I will set the alarm for 4:30. Who did I book again, and when does he come?
You booked Babu, the auto driver, and he will come at five. Your alarm at half past four gives you thirty minutes to get ready before he arrives.
My grandparents are moving into our house next month. I will have to share my room with my little brother.
That is a big change. Having your grandparents close is lovely, but giving up your room is not easy. How do you feel about it?
Mixed. I will miss my space, but I like having them around. My brother Aditya is eight and messy.
That is understandable. You could set up clear rules with Aditya, like a line on the floor or a shelf that is only yours. Ask him to help decide, so he feels fair about it.
Good point. Maybe I can also keep my desk area private.
Yes, a desk area is a good boundary. Put up a small sign, or use a screen from a cardboard box. Tell Aditya it is for homework time, and he can have a similar place for his toys.
My grandmother says she will tidy for us. I do not want her to work.
That is kind of you. Tell her gently that you and Aditya will manage the room, and ask her to teach you recipes instead. She may be happier sharing skills than cleaning.
I will talk to her. Is it fine to say I like having Aditya as a roommate even though I am not sure?

A small white lie like that is not needed. You can say honestly that you are still getting used to sharing with Aditya, but you are happy to try. Honest words usually build trust with a younger brother.
I took a wrong turn in a mall and ended up in a car park. I cannot find my friends.
Stay calm. Go back to a lit area or to a mall entrance, and call one of your friends. Is your phone working?
Yes, but nobody answers. I think they are in the food court.
Then walk to the nearest information board or ask a security guard how to reach the food court. Keep trying to call, and send a message saying where you are. Which floor is the food court on?
The second floor. I am on the ground level near gate three.

Then take the escalator or lift near gate three up to the second floor. Look for signs with a fork and spoon. When you arrive, call your friends again, since the noise may have stopped them hearing the phone.
I reached the food court and saw Tara waving. She was worried.
Good. Tell her you are fine, and next time agree on a meeting spot in case you get separated. Something simple like the pillar near the main door works.
Okay. Which gate was I at, and which floor did I need?
You were near gate three on the ground level, and the food court is on the second floor. If this happens again, tell Tara that gate three is your meeting spot.
My uncle is taking me fishing on Sunday. I have never held a fishing rod.
That sounds like a calm and fun day. Fishing needs patience more than skill. What time do you start?
Very early, about five in the morning, at a pond near his house. His name is Uncle Ravi.
Dress warmly, since mornings by water are cool, and wear shoes that can get wet. Listen to Uncle Ravi when he shows how to hold the rod. He will give you a few tips to begin.
What if I do not catch anything?
Many people do not, even the experts. The best part is the quiet time by the water and the chat. Take a flask of tea and some biscuits, and enjoy the morning.
I like that. Should I take a camera?
A phone camera is enough. Keep it in a plastic bag in case it gets wet, and take a picture of the sunrise over the pond. You can show it to your family later.
Great. Remind me, who is taking me and what time do we go?
Uncle Ravi is taking you, and you start at five in the morning at the pond near his house. Set your alarm early and pack your tea and biscuits the night before.
Our class is planning a farewell trip, but the teachers are asking us to pick a place within a day's drive.
Good, a day trip is easier to manage. What kind of place does your class like? Is it nature, fun rides, or something to learn from?
Most want a water park. A few want a museum. I am in charge of collecting votes.
Then make a simple list on paper or a message, ask each classmate to choose one, and count the results. A fair method keeps everyone happy, even if their choice does not win.
The water park got nineteen votes. The museum got eight.
That is a clear result. Tell the class and the teachers the winner. Thank the museum supporters, and maybe suggest the museum for another outing so their idea is not forgotten.
Good idea. The teacher, Mrs. Fernandes, wants a list of names.
Then make a clean list in alphabetical order, and ask each student to confirm. Include parent contact numbers if the school needs them, so Mrs. Fernandes has everything in one place.
Done. Who did I say asked for the list, and which place won?
Mrs. Fernandes asked for the list of names, and the water park won the vote. Hand her the list soon so she can organise permission slips and the bus.
There is a girl on my bus who always looks sad and sits alone. Should I talk to her?
It is kind of you to notice. A small hello can mean a lot. You do not need to ask anything personal. Do you see her every day?
Mostly, yes. She gets on at Gandhi Park and carries a big sketchbook.
A sketchbook is a good way to start. You could ask, That looks interesting, do you draw? People often enjoy talking about what they love. Smile and keep it light.
I did. She said she draws birds and her name is Anjali.
That is a lovely start. Anjali may be shy, so give her time. Ask her what bird she likes most, and listen. You do not have to be best friends right away.
She showed me a drawing of a kingfisher. It was beautiful.
Tell her so, and be specific about what you liked, like the colours or the fine details. A real compliment will brighten her day, and she may show you more.
Maybe I can ask her to draw one for me. Is that too much?
Wait a few days and then ask, since Anjali has only just opened up. You could say you would love a small kingfisher drawing, and offer to swap it for something small of yours.
Our school trek is coming up and the teacher gave us a list, but I do not understand some things.
Tell me the items you are unsure about, and I will explain. What is on the list?
One thing says energy food and another says a ground sheet.
Energy food is light snacks that give you quick strength, like nuts, dates, chikki or glucose biscuits. A ground sheet is a plastic or cloth sheet you sit or lie on, so you stay dry and clean.
Okay. And what about a whistle? That is on the list too.
A whistle is for safety. If you get separated from the group, three loud blasts tell others you need help. Keep it on a string around your neck, not at the bottom of the bag.
Good to know. Do I need a rain jacket if it is not forecast to rain?
Yes, take a thin one. Mountain weather can change quickly, and a jacket weighs very little. It also keeps the wind off when you rest.
Thanks. What was the first thing I asked about, and what is it for?
The first was energy food, such as nuts, dates or chikki, which gives you quick strength on the trek. Pack a small bag of it where you can reach it without stopping.
First time at the sea this week with my family. What should I know?
The sea is wonderful, and a few rules keep it safe. Stay in shallow water, watch the flags if there are any, and never swim alone. How old are you, and can you swim?
I am twelve and I cannot swim well. My sister Neha can.
Then stay near the shore and hold an adult's hand when waves come. Waves can be stronger than they look. Enjoy the wet sand and shells, and let Neha show you how she moves in the water.
Can I build sandcastles too?
Yes, and the best ones are made near the wet sand, where it holds its shape. Use a bucket for towers and dig a moat around the castle. The sea may wash it away, which is part of the fun.
Neha says she will help me build a big one. What should we do about the sun?
Wear a hat, put on sunscreen and drink water often. Take a break under an umbrella after an hour. Your skin burns quickly at the sea, even on cloudy days.
Good. What did you say about being in the water since I cannot swim well?
Stay near the shore in shallow water and hold an adult's hand when the waves come. Neha can swim, but you should still keep an adult nearby.
I want to spend my holidays learning something instead of just sitting at home.
A great plan. What kind of thing interests you: music, cooking, art, a sport, or a language?
Cooking. But my mother says the kitchen is too busy in the morning.
Then pick a quiet time, like late afternoon, when the kitchen is free. Choose one easy dish a week, like upma, an omelette or a sandwich, and ask your mother to guide you for the first steps.
I like that. My brother Rahul will be my taster.
Rahul will make an honest judge. Keep a small notebook to write down what you cooked, and what Rahul said. Over time you can see what improved, and share the best recipes.
By the end of the holidays I could cook a whole meal for the family.
That is a good goal, and a very doable one. Try one dish each week and add a side dish in the last week. By then you will cook a meal with confidence.
Which dish should I start with, and who will taste it?
Start with a simple dish like upma, which is quick and hard to ruin. Rahul will taste it, and ask him to be honest, so you learn what to change next time.
A stranger on the train offered me some of his food. Should I take it?
It is polite to say no thank you, even if he seems friendly. Accepting food from strangers on a journey is not safe. Is he sitting close to you?
Yes, he is across from me. He says he is travelling to Surat too.
You can be pleasant without taking anything. Say, Thank you, I have my own food. If you feel uneasy, move to a seat near other families or tell the ticket checker or a coach attendant.
I moved next to an aunty who is travelling with her two children.
Good choice. Families usually make a seat feel safer. You can chat with her a little, and stay alert until you reach Surat. Keep your bag on your lap.
She offered me a biscuit. Is that all right?
A biscuit from a family sitting next to you, in a sealed packet, is much lower risk, and you can see it is shared with her children. Still, you can refuse politely if you prefer your own food.
My grandfather forgets things sometimes and it makes me sad.
I am sorry, that must be hard to watch. Memory changes are common as people age. Is your family helping him?
Yes, my mom takes him to the doctor. His name is Dada Prakash and he loves cricket on the radio.
That is a good sign that your mother is taking care. You can spend time with Dada Prakash listening to cricket and chatting about old matches. Old memories are often the clearest ones.
He remembered a match from 1983 perfectly today.
What a lovely moment. Ask him more about it, and maybe write it down so the family keeps the story. It will also make him happy to be remembered for what he knows.
I will write it in a small diary and read it to him.
That is thoughtful. Reading the diary aloud to Dada Prakash will give him joy and keep the old stories alive. Add a new memory each week, and let him add details too.
I always forget something when I travel. Is there a trick?
Make a list a few days before, and tick things off as you pack. Keep a standard list for toiletries and chargers. What do you forget the most?
Mostly my toothbrush and chargers.
Then put those on the top of your list and keep a spare toothbrush and charger in the bag all the time. Pack them first, so they are never an afterthought.
A spare charger. That is smart. I think I will buy a cheap one.
A cheap spare is a good buy, and a long cable helps in trains and hotels. Keep it in a small pouch with your toothbrush, so the pouch itself becomes your reminder.
My little cousin Emma was lost at the railway station for ten minutes. We found her, but I am shaking.
That must have been very scary. Take a few slow breaths and sit down. Emma is safe now, which is the most important thing. Where was she?
She was near the tea stall, holding a balloon someone gave her.
Thank goodness. It is a good moment to teach her what to do in a crowd, in a gentle way. Tell Emma to stay still and call for help, and to look for a uniformed person.
She is only five. Does she understand that?

A simple version works for a five year old. Teach Emma: If you cannot see us, stand still and shout. Practise it like a game, and put a card with your phone number in her pocket so a helper can call you.
I need to study all weekend but I also want to relax. I feel stuck.
You can do both with a plan. Break the work into small blocks with real breaks in between. What do you need to study?
Chemistry and some history. The test is on Monday.

Study chemistry on Saturday morning when your mind is fresh, then history on Sunday morning. Use the afternoons to relax, go out or see a friend. Short breaks every forty minutes help you remember more.
That seems doable. On Saturday evening Farhan wants me to come for a walk.
Then go for it. A walk with Farhan is a good break, and fresh air helps your mind settle. Just be back by dinner and look at your chemistry notes once before sleeping.
We had planned a trip to the zoo, but my sister Mia fell ill.
I am sorry to hear that. Her health comes first. Is it a mild illness or does she need to rest for some days?
Just a fever. She should be better in two days.
Then postpone the zoo trip by a few days. Mia needs to rest, and a trip while she is weak would not be fun. Meanwhile, you could plan something small at home, like a movie or a board game.
Good. Mia likes drawing. I could bring her paper and colours.
That is a kind gesture. Draw something together on her bed, like the animals you will see at the zoo. It will cheer her up and build excitement for the trip.
My daily bus has changed its route and now I walk fifteen minutes to the new stop.
That is annoying, but a daily walk has a small benefit for your health. Is the walk safe, and does it take you through well lit streets?
Mostly yes. There is one dark stretch near an empty plot.

For the dark stretch, walk with a friend if you can, or at a quick pace, and keep your phone torch ready. You can also ask the local police or municipality to fix the street light, since others must face it too.
I will ask my neighbour Aditya to walk with me. He goes the same way.
That is a very sensible choice. Walking together with Aditya makes the dark stretch less worrying, and you will have someone to chat with on the way to the new stop.
Our family is visiting the Taj Mahal on Sunday. Is it worth getting up early?
Yes, early is better. The crowds are smaller, the light is soft, and it is cooler. Many people find the sunrise view special. Who is going?
Mom, dad, my grandmother and me. Grandmother cannot walk fast.
Then plan a slow visit and book tickets in advance so you do not stand in long queues. Ask the staff whether a wheelchair is available for your grandmother, and rest on the benches in the gardens.
Mom says to carry water and a cap. Anything else for grandmother?
Bring her medicines, a light shawl and a small cushion for the benches. Keep snacks she likes in the bag. Walk at her pace, and make her comfort the main plan of the day.
Good. Should we go to see the sunrise anyway?
If she can wake up early without strain, yes, but you can also go a little later when it is calmer for her. Her comfort matters more than the exact time of the sunrise.
I am so excited because we are going to Sikkim for the winter break!
That sounds beautiful. Sikkim has mountains, monasteries and lovely weather in winter. How long will you stay?
Seven days. My friend Jack is coming with his family and we are going together.
A trip with Jack will be even more fun. Pack warm layers, thermals, gloves, and sturdy shoes, since it can be very cold. Book rooms with heating if you can.
Jack wants to see snow. Will we see any?

In winter, higher places in Sikkim often get snow, but it depends on the year and the weather. Ask your hotel or driver once you are there, and keep the plan flexible so Jack can still enjoy the trip.
I got my passport today! I have never been abroad.
Congratulations, that is a big step and a fun one. Where would you like to go first with your new passport?
Maybe Singapore. My aunt Sana lives there and has invited me.

That is a good first trip, as you will have family to guide you. Check the entry rules and the visa requirements on the official website well in advance. Then plan your dates around your aunt's availability.
She said she will pick me up from the airport.
That will make arrival much easier. Share your flight details with Aunt Sana a few days before, so she knows when to come, and keep her phone number saved in your phone and on paper.
My day so far has been strange. First, I woke up late and ran to the bus stop.
Sounds like a busy start. Did you manage to catch your bus, or did it leave without you?
It was just leaving but the driver saw me running and waited. His name tag said Vijay.
That was kind of Vijay. A small act like that can change a whole morning. How did the rest of the day go?
Good. I told my friend Neha about it and she said I should thank him tomorrow.
Neha is right. A quick thank you to Vijay tomorrow would be a nice gesture. You could say, Thank you for waiting yesterday. He will likely remember you and smile.
I have been waiting at the bus stop for an hour and no bus has come.
That is tiring. Buses sometimes get delayed because of traffic or a breakdown. Is there anyone who can tell you, like a shopkeeper nearby?
A tea seller says the road ahead is blocked for a procession.
Then it may take a while. You could use another route, such as a shared auto, or walk to a stop on the other side. Ask the tea seller which road is clear.
He says buses are running from the next stop. I will walk there.
Good. Before you go, tell your family where you are heading, and keep to the main road. If the tea seller was helpful, buy a cup of chai from him as a thank you.
Packing a lunch for my daughter's school trip tomorrow. She is seven.
Keep it simple and easy to eat, like a sandwich or a roll, a fruit, and a small snack. Use a leak proof box and a water bottle. Does she have any allergies?
No allergies. She likes cheese sandwiches and grapes.
Then a cheese sandwich cut into small pieces, a small box of grapes, and a few biscuits will be just right. Pack a napkin and a small spoon in case.
Also a letter. She is nervous and I want to tuck a note in her bag.

A small note is a lovely idea. Write something short and warm, like, Have fun today, I am proud of you. Tuck it next to the cheese sandwich and grapes, and she will smile when she opens her lunch on the trip.
I planted tomato seeds last week and nothing has come up. I'm Ananya.
Seeds can take a week or two, so do not worry yet. Where did you plant them, and how often do you water?
In a pot on the balcony. I water every morning.
Daily watering is fine if the soil dries quickly, but too much water can rot seeds. Touch the soil with your finger. If it is damp an inch down, skip a day.
It felt very wet today. Should I stop?
Yes, skip watering for a day or two and let the top dry slightly. Make sure the pot has holes at the bottom so extra water can drain out. Seeds need moisture, not a puddle.
How long until I see leaves?
Tomato seeds usually sprout in one to two weeks, so yours should appear soon. Keep the pot in a warm, sunny spot. If nothing shows after three weeks, you can try a fresh seed.
Okay, I'll wait till next week. Where did I plant them again?
You planted them in a pot on your balcony, Ananya. That spot sounds good as long as it gets sunlight. Check the soil each morning and keep an eye out for little green shoots.
Is it better to learn football from a coach or from friends in the street?
Both help in different ways. Friends in the street give fun and quick thinking. A coach gives skills, fitness and rules of play. Many good players have done both. What are you hoping to improve?
Mostly passing and stamina. My cousin Ritu says her coach is good, but the fees are high.
If fees are a worry, ask whether the school or a local club has a cheaper group. Meanwhile, you can practise passing against a wall and go running in the park to build stamina.
Can you remind me what Ritu's coach was good at?
I only know what you said, that Ritu's coach is good, and that the fees are high. You did not say what the coach does best, so ask Ritu what she has learned from the coach.
I'm Lily and I'm the only girl in my street football group. Sometimes the boys don't pass to me.
That sounds frustrating, Lily. You deserve to be included. Have you spoken to them about it?
No. I don't want a fight.
You can say it calmly without a fight. Something like, 'I'm open, so pass to me, and I'll score.' Then show them with good play when you get the ball.
What if they still ignore me?
Ask a friend in the group, like the one who treats you well, to support you. If it continues, you could talk to an older person in the street who can help the group play fairly.
Karan is nice to me. Maybe I'll talk to him.
That is a good plan, Lily. Karan can pass to you and encourage the others to do the same. Start by asking him quietly before the next game.
I'm Aisha. My art teacher said my shading is too dark. How do I fix it?
Dark shading often comes from pressing too hard too early. Do you use one pencil for everything?
Yes, a 2B. I press hard to get the shadows.
Try pressing lightly and building up the shadow in layers. Light layers are easy to fix and give a smooth look. Also keep some parts of the page almost white for the light areas.
Should I use a different pencil?
A harder pencil like HB for the light areas, and your 2B only for the darkest shadows, can help. Using two pencils gives you control over the tones.
I'll try both. My teacher also said I should get a better eraser.
She is right. A kneaded eraser is soft and can lift a little graphite, so you can lighten areas that went too dark without rubbing a hole in the paper.
Okay. What did my teacher say about my shading?
She said your shading is too dark, Aisha. Press lightly, build the shadows in layers, and use the 2B only for the deepest areas, with an HB for the lighter parts.
I'm teaching my younger cousin Lily to ride. I'm Noah and I'm fourteen.
That is kind of you, Noah. How old is Lily, and does she have a bike of the right size?
She's seven. Her bike is a bit big, but my aunt says she will grow into it.
A bike that is too big makes learning harder, since she must reach the pedals and ground. Lower the seat as far as it goes, and she should be able to touch the ground with her toes.
I lowered it. She can touch with her toes now.
Good. Let her glide first, pushing with her feet and lifting them off the ground, to get a feeling for balance. Pedalling comes after she can glide a few metres.
She wants to pedal right away. She is very stubborn.
Keep it fun. Let her try a few pedal turns, then go back to gliding when she wobbles. Praise her for each small success, and she will enjoy the practice.
What was the problem with her bike?
It is a little big for her, Noah. You lowered the seat so her toes touch the ground, which is a good fix. She can grow into it as she gets taller.
I can't kick with my left foot at all. I'm Ritu. Is it too late to fix it?
It is never too late, Ritu. Many players improve their weaker foot with regular practice. Start with simple passes against a wall.
Okay. How many times a day?
Do about fifteen minutes each day, using only your left foot. Pass the ball against a wall, receive it, and pass it again. Keep the touches soft.
It feels strange and slow.
That is normal. The weak foot needs time to learn. Be patient and focus on clean contact with the ball, not on power.
Should I use the left foot in games too?
Yes, in easy moments, like short passes when no one is near. That builds trust. Use it slowly in games, and soon you will feel comfortable.
What foot am I training?
Your left foot, Ritu. Keep passing against the wall each day, and use it in simple moments during games, so your weaker foot gets stronger.
I want to draw my grandmother as a gift for her birthday. I'm Lily.
What a lovely gift, Lily. Do you have a clear photo of her that you can look at while you draw? A photo helps you copy the shapes and keep her likeness.
There is one from Diwali where she's smiling in a green saree.
That sounds perfect. A smile shows warmth. Draw her face lightly first, then the saree folds, since folds are made of long soft lines. Add the green colour last, so the face stays the focus.
How should I show the saree border?

Draw the border as two thin lines that follow the curve of the folds, then fill the space between with a pattern, like tiny dots or leaves. It will make your grandmother's green saree stand out in the picture.
Dad wants me to join a cricket academy. I'm Ritu, and I'm not sure.
It is okay to feel unsure, Ritu. An academy means regular training and discipline. Do you enjoy cricket?
I love it, but the academy is two hours away by bus.
Two hours each way is a lot, especially with school. Ask if there is a nearer coach or a weekend batch. You could also try a trial day first, to see how it feels.
Dad says he'll drive me on Saturdays only.
That sounds more manageable. Saturday sessions give you time for school during the week. Talk to the coach about what you can practise at home between Saturdays.
Good. What was the problem with the academy?
The academy is two hours away by bus, Ritu. A Saturday drive with your dad solves the long trip, so a trial day on a Saturday is a good way to decide.
How many hours should a beginner practise piano each day?
For a beginner, twenty to thirty minutes a day is plenty. Short, focused sessions are better than a long one once a week. What age are you, or who are you asking for?
For my daughter Lily. She's seven.

At seven, fifteen to twenty minutes is enough. Break it into small parts: a few minutes of scales, a few on the new piece, and a few playing something she loves. Keep it playful so she wants to return.
She dislikes scales though.
Many children do. You can turn scales into a game, like playing them softly and then loudly, or racing against a timer. Short and fun beats long and dull, especially at her age.
I will try that with Lily tonight. Any tip for when she gets stuck on a piece?
Ask Lily to play only the hard bar, slowly, three times. Do not rush her. When she gets it right, praise the effort. Practising a small part at a time stops her from getting frustrated.
What do you do when you don't understand a word while reading?
First, try to guess from the sentence around it. If it still is not clear, look it up in a dictionary and write it in a small notebook. That way you learn it for good. Are you reading something hard?
A story with old words, called a classic. I'm Siddharth.
Classics have many old words. Do not worry about every one. Look up only the ones that appear again and again, since those matter most. The rest you can understand from the story.
Should I use a paper dictionary or an online one for the classic?
Either works. A paper dictionary is good because you notice nearby words too. An online one is faster. Choose whichever you will actually use, Siddharth, so that the classic does not become a chore.
My cousin Siddharth thinks cricket is better than football. I disagree. I'm Dev.
Both games have strong fans. Siddharth might like the strategy of cricket, and you may like the speed of football. Why do you prefer football?
It's faster, and everyone is always moving.
That is a fair point. In football there is constant action, and every player is involved. In cricket there are quiet moments, but they build to big ones.
What does Siddharth like about cricket?
I do not know, since you have not told me. Ask Siddharth. He may say he likes the long contest between batter and bowler, or the team strategy.
I'll ask him. Maybe we can play both. Who did I say prefers cricket?
Your cousin Siddharth prefers cricket, Dev, and you prefer football. Playing both sounds like a fair plan, with football one day and cricket the next.
Karan here. Dad says I should give up my video games and take up a hobby outdoors.
A balance is helpful, Karan. Games are fun, and outdoor time is good for your body and mind. Is there something outside you would try?
Maybe birdwatching. I've seen parrots on the wall near our house.
Birdwatching is a lovely hobby and needs very little. Watch quietly, note the colour and size, and try to identify the bird with a picture book. Parrots are a great start.
I don't have binoculars though.
You can start without them. Many birds come close if you sit still. A notebook and pencil are enough to note what you see, and you can add binoculars later.
Okay. Which bird did I say I'd seen near my house?
You said parrots, on the wall near your house, Karan. Sit still in the same spot each morning, write down how many come, and note their colours. Your dad may enjoy joining you.
I have a tabla exam next month. Dev, my teacher, says I need to improve my taal.
Preparing for an exam takes steady work, so a month is a good amount of time. Which taal is giving you trouble?
Teentaal. I speed up in the second half.
Speeding up is very common. Practise with a slow metronome or a clock tick, and say the bols aloud while you play. Saying the syllables helps your hands stay steady through all sixteen beats.
Can I practise without the tabla? It is at the music school.
Yes. Tap Teentaal on your knees or a table, and say the bols aloud. You can practise the rhythm and the timing anywhere. When you reach the school, your hands will already know the pattern.
Okay, I'll do that on the bus. What was the taal I should fix first?
Teentaal, the one where you speed up in the second half. Fix that first, since it is in your exam. Tap it on the bus slowly and keep the second half as steady as the first.
Squirrels keep digging up my flower pots. Ritu here, and I'm fed up.
That is annoying, Ritu. Squirrels dig for food or to bury nuts. Are you planting bulbs or seeds that they might want?
Mostly marigold seeds and some bulbs.
They may be looking for bulbs. Try covering the soil with small stones or a piece of mesh, with holes for the plants to come through. Squirrels dislike digging through that.
Is there a way to keep them away without hurting them?
Yes. Stones or mesh do not hurt them. Some gardeners also scatter a little dried chilli powder around the pot edge, but keep it away from your hands and eyes. Moving the pots higher can also help.
Do you think the mesh will work for the marigold pots?
It should work well for your marigold pots, Ritu. Cut the mesh to fit the pot, leave space for the stems, and press it down gently. Check it after the first rain to see whether it stays in place.
What does offside mean? My dad explains it but I get confused.
A player is offside if, when a teammate passes the ball forward, they are closer to the opponent's goal line than the last defender. It stops players from just waiting near the goal.
So if I stay level with the defender, it's okay?
Yes, being level with the last defender is allowed. You are only offside if you are ahead of them when the pass is made, and you are in the opponent's half.
Then why do people shout offside even when the ball hasn't reached the player yet?

The moment that counts is when the pass is made, not when the ball arrives. If the player was ahead of the last defender then, it is offside, even if they run back later. That is why staying level, as you asked, keeps you safe.
I want to get better at dribbling. Any exercises at home?
Yes. Place five bottles or shoes in a row, about one step apart, and weave the ball between them using both feet. Start slowly and speed up as the touches get cleaner.
I only have a small balcony. Is that okay?

A balcony works fine if you keep the ball close. Do tiny touches with the inside and outside of your foot while standing in place, or move between two cones only a few steps apart. Soft touches build control.
I'll try the bottles in the balcony then. Dev says I should also try juggling.
Dev is right. Juggling helps your first touch. Start by letting the ball bounce once between kicks. Do that after your bottle weave, and you will build control from two sides.
I want to read more but my phone distracts me. Any ideas?
Try keeping your phone in another room when you read, even for twenty minutes. Having to get up to check it makes you think twice. Do you have a favourite place to read?
My bed, but I end up on the phone. I'm Ritu.
Then try a different spot, like a chair near a window, only for reading. Your brain learns that this place is for books. Keep a book and a glass of water there.
I like that. Should I set a timer?
A timer can help. Twenty minutes is a good start, Ritu. When it rings, you can stop or keep reading if you are enjoying the book. Often you will keep going.
I want a small herb garden in my kitchen window. I'm Karan.
Good idea, Karan. Herbs like mint, coriander and basil grow well in small pots by a sunny window. How much sun does your window get?
About four hours in the morning.
Four hours is decent. Basil and coriander like sun. Mint is happy with a little less and spreads quickly, so give it its own pot.
Why does mint need its own pot?
Mint grows long roots that take over the pot and push out other plants. Keeping it alone saves your basil and coriander from being crowded.
Okay. I'll start with basil and mint. How often should I water them?
Water basil when the top of the soil feels dry, about every two days. Mint likes more moisture, so check it daily. A small pot dries faster than a big one, so feel the soil first.
Thanks. Which two herbs did I pick?
You picked basil and mint, Karan. Put them in separate pots, since mint spreads fast, and place both on the window that gets the four hours of morning sun.
My bicycle chain keeps slipping. How do I fix it? I'm Dev.
A slipping chain may be loose, rusty or worn. Look at the chain. Is it dry or dirty?
It looks dry and has some rust.
Wipe off the dirt with a cloth, then put a few drops of chain oil on it, and turn the pedals so the oil spreads. Wipe any extra off, so it does not collect dust.
What if it still slips?
Then the chain may be stretched or the gear worn. Take it to a cycle repair shop, where it can be replaced cheaply. Ask an adult to go with you, Dev.
Do you think knitting is only for grandmothers? I'm Aisha, and I'm twelve.
Not at all, Aisha. People of all ages knit, and many find it calming. What made you think about it?
My grandmother is teaching me. I made a very crooked scarf.
A crooked first scarf is normal. Every knitter has one. The crooked edges usually come from adding or dropping stitches without noticing. It improves quickly.
How do I stop the edges from going crooked?
Count your stitches at the end of each row, and keep the same number every time. If the count changes, you can fix it early. Your grandmother can show you where you added one.
I'm Ava. My little sister Lily keeps kicking the football into our neighbour's garden.
That sounds like a busy afternoon for you! Neighbours often understand, but it helps to be polite. Does Lily go and fetch it herself, or do you do that?
I go and ring their bell. Mr. Rao is kind but he looks tired of it.
Then maybe a small thank-you would help, like a drawing from Lily. Also, try moving the game to a different corner or to the park nearby, so the ball stays away from Mr. Rao's plants.
The park is a bit far. Could we just play with a softer ball?
A softer ball is a good idea. It will not damage Mr. Rao's flowers if it lands there. It also works well for Lily, since a lighter ball is easier for a small girl to kick.
How can I remember more of what I read? I forget everything after a week.
A simple way is to write two or three lines after each chapter, in your own words. It takes only a minute and helps the memory stick. Do you read for school or for fun?
For fun, mostly detective stories. I'm Siddharth.
For detective stories, you could keep a small notebook with the clues. Write each suspect's name and one fact about them. It makes the story more fun and you will remember who did what.
That sounds like a game. Can I also draw the suspects?
Yes, Siddharth. Quick drawings of faces or objects help memory, since you link a picture with a name. Keep them small and simple so they do not slow your reading.
Perfect. What was it I should write for each suspect again?
Write the suspect's name and one fact about them, like where they were or what they said. After a few chapters, you can compare the facts and see who is lying.
I got a cramp in my leg while swimming. It scared me. I'm Siddharth.
That sounds scary. Cramps can happen when you are tired or cold. What did you do?
I stopped and held onto the wall. It went away after a minute.
That was a smart thing to do. Hold the wall, stretch the leg slowly, and rest. Tell your coach, and warm up properly before each swim.
Should I stop swimming for a few days?
If you feel fine, you can swim again, but take it easy and tell an adult if the cramps come back. If you are worried, ask a doctor to check.
Okay. What should I do before swimming?
Do a short warm-up with light movements, like arm circles and leg swings, and a few easy laps. Drink water too, Siddharth, and always swim where an adult can see you.
Can you explain what a penalty is? My cousin is confused. I'm Dev.
A penalty is a free shot at the goal from a mark near the goal, given when a defender fouls an attacker inside the penalty box. Only the shooter and the goalkeeper take part.
Why does it happen inside the box only?
The box is the area near the goal where a foul is most harmful, because it stops a chance to score. Fouls outside the box give a free kick instead, which is less dangerous.
That makes sense. Is it hard to score from one?
It is easy to miss if you panic. Most players aim for a corner and shoot hard. Goalkeepers try to guess the side.
Okay. I'll explain it to my cousin. What was the reason for the box?
The box is where fouls hurt most, since they stop a clear chance to score, Dev. So a foul inside the box earns a penalty, and a foul outside only gets a free kick.
Can you help me name my cricket team? We are eight boys from one lane in Pune.
Sure. Since you share a lane, you could use the lane name, like Lane Lions or Gully Giants. Does your lane have a nickname or a landmark nearby, like a temple or a tree?
There is a big neem tree where we play. Everyone calls the spot the Neem Corner.
Then Neem Corner Kings sounds great. It is short, easy to shout, and tells people where you are from. You could also try Neem Warriors if you want something stronger.
I like the first one. Ananya said we should add a motto too.
Ananya has a good idea. Something like 'Under the neem, we play as one' would match Neem Corner Kings. Keep it short enough that eight of you can shout it together.
Our school band needs a drummer and nobody wants to do it. Should I volunteer? Karan here.
Being the drummer is an important job because the whole band follows your beat. Have you played drums before?
No, but I play the dholak at home during festivals.
That helps a lot, Karan. Dholak gives you a good sense of rhythm and hand coordination. A drum kit uses sticks and feet, so you will need to practise, but your beat sense is already there.
Do you think the teacher will let me try?
Most teachers welcome a keen volunteer. Tell the band teacher that you play dholak and are willing to practise. Offer to try a simple beat for a short song, so they can hear you.
Good. Should I mention that I've never used sticks?
Yes, be honest about the sticks, Karan. Say you play the dholak well and are ready to learn the kit. Teachers like honesty and a willing student, and they can show you a basic grip.
Can anyone learn to sing, or do you need to be born with a good voice?
Almost anyone can improve. Some people start with an easier voice, but breathing, pitch and practice can be learned. Do you want to learn for yourself, or for a group?
For myself. I sing in the bathroom but my brother laughs. I'm Dev.

Do not let that stop you, Dev. Many people feel shy at first. Singing in the bathroom is a fine start, since the walls make your voice sound full. Try singing along with a recording, matching each note.
What if I go out of tune?
Going out of tune is part of learning. Sing slowly and listen carefully. When a note feels off, stop and sing it again, aiming to match the recording. Your ear will improve with practice.
Should I tell my brother to stop laughing?
You could say calmly that you are learning and his laughing makes it harder. Many brothers stop when they see you are serious. Then maybe even invite him to sing along sometime, Dev.
I'm Ananya. I'm afraid of diving. My coach wants me to try on Saturday.
Diving feels scary at first because your head goes down. Your coach will begin small. Does she start from the pool edge?
I think so. She said sit-down dives first.
Sit-down dives are a good start. You sit on the edge, put your hands together over your head, tuck your chin, and fall in slowly. It is a gentle way to get used to going head-first.
What if I belly flop?
A belly flop stings a bit but is not dangerous, and many beginners do it. Tuck your chin and keep your arms straight above your head, and you will go in smoothly.
Okay. Can my mother come to watch?
Yes, Ananya. Ask your coach if parents can sit near the pool. Having your mother there may make you feel braver on Saturday.
What kind of dive did the coach say?
The coach said a sit-down dive first, Ananya. You sit on the pool edge, hands together above your head, chin tucked, and slide in gently.
Our school is starting a garden club and I'm in charge of the compost. I'm Aisha.
Congratulations, Aisha. Compost turns waste into food for plants, so it is a useful job. Do you know what goes in?
Vegetable peels and dry leaves, I think.
That is right. Add peels, fruit scraps, dry leaves and tea leaves. Avoid cooked food, meat and dairy, since they smell and attract pests. Keep it a bit moist and turn it once a week.
How long until it turns into soil?
In warm weather, about six to eight weeks if you turn it and keep it damp. It will look dark and crumbly and smell earthy when it is ready.
Can we add the canteen's leftover rice?
Cooked rice is better left out, because it can attract rats and smell. Stick to raw vegetable and fruit waste from the canteen, plus dry leaves from the school grounds.
Got it. So what were the two things we can use, the ones I first said?
You said vegetable peels and dry leaves, Aisha. Both are right. Fruit scraps and tea leaves can go in too, and just keep out cooked food, meat and dairy.
I'm learning to sing a ghazal and I don't understand the Urdu words. Aisha here.
That is a good thing to notice, Aisha. When you know what you sing, your feeling comes through. Does your teacher explain the meanings?
She says to look them up, but it takes so long.
You could ask her to explain one line each class, and write the meaning in simple English above the line. Over time, you will learn many words together.
That's a nice idea. Do you think I should learn a different language song for variety?

Yes, but only after you are comfortable with the ghazal. Trying another language later gives your voice new shapes to practise. For now, understanding your ghazal will make it sound much more natural.
Okay. Let me do the one-line plan first. How many lines should I write in a week?
Two or three lines a week is steady and not tiring. Write the meaning above each line of the ghazal, and sing it again after each one. In a month you will understand the whole piece, Aisha.
Do plants really grow better with music? Noah's cousin says so.
Some people believe it, but scientists have not found strong proof. Plants respond more clearly to light, water and soil. The gentle vibrations may help a little, but it is not certain.
So I don't need to play music for my plants?
No, you do not need to. If you enjoy music while gardening, there is no harm. Your own mood may improve and you may look after the plants better.
What matters most then?
Sunlight, the right amount of water, good soil and some space for roots. Get those right and the plant will grow well, with or without music.
I started harmonium lessons last week. I'm Ananya, and my teacher is Sharma Sir.
Welcome to the harmonium, Ananya. It is a lovely instrument to begin with because the keys are easy to see. How was your first week with Sharma Sir?
He only taught me how to sit and pump the bellows. I wanted to play a song already!
That feels slow, but sitting well and pumping evenly gives you a steady sound later. Many teachers begin this way so that bad habits do not form. You will play a song sooner than you think.
Today he taught me Sa Re Ga Ma. It sounds simple but my fingers get mixed up.
That is normal. Your fingers are learning a new map. Play the four notes slowly, up and down, five times a day. Do not rush. Speed will come on its own once the notes feel familiar.
Should I tell Sharma Sir that my fingers get confused?
Yes, Ananya. Teachers like honest feedback, and Sharma Sir can show you a finger pattern or an easier way to practise. Saying it early will save you weeks of confusion later.
I keep sinking when I try to float on my back. I'm James.
Sinking is usually because the hips or head are too low. Lie back, look up at the ceiling, stretch out your arms, and push your tummy gently up. Is someone helping you?
My coach holds my back, but when she lets go I sink.
That is normal at the start. Take a deep breath and keep it in, since air makes you more buoyant. Also, keep your ears in the water and your chin slightly up.
My ears feel strange in the water though.
Many people feel that at first. Letting your ears go under helps your head lie back, and then your hips rise. It gets easier, James, and your coach will support you till you can float alone.
I'll try again tomorrow. Remind me what helps me float?
Take a deep breath and hold it, keep your ears in the water, chin slightly up, and push your tummy gently up. Your coach can support your back till you float on your own, James.
I'm eight and I want to learn to ride a bike without training wheels. I'm Ava.
That is a great goal, Ava. The key is balance. Start in an open, flat place with no traffic, like a park or an empty lane. Is there an adult who can help?
My father can. He says he'll hold the seat.
That works well. Ask him to hold the seat, not the handlebars, and to let go slowly when you get steady. Look ahead, not at your feet, and pedal smoothly.
What if I fall?
Falling happens to everyone. Wear a helmet and knee pads if you can, and ride on grass or a soft path at first. Get back on after a short rest.
Should I do it in the evening or morning?
Morning or late afternoon is best, when the park is quiet and the sun is not too strong. Ask your father, Ava, to pick a time when the lane is empty.
Okay. What was it that my father holds, the seat or the handlebars?
Your father should hold the seat, Ava, not the handlebars, because holding the handlebars makes it hard for you to steer and balance. He should let go slowly when you start to feel steady.
I'm bored on holidays and my parents keep saying I should find a hobby. I'm James.
Boredom can lead to a good hobby. What do you enjoy when you are free, even small things?
I like fixing things. I opened my old radio last week.
That is a strong clue. You may enjoy repairing or building things. Ask an adult for a safe old gadget to take apart, and learn what each part does.
Is it safe to open old electronics?
Not always. Never open anything that is plugged in, and be careful with old devices that may hold stored electricity. Do it with an adult, and start with simple things like a toy or a clock.
I'll ask my uncle. What did I open last week?
You opened your old radio, James. That shows real curiosity. With your uncle, try a simple toy or a clock next, and keep every screw in a small box so you can put it back together.
What is the difference between freestyle and breaststroke? I'm Dev and I'm starting classes.

In freestyle, your arms move one after the other, and you kick up and down. In breaststroke, both arms pull together in a circle and your legs kick like a frog. Breaststroke is slower and easier for many beginners.
Which is better to learn first?
Many coaches teach freestyle first, but some start with breaststroke because you can keep your head up. Ask your coach, Dev, since they know how you move in the water.
Okay. What does the frog kick look like again?
Bend your knees, turn your feet out, then push your legs round and together, like a frog. The push gives the speed. Practise it holding the pool edge before trying it with your arms.
I got a yellow card in today's match for a bad tackle. I'm Karan. I feel terrible.
A yellow card is a warning, and it is possible to learn from it. What happened?
I slid in late and hit the other boy's leg. It wasn't on purpose.
Even an accident can be a foul if the tackle is late. Next time, wait for the ball to be near before you challenge. Check if the boy is okay.
I apologised to him, and he said it's fine.
That was the right thing to do, Karan. Good players show respect. You can learn from this and be a more careful defender.
Should I tell my coach?
Yes, tell him honestly about the late tackle, and that you apologised to the boy. Say you will work on timing your tackles. Coaches value honesty, Karan, and he can help you practise.
How do I stop getting out to the same kind of ball? I'm Aisha.
First, notice what the ball is doing. Is it bouncing high, swinging or turning? Knowing the pattern helps you fix it.
It swings away and I nick it to the keeper.
That means you reach for the ball too far from your body. Let the ball come closer before playing, and keep your bat close to your pad. Leave the ones outside off stump.
What does leaving the ball mean?
It means letting the ball pass without playing a shot. It is a skill, because you must judge which balls are dangerous and which are safe to leave.
Okay. Will practice help me judge it?
Yes. Ask a friend to bowl outside off stump and practise leaving those balls. After a while your eyes and body will know which ones to leave.
What was my problem again?
The ball swings away and you nick it to the keeper, Aisha. Let it come closer, keep the bat near your pad, and leave balls that are wide outside off stump.
I'm Ananya, and Dev, my kid brother, wants to grow a plant from a bean.
That is a classic and fun experiment, Ananya. Put a bean in a wet paper towel inside a clear glass or bag. He can watch the root and shoot appear. Has he got a bean ready?
Yes, a big rajma bean from the kitchen.
Rajma works well. Soak it overnight, wrap it in a wet tissue and put it in a clear bag near a window. In a few days, a root will come out.
Then what? He is impatient.
After the root and little shoot appear, move the bean into a small pot of soil with the root pointing down. Give Dev a job, like checking and measuring it every morning with a ruler.
Good idea. He'll love the ruler part.
Yes, writing down the height every day makes the waiting fun. Let Dev draw the rajma plant on a chart, and you can both see how fast it grows over the week.
I'm Ritu. My cycle got a puncture on the way to school today.
That is annoying, Ritu. A puncture on a school morning can ruin the plan for the day. Did you manage to get to school on time?
Yes, I walked it to a repair shop near the market. The man fixed it in ten minutes.
Good that there was a shop close by. Punctures are common, and a quick fix like that gets you riding again. Did he tell you what caused it?
He found a small nail in the tyre. He said I should check my tyres each week.
That is good advice. Look for small stones, thorns or nails stuck in the rubber, and press the tyre to check it is firm. It takes only a minute.
Should I carry a repair kit?
A small kit with a patch, glue and a pump is useful for longer rides. For a short school ride, knowing where the nearest shop is, like the one near the market, may be enough.
What did the repair man find in the tyre?
He found a small nail, Ritu. Checking the tyre each week for nails and thorns, and keeping the market shop in mind, should keep you on the road.
I swam fifty metres without stopping today. I'm so proud. Karan here.
That is a real achievement, Karan! Fifty metres without a break takes steady breathing and practice. How long have you been learning?
Three months. I started with just floating.
That shows how far you have come. Floating teaches balance and calm, which you need for longer swims. What stroke did you use today?
Freestyle. But my arms got tired near the end.
That is normal in the early months. Keep your strokes long and smooth instead of fast, and kick gently from the hips. Tired arms often mean you are pulling too hard.
Should I try backstroke next?

Yes, backstroke is a nice next step, Karan. Your face stays out of the water, so breathing is easy. Since your arms got tired at the end of your freestyle, keep the backstroke arms slow and long, and practise with your coach nearby.
Noah here. My teacher gave us a book list and I don't know which to pick first.
A good way to choose is to read the first page of each. Pick the one that makes you want to turn the page. Do you remember any titles from the list?
There's one about a boy who lives on a boat, and another about a girl and her dog in a village.
Both sound fun, Noah. If you like water and adventure, pick the boat book. If you like warm, small-town stories, pick the village one. Read a page of each tonight to decide.
I think I'll do the boat one first. Can I read the village one next month?
Yes, that is a fine plan. Finish the boat book first and enjoy it. Next month, the village book with the girl and her dog will feel fresh, and you will have time to enjoy it.
My daughter Lily is afraid to put her face in water. She's six. I'm her mother.
That is common at six. Keep it playful and without pressure. Let her splash, blow bubbles in the bath, and watch other children enjoying themselves. Does she like the bath?
She does. She sits for an hour with her toys.
Then use the bath. Let her blow bubbles on the surface with her mouth, then her nose, then put her chin in. Praise each small step. Each day, add a tiny bit more.
What if she cries at the pool?
Do not force her. Stay near her, stand in the shallow end, and let her watch for a while. Another day, bring a favourite floating toy and play near the edge.
That makes sense. What was the first bath game again?
Blowing bubbles on the surface of the water. Lily can start with her mouth, then add her nose, then her chin. Because she loves her bath, that game can lead to the pool when she is ready.
My school match is tomorrow and I can't sleep. I'm Ananya.
It is normal to feel excited before a match, Ananya. Try slow breaths and keep your kit ready, so there is nothing left to worry about. Do you know what time you have to be at school?
7:30 am. I'm playing in defence for the first time.
A new position can feel scary, but defence is mostly about staying calm and staying close to your player. Talk to your goalkeeper and the other defenders so you all know who covers whom.
I think I'll set my bag by the door now. Thanks for the tip about breathing.
Good plan, Ananya. A packed bag by the door saves time in the morning and lets you relax. Do a few slow breaths before bed, and remember that your first defence game only needs calm and teamwork.
My friend Noah plays a lot of marbles. I'm Ritu. Is it a real sport?
Marbles is a traditional game with real skill. Players use aim and control to hit other marbles. Many cultures have versions of it. Do you want to try?
Yes, but I'm bad at aiming.
Aiming gets better with practice. Place a marble on the ground, flick another with your thumb and index finger, and try to hit it from a short distance. Move back as you improve.
Does Noah play for fun or for winning?
I cannot say, since I only know that Noah plays a lot. Ask him how he plays, Ritu. Most marble players do both, and he may teach you his best flick.
I just finished a thick book and now I feel empty. Is that normal? I'm Karan.
Yes, it is very normal, Karan. After spending days with characters, closing the book can feel like saying goodbye. It means the book mattered to you.
The hero, Arjun, was so brave. I miss him.
Characters like Arjun stay with us because we follow them for so long. You could write a short note about what you liked in him, or tell a friend about the book. Sharing helps the feeling settle.
Maybe I'll lend it to Ritu. She likes adventure.
That is a kind idea, Karan. Ritu will enjoy meeting Arjun, and you will get to talk about him with someone who knows him too. Tell her your favourite part when she finishes.
My teacher says I should learn to read notes. Is it really needed? I just play by ear. I'm James.
Playing by ear is a real skill, James, and many great musicians have it. Reading notes adds another skill, and it lets you learn new pieces without hearing them first.
But it seems boring.
At first it can feel like homework. A good way is to start with songs you already know by ear and look at how they appear on paper. Then reading feels like a puzzle you have already solved.
That sounds easier. Which song should I try first?
Pick the simplest tune you can play by ear, perhaps a short nursery tune. Find its notes in your book and match them to what you hear. Start slowly and do only a few bars each day.
My teacher also said something about keeping the tempo steady. What was that for?

Tempo is the speed of the music. A steady tempo keeps the song smooth and keeps you in time with others. Your teacher likely means it will help with reading notes, James, because you count the beats on paper, and counting only works if your speed stays the same.
I'm Karan. I want to ride up the hill near my house but it's very steep.
Hills are hard work, and a steep one needs patience. Does your bike have gears?
Yes, it has gears. I just don't know when to use them.
Shift to a lower, easier gear before the hill starts, not in the middle. Pedal in smooth circles and sit back a little. Use easy gears for slopes and harder gears for flat ground.
What if I can't make it up?
Get off and walk. There is no shame in that. Walking the steep part is safer than being too tired, and you can try again as your legs get stronger.
Okay. And going down?

Coming down that steep hill near your house, go slowly and use both brakes gently. Keep your weight back and your eyes on the road. Stay in control, Karan, and check for walkers or vehicles at the bottom.
Which is better for a beginner: watercolour or crayons?
Crayons are simpler. They do not need water, brushes or drying time. Watercolour is lovely but needs practice with how much water to use. If you enjoy neat lines, start with crayons.
I picked crayons. I'm Ritu and I want to draw a sunset.
A sunset is perfect for crayons. Blend yellow, orange and a little red, pressing lightly and layering them from the horizon upward. Add a thin dark band for hills or trees at the bottom.
How do I make the sky look warm and not messy?

Colour in one direction, from the sun outward, and press softly. Keep the colours in a neat order: yellow near the sun, then orange, then red, Ritu. Light layers mix more smoothly than one heavy layer.
I'm saving for a new cycle. I'm Aisha. My brother says the red one is best.
A cycle is a good thing to save for, Aisha. Do you know why he thinks the red one is best?
He says it has better brakes and a lighter frame.
Those are useful points. Check the size too, since a bike that is too big or small is hard to ride. Sit on it, and make sure your feet can touch the ground.
Is it a good idea to get gears?
Gears help on hills and long rides, but for short rides in town, a single-speed bike is simpler and needs less care. Think about where you will ride most.
Okay. What colour did my brother choose?
Your brother said the red one is best, Aisha. Check the brakes, the frame weight and the size before you decide, and try riding it in the shop.
I have a tiny balcony but I want a lot of plants. Any ideas? I'm Lily.
A tiny balcony can hold many plants if you use space upward. Hanging pots, wall shelves and a ladder-style stand all help. What sort of plants do you like?
Flowers mostly. Petunias and marigolds.
Both like sun, so keep them on the sunniest side. Use hanging pots for petunias, since they trail down, and put marigolds in small pots on a shelf.
My balcony faces north. Will they still bloom?
