North-facing balconies get little direct sun, so petunias and marigolds may struggle. Try shade-friendly plants like money plant, snake plant or ferns, and keep a few flower pots near the railing for the brightest light.
That's a shame. Which flowers were the ones I wanted?
You wanted petunias and marigolds, Lily. If your balcony is shady, you could try them in the brightest corner and see how they do, with leafy plants filling the rest of the space.
We play five-a-side and I always end up as goalkeeper. I'm Ananya.
Being the goalkeeper is an important role, but it is fair to want a change. Do the others take turns?
No. They say I'm good at it.
It is a compliment, but you can still ask for a turn in the field. Suggest each player takes a turn in goal for ten minutes, so everyone gets variety.
They might say no.
Then explain you would like to learn other skills too. Show you can still be a keeper when needed, but ask for a fair share of outfield play.
Okay. Should I ask Ritu first? She's the captain.
Yes, talk to Ritu first, Ananya. If the captain supports the turns plan, the others will likely agree. Be friendly and say what you want to try, like passing and dribbling.
I'm Dev. Is it okay to draw my favourite cartoon characters?
Drawing characters you like is good practice, Dev. Just remember that the characters belong to their creators, so avoid selling your copies. Do you have a favourite?
A friendly robot that makes tea.
A robot that makes tea sounds charming. Try breaking it into basic shapes, like a box for the body and circles for the eyes. Then add small details such as a spout.
What if I try to invent my own robot?
That is even better. Use the same shapes you learned, and give your robot a special job, like a robot that waters plants. Then the design is all yours.
Nice. I'll make a robot that waters the garden.
Good plan. Draw a tank for water in its body and a hose for an arm. Put a smile on it, so the garden robot looks friendly.
What did I say my favourite cartoon character does?
You said it is a friendly robot that makes tea, Dev. Use that charm to design your own garden robot, with a water tank and a hose arm.
Can I read the last page first? My friend says it's cheating.
It is not cheating. Some readers like to know the ending so they can enjoy how the story gets there. Others prefer surprises. It depends on what you enjoy most.
I get nervous when stories are sad. I'm Aisha.
Then peeking at the ending is a good idea, Aisha. If you know the story ends well, you can relax and enjoy the journey. If it ends sadly, you can decide whether you want to continue.
What if my friend still says I'm cheating?
Smile and say that you read in the way that suits you. There is no rule on how to read a book. You can also say that peeking helps you enjoy it when a story is a bit scary.
I'm Noah. Can I grow a mango tree from a seed?
Yes, you can, but it will take years to bear fruit, and the fruit may differ from the mango you ate. It is a fun project. Do you have a seed?
Yes, from a mango we ate yesterday.
Wash it and remove the thin hard shell if you can, carefully. Plant the seed with the curved side up in a big pot of loose soil, about an inch deep, and keep it moist.
How long until it sprouts?
Usually two to three weeks in warm weather. Keep the pot in a warm place. Then it needs a big spot in the garden, since a mango tree grows tall.
I made a paper boat today and it floated! I'm Dev, and I'm seven.
Well done, Dev! A paper boat that floats is a real success. How did you fold it?
My grandmother showed me. She also made a hat from newspaper.
That sounds fun. A newspaper hat is a classic fold, and it uses the same careful creasing as the boat. Did you wear the hat?
Yes, and my sister laughed. Can we make something else?
You could try a paper plane next, or a jumping frog. Ask your grandmother if she knows another fold. Make sure to crease each fold sharply, as it helps the paper stay in shape.
I want to join a cycling club. Is twelve too young? I'm Siddharth.
Many clubs have junior groups for children. Twelve is a good age. Do you know of one near you?
There's one in our area that meets on Sundays. They ride about fifteen kilometres.
Fifteen kilometres is long for a beginner. Ask whether there is a shorter route for juniors, and build up your stamina by riding a few kilometres on weekdays first.
Do I need a special bike?
Not at first. A well-kept bike with working brakes and gears is enough. Check the tyres, brakes and chain before a ride. A helmet is a must.
Should I bring my parents on the first day?
Yes, it is a good idea to bring a parent, Siddharth, so they can meet the group and see how it works. They can also decide with you whether the fifteen kilometre route is right.
I want to try swimming in the sea during our holiday but I'm nervous. I'm Siddharth.
Sea swimming is very different from a pool, so being careful is wise, Siddharth. Waves, currents and tides can be strong. Will an adult be with you?
My uncle will be, and he is a good swimmer.
Good. Stay close to him, swim only where the lifeguards say it is safe, and never go in alone. Look at the red and yellow flags on the beach, as they tell you where to swim.
What if a wave pushes me?
Stay calm and let the wave pass. Keep your feet on the sand if you are in shallow water. If you feel pulled away from shore, swim sideways and call for help. Your uncle can show you.
I'll stay with my uncle then. Can you remind me what the flags are for?
The red and yellow flags show the safe swimming area, with lifeguards watching. Stay between them, Siddharth, close to your uncle, and ask a lifeguard if you are unsure about the day's conditions.
Ananya here. Cycling around our colony at night with friends sounds fun, but am I allowed?
That depends on your parents and on the safety of the colony. Are the roads lit and quiet?
There are street lights and few cars, but some roads are dark.
Then you need lights on your bike and reflective clothes or bands. Stay on the lit roads, and ride together, not alone. Tell your parents the route and the time you will return.
What if my parents say no?
Accept their decision, and offer a safer plan, like riding in the early evening before dark, in a group, on the lit roads only.
Good idea. I'll tell Aisha about the lights.
Yes, Ananya, share the light idea with Aisha so everyone has a front and back light. A group with lights and reflectors is much easier to see than a single rider.
Which friend am I telling?
You said you would tell Aisha about the lights, Ananya. Remind her to bring a white front light and a red back light, and ride on the lit roads together.
I made a comic strip about a cat who goes to school. I'm Karan. Want to hear it?
Yes, please tell me, Karan. A cat who goes to school sounds fun. What happens in the first panel?
The cat, Mitu, wakes up late, grabs a tiffin and runs. In the second panel she sits in class and the teacher is a dog.
I like that the teacher is a dog, since it makes the class funny. A good third panel could be a problem, like Mitu forgetting her homework or sleeping on her desk.
She forgets her homework and the dog teacher gives her an extra day. Is that a good ending?
It is kind and fits the funny mood. To make it stronger, show Mitu's happy face in the last panel and let her promise to pack her bag the night before. That way the cat Mitu learns something small.
I'm eleven and I still can't swim. I'm embarrassed. My name is Ritu.
There is no need to feel embarrassed, Ritu. Many people learn to swim at different ages, and eleven is a fine time. Do you have a pool or a class nearby?
There is a pool at our society but I'm scared of deep water.
That is a common fear. Begin in the shallow end, where you can stand, and get used to the water on your face first. Learn to blow bubbles and float with support before moving deeper.
My cousin Aisha swims well. Can she teach me?
She can help, but a trained coach is safer for the start. Aisha can come along for company and cheer you on. Never swim without an adult watching, whoever is teaching you.
Good point. What's the first thing I should learn?
Learn to blow bubbles and hold your breath for a few seconds with your face in the water. Then try a front float holding the pool edge. Those two steps build the confidence you need.
Okay. What did you say was the safe way to learn with Aisha?

Learn with a trained coach and an adult watching, Ritu, and let Aisha join you for company and encouragement. Start in the shallow end with bubbles and a float, and move deeper only when you feel ready.
I want to watch a full test match with my grandfather but I find it boring. Any tips?
Test cricket is slow on purpose. Try watching the battle between bowler and batter, like a long chess game. Ask your grandfather what he sees, as he may explain plans that you miss.
He always says the pitch matters. What does he mean?
The pitch is the strip in the middle. If it is dry, the ball turns more. If it is green with grass, the ball bounces and swings. So the pitch decides whether bowlers or batters have the easier day.
Oh, so that's why he looks at it before the match. I'm Lily, and I think I'll try this on Saturday.
Yes, Lily. Your grandfather checks the pitch to guess how the day will go. On Saturday, ask him what he thinks before the first ball, then see if he was right by the evening.
Dev is my little brother, and he cries at every swimming class. I'm Ritu.
Tears are common with new swimmers. Does he cry when he gets in or later?
At the start. He holds the coach tightly.
That means he is afraid of the water. A patient coach will let him stay close at first. You could talk about the class on the way, and say you are proud of his effort.
Should I go with him?
If the coach allows it, yes. Your presence may give him courage. Stand where he can see you, and wave and smile at him.
Okay. I'll ask the coach. Anything I should say to Dev?

Say something kind and true, Ritu. Tell Dev that many children cry at first, that the coach will keep him safe, and that you will be there watching. Praise him after class for getting in, even if he cried.
My sister Ananya says drawing is a waste of time. How do I answer her?
You do not have to argue. You can say that drawing relaxes you and helps you notice details. Sometimes a calm answer works better than a debate. Why does she say that?
She thinks I should study more instead. I do study, though.
Then you could show her that you do both. Share your study timetable and say that drawing is your short break after homework. If she sees a balance, she may stop worrying.
Good idea. Can you help me say it kindly?
Try this: 'Ananya, I finish my homework first and draw only after that. It helps me rest my mind.' It is calm and honest, and it answers her worry about studying without any fight.
I'm Lily. How do I stop wobbling when I start pedalling?
Wobbling at the start is common. Push off with one foot, then quickly put the other foot on the pedal and push down. Look far ahead, and the bike will go straighter.
I look down at my feet. Is that bad?
Yes, looking down makes it harder to balance, so the bike drifts and wobbles. Keep your head up and look at where you want to go.
Okay. Where did you say I should look when I start?
Far ahead, Lily, not at your feet. Push off with one foot, put the other on the pedal and push down, and keep your eyes on where you want to go. A little more speed actually makes balancing easier.
Ants are eating my rose plant. What should I do? I'm Lily.
Ants on roses often come for the sweet juice of tiny insects called aphids. Look closely at the stems. Do you see tiny green or black bugs?
Yes, lots of tiny green ones on the new buds.
Those are aphids. You can spray them off with a gentle stream of water, or wipe them with a soft cloth dipped in mild soapy water. Do it in the morning, a few days in a row.
Will the soap hurt the plant?
A very mild mix, only a few drops of soap in a bottle of water, is usually fine. Test it on one leaf first and wait a day. Rinse with plain water afterward.
Good. Why were the ants there in the first place?
Ants protect aphids because aphids give them a sweet liquid. So when the aphids go, the ants usually leave too. Treat the green bugs on the buds, Lily, and the ants will follow.
I borrowed a book from the library and I'm a week late returning it. I'm worried.
A late book is a small problem. Libraries usually charge a small fine or just ask you to return it soon. Do you still have the book?
Yes, at home. I'm James. I haven't finished it.
Then you can ask the librarian if you can renew it, or return it and borrow it again later. Being honest about the delay usually goes over well.
I'll go tomorrow. Is it rude to ask for more time?
No, it is not rude. Librarians get this request all the time. Go tomorrow, James, say you need a few more days to finish the book, and ask politely if you can renew it.
Our colony match is on Sunday morning, and I'm captain for the first time. I'm Ritu.
Good luck, Ritu! Being captain for the first time can feel heavy, but the main job is simple: keep the team calm and talk to everyone. Do you know your team's strong points yet?
Aisha bowls fast, Noah keeps wicket, and James is the only one who can hit sixes. The rest are beginners.
That is a decent mix. Open with Aisha's pace while the ball is new, and keep James for the end overs when runs matter most. Give the beginners a short, easy role so they feel part of it.
Who should I put at the start of the batting order?

Put a steady batter first so the team does not collapse early. From your list, Noah is a good choice, since a wicket-keeper watches the ball closely all game. Keep James for the end overs, as we said.
I can't finish books. I start one, get bored and leave it. I'm Ava.
Many people do that, Ava. It often means the book was not the right match. Do you remember what kind of books you started?
Mostly big novels. The last one was about a girl in a boarding school.
Long novels can feel heavy at the start. Try a shorter book, or one with short chapters, so you feel progress quickly. Finishing a small book builds the habit.
Good point. Maybe a story collection?
Yes, a collection of short stories is ideal. Each story ends in a sitting, so you get the feeling of finishing again and again. Read one story a night before bed.
I'll try that. What was the boarding school book problem again?
You said it was a big novel about a girl in a boarding school and you got bored and left it. It was probably too long for a start, Ava, so short stories make sense.
I want to start a diary. What should I write about? I'm Ananya.
A diary can hold anything you like. Write about your day, what made you happy or upset, or something funny you heard. Even three lines are enough.
What if I run out of things to say?
Use prompts. Write about the best part of your day, one thing you learned or a person you talked to. On quiet days, describe a small thing around you.
Should I write every day?
Daily is ideal, but it is fine to skip a day. A short regular habit is easier than a long one. Keep the diary where you will see it, like on your study table.
Okay, I'll start tonight. What was the first prompt you gave?
The best part of your day, Ananya. Write it in two or three lines, and add one thing you learned if you like. Tomorrow you can try another prompt.
My mother says cycling to school is unsafe, but I want to try. I'm Ananya.
Your mother's worry is natural. Roads can be busy. Are there bicycle lanes or a quiet route to school?
There's a quiet back road, but it has no lane. It's about two kilometres.
Two kilometres is a good distance. You could ride it first with your mother or a friend, so she can see how the road is. Wear a helmet and use lights if it's dark.
What if she still says no?
Then respect her decision and ask again after some time, with a plan. You could say you will ride only on the back road, only with a friend, and in daylight.
A friend could join me. Karan lives nearby.
That helps, Ananya. Karan could ride with you on the back road, and your mother can meet him. A plan with a friend, a helmet and a quiet route may make her feel more at ease.
My grandfather plays carrom every evening. I'm Dev and I want to join.
Carrom is a fun game, Dev. It uses a flat board and a striker to pocket coins. Does your grandfather play with friends?
Yes, with two neighbours. They are very serious.
Serious players usually enjoy teaching a keen newcomer. Ask your grandfather to show you how to hold the striker and where to stand. Watch a few games first, to learn the rules.
Is it hard to pocket the coins?

It takes practice, Dev. Aim carefully, flick with a steady finger, and do not use too much force. Start with coins close to a pocket, and ask your grandfather to set up a few easy shots before his evening game.
Great. Who plays with my grandfather again?
Two neighbours play with your grandfather, Dev. You could ask to watch a game with them, then ask your grandfather to teach you the striker grip afterward.
I just learned to play chess and I keep losing to my sister. I'm Ananya.
Everyone loses a lot at the start. Each loss teaches you something. Do you know why you lose the games, like losing your queen early?
Yes! I lose my queen almost every time.
A common reason is moving the queen out too soon. Try developing your knights and bishops first, and keep the queen safe until you know what the other side is planning.
Okay, I'll keep the queen back. Can you tell me a simple opening?
Move a central pawn two squares, like the pawn in front of your king. Then bring out a knight and a bishop, and castle to keep your king safe.
What does castling do?

Castling moves your king two squares toward a rook, and the rook jumps to the square on the king's other side. It protects the king and brings the rook into play in one move. You can only do it if neither piece has moved, the squares between are empty and your king is not in check.
Got it. So what was the mistake I keep making with my sister?
You keep losing your queen, Ananya. It usually happens when the queen goes out too early. Try bringing out your knights and bishops first and castle, and keep the queen back for now.
My little sister Ava draws on the walls. I'm James, and my parents are upset.
Many young children do this. They are curious and have not learned limits yet. How old is she?
Four. She says the wall is her big paper.
That is a clever way to think. Give her a large sheet of paper taped to the wall, or a chalkboard in a corner. That keeps her creativity and protects the paint.
I like that. Where should I put the paper?
Choose a low wall in her room or the hall, so she can reach it without stretching. Tape the paper at her height, and let her fill it and replace it often.
Good. Should I punish her for the old drawings?
No, a calm talk is better. Explain that walls are not for drawing and show her the new paper. Ava will learn the difference more easily from a clear space of her own.
That seems fair. What did Ava call the wall again?
She called it her big paper, James. That is why the taped paper at her height should suit her. She still gets a big space to draw on, and the walls stay clean.
My parents want me to learn guitar but I prefer drums. What should I do?
It is good that you know what you like. Try talking calmly with your parents and explain why drums attract you. Does something about the beat or the energy appeal to you?
I love the rhythm and I tap on the table all day. My name is Karan.
Tapping all day is a sign of real interest, Karan. You could tell your parents that you already practise rhythm without a teacher. That shows you are serious.
They said drums are too loud for our flat.
That is a fair concern. A practice pad is a flat rubber surface that gives the feel of drumming with little noise. You could offer to practise with it at fixed hours, so neighbours are not disturbed.
That could work. Do you think I could try one lesson of each?
It is a sensible plan, Karan. One trial lesson of guitar and one of drums will help your parents see which one you enjoy. Mention the practice pad and the quiet hours when you ask them.
My grandmother wants me to read the Panchatantra to my little cousin. How should I do it? I'm Lily.
Reading aloud is a lovely thing to do. Use different voices for the animals, and pause before surprises. How old is your cousin?
Five. His name is Dev and he gets restless.
Then choose short stories, one at a time, and let Dev ask questions. For a restless child, ask him to guess what the animal will do next. It keeps him involved.
Which story is good for a five-year-old?
For Dev, try the monkey and the crocodile. It is short, and he can guess how the clever monkey escapes. The hare who tricks the lion is another good one for a restless five-year-old.
I keep losing my place when I play the sitar. My teacher, Mr. Banerjee, says to count. How do I count?
Counting is the way to stay in time. For a taal, you say the beats in your head, like 1, 2, 3, 4, and clap on the strong beats. Which taal are you playing?
Jhaptaal, with ten beats. I'm Ritu.
Jhaptaal is grouped as 2, 3, 2, 3. Clap on 1, 3 and 8, and wave on 6. Say each beat aloud while you play, slowly at first, until you can keep the count silently.
That seems complicated. Can I just use a metronome?
A metronome helps with a steady speed, but it does not show the groups of the taal. Use it, but also clap the groups while the metronome ticks. Your teacher Mr. Banerjee will like the effort.
Which beats did you say I should clap on?
Clap on beats 1, 3 and 8 of Jhaptaal, and wave on beat 6, Ritu. Remember the groups 2, 3, 2, 3 and the pattern will feel easier.
What do cycle lights do and do I need them? I'm Karan, I ride in the evening.
Lights make you visible to others, especially drivers, and help you see the road. Yes, you should have a white light in front and a red one at the back for evening rides.
Are they expensive?
Basic ones are inexpensive, and many are rechargeable. Ask at a cycle shop, and a parent can help you choose. A bright reflector on the pedals or bag also helps.
I'll ask my father. What colour was the back light?
Red, Karan. The front light is white and the rear light is red. Switch them on before you leave, so drivers can see you from far away in the evening.
I'm going on a school trip to a fort. Should I carry my sketchbook?
Yes, a small sketchbook is a good idea. Forts have strong shapes, like arches, towers and walls, which are fun to draw. Bring a pencil, an eraser and maybe a cap to shade your eyes.
My teacher might not give us time. I'm James.
Then use short moments, like waiting for the bus or eating lunch. Even a five-minute sketch of one tower counts. You can also take notes in words and finish the picture at home.
That works. Which part of the fort should I sketch first?
Start with the largest tower or gate you can see, James. A big shape gives your sketch a strong base, and you can add details like arches and the walls beside it when you get home.
We play cricket on the terrace and the ball keeps falling into the lane. I'm Karan.
That can be a problem for people walking below. Is there a way to stop the ball from going over, like a net?
The wall is low. My neighbour Mrs. Iyer has complained once already.
Then safety comes first, Karan. Ask your parents if a net or a taller barrier can go up, and use a soft ball in the meantime. Apologise to Mrs. Iyer politely if the ball landed near her.
We could play indoor cricket instead, using a foam ball.
A foam ball is a smart idea. It does not hurt anyone or break things. You could also add a no-shot-over-the-wall rule, where hitting it out means you are out.
That'll make the batters careful. Which rule was it?
The no-shot-over-the-wall rule, Karan, where a hit that goes over the wall counts as out. It will teach everyone to keep the ball low and keep the lane below safe for Mrs. Iyer.
I forgot my flute at home and today was my class. I'm Aisha.
Oh no, Aisha. That is annoying but not a disaster. Did you tell your teacher what happened?
Yes. She asked me to sit and listen to the other students and write down what I noticed.
That is actually a useful exercise. Listening teaches you about tone and timing. What did you notice about the other flute players?
One girl's notes were very smooth and another had breathy sounds. I think the smooth one holds her breath longer.
That is a sharp observation, Aisha. Breath control makes a flute sound smooth. Ask your teacher for a breathing exercise this week, so you can aim for the same smooth sound as that girl.
I'm Ritu, and I'd love to learn photography, but I only have my mother's phone.
A phone camera is enough for learning, Ritu. Good photos depend more on light and where you stand than on the camera. What do you want to photograph?
Flowers and street scenes near my house.

For flowers, take photos in the morning or late afternoon, when the light is soft. Get close and keep the background simple. For street scenes, look for lines, like a road or a wall, to guide the eye.
Why is morning light better?
Morning light is gentle and warm, so colours look rich and shadows are not harsh. At midday the sun is strong and flowers can look washed out.
Okay. I'll try it tomorrow. Should I ask my mother first about her phone?
Yes, always ask first. Tell your mother your plan to photograph flowers in the morning, and show her the pictures afterward. She may let you use it regularly if she sees you take care of it.
What were my two subjects again?
Flowers and street scenes near your house, Ritu. Try the flowers in soft morning light and look for roads or walls in the street scenes to give the pictures strong lines.
I joined the school cricket team today. I'm Siddharth, and the coach made me a spinner.
Congratulations, Siddharth! Spin bowling takes patience, so it is a good fit if you like thinking. How did the coach pick you for it, and do you enjoy it so far?
He saw my fingers are long. My first net session is on Thursday, and my friend Karan bats first against me.
Long fingers help with grip, which is what makes the ball turn. Bowling to Karan will be a fun test. Try to keep a steady line on Thursday and not worry about big turn yet.
Okay. What should I focus on if I only get ten minutes of practice at home before Thursday?
Practise your grip and your landing spot. Put a small cloth on a patch of floor or ground and try to land the ball on it, over and over. Accuracy matters more than spin in the first week, Siddharth.
Do you think stamp collecting is boring? My friends say so. I'm Noah.
It is not boring if you enjoy it. Stamps show places, animals, history and art in small pictures. What do you like about them?
I like the little pictures of birds from different countries.
Then you could collect only bird stamps. A theme makes a collection special, and you will learn about many birds as you go.
That's a good idea. Where can I get more?
Ask relatives for stamps from letters, check with a local stamp shop, or swap with other collectors. Some schools have a hobby club too.
Okay. I'll tell Aisha about it too. She collects feathers.
That is a lovely match, Noah. Your bird stamps and Aisha's feathers go together. You could show each other what you find and maybe learn about the birds the feathers come from.
I can't draw hands. They always look like claws. Aisha here.
Hands are hard for almost everyone, Aisha. Try drawing a flat palm as a rounded square first, then add the fingers as simple tubes. Think shapes before details.
What about the thumb? It always looks wrong.
The thumb starts lower than the other fingers, near the wrist, and it bends in a different direction. Draw it as a short, thick tube at an angle from the palm, not from the top.
Okay, I'll try it tonight with my own hand as a model.
That is the best way, Aisha. Hold your hand in front of you, and draw what you see, not what you think a hand looks like. Pay attention to the thumb you asked about, since it starts low.
My mother's money plant is turning yellow. I'm Siddharth and I want to help.
It is kind of you to help, Siddharth. Yellow leaves often mean too much water. How often does the plant get watered?
Every day, because it is hot.
Daily watering may be too much, even in heat. Let the top of the soil dry a little before watering again. Also check that the pot lets extra water out.
There's a plate under the pot with water in it.
That standing water keeps the roots wet. Empty the plate after each watering, so the roots can breathe. Pull off the yellow leaves gently too.
Will it turn green again?
The yellow leaves will not turn green, but new leaves should grow healthy once the roots dry out a bit. Give it a week or two, Siddharth, and keep the plate empty.
I love baking but my cakes come out flat. I'm Lily.
Flat cakes usually have a simple cause. The baking powder may be old, the batter may have been mixed too hard, or the oven may not have been hot enough. Which do you think it was?
Maybe the oven. I opened the door to check.
Opening the door often makes a cake sink, since cold air rushes in. Wait until the last ten minutes before checking, and keep the door closed before that.
I'll try that. How can I tell when a cake is ready?
Gently press the top. If it springs back, it is ready. You can also poke a thin stick in the middle, and if it comes out clean, the cake is done.
Thanks. What did I do wrong with the oven again?
You opened the door to check the cake, Lily. That lets cold air in and can make it fall flat. Keep the door shut until the last few minutes, and use the stick test.
Karan here. My school has a swimming gala next month and I'm entered in the backstroke.
Good luck, Karan. A gala is a great chance to enjoy racing. How is your backstroke now?
Okay, but I keep drifting toward the lane ropes.
Drifting happens when your arms are uneven or you look sideways. Fix your eyes on the ceiling or the flags above, and keep your arms pulling straight back.
What about my turns?
For backstroke turns, count your strokes from the flags to the wall, so you know when to turn. Practise this at your pool until the count feels natural.
I'll practise. Should I rest before the gala?
Yes, ease off in the last two days with light swimming. Eat well and sleep early the night before. Your body needs to be fresh.
What was I drifting toward?
You drift toward the lane ropes, Karan. Keep your eyes on the ceiling, pull your arms straight back, and use the flags to count strokes before each turn.
Should I use a pen or a pencil for drawing a landscape?
Pencil is easier for beginners because you can erase and fix. A pen gives bold lines but forgives nothing. Start with a pencil for the outline and use a pen only to go over what you like.
I picked pencil. My landscape has a river, two hills and a hut. I'm Noah.
Good picture, Noah. Draw the hills first, far at the top, then the river curving in front of them, and the hut near you, larger than the hills. Things closer to you look bigger and clearer.
Where should I put the sun?
Put it behind one of your hills, so only half shows. That adds depth and makes the hills look layered, Noah. Then add a light shadow on the side of the hut away from the sun.
My team lost 5-0 today and my friends are blaming the goalkeeper, who is Karan.
That sounds like a rough match. A big score usually means many things went wrong, not one player. How is Karan feeling about it?
He is quiet and didn't talk on the bus. I want to help but I don't know how.
A short and kind word can mean a lot. Sit near him and say something simple, like that the defence also let many shots through. You do not need a long speech, just show him you are on his side.
What if the others keep blaming him tomorrow?
You can say that a team wins and loses together. Something like, 'We all missed chances, not only Karan.' Standing up for him once, calmly, may be enough to stop the blaming.
I rode in the rain and my brakes didn't work well. I'm Dev.
Wet brakes are weaker, so stopping takes longer. It is good you noticed. Did you get home safe?
Yes, but I was scared at the traffic light.
Next time, brake earlier and more gently on wet roads, and keep more distance from vehicles. Wet roads are slippery, so avoid sudden turns.
Can I fix the brakes?
Dry them with a cloth, and ask an adult or a cycle shop to check the brake pads. Worn pads are often the reason.
I'll ask my father to check. What should I do at a light when it rains?
Brake early and gently, Dev, and keep your distance from the vehicle in front. Your father can check the pads, so your brakes are ready for the next rainy day.
My eyes get tired when I read at night. What should I do?
Use a good light, hold the book a little away from your face, and take short breaks to look at something far away. If the tiredness stays, an adult can take you to an eye doctor. Do you read in bed?
Yes, with only a small lamp. My name is Dev.
A small lamp may be too dim, Dev. Try a brighter light that falls on the page and not into your eyes, and sit up instead of lying flat. Lying down can also strain your neck.
Okay. I'll move the lamp. What else was there, after the lamp?
After the lamp, take short breaks to look at something far away, like the window or a wall across the room. And sit up when you read. If the tiredness stays, tell an adult so a doctor can check.
My drawing teacher says I should draw every day. I'm tired after school though.
Daily drawing helps, but it can be small. Even five minutes of sketching a cup or your shoe counts. Short and regular practice beats one long session a month.
Oh, five minutes is doable. My name is Siddharth and I mostly draw cars.
Cars are great for practice because they have curves and straight lines together. Try drawing one car from the side each day and change one thing, like the wheels or windows, every time.
What's a good first car to try?

Start with a simple hatchback seen from the side, Siddharth. It is a long, low box with a smaller box on top for the windows, and two circles for wheels. Once that looks good, change one thing each day, like the wheels or the windows.
I got a keyboard for my birthday. I'm Lily and I'm nine years old.
Happy birthday, Lily! A keyboard is a great gift. Have you tried playing anything yet?
I played Twinkle Twinkle using one finger. It was hard to find the notes.
That is a good start. Notes repeat across the keyboard, and groups of two and three black keys help you find your place. The note C always sits just left of the two black keys.
Oh, so C is next to the two black keys. I'll remember that.
Yes, find any pair of two black keys, and C is the white key to the left of them. Once you can find C quickly, finding D and E to the right will be easy, and you can play many songs.
Which key did you say again, the one next to the two black keys?
It was C, Lily, the white key just to the left of the group of two black keys. Start Twinkle Twinkle on that note and you will find the rest of the tune.
My grandfather has a vegetable patch and he's teaching me. I'm Dev.
That is a great way to learn, Dev. Gardeners learn the most by working beside someone with experience. What did he teach you first?
How to dig the soil. He said it should be loose, like cake.
He is right. Loose soil lets roots spread and water move through. Digging it in the morning, before the sun gets strong, is more comfortable for both of you.
Today we sowed spinach and coriander. They are quick, he says.
He is correct. Both grow fast, and you can often pick the first leaves in three or four weeks. Water gently so the tiny seeds do not wash away.
How do I know when to pick the spinach?
Pick the outer leaves when they are about the size of your palm, and leave the small centre leaves to keep growing. Ask your grandfather to show you the first time, Dev.
I will. He also told me a proverb about patience. I forgot the vegetable he mentioned.
You mentioned only that he taught you to dig loose soil, like cake, and that you sowed spinach and coriander. I do not know which vegetable he named in the proverb, so ask him to tell you again.
I want to sing at my school function but I get scared on stage. Noah here.
Many singers feel scared, Noah, even experienced ones. What song are you planning to sing?
A simple folk song that my grandfather taught me. It has only four lines that repeat.
A simple song is a wise choice for a first time, and it carries a special meaning because of your grandfather. The repeated lines will also help you stay calm, since you know them well.
Do you think I should sing without a mic?
With a hall full of people, a mic helps a lot, and a soft voice sounds better when it is amplified. Ask your teacher to let you try it once before the function, so the sound is not a surprise.
Okay. Should I tell my grandfather about the function?
Yes, Noah. Since he taught you the song, he will be proud to hear about it. You could even sing it for him once at home as a rehearsal before the function.
I bowl fast but I keep bowling wides. I'm James.
Wides usually come from a rushed run-up or a loose front arm. Do you bowl on a proper pitch or in the street?
On a street, with a tennis ball. There's a drain at one end that I try to avoid.
Then you may be steering away from the drain mid-run. Pick a spot ahead of you, like a crack in the road, and aim at it every time. A clear target helps your arm follow the same line.
My friend Dev says I look at the batter, not the spot.
Dev has spotted something useful. Looking at the batter pulls your arm toward him. Keep your eyes on your target spot until the ball leaves your hand, then look up.
I'll try it tomorrow. Anything for my run-up?
Keep it the same length every time. Count your steps, maybe six, and practise them without a ball first. A steady run-up means your body arrives at the crease in the same way each ball.
What did Dev tell me about my eyes?
Dev said you look at the batter instead of your target spot, James. That can pull your arm off line, so fix your eyes on the crack in the road and your wides should reduce.
My brother Dev wants to learn cricket but he's only six. Where do I start?
Start with a soft ball and a plastic bat. At six, the goal is to enjoy hitting and catching, not to learn rules. Short games in the lane or a park work well.
He gets angry when he is out. Yesterday he threw the bat.
That is common at his age. Calmly say that being out is part of every game, even for big players. Maybe let him have a few extra tries at first, so he sees that one miss is not the end.
We did that today and he laughed. Should I tell Mummy about the bat thing?
Yes, a short and kind chat is fine. You can say Dev threw the bat but then calmed down and learned the extra-turn rule. That way she hears the whole story and not only the angry part.
Siddharth here, thirteen. What should a young footballer eat?

Eat a mix of foods, such as roti or rice for energy, dal and eggs or paneer for protein, and fruit and vegetables for vitamins. Drink plenty of water. This is general guidance, not medical advice, so your parents or a doctor can help with specifics.
I sometimes skip breakfast on match days.
Try not to skip it, since your body needs fuel. A light breakfast like a banana and some toast or poha can give you steady energy without feeling heavy.
I'll try the banana and poha. What was the thing about drinking?
Drink plenty of water, Siddharth, before, during and after the match. Pair it with your banana and poha breakfast, and you will feel more ready for the game.
I fell off my bike today and scraped my knee. I'm Noah. Should I stop riding?
I am sorry about your knee, Noah. Clean the scrape with water and tell an adult so they can look at it. A small scrape does not mean you need to stop riding for good.
Mum cleaned it. I fell because a dog ran across the road.
That would surprise anyone. Next time, slow down when you see animals near the road, and ring your bell to warn them. Ride where there is less traffic if you can.
Do you think I should wear knee pads?
Knee pads are a good idea, along with a helmet. They protect you when you fall. Ask your mum to help you choose a pair that fits well and does not slip.
Okay. Why did I fall again?
You told me that a dog ran across the road and you fell, Noah. Slowing down near animals and ringing your bell can help, and knee pads will protect you in case it happens again.
I've started drawing faces but they all look flat. I'm Ritu.

That is very common at the start, Ritu. Faces look flat when there is no shading. Try adding soft shadows under the nose, below the lower lip and along one side of the face, using the side of your pencil.
I only have an HB pencil. Is that enough?
An HB pencil is fine for learning. Press lightly for light parts and a bit harder for shadows. Later, a softer pencil like 4B will give you darker tones, but you can get far with HB.
Good. Which part of the face should I practise first?
Start with the eye, Ritu. It has a small, clear shape, and shading around it teaches how to show depth. Once the eye you draw looks round and not flat, try the nose using the same soft shadows.
Our swimming class starts at 6 am. It's too early. I'm Aisha.
Early classes are hard at first. A fixed bedtime helps a lot. What time do you go to sleep now?
About ten thirty.
Try sleeping by nine thirty, so you get enough rest. Lay out your swim bag the night before, so the morning is quicker. A light snack like a banana will give you energy.
I'll try. Is it okay to eat before swimming?
Yes, a small snack like that banana is fine, Aisha. Eat it soon after you wake up, so it settles before the 6 am class. Avoid a heavy meal just before swimming, and drink some water too.
My friend and I want to start a small book club. How do we begin? I'm Ava.
Start small. Pick one short book, set a date to talk about it, and meet for an hour. Who else would like to join?
Maybe four friends. My friend is Noah and he reads comics.
Comics count as reading, and Noah can bring a different view. You could take turns choosing the book each month, so everyone gets to share their taste. Start with a book that is short.
Do we need to read the whole book before meeting?
It helps, but you could also read it in parts, a few chapters per meeting. For a first club, a short book that you can finish in a week is best, so Noah and the others stay keen.
I'm Lily and I swim in a pool at my grandmother's house. She wants me to be careful. What are the rules?
Good rules are never to swim alone, to walk and not run on the pool edge, to stay in your depth, and to get out if the weather turns stormy.
Is it okay to swim after eating?
A big meal before swimming can make you feel heavy, so wait a little. A light snack is fine. Listen to your body.
My grandmother also said no running. Is it the same as your rule?
Yes, it is the same. The pool edge is slippery, and running can cause a bad fall. Your grandmother is right, Lily.
What was the first rule you said?
Never swim alone, Lily. Always have an adult nearby who can see you, like your grandmother, before you get in the water.
The leaves of my curry plant have white spots. I'm Ava.
White spots can be a dust-like fungus or tiny insects. Rub a spot gently. Does it wipe off like powder?
Yes, it feels like powder.
That sounds like a fungus called powdery mildew. Remove the badly affected leaves and keep the others dry. Water the soil, not the leaves, and give the plant more air.
Should I throw the leaves in the compost?
It is better to bin them, since the spores can spread. Wash your hands and tools afterward before touching other plants, Ava.
What if it comes back?
Then spray the leaves with a mix of one spoon of baking soda in a litre of water, in the evening, and keep the plant in the light and air. If it keeps spreading, ask a nursery for guidance.
Should I read in English or my mother tongue? I'm Ritu and I speak Marathi at home.
Both are valuable. Reading in Marathi keeps your first language strong, and English opens more books. Which one do you find easier?
Marathi is easier, but my school books are English.
Then keep reading Marathi for fun, and read simple English books for practice. Easy English story books, with short sentences, will build your vocabulary gently.
What easy English books would you suggest for a ten-year-old?

Short story books with pictures, or chapter books with simple words. Folk tales and animal stories are a good start, Ritu, because the plots are clear, and you can compare them with the Marathi tales you already know.
My son Dev wants to draw a tiger for his project. He is nine.
A tiger is a great choice for a nine-year-old. Start with simple shapes, like a big oval for the body and a circle for the head, then add legs and a tail. Stripes come last.
He's afraid the stripes will spoil it.
Tell him to lightly sketch the stripes first with a pencil, then go over them with ink or a marker only when he likes them. That way he can erase mistakes before they become permanent.
What colours should he use for the tiger?
Orange for the main body and white around the face and belly. Black for the stripes, which he can add last. Since Dev was worried about the stripes, he should do them very carefully at the end.
Does tracing pictures count as cheating when I'm learning?
Tracing is okay for practice, as long as you do not call the tracing your own original art. It helps you learn shapes and proportions. After a while, try drawing the same picture without tracing.
I traced a photo of a bird. I'm Ava. I'll try drawing the bird again freehand tomorrow.
That is a smart plan, Ava. Compare your new bird to the traced one afterward. Notice where the beak, wing and tail were different, and fix those next time.
What kind of bird should I draw after that?
After the bird you traced, try a simpler one, like a sparrow or a crow. Their shapes are easy to find outside your window, and you can watch them for a few minutes before drawing.
Our school football trials are next week. I'm nervous because I'm small.
Being small is not a problem. Quick feet and good passing matter a lot in football, and smaller players are often better at turning fast. What position do you like playing?
Midfield. My name is Noah, and I like passing more than shooting.

Midfield fits you, Noah. A midfielder who sees gaps and passes well is valuable to any coach. At the trial, show that you look up before passing and that you keep running even when you do not have the ball.
What if I make a mistake in front of the coach?
Everyone makes mistakes in trials, and coaches know it. What they watch is how you react. Forget the error quickly, call for the ball again, and keep playing like a midfielder, Noah.
Is it safe to ride a bicycle with headphones? I'm Siddharth and I like listening to songs.
It is not a good idea. You need to hear horns, bells and people calling out. Headphones hide those sounds and make riding riskier.
But I get bored on long rides.
You could listen to music before or after the ride, or sing in your head. Chatting with a friend while riding on a quiet road also passes the time.
What if I keep only one earbud in?
It is still risky, because you hear less on one side. If you want music, a small speaker on a quiet path is better, but it is best to keep your ears free.
Okay. My friend Ava rides with me. Maybe we can talk instead.
That is a good plan. Talking with Ava keeps you alert and keeps the ride fun. Ride side by side only on quiet roads, and in a line when there are vehicles.
Who rides with me?
Your friend Ava rides with you, Siddharth. Chat with her on quiet roads, save the songs for after the ride, and ride in a line when traffic comes.
I am saving up to buy a violin. Is it better to buy new or used? I'm Ritu.
A used violin can be a good buy if it is in good condition, and it costs less. A new one is simpler to trust. Does your teacher know about violins?
Yes, Mrs. Fernandes. She can check it for me.
Then ask Mrs. Fernandes to look at any violin before you pay. She can check for cracks, the strings and how it sounds. A teacher's eyes are the best protection when buying.
Good. What size should I get? I'm eleven.
Violins come in sizes, and the right one depends on your arm length, not just age. Ask Mrs. Fernandes to measure you. A wrong size can make playing hard and cause aches.
I've been picked as twelfth man for our school match. I'm Noah and I'm disappointed.
It is natural to feel that way, Noah. But being twelfth man matters. You bring water, give messages and you may get to field. Do you know why you were picked?
The coach said I'm good, but the others are slightly better right now.
That is honest feedback, and it means you are close. Use the time to watch the game carefully and learn from the team. Ask the coach what to work on.
Maybe I could improve my fielding.
Fielding is a great place to start, because it can get you into the team. Practise catching and throwing every day, and work on your speed to the ball.
Good idea. What should I do during the match as twelfth man?
Stay ready, Noah. Bring water on time, watch the game closely, and be quick to field if someone is hurt. A good twelfth man impresses the coach, which could help you next time.
Is it too late to start a garden in October? I'm James.
Not at all, James. Many vegetables like radish, carrot, spinach and peas grow well when the weather turns cooler. Do you have a place with sun?
A small yard that gets good sun until the afternoon.
That is a good spot. Radishes are the easiest to start. They sprout in a few days and are ready in about a month, so you will see results soon.
Do I need to buy special soil?
Not necessarily. Loosen the soil in your yard, mix in some old compost or dry cow dung manure if you can get it, and remove stones. Radishes and carrots like loose soil.
Okay. I'll try radish first. How far apart should I plant them?
About two finger-widths apart, in rows a hand-width apart. Thin them out later if they crowd. Since you want quick results, James, radishes will be a nice first crop.
Karan here. I'd like to draw people in motion, like runners.
That is a challenging subject, Karan. Start with stick figures. Draw a line for the spine, a circle for the head and lines for arms and legs, bent to show the pose. Have you tried?
Not yet. My figures always look stiff.
Stiffness comes from straight lines. Draw the spine with a gentle curve, and bend the elbows and knees. Think of the body leaning in the direction of the run.
How can I see real movements?
Watch runners in a park, or ask a friend to hold running poses. Take quick sketches of one pose each, spending only thirty seconds on each. Fast sketches catch the motion.
Maybe my friend Dev can pose for me. He runs every day.
That would be perfect. Ask Dev to pause in a running stance for a few seconds, and draw the curve of his spine and bent knees first.
Who did I say would pose?
You said your friend Dev, Karan. Since he runs every day, he will know good running poses. Start each sketch with a curved spine and bent knees.
I dropped an easy catch today and we lost by two runs. I feel awful.
That is a hard feeling, and it is normal after a close loss. One catch is not the whole match, because many other balls and runs decided it. Do you want to talk about what happened?
Aisha said it was fine, but I saw the others looking at me. My name is Karan by the way.
Thanks, Karan. Aisha sounds kind. The looks you saw might just be disappointment about the score, not blame. Teams usually forget a dropped catch faster than the person who dropped it.
Should I practise catches before the next match?
Yes, that helps a lot. Ask Aisha to throw you high catches for ten minutes each day. Since she was kind about it, she may be happy to help, and it will build your confidence, Karan.
I get water in my ears every time I swim. What can I do? I'm Noah.
It is common. Tilt your head to each side and gently shake out the water after swimming, or dry the outside of your ear with a towel. If you often have ear pain, tell an adult so a doctor can check.
Can I use a swim cap?
Yes, a swim cap or ear plugs designed for swimming may help. Ask the coach or a pool shop to show you the right type. They keep a lot of water out.
Okay. Will the swim cap you mentioned also stop my goggles from slipping?

It can help a little, Noah. Put the cap on first and the goggle strap over it, so the strap grips better. If the goggles still leak, they may be the wrong size, so press them to your eyes without the strap to check the fit.
My brother and I want to build a kite. I'm Karan. Is it hard?
A simple kite is not hard, Karan. You need light paper, two thin sticks, string and glue. Do you have these?
We have paper and thread, but no sticks.
Thin bamboo sticks are ideal, and you can sometimes find them in a stationery shop or from an old broom. Cut one longer than the other and tie them in a cross.
Then what do we do with the paper?
Stretch the cross over the paper, cut the paper in a diamond shape a little bigger, fold the edges over the string and glue them. Add a tail made of a long strip of cloth for balance.
Why does a kite need a tail?
The tail adds weight at the bottom and keeps the kite from spinning in the wind. A longer tail makes it steadier, Karan, so when you and your brother test it, add more tail if the kite flips around.
I love fantasy stories about dragons. I'm Ava. What should I read next?
Dragons are a great topic. Have you read any stories with dragons that you loved?
One where a girl named Maya trains a baby dragon. I finished it in two days.
That sounds exciting. If you liked a girl training a dragon, look for stories about friendship between a young person and a magical creature, or stories with quests and maps.
Do you know any books like that?
I cannot check a catalogue, so ask your librarian for books like the one about Maya and her dragon. They can suggest similar series and may know new ones.
Okay. I'll go to the library tomorrow.
Good plan, Ava. Tell the librarian you finished the dragon book in two days, and she will know you enjoy fast-paced fantasy. Bring a list of titles you have already read.
What was the girl's name in my book?
The girl's name was Maya, Ava. Tell the librarian that Maya trains a baby dragon, and you want something with the same sense of adventure.
I want to swim faster. I'm Noah and I do about one lap in a minute.
Good effort, Noah. Speed comes from technique more than strength. Which stroke do you use?
Freestyle mostly.
Focus on a smooth stroke, a streamlined body and strong leg kicks. Reach forward with each arm and pull the water past your hip. Keep your head down, looking at the pool floor.
My coach says I lift my head too much.
That is a common problem. Lifting your head drops your hips and creates drag. Look down and turn your head only to the side to breathe.
I'll work on that. What helps with turning to breathe?
Rotate your whole body slightly, Noah, not just your head, so you do not lift it as your coach warned. Breathe out underwater before you turn, and then you only need a quick breath in.
I'm learning origami from a book. The crane is so hard. I'm Ava.
The crane is a tricky fold, Ava. Many people need a few tries. Which step do you get stuck on?
The part where you open and flatten the paper into a diamond.
That is the square base, and it is hard for most beginners. Crease the paper well first, and open it gently, pushing the sides inward as it flattens.
It finally worked but the paper is crumpled.
That happens at first. Try again with a fresh sheet, and fold with sharp, slow movements. The second one will already look cleaner.
Should I use a special paper?
Origami paper is thin and holds creases well, but any thin square paper works, like gift wrap. Large paper is easier to fold, so start with a big square before trying a small one.
Which step did I say was hard?
The step where you open and flatten the paper into a diamond, Ava. Take your time with that step, use a fresh sheet, and press the creases well before opening it.
Our coach says we need to build stamina. What should we do? I'm Aisha.
Running is the base of stamina. Start with easy jogging for ten minutes, then add short sprints. Keep your breathing steady. Do you run now?
Only during practice, once a week.
Try adding two short runs a week at home, around twenty minutes each. Mix jogging with fast bursts, like sprinting between two lamp posts and walking to recover.
That sounds like football itself.
Yes, football has bursts of running and short rests. Training this way prepares your body for the real match.
Should I run in the morning?
Morning is good because it is cooler and you start the day well. Drink water before and after. Whatever time you pick, Aisha, keep it the same each week so it becomes a habit.
How do I teach my little sister Lily to love books? She's four and prefers cartoons.
At four, picture books are best. Read with her every day at the same time, even for five minutes, and make it cosy, with a blanket and a soft voice. Let her pick the book.
She likes animals, especially elephants. I'm Ananya.
Then find picture books about elephants, Ananya. You can pause and ask what the elephant might do next. Pointing to pictures and making the elephant sounds will make it a game.
Good. What if she asks for the same book every night?
That is normal and good for her. Young children learn through repetition. Read it with feeling each time and let her say the words she remembers. She will soon read along with you.
Okay. And should I keep cartoons away?
You do not need to ban them. Keep a calm time for books, maybe just before bed, and let Lily watch cartoons at other times. The elephant books will grow on her slowly.
I want to be a wicket-keeper but I'm scared of the ball hitting me. I'm Ava.
That fear is normal. Keepers wear gloves and pads, and learning to stay low and watch the ball reduces the risk. Have you tried keeping before?
Only in the garden, with a soft ball. My brother Noah throws.
That is a good start. Ask Noah to throw gently from a short distance and gradually increase the speed. Practise keeping your eyes on the ball until it is in your gloves.
What about the stance? I don't know how to stand.
Crouch with your feet about shoulder-width apart, weight on your toes, and gloves open in front of you. Stay balanced, so you can move left or right quickly.
Should I get proper gloves?
Yes, if you decide to keep seriously. Proper gloves with padding protect your fingers. Ask your coach to help you choose a size that fits snugly, neither too tight nor too loose.
Okay. And who was throwing in the garden?
Your brother Noah, Ava. Keep practising with him in the garden and slowly raise the pace. When the ball feels less scary, ask your coach about a trial as wicket-keeper.
I hurt my finger and can't play the guitar for a week. I'm so bored.
That is unlucky. A week of rest is fine, and it is important to let the finger heal. Is it a small cut or something else?
It's a small cut from the string. My name is Siddharth, by the way.
Thanks, Siddharth. A small cut should heal soon. In the meantime, you can still practise your music without the guitar. You could listen to your favourite songs and try to find the chords by ear.
How do I know which chords they use?
Listen for the changes in the bass note. When it moves, the chord has usually changed. Hum the bass line and try to find that note later on your guitar. It is slow at first, but it trains your ear.
Great idea. I'll do it with the song my cousin sent me.
Good plan, Siddharth. Do a few lines each day, and write down the chords you guess. When your finger heals, you can test them on the guitar and see how close you were.
I've started collecting old coins. My uncle gave me a few from his trips. I'm Siddharth.
That is a lovely hobby, Siddharth. Coins carry history. What do you plan to do with the ones from your uncle?
I want to sort them by country. Some have writing I can't read.
Sorting by country is a good start. For the writing, look at the numbers and pictures first, and then ask your uncle where each one came from. A library book on coins can help too.
He said one is from Sri Lanka and one from Nepal.
Great, then you already have two groups. Keep each coin in a small paper or plastic pocket and write the country and year on a label. Do not clean old coins, since cleaning can lower their value.
Why shouldn't I clean them?
Cleaning can scratch the surface and remove the natural darkness that shows age. Collectors prefer coins as they are. If one is very dirty, only brush off loose dust with a soft cloth.
Hi, I start at a new college on Monday and I'm nervous. My roommate is called Nikhil.
That's a big step, and feeling nervous is normal. Starting on a Monday gives you a clear fresh start. Having a roommate's name already is a good head start too. Do you know what course you will take?
Engineering, mechanical branch. Nikhil is in the same branch, so we'll share some classes.
That helps a lot. Sharing classes with Nikhil means you can walk in together, swap notes and ask each other when something is unclear. You will not be alone on the first day.
Should I talk to him tonight or wait until we meet?

Send him a short, friendly message tonight. Something like asking when he arrives and what he needs for the room is enough. Then meeting Nikhil on Monday will feel like seeing someone you already know.
I got my first job offer today! It's at a small packaging company in Pune.
Congratulations, that is lovely news. A first offer is something you remember for years. A small company in Pune can also teach you a lot, because you often get to see many parts of the work.
Thank you. They want me to join as an assistant to the production manager, Ms. Kulkarni.

That sounds like a good place to learn. Working beside Ms. Kulkarni, you will see how orders, deadlines and people all fit together. Watch how she plans her day, and ask questions in your first weeks.
What should I do on my first day?

Arrive a little early, carry a notebook, and listen more than you speak. Introduce yourself politely to the team. Write down names, and note anything Ms. Kulkarni explains so you do not need to ask twice.
I'm worried I'll forget names. Will the notebook you mentioned really help with that?
Yes, it will. Write each name in your notebook with one detail, like the desk they sit at. When you meet Ms. Kulkarni's team again on day two, a quick look at your notes will help.
I have an interview for a library assistant post tomorrow at ten. My friend Shreya says I should wear a blue shirt.
A blue shirt is a good choice. It looks neat and calm. Make sure it is ironed and comfortable, and keep the rest of the outfit simple. Do you know who will interview you?
No, but the letter says to bring two copies of my CV and my marksheets.
Then pack those tonight. Put the two CV copies and the marksheets in a clean folder, so you do not need to search in front of anyone. Also keep the interview letter handy.
Can you give me one question they might ask?
A common one is, why do you want to work in a library? Think of a true reason, like loving books or enjoying helping people find things. Say it in two or three simple sentences.
Okay. And what time should I reach again?

Your interview is at ten, so aim to reach the library by a quarter to ten. That gives you time to find the right room, sit down, and breathe before you go in. Remember the blue shirt Shreya suggested.
My hostel room has three beds and I'm the last one to arrive. The other two are Adam and Imran.
Arriving last can feel awkward, but it also means the others already know where things are. Say hello to Adam and Imran first, and ask which bed is free before you unpack.
The only free bed is next to the window. Is that bad?
Not at all. A window bed gives you fresh air and morning light. It can be noisy or warm at times, but a curtain or a small fan usually fixes that. Many people actually prefer it.
Adam already told me the window gets very hot in the afternoon.
Then it is good you know early. You can keep the curtain drawn after lunch and study in the common room during those hours. Ask Adam if he has any other tips about the room.
I'll ask him. Imran seems quiet though.

Quiet people are often just watching and getting comfortable. Greet Imran by name, offer him a snack or ask where he is from, and give him a few days. Sharing a room with Adam and Imran will get easier.
I started a weekend job at a bookshop. The owner, Mr. Rao, wants me to arrange the new stock.
That sounds like a pleasant weekend job. Arranging new stock is a good way to learn where everything lives. Take your time and keep similar books together so customers can find them.
Mr. Rao said to put the school textbooks near the door, because students come in first for those.
That is sensible. Putting the textbooks near the door means students find them quickly and do not need to ask. Keep the heavy ones on lower shelves so they are easy to lift.
What if a student asks for a textbook I can't find near the door?
Be honest and polite. Say you will check, then ask Mr. Rao or look at the stock list. Since he wanted the textbooks near the door, tell him about any missing title so he can restock it.
I moved to Bengaluru last week for work. I don't know anyone yet except my cousin Divya.
Moving to a new city is tiring, so it is good that Divya is nearby. A familiar face makes the first weeks much easier. How are you finding the city so far?
The traffic is huge, and I get lost often.
That is very common in a new city. Try learning one route well, such as your home to office, and add others slowly. Asking locals for directions is normal and most people are happy to help.
Divya says I should join a weekend walking group. Do you think that's a good idea?
Yes, it could be. A walking group is a gentle way to meet people who share an interest, and you also learn the area. Since Divya suggested it, maybe she will come along for the first time.
Divya can only go on Sunday mornings. Does that still work for the walking group?

Sunday mornings are often a good time for a walking group, since the city is quieter and cooler. Check that the group meets then, and ask Divya whether she knows the organiser, so you can join together.
One of my colleagues, Varun, keeps interrupting me in meetings. How do I handle it politely?
That can be frustrating. A calm way is to say, one moment, Varun, let me finish this point. Say it in a friendly voice, without anger, and then continue with what you were saying.
I don't want to upset him. He's actually quite helpful otherwise.
Then a private chat may suit you better. After a meeting, tell Varun you value his help and ask if he can wait for you to finish speaking. Most people respond well when they hear it kindly.
Okay. What would I say exactly?
You could say, Varun, I like your ideas, but I lose my train of thought when I am interrupted. Could you let me finish first? It is short, kind and clear.
Thanks. Is it fine to say it by message instead?

A message is fine if you are more comfortable that way. Keep it warm and short, and mention that you appreciate his help. Speaking in person usually feels more friendly, but a kind message to Varun still works.
My college fest is next month and I've been asked to lead the quiz event. I'm Sarah, by the way.
Nice to meet you, Sarah. Leading the quiz event is a real responsibility and a good compliment too, because someone trusts you with it. What do you need to plan first?
Questions, a venue and a few volunteers. I think I'll have six rounds.
Six rounds is a good length if each is short. Split the work, so one volunteer collects questions, another checks the venue, and others keep score. That leaves you free to run the event.
Should I make the last round the hardest?
Usually yes. A hard last round builds excitement and separates close teams. Just keep a couple of easier questions in it, so nobody feels left out before the finish.
Right. How many volunteers did I say I would need?
You said a few volunteers, Sarah, but not an exact number. With six rounds, a team of four or five would cover questions, scoring and the venue. Decide once you see how big the crowd will be.
I have a video interview tomorrow and my internet is slow at home. My friend Lucas lives nearby.
Slow internet can add stress. Test your connection tonight and see how stable the call is. If it is poor, using a quiet place with better signal is a smart backup.
Lucas has fast internet. Do you think I should ask to use his room?
It is a reasonable thing to ask a good friend. Ask Lucas early today, so he can make sure the room is quiet and free. Offer to arrive a bit before your start time.
He agreed. What should I check before I begin?
Check your camera, microphone and light, and keep water nearby. Close other tabs, and keep your notes and CV open on the screen. Ask Lucas to keep the room quiet during the call.
Good. Where was I going to do it again?
You planned to use Lucas's room, since he has the faster internet. Reach there a little before your start time and run a quick test so you can begin calmly.
The mess food in my hostel is the same every day. Megha, my neighbour, says it's the same in all hostels.
Repeating menus are common in hostels, so Megha may be right. It does get tiring after a few weeks. Is it the taste or just the repeat that bothers you?
Mostly the repeat. Dal and rice every night.
That would bore anyone. Small things help, like adding pickle, curd or a fruit from outside, and sharing a snack with friends. Variety in even one meal can lift the whole day.
Megha keeps a small box of dry fruit and puffed rice in her room. Maybe I will do the same.
That is a good habit. A snack box is easy to keep, and it saves you on nights when dinner does not appeal. Ask Megha what she stocks and how she keeps it fresh.
What did Megha say about hostels in general?
She told you the menu repeats in all hostels, so you should not take it personally. Her snack box of dry fruit and puffed rice is her way of coping, and it could work for you too.
Today my manager praised my report in front of the team. I felt shy but happy. My name is Ella.
That is wonderful, Ella. Public praise can feel strange, but it means your effort was noticed. It is fine to feel both shy and happy at once. What was the report about?
A customer survey summary. I worked on it for two weeks.
Two weeks of steady work, and it paid off. A good summary takes patience, because you must choose what matters. Remember what you did well so you can repeat it next time.
Should I thank my manager? I was too shy to say anything at the time.
Yes, a short thank you is nice, Ella, and it is fine that you were shy then. You could say you appreciated the kind words and the chance to work on the survey summary. Keep it simple and sincere.
I'm moving to Hyderabad for college next week. Adam, my brother, already lives there.
Exciting, and lucky you to have family there. Adam can show you around and help you settle. Do you know where you will stay?
I'll stay in a hostel near campus, but Adam wants me to visit every Sunday.
Sunday visits are a lovely idea. They give you home food and a break from hostel life, and Adam can guide you as you learn the city. Just balance it with study and new friends.
What should I pack for the first week?
Pack light but useful things, such as clothes for the weather, a lock, a water bottle, a charger and your documents in a folder. Adam can help you buy anything you forget once you arrive.
Adam said the weather is mild. Does that change what I pack?
Yes, a little. If Adam says the weather is mild, you can skip heavy woollens and take light clothes with one thin jacket. You will still want an umbrella in case of rain.
I babysit on weekends for a family nearby. The little girl, Anaya, won't eat her vegetables.
That is a very common problem with young children. Staying calm and cheerful helps. Does Anaya like any particular food that you could mix them with?
She loves pasta. She also likes stories.
Then you have two helpers. You could add soft, chopped vegetables to the pasta, and tell a short story where the vegetables are the heroes. Keep it playful and never force her.
Is it okay to give her a small reward if she eats?
A small, friendly reward like a sticker or an extra story is fine, but check with her parents first. They know what they prefer, and they may have a rule about food and treats.
What did I say she loves?
You said Anaya loves pasta and also stories. So mixing finely chopped vegetables into her pasta and telling a story while she eats is a gentle way to begin.
My team is planning a farewell for Shreya, who is leaving the company. They want me to write the card.
What a kind thing to be asked. A farewell card is personal, so a few warm lines will mean a lot. Do you know Shreya well?
We worked together for three years. She taught me how to handle clients.
Then you have something real to say. Thank her for teaching you to handle clients, and mention one memory you share. Short, true words work better than long fancy ones.
Could you suggest an opening line?
You could begin with, Dear Shreya, working with you for three years has taught me more than any training. Then thank her for the client lessons and wish her well in the new place.
Perfect. How long had I worked with her?
You told me three years. You can mention that in the card, perhaps by saying that those three years with Shreya made you more confident with clients.
I missed the lecture on statistics yesterday. My classmate Lucas usually takes good notes.
Then Lucas is a good person to ask. Missing one lecture is usually fixable if you catch up soon. Ask him politely if you can see his notes and maybe borrow them for a day.
He said yes, but I don't understand the topic called probability yet.
That is fine. Read Lucas's notes first, then try a few simple examples like flipping a coin or rolling a die. If you still feel stuck, ask your teacher during doubt hours.
Can you explain the coin example?
Sure. When you flip a fair coin, there are two equal outcomes, heads or tails. So the chance of heads is one out of two. Each flip stands alone, so earlier flips do not change the next.
Whose notes did I say I'd use?
You said you would use Lucas's notes. Read them after the coin example, and mark anything that is unclear so you can ask your teacher about it.
I'm interviewing for a sales trainee job on Friday. They asked me to prepare a two minute talk about myself.
Two minutes is short, so keep it focused. Cover who you are, what you studied, one strength and why this job interests you. Practise saying it aloud a few times.
I'm Varun, I studied commerce, and I'm good at talking to people. Is that enough?
It is a start, Varun, but add a small proof. For example, mention a time you helped a customer at a family shop or led a college stall. A short story makes talking skill believable.
I helped run a stall at our college fair last year.
That is perfect. Say that you ran a stall at the college fair, spoke to many visitors and learned to handle questions calmly. That one example shows exactly what a sales trainee needs.
What else should I include in the two minutes?
Add why you want this role and where you hope to grow. Then finish with your commerce studies and the college fair stall, so the listener remembers a clear picture of you.
My roommate Imran snores loudly and I can't sleep. I don't want to start a fight.
That sounds exhausting. You can handle this without a fight. Choose a calm moment in the daytime, not at night when both of you are tired, and speak kindly.
What should I say?
Something like, Imran, I am having trouble sleeping at night. Could we think of a solution together? Blame no one. Snoring is not something people choose, so a gentle tone matters.
Could earplugs help?
They often do, and they are cheap and simple. Try them for a few nights. If the noise is still too much, you can ask the warden if a different bed arrangement is possible.
Okay. Who did I say snores?
You said your roommate Imran snores loudly. Keep the talk kind and focused on your sleep, and try the earplugs while you wait to see how he responds.
I work at a small cafe three evenings a week. Today a customer shouted at me over a wrong order.
I'm sorry, that is unpleasant, especially when you are still learning. A wrong order is a small mistake, even if it feels big in the moment. Are you feeling okay now?
A bit shaky. My supervisor Divya helped me fix the order.
It is good that Divya stepped in and helped. Watching how she spoke to the customer is a lesson too. Calm, polite and quick is a good way to solve most complaints.
What should I do next time it happens?
Listen without arguing, say sorry for the trouble, and offer to fix it. If the customer stays angry, call your supervisor. You do not have to handle everything alone.
Who helped me today again?
Your supervisor Divya helped you today by fixing the order. Next time, you can follow the same steps she used and ask her afterwards for any advice.
I just arrived in Chennai for my new job and I can't find the bus stop my office told me about.
Don't worry, this happens to almost everyone in a new city. Try asking a shopkeeper nearby, since they know the local stops well. Do you have the name of the stop?
It's called Lake View stop. My office is the grey building next to it.
Good, that is helpful. Ask a shopkeeper or an auto driver for the Lake View stop, and look for the grey building as a landmark once you get closer.
Found it! How early should I leave tomorrow?
Glad you found it. For tomorrow, leave earlier than you think you need to, maybe half an hour extra, since you do not know the traffic yet. After a few days you will learn the right timing.
What was the building like again?
You told me your office is the grey building next to the Lake View stop. Keep that picture in mind tomorrow and you will spot it easily.
I've been at my first job for two months and I still feel like I don't know anything. I'm Megha, by the way.
Hello, Megha. Two months is a very short time, and almost everyone feels this way at first. Feeling you have much to learn actually shows you care about doing well.
My senior, Nikhil, never seems confused. How does he do it?
He probably felt just like you once. People who look confident have usually practised the same tasks many times. Ask Nikhil how he learned his work, because most seniors enjoy sharing.
That's a nice idea. What question should I ask first?
You could ask, what helped you most in your first year? It is open and friendly, and it invites a story. His answer may give you ideas you can use right away.
Who did I say seems confident?
You said your senior, Nikhil, never seems confused. Remember he was a beginner once too, so asking him about his first year is a good way to feel less alone.
Two of my colleagues, Ella and Adam, have stopped talking to each other and now I'm stuck in the middle.
That is an uncomfortable spot. You can stay kind to both without taking sides. Do you know what caused it?
Something about a shared project. Each thinks the other didn't do their part.
That kind of misunderstanding often grows when people do not speak directly. You could gently suggest that they talk, but avoid carrying messages between them. That tends to make things worse.
What if they ask me to agree with them?
You can say you do not know the full story, so you would rather not judge. Stay friendly and calm. Most people respect that, even if they wish you would agree at first.
Which two people were fighting?
You mentioned Ella and Adam. Since the argument is about their shared project, a short talk between the two of them, perhaps with your manager nearby, is the best way to clear it.
