I'm choosing between joining the music club and the debate club in college. My friend Shreya is in debate.
Both are great ways to meet people. Think about which one you would look forward to even on a tired day. What do you enjoy more, singing or arguing a point?
I enjoy both, but I'm a bit shy about speaking in front of people.
Then the music club may feel gentler, since you share the stage with others. Debate, though, can build confidence slowly. You could try one meeting of each before you decide.
That's a good idea. Shreya can take me to debate this Thursday.
Perfect. Going with Shreya makes it easier, since you will know at least one person in the room. Just watch the first session and see how it feels, with no pressure to speak.
Which day did I say I could go?
You said Shreya can take you to the debate club this Thursday. Then you can plan a music club visit another day and compare how each one feels.
I didn't get the job I interviewed for last week. I'm trying not to feel too bad.
I'm sorry, that is disappointing. It is fine to feel sad for a bit. One interview result does not decide your worth, and you showed courage by going.
They said I was good but another candidate had more experience.
That is actually useful to hear. It means your interview went well, and the gap was only experience. You can build that through projects, internships or part-time work.
Can I ask them for feedback?
Yes, a short polite message is fine. Thank them for the chance and ask if they can share one thing you could improve. Not everyone replies, but many do.
What reason did they give for choosing the other person?
They said the other candidate had more experience. So in your message, you could ask what kind of experience matters most, and use the answer to plan your next steps.
I'm homesick in my new hostel. It has been ten days. I miss my mother's cooking.
Ten days is still early, and missing home is very normal. Your mother's cooking is a comfort, so of course you miss it. Have you spoken to her recently?
Every night, for a few minutes. She sends me recipes too.
That is a sweet way to stay close. Cooking one of her recipes with friends could make the hostel feel warmer. Even a simple dish shared in the common room helps.
Maybe I will make her lemon rice this Sunday.
Lovely idea. Lemon rice is simple, and the smell alone might make the room feel more like home. Invite a couple of floormates to taste it, and tell your mother how it went.
What dish did I want to make?
You said lemon rice, one of the recipes your mother sent. Sunday is a good day for it, and your floormates will enjoy a taste of something home-made.
I was offered a part-time job tutoring a ten year old, Lucas, in maths on Saturdays. I'm nervous about teaching.
That is a nice opportunity. Being nervous shows you care. Teaching a ten year old is mostly patience and clear steps, so you are probably more ready than you think.
What if he doesn't understand what I explain?
Then try explaining it a different way, with a drawing or a real example. Ask Lucas to say it back in his own words. That shows you where the confusion is.
Good tip. Should I give homework?
A little is fine, but ask his parents what they prefer first. Keep it short, so Saturday sessions stay pleasant. A few practice questions on what you covered is plenty.
Which day did I say the tutoring is on?
You said Saturdays. So you can plan each session ahead on Friday evening, thinking of one clear example for Lucas and a few short practice questions.
I want to start waking up at five to study before the hostel gets noisy. I share a room with Varun.
Early mornings can be very productive, and hostels are often calmest then. Since you share with Varun, think about light and sound so you do not wake him.
Good point. I could study in the common room downstairs.
That solves the noise problem. Carry a small bottle of water and a light jacket, because common rooms can be cold early on. Keep your books in a bag so you can leave quietly.
Actually, the common room is locked until six. Now what?
Then you can either start at six or study in the room with a small desk lamp pointed at your book. If you choose the lamp, tell Varun tonight so he is not surprised.
There's an interview at a lab for me, and they asked me to bring a project I'm proud of. I have two: a weather logger and a plant watering timer.
Both sound practical. For an interview, pick the one that shows the skills the lab needs. Tell me a little about each, and we can decide.
The weather logger records temperature every hour. The plant timer just switches a pump on at set times.
The weather logger shows measuring, recording and checking data, which a lab values. The plant timer is neat but simpler. I would lead with the logger and mention the timer briefly.
Okay, the logger it is. How do I explain it in under a minute?
Start with the problem you wanted to solve, say how the logger works in two sentences, and end with one thing you learned. Practise it aloud once or twice so it sounds natural.
What did I say the second project was?
You said the second one was a plant watering timer that switches a pump on at set times. You can mention it in one sentence after the weather logger, as a sign you enjoy building small useful things.
I'm thinking of moving from Jaipur to Mumbai for a job next month, and I'm excited and scared.
Both feelings make sense. A big city move is a change in almost everything. What about it excites you most?
The chance to learn from a bigger team. What scares me is finding a place to live.
Housing is a common worry. Ask your new company if they have any guidance for newcomers, and talk to colleagues or friends who already live there. Take your time to see places in person.
My friend Imran lives in Thane. Could he help with the worry I told you about?

Yes, he could help with finding a place to live in Mumbai. Ask Imran about areas that are easy to commute from, and whether he knows anyone with a spare room. A trusted introduction is much better than searching alone.
My boss, Mr. Fernandes, asked me to give a presentation to the whole department on Friday. I've never done this before.
That is a big ask, but it also shows he trusts you. Presentations get easier with preparation. What topic do you have to cover?
The results of our last customer visit. Maybe ten slides.
Ten slides is a lot for a short slot. Keep each slide to one idea, with few words. Practise speaking about each for about a minute, and you will finish on time.
Should I memorise everything?
No, memorising makes you sound stiff and one slip can throw you. Know the main point of each slide and speak naturally. A small card with key words is fine.
I'm still scared of Friday.
That is natural. Try a practice run today in front of a friend or even a mirror. By Friday, the talk for Mr. Fernandes and the department will feel familiar, and your nerves will drop.
I'll ask my friend Sarah to listen to all ten slides. Is one practice enough before Friday?

One full run with Sarah is a good start, and a second short one on Thursday is even better. Ask her which of the ten slides confused her and fix those. Then the talk for Mr. Fernandes will feel familiar.
Our professor gave us a group project and I got stuck with Lucas and Ella, who never reply to messages.
That is frustrating, especially when marks depend on it. Try a clear, short message with a specific question, like asking them to confirm a meeting time by tonight.
I did that. Ella replied, but Lucas is still silent.
Good, Ella is on board. You can plan the work with her, and leave Lucas a clear task with a deadline. If he still does not respond, tell your professor honestly and calmly.
What task should I give Lucas?

Since Ella already replied, pick something Lucas can do alone, like collecting data or writing one section. Tell Lucas exactly what you need and by when. A small clear task is easier to say yes to than a vague one.
I started working at my uncle's hardware shop on weekends. My cousin Nikhil also helps there and he's always bossing me around.
Working with family can be tricky because the lines are blurry. It helps to separate who is actually in charge. Is your uncle the boss, or does Nikhil have a role?
My uncle is the boss. Nikhil is just older and thinks he's my manager.
Then talk to Nikhil in a friendly way. Say you are happy to help, but you take your instructions from your uncle. Keep your voice calm and avoid sounding rude.
What if he tells my uncle I'm being difficult?
Your uncle will probably see the truth if you work well and stay polite. You can also tell him yourself that you and Nikhil are still working out how to share jobs. Honest and calm is safest.
Okay. Remind me who the boss is?
Your uncle is the boss of the hardware shop, as you said. Nikhil is your cousin and a fellow helper, so you can respect him without taking orders from him.
My colleague Megha always brings homemade sweets for everyone on Mondays. I want to do something nice for her.
That is a kind thought. A small, sincere gesture is best. Do you know something she likes besides sweets?
She loves gardening. She talks about her tomato plants all the time.
Then something related to plants would be lovely. A small pot, a packet of seeds, or even a handwritten note saying you enjoy hearing about her tomatoes would feel personal.
I'll get a small pot with a little herb plant. Is that okay?
Yes, a herb pot is a thoughtful gift for a gardener, and it is easy to keep on a desk. Add a short note thanking her for the Monday sweets.
What did she grow again?
She grows tomatoes, which you said she talks about all the time. You could mention them in your note, maybe saying you hope the herb grows as well as her tomato plants.
I'm applying for a college scholarship and need a recommendation from a teacher. I'm thinking of asking Mrs. Banerjee.
That is a sensible step. Choose a teacher who knows you well and can describe your work. Why do you want to ask Mrs. Banerjee?
She taught me biology for two years and said I had real curiosity.
That is a strong reason. A teacher who has seen you grow can write something specific. Ask politely and early, and give her your deadline and a short list of what you have done.
You said to ask early. How many weeks before the deadline should I go to Mrs. Banerjee?

At least two or three weeks before the deadline. Teachers are busy, and a good letter takes time. Remind Mrs. Banerjee of your two years in her biology class, tell her the date clearly, and thank her afterwards.
I'm Divya and I have a group discussion round tomorrow. I'm afraid I'll stay silent the whole time.
Many people feel that way. A simple plan helps. Aim to speak up two or three times, with short, clear points, rather than trying to speak a lot.
What if someone else says my point before I do?
Then add to it. You can say, building on that, and give an example or a new angle. That still shows you were listening and thinking.
Good idea. And how do I begin?
Wait for a natural pause, then say something like, I would like to add a point on this. Keep it to two sentences. Starting early in the discussion makes the rest easier.
I'll try. Remind me how many times I should speak?
Two or three times is a good target, Divya. Make each point short and clear, and use the building on that phrase if someone else already said your idea.
Someone keeps taking my milk packets from the hostel fridge. I live on the third floor.
That is annoying, and it is hard to be sure who it is. Try labelling your things with your name and room number. A label alone stops many people.
I did that last week. The labelled ones still go missing.
Then talk to the floor warden or your floor rep and explain what is happening. Do not accuse anyone, just ask if a shared rule or a lockable box can help.
The rep on my floor is Shreya. Should I tell her about the labels too?

Yes, tell Shreya that even your labelled milk packets still go missing. It shows you tried the simple fix first. Then ask if the third floor can agree on a fridge rule, since a rule for everyone feels fair.
I've been in Delhi for three weeks and I still haven't made a single friend. I'm Adam, a software trainee.
Three weeks is short, Adam, though it can feel long when you are alone. Making friends takes repeated small contact. Do you see the same people at work or near home?
Mostly at the canteen. A man named Imran always sits near me.
Then Imran is a natural first step. Say hello, ask about his work, and try sitting with him a few times. Friendships often begin with simple, repeated chats like these.
We did talk once about cricket. Should I invite him to watch a match?
That could work well, since cricket is already something you shared. Keep the invitation casual, like asking if he wants to catch a match on Saturday, and be fine with a no.
He said yes! Which friend did I want to invite again?
You wanted to invite Imran, the man from the canteen, to watch a cricket match. Great news that he said yes. Pick a place and time, and enjoy it without pressure.
I've been doing evening shifts at a bakery for a month. The head baker, Mr. Joseph, is strict but fair.
Strict but fair is a good kind of boss to learn from. A month in, you must have picked up quite a bit. What have you been doing?
Mostly shaping bread dough and cleaning. Yesterday he let me glaze the buns.
Being trusted with the glaze is a sign of progress. Bakers often start with small steps before getting more tasks. Keep your station clean and he will notice.
I want to learn to make the sweet buns from start to finish. Can I ask him?
Yes, ask politely and tell him you are keen to learn. You might say you would like to watch the whole process one evening. Most bakers are glad when a helper shows real interest.
What was I allowed to do yesterday?
You said Mr. Joseph let you glaze the buns yesterday. You can mention that when you ask him, saying you enjoyed glazing and now want to learn the whole sweet bun recipe.
I'm worried about my first exam in college next week. It's for physics, and I've only done half of the syllabus.
A week is enough to make real progress if you plan. Start by listing the topics you have not covered and see how many there are.
There are five chapters left.
Five chapters in about seven days is manageable. Try one chapter every day and keep two days for revision. Focus on understanding examples rather than reading everything again.
Should I ask my friend Varun to study with me?
If Varun studies seriously, yes. A study partner can explain things you miss, and you can do the same for him. Agree on a clear plan so the time is not lost in chatting.
He is good at the chapters I find hard.
Then it is a fair swap. Ask Varun to go through those hard chapters with you, and you can help him with whatever you find easier. Both of you gain.
Which exam is it again?
It is your physics exam next week, your first one in college. You have five chapters left, so plan one a day with Varun's help on the hard ones.
I was asked at an interview why I left my last job and I froze. I want to be ready next time. My name is Sarah.
Thanks for sharing that, Sarah. It is a common question and freezing happens to many people. The best answer is short, honest and looks forward.
I left because my manager and I did not get along.
You can be honest without criticising anyone. Try something like, I wanted a role with more learning and better teamwork, and this job offers that. Keep your tone positive.
Instead of mentioning my manager at all, could I just say I wanted new challenges?

Yes, Sarah, you do not need to mention your manager. Just add one detail so it does not sound empty, such as handling clients or leading a small project. That makes your reason believable and positive.
My first salary day is tomorrow and I'm planning to take my parents out to dinner. I'm Nikhil.
That is a lovely way to mark the day, Nikhil. Treating your parents on your first salary day is something they will remember. Do you know where you want to go?
A small family restaurant near our house. My father loves their dosa.
A place your father loves is the right choice. Call ahead and book a table so you do not wait, and tell the staff it is a special day if you like.
My mother prefers sweets to dosa. Should I get her something after dinner at that restaurant?

That is thoughtful, Nikhil. A small box of her favourite sweets after dinner will make her feel included, while your father enjoys his dosa at the family restaurant. Both parents get something chosen just for them.
My team lead, Sarah, asked me to train a new joiner, Lucas, and I've never trained anyone before.
That shows Sarah trusts you. Training is mostly patience and clear explanations. Think back to what helped you in your first week.
I liked when someone showed me where everything is and who to ask.
Then start there with Lucas. Give him a short tour, introduce him to key people, and tell him who to ask for what. Small things like that remove a lot of first-week worry.
How much should I explain on day one?
Not too much. Cover the basics, like his desk, tools and daily routine, and leave the details for later days. Let Lucas ask questions, and write a short list he can keep.
Good. Who asked me to train him again?
Your team lead, Sarah, asked you to train Lucas. If you are unsure about anything, check with Sarah, so you teach the same way your team does.
My hostel has a curfew of nine in the evening and I have an evening class that ends at eight thirty.
That is a tight window. Check the exact rule with your warden, and ask whether there is a way to register for late class timings.
The warden is Mrs. Pillai. She seems strict.
Strict wardens usually respect a clear reason with proof. Take your class timetable to Mrs. Pillai and explain politely. Showing the paper makes your request easy to accept.
Okay. What if she says no?
If Mrs. Pillai says no, ask her what the rule allows. Your class ends at eight thirty, so going straight back by the shortest route may still get you in before nine. Stay respectful and do not argue.
My sister Ella just moved to Kolkata for her first job and she's calling me every night, crying a bit.
That must be hard for both of you. Moving to a new city is lonely at first, and a familiar voice helps her. It is kind of you to pick up the calls.
I don't know how to cheer her up.
You do not have to fix everything. Listening matters most. You can also remind her of small wins, like finding a good tea stall or finishing her first week.
She likes old Hindi songs. Maybe I can send her a playlist.
That is a sweet idea. Old songs can feel like a piece of home. Add a few that remind her of family, and write a short note saying you are thinking of her.
Where did I say she moved?
You said Ella moved to Kolkata for her first job. Tell her in your note that you are proud of her for settling into Kolkata, and that the songs are from home.
I tutor children on weekends, and a parent, Mrs. Das, keeps asking me to teach extra hours without telling me in advance.
That is tiring when plans change last minute. You are allowed to set a clear boundary in a polite way. Do you want to say yes sometimes?
Sometimes yes, but I need notice, at least a day before.
Then tell Mrs. Das that clearly. Say that you are happy to add sessions when you have a day's notice, because you plan your weekend around your studies and other tasks.
What if she insists on same-day requests?
You can kindly say that same-day requests are hard for you, but you can offer another day. Repeat your rule calmly. Most parents respect a clear and friendly limit.
What notice did I say I need?
You said you need at least a day's notice. Use that exact phrase with Mrs. Das, so the rule is clear, and offer another day when she asks for a same-day session.
I just got my first semester results and I did worse in chemistry than I expected. I'm Megha.
I'm sorry, Megha. That is disappointing, especially when you worked hard. One result is not the whole picture, though. Do you know what went wrong?
I think I didn't practise enough numerical problems.
That is a clear and fixable cause. Try solving a few problems each day, starting with simple ones, and check the method in your notes when you get stuck.
Could I ask my chemistry teacher where I lost marks on the numerical problems?
Yes, Megha, asking to see your answer sheet is normal. Go politely, and ask which numerical problems cost you marks. Then you will know exactly what to practise before the next chemistry test.
Next week there is a school interview for an assistant teacher post. They want a demo class on fractions with Class five.
A demo class is a good chance to show how you explain. Fractions work well with real things. What materials can you bring?
Maybe some paper and a chocolate bar for the children.
Paper folding is a lovely way to show halves and quarters. Check with the school whether food is allowed, since some places do not permit it. Paper alone works perfectly.
Okay, only paper then. How long should the demo be?
Ask the school, but usually fifteen to twenty minutes. Plan a short start, one clear example, a small activity and a quick check at the end to see who understood.
Remind me what topic they gave me?
They gave you fractions for Class five. Using folded paper to show halves and quarters, and asking the children to try it themselves, will make the demo clear and active.
Tonight my floor is having a small birthday party for Megha in the common room. I'm in charge of snacks.
Fun job. Think about what people can eat without plates, like samosas, chips and fruit. Do you know how many people are coming?
About twelve. A couple of them don't eat onion or garlic.
Then include a few snacks without them, such as plain fruit chaat, roasted peanuts or sweet biscuits. Keep those items on a separate plate so nobody has to ask.
The party moved to Saturday because of exams. Does that change the snacks?
A little. If the snacks are fried, buy them on Saturday so they stay fresh. Dry things like peanuts and biscuits can be bought earlier. Megha's party will be a good break after the exams.
In two days I join a hospital as an office clerk. I'm Imran. I don't know what to wear.
Congratulations, Imran. For an office job in a hospital, neat and simple clothes work best. Think plain shirt and trousers, comfortable closed shoes, and nothing flashy.
Is it okay to wear jeans?
On the first day it is safer to dress a little more formally. Look at what others wear after a day or two, then decide. Plain trousers will not go wrong.
I'll go with a light blue shirt and grey trousers. Good?
That is a good, calm combination for a hospital office, Imran. Iron both the night before, keep your shoes clean, and carry a small notebook. You will look ready and tidy for your first day.
My friend Adam asked me to practise interview questions with him. He's applying to be a bank cashier.
Happy to help you two. Mock interviews are useful. Do you want me to suggest a few questions Adam can practise?
Yes, three simple ones.
Try these. Tell me about yourself. Why do you want this job? How do you handle a customer who is upset? Adam can answer each in two or three sentences.
The third one seems hardest. How should Adam answer it?

Adam should say he would stay calm, listen fully, and say sorry for the trouble, then fix the problem or ask a senior for help. For a bank cashier, a short real example of helping an upset person would make it stronger.
Last month I started delivering newspapers before college. I wake up at four thirty.
That is early. It takes real discipline to do that every morning. How are you finding it?
Tiring, but I like the quiet streets. I'm Lucas, by the way.
Nice to meet you, Lucas. Quiet streets in the early morning have their own calm. Try sleeping early at night so your body gets used to the routine.
Today I almost slept in. Any tips so I don't?
Put your alarm across the room so you must stand up, and lay out your bag and clothes the night before. Think of the quiet streets you enjoy, Lucas, as a reason to get up.
Varun at my office keeps eating lunch alone and I think he's lonely. I've never really spoken to him.
It is kind that you noticed. You do not need a big gesture. Start with a simple, friendly hello, or ask if he would like to join you for lunch.
What if he says no?
Then smile and say maybe another day. Some people need a few invitations before they feel comfortable. Saying no today does not mean he did not appreciate it.
I'll ask Varun to join me tomorrow. What can I talk about, since he always eats alone?

Ask something light, like what he usually eats or how his week is going. Since Varun is used to eating alone, keep it easy and short, so he does not feel pressured, and let him answer at his own pace.
Next week I'm travelling to Lucknow to look for a flat before I start work. My sister Divya will come with me.
That is good, having Divya along. Another pair of eyes helps when you look at places. Do you have a few areas in mind?
Two areas near my office, but I haven't visited either.
Then plan the trip to see both on the same day if you can. Check how long it takes to reach the office from each area, and look at the lanes, light and water supply.
Divya says we should visit the nearer one first. Is that smart?
It is. Seeing the nearer one first with Divya's opinion helps you compare. If it feels right, you can still see the second to be sure, but you will not be rushed.
I want to join the college football team but I've never played before. My friend Ella says it's for experienced players.
Many college teams welcome beginners, especially for practice sessions. Ask the captain or coach directly rather than guessing. Is there a trial?
There's a trial this Friday.
Then go and try. Wear comfortable shoes, drink water, and be ready to run and pass. Coaches often look for effort and attitude, not only skill.
What if I embarrass myself at the trial, like Ella expects?

Almost everyone at a trial makes mistakes. Showing up on Friday is already brave. Ella may be wrong about the team being only for experienced players, and if it goes badly, you can still join friendly games.
I got an interview call from a company called Greenfield Foods, for a quality checker role. It's on Wednesday.
Congratulations. Quality checker roles need careful eyes and honest reporting. Think of examples where you noticed small errors and fixed them.
At college I found mistakes in a lab report once.
That is a good example. Tell it simply, what you noticed, what you did, and what happened next. It shows attention to detail, which is exactly what they need.
Right. What day is the interview?
You said Wednesday, with Greenfield Foods for the quality checker role. Use the days before it to practise your lab report example aloud until it feels natural.
My neighbour Mrs. Sharma asked me to help in her small tailoring shop for a few weeks. I don't know how to sew.
You can still be useful. Ask Mrs. Sharma exactly what she needs. There are many tasks in a tailoring shop beyond sewing, like cutting threads, ironing and organising cloth.
She wants help organising and delivering finished clothes to customers.
That is useful work. Keep a clear list of whose clothes are ready, and check each name before handing anything over. Being careful will earn her trust quickly.
Since I can't sew, should I learn a little while I help her?
It would be a nice bonus. Ask Mrs. Sharma to show you how to sew a button or a simple hem in quiet hours, between deliveries. Small skills like that are handy for life.
Two of my floormates are getting loud every night and I have exams. I'm Shreya, in the next room.
That is tough when you need to focus. A kind talk usually works better than a complaint. Do you know them well?
Not very well, but they seem nice.
Then speak to them in a friendly way. Tell them you have exams and ask whether they could lower the volume after ten. Most people agree when they know the reason.
What if they forget about lowering the volume after one day?
Give a gentle reminder about your exams. If it keeps happening, speak to your warden or floor rep, and explain what you tried. That shows you handled it politely first, Shreya.
I just moved to Ahmedabad and I want to find a good place to eat vegetarian food near my office.
Ahmedabad is known for good vegetarian food, so you have luck there. Start by asking your colleagues, since they know which places are clean and affordable.
I did ask, and two people recommended a thali place near the river.
A thali place is a good choice for a proper meal. Go at a quiet hour the first time so you can see the menu and ask about spice levels.
What if I find it too spicy?
Tell the server when you order that you prefer mild food. Many places adjust, and a glass of buttermilk or curd helps. Starting with the thali near the river is still a good plan.
Which place was recommended again?
Your colleagues recommended a thali place near the river. Try it at a quiet hour and mention that you want mild food, so you can enjoy the first visit.
I'm six months into my first job and I'd like to ask for more responsibility. I'm not sure how to bring it up with my manager, Ms. Thomas.
That is a positive thing to want. Choose a calm time and show what you have already done. Ms. Thomas will take the request more seriously if you have examples.
I've been handling all the customer emails on time.
Then lead with that. Say you have managed customer emails well for six months and you would like to take on one new task. Name a task you are curious about.
I'd like to try preparing the weekly report.
That is a clear, realistic request. Tell Ms. Thomas you would like to prepare the weekly report, and offer to show a draft first so she can check it.
Should I send an email or ask in person?
Ask in person if you can, since it feels more sincere, and follow with a short email so Ms. Thomas has it in writing. Mention the customer emails and the weekly report in both.
Okay. What was the new task I wanted?
You wanted to prepare the weekly report. Say it clearly to Ms. Thomas, along with your six months of on-time customer emails, as proof you are ready.
I have to give a seminar next week on climate and farming. I'm choosing between talking about rainfall changes or crop choices.
Both are good. Rainfall changes are the cause and crop choices are one response. Which one do you have more material about?
I have a few articles on rainfall, but nothing on crops yet.
Then start with rainfall, since you can prepare faster. You can end the seminar with a short note on how farmers adjust, which keeps the second topic in view.
I like that. Which part should be longer?
Make rainfall the main part, maybe two thirds, and the crop note the last third. A seminar feels clear when it has one strong main idea and a small ending.
Can I ask my teacher Ms. Iyer for a crop article?
Yes, that is a good idea. Ms. Iyer may know a reliable article or book. Ask politely and tell her the seminar is on rainfall changes with a short ending on crops.
Thanks. What were the two topics I was choosing from?
You were choosing between rainfall changes and crop choices. You decided to lead with rainfall and add a short note on crops, which Ms. Iyer may help with.
Tomorrow is my interview for a data entry job. I'm Ella, and I type fast but I'm afraid of the typing test.
Typing fast is a real strength, Ella. Nerves can cause mistakes, so slow down a little and aim for accuracy. Accurate typing counts more than speed.
What if my hands shake?
Take a slow breath before you start and rest your wrists lightly on the desk. Look at the text, not the keys. After the first few lines, most people settle down.
Do you think they will also ask about Excel?
Quite possibly, since many data entry jobs use spreadsheets. Be ready to talk about what you have done, like sorting a list or using simple formulas. Be honest about what you know.
I only know the basics. Is that a problem?
Not necessarily. Say you know the basics and are happy to learn more. Companies often train new staff. Your fast typing is a good strength to mention.
Ok. Which test was I scared of?
You were scared of the typing test, Ella. Slow down for accuracy, keep your wrists relaxed, and remind yourself that your typing speed is already a strength.
I'm helping at my aunt's flower stall on festival weekends. Today a customer asked for something I didn't have, and I said no and he left.
That happens, and it is not your fault. Next time, you could say you do not have it today but offer something close. Customers often stay when you suggest an alternative.
He wanted marigold garlands, but we only had jasmine.
You could have shown him the jasmine garlands and said they smell lovely and last well. You could also have promised to ask your aunt about marigolds for tomorrow.
I'll try that. Mostly I felt bad for losing a sale.
It is normal to feel that, but one lost sale is small. You learned a useful trick. Tell your aunt what happened, and ask if she can stock more marigold next time.
Good idea. Maybe I'll keep a notebook of what people ask for.
That is smart. A notebook of requests will show your aunt which flowers sell most on festival days. Write the date and the flower, like the marigold garland that man wanted today.
What did he ask for again?
He asked for marigold garlands, but the stall only had jasmine. Write that first in your notebook, since it shows exactly what was missed.
My office is organising a secret gift exchange. I picked Adam's name and I know almost nothing about him.
Gift exchanges are a nice way to know colleagues better. You can find out a little about Adam without asking him directly. Does anyone sit near him?
Shreya sits next to him.
Ask Shreya casually what Adam enjoys, like a hobby or a favourite snack. Keep it light so the secret stays safe, and she may even have a good idea.
She said he loves cycling and always carries a steel bottle.
Then you have two clues. A small cycling accessory, like a bottle holder or a small bell, would match both. Keep it simple and within the office limit.
A bottle holder sounds perfect.
Great choice. It suits his steel bottle and his cycling. Wrap it neatly and add a short note, so Adam enjoys it even if he never guesses who gave it.
Who gave me the clues?
Shreya gave you the clues, since she sits next to Adam. She said he loves cycling and carries a steel bottle, which led you to the bottle holder.
I'm going to move into a shared flat in Pune with two strangers next month. I'm Varun and I'm a bit anxious.
That is a normal feeling, Varun. Living with new people can work very well when you talk early about habits. Have you met them?
Only on a video call. Their names are Imran and Sarah.
Good, you have already seen their faces. Before you move in, ask simple things like cooking times, cleaning turns and quiet hours. Agreeing early avoids small fights.
Imran said he works night shifts.
That matters. Ask how you can keep the flat quiet in the daytime, and agree when you cook or play music. It shows you are thoughtful.
Sarah suggested a chore chart. Sounds good?
A chore chart is a very good idea. It makes the sharing clear, and nobody has to nag. Put it on the fridge, and swap tasks each week so it feels fair.
Which one works night shifts?
Imran works night shifts. So agree with him on quiet hours in the daytime, and let Sarah's chore chart include small tasks that he can do before or after his shift.
I forgot my room key inside and I'm standing outside my hostel room. My roommate Lucas is at class.
That is annoying but fixable. The warden or caretaker usually has a spare key. Do you know who to ask?
The caretaker is a man called Ramesh.
Then go to Ramesh and explain politely. He may ask for your name and room number, and maybe a note to confirm. Keep your ID handy.
He opened the door. How do I avoid this next time?
Keep your key on a lanyard or a ring attached to your bag, and check your pocket every time the door closes. You could also leave a spare key with a trusted friend.
Lucas could keep one. He's reliable.
That is a sensible idea since you share the room. Just make sure Lucas knows where the spare key is kept, and tell him if you swap locks.
Thanks. Who opened the door?
The caretaker, Ramesh, opened the door for you. You could also thank him with a short word the next time you pass him.
Today my supervisor told me I made a mistake in the stock list and everyone heard. I felt humiliated. I'm Nikhil.
I'm sorry, Nikhil. Being corrected in front of others stings, even when the correction is fair. Take a moment to breathe. Do you know what exactly went wrong?
I entered 120 instead of 102 for one item.
That is a simple swap of digits, and it happens to many people. Fix the entry and check similar items for the same slip. Then move on without carrying it all day.
Should I say something to my supervisor about how it felt?
You can, but wait until you are calm. Say that you want to be accurate, and ask if corrections can be given privately next time. Keep it polite and short.
I might. Which numbers did I swap?
You entered 120 instead of 102. Correct that figure in the stock list, and double check any numbers close to it, since swapped digits are easy to miss.
I want to switch from commerce to arts in my second year. My parents think it's a bad idea.
That is a big decision, and it is good that you are thinking about it carefully. What draws you to arts?
I love history and writing. Commerce feels like a lot of numbers.
Those are real interests, and they matter. Talk with your parents about what you enjoy and what you could do with history and writing. Showing a plan helps them listen.
My cousin Shreya studied arts and works as an editor. She might talk to them.
That is a helpful example. Hearing from Shreya about her work could make your parents more comfortable. Ask her kindly if she is willing to share her experience.
Good. Can you remind me what Shreya does?
Shreya is your cousin who studied arts and now works as an editor. Her story shows your parents that history and writing can lead to real work.
A receptionist job at a clinic is what I'm applying for. I'm worried because my English isn't perfect. My name is Megha.
Thank you for telling me, Megha. Receptionists need clear, polite speech more than perfect grammar. Practising a few key phrases will help your confidence.
What phrases should I practise?
Try, Good morning, how may I help you? Please take a seat. Could you tell me your name, please? Short and kind phrases are enough for most front desk work.
Can you give me one to use for a phone call?
Yes. You can say, Good morning, this is the clinic, how may I help you? Speak slowly, and if you do not hear something, say, could you repeat that, please?
Okay. And what job is it for again?
It is for a receptionist at a clinic. Practise your greeting and your phone phrase aloud a few times, Megha, and tell the interviewer you are learning and happy to improve.
I've been volunteering at a library in the evenings. I stack books and help children find stories.
That sounds like a lovely way to spend evenings. Helping children find stories is a real service. What do you enjoy most?
A boy named Adam asks for dinosaur books every day. I like seeing his face.
That is sweet. Children who find books they love often become readers. You might keep a few dinosaur books aside for Adam, if the library allows it.
The librarian said she might hire me part-time next month.
That is great news. Volunteering shows commitment, and it gives the librarian a chance to see your work. Ask about the hours and tasks when she raises it.
Thanks. Remind me which books Adam loves?
Adam loves dinosaur books and asks for them every day. If you are hired, you could suggest a small dinosaur shelf, which the other children might enjoy too.
My colleague Ella is always late to our shared morning call and it makes me look bad because we present together.
That is frustrating. It affects your work even though it is not your fault. Have you spoken to Ella about it?
Not yet. I don't want to seem rude.
You can be kind and clear. Ask Ella privately if the morning time is hard for her, and explain that her being late makes your joint presentation harder.
What if she has a real reason, like a long commute?
Then listen and look for a solution together, such as moving the call fifteen minutes later or starting with your part. A small change may help both of you.
She says the bus is the reason. What was your idea about the call time again?

I suggested moving the morning call about fifteen minutes later, or letting your part come first if Ella is late. With her bus delays, a slightly later call may suit both of you and your presentation.
My friend Imran just moved to Goa for a hotel job and wants me to visit. I've never travelled alone.
That could be a lovely first solo trip, with a friend waiting at the other end. What are you most nervous about?
Reaching the right place from the station, mostly.
Ask Imran to send you clear directions or the name of a landmark, and keep his phone number handy. Reach in daylight so you can see the route well.
He said he'll meet me at the station.
Even better. Then the hard part is only buying the ticket and boarding the right train. Check your coach and seat number, and keep your bag close.
That makes me feel better. Where was Imran's job?
Imran works at a hotel in Goa, as you said. Enjoy the trip, and tell him your train time so he is at the station when you arrive.
My lab partner, Nikhil, broke a glass beaker today and now he's afraid to tell the lab assistant.
That is a stressful moment for him, but beakers break in labs all the time. The best step is to tell the assistant calmly and clean up carefully.
He's worried he'll be scolded.
Lab assistants see this often. Honesty usually goes down much better than hiding it. You can stand beside Nikhil while he explains, so he does not feel alone.
Okay, I'll go with him. Should we pick up the glass ourselves?
Better to let the lab assistant handle the broken beaker, or ask for the right brush and tray. Sharp pieces can cut easily. Stand with Nikhil while he explains, and warn others nearby to keep away.
I started helping at a chai stall near my college. The owner, Raju bhai, wants me to take orders.
That is a busy job, but taking orders is a good way to learn how to talk to many people quickly. Keep a calm voice and repeat each order back.
The stall gets crowded after four. I'm afraid of mixing up orders.
Then use a small pad and write the table or the customer's description next to each order. Fill them in the same order they came, so nobody feels skipped.
Raju bhai said I can take the lunch break at three instead.
That sounds smart, since three is before the rush at four. Thank Raju bhai, eat properly and rest a little, so you have energy to take orders in the crowded hour.
A new girl, Divya, moved into the room opposite mine today. She looked lost with her bags.
That was a good moment to help. New hostel residents often feel unsure about everything. Did you speak to her?
I offered to carry a bag. She smiled and said thanks.
A small act like that makes a big difference on the first day. She will probably remember it when she settles in. Maybe invite her to the mess with you tonight.
Good idea. I'll tell her about the dinner timing.
Do that, and also mention where the water filter and laundry area are. Little details like these save a new person a lot of confusion, and Divya will appreciate it.
I have to introduce myself in a campus placement round. I'm Varun, from a small town, and I'm afraid they will look down on me.
Your background is part of your story, Varun, and it can be a strength. People often respect someone who has worked hard to reach a place. Say it simply and proudly.
What should I say about my town?
You can say where you are from and one thing you learned there, like independence or hard work. Keep it to a sentence or two, then move to your studies and goals.
I learned to fix bicycles at my uncle's shop as a boy.
That is a lovely detail. It shows practical skills and curiosity. You can say, in my town I learned to fix bicycles in my uncle's shop, and that taught me patience.
I'm about to resign from my first job because my team is really unfriendly. I'm Sarah and I've been here for four months.
I'm sorry that it has been hard, Sarah. Before you decide, take a day to think about what exactly feels wrong. Is it everyone, or a few people?
Mainly two people who ignore me in meetings. The others are okay.
Then it may be worth giving a conversation a try before quitting. A senior or your manager might be able to help. Leaving is still your choice, but you can leave later with a clear mind.
I might speak to my manager, Mr. Khan, this week.
That is a calm step. Tell Mr. Khan what you have noticed with the two colleagues, using facts such as being ignored in meetings, and ask what could improve things.
What exactly should I describe?
Describe only what you saw, such as not being asked for ideas in meetings, and how it affects your work. Do not guess their reasons. Mr. Khan can then decide how to help.
And what was my plan again?
You plan to speak with Mr. Khan this week about the two colleagues who ignore you, before deciding whether to resign. That gives the team a fair chance to improve.
I live in Bhopal and I'm moving to Indore for a new college. I've never lived away from my parents.
That is a big first step towards independence. It will feel strange at first, and that is fine. Do you know where you will live in Indore?
In a paying guest place that my uncle found. The owner is Mr. Joshi.
Good that your uncle helped. Ask Mr. Joshi simple things when you arrive, like meal times, water timings and rules for visitors. Knowing the rules early avoids trouble.
My mother wants me to call every day. Is that too much?
It depends on what you both feel good about. A short call each evening can keep her calm. You can agree on a time that suits your classes.
Good. Who found the place?
Your uncle found the paying guest place, and the owner is Mr. Joshi. Mention your uncle's name when you meet Mr. Joshi, as it will help him place you.
Okay, and could you suggest a time for the calls?
Choose a time after dinner, maybe eight or nine, when you are done with classes. A fixed time helps your mother plan, and you will not need to rush while still in Indore.
Our office has a new rule that everyone must clean their own cups. My colleague Lucas says it's silly.
Small rules like that can annoy people, but they often keep the shared kitchen tidy. What do you think about it?
I don't mind, but I think Lucas will keep leaving his cup.
Then you could remind him lightly, in a friendly way. Something like, let us all keep it clean so no one has to scold us. Humour usually works better than a lecture.
He might get annoyed. He's a bit sensitive.
Then stay gentle and do not make it public. A quiet word, or a joke while you both wash cups, is better. If the cups still pile up, leave it for your supervisor.
Honestly, I'd rather just wash his cup myself.
That is kind, but it may teach Lucas that he does not need to wash his own. Do it once with a smile, and mention the new rule lightly so he understands.
I'm Ella. Tomorrow I'm presenting my project to the class. Today my laptop crashed and I lost my slides.
That is stressful, but you have time. Do you have an older copy, or did you send the slides to anyone?
I emailed them to Shreya last week, but they're not the final version.
Then ask Shreya to send them right away. Even an older copy gives you a base to rebuild from. You will remember most of the changes you made.
She sent them. I need to redo the last three slides.
That is a manageable amount. Write short notes first, then rebuild the slides. Save your work in two places this time, such as your laptop and a pen drive.
Where was I going to save it?
I suggested two places, your laptop and a pen drive, so a crash cannot take everything. Thank Shreya for the older copy, since it saved you hours of work tonight.
I'm sharing a hostel room with a girl who leaves the light on all night. I'm Megha, and I have a headache every morning.
That sounds uncomfortable, Megha. Poor sleep can really affect your day. A polite talk is a good first step. Have you spoken to her about it?
No. I'm afraid she'll say I'm being fussy.
It is reasonable to ask for a dark room at night. You could offer a compromise, such as a small desk lamp for her or a sleep mask for you.
A sleep mask sounds easier. Where do I get one?
Most small shops and pharmacies near campus sell them cheaply. Ask a friend or a floor mate where she bought hers. It is a simple fix that does not need an argument.
Maybe I'll try it before I say anything.
That is fine. Try the mask for a week and see if the mornings improve. If the headaches stay, tell her gently about the light, and think about seeing a doctor.
What did I plan to try first?
You planned to try a sleep mask first, before talking to your roommate. Give it a week, and speak up kindly if the light still bothers you.
I applied to teach at a coaching centre and they want a sample class on the water cycle. I'm Lucas.
A sample class is your chance to show how you teach. The water cycle is a good topic because you can use drawings and simple steps. Who is the class for?
Class seven students, around twelve years old.
For that age, keep the steps clear, evaporation, condensation, rain and collection. Draw a simple cycle on the board and ask them to guess what comes next.
Should I do an experiment too?
A tiny one helps. You could show a steamed glass lid with drops forming, to show condensation. Check first that it is allowed and safe, and keep it short.
Good. What age group was it again?
The class is for Class seven students, around twelve years old. Keep your language simple, use the drawing, and invite them to explain each step back to you.
After college, I work part-time at a photocopy shop. A customer left an original certificate in the machine yesterday. It's still here.
Good that you noticed it. A certificate is important to its owner and they are probably worried. Tell your shop owner right away and keep it somewhere safe.
The owner said to keep it in the drawer. How do I find the person?
If the shop has a record of the job, check it for a name or number. Otherwise, the owner can put up a small note, or you can tell regular customers to pass the word.
I'm not sure the shop keeps records.

Then a short note on the door saying that an original certificate is waiting at the counter may work. Keep it in the drawer as the owner said, and do not mention the name on it, so only the true owner claims it.
I moved to Nagpur and I miss my old city. My new colleague Shreya keeps inviting me out but I keep saying no.
It is understandable, since missing a place is real. It might be worth saying yes to one invitation. Shreya seems to want to help you settle.
She asked me to try a local snack shop on Saturday.
That sounds like an easy, short outing. Trying a local snack with Shreya is a gentle way to enjoy the new city without a big commitment.
Okay. What if I run out of things to talk about?
Ask her about the city and the snack itself, such as what to order and where else she goes. People enjoy sharing local tips, and the food gives you something to talk about.
Good tip. Where did she invite me?
Shreya invited you to a local snack shop on Saturday. Say yes this time, ask her for her favourite snack there, and see if you feel a little more at home afterwards.
I'm six weeks into a call centre job and the late shifts are affecting my sleep. I'm Adam.
Shift work can be hard on the body. Setting a steady routine around your sleep helps. Do you get a chance to rest during the day?
I sleep from about nine to three, but it's noisy at home.
Noise is a common problem for day sleepers. Try earplugs, a dark curtain and a quiet corner. Tell your family your sleep hours so they can help keep it calm.
My sister Divya has exams so she is home all day.
Then you could both agree on a quiet time, maybe with her studying in another room during your sleep hours. Both of you need peace, so a short chat could help.
I'll talk to her tonight. And what are my sleep hours again?
You sleep from about nine to three. When you talk to Divya, say these hours clearly, so she knows when to keep the house quiet while she studies.
My hostel is organising a cultural night and I volunteered to sing. I haven't told my roommate Imran.
That is brave of you to volunteer. Singing in front of the hostel takes courage. Why haven't you told Imran?
I wanted it to be a surprise, but I need to practise.
Then you could practise somewhere else, like the terrace or an empty classroom. Or tell Imran, and ask him to keep it secret. That way you can practise in the room too.
I'll tell him. He might even help with the song.
That would be nice. If Imran likes music, he can give honest feedback and cheer you up. Choose a song you know well and can sing comfortably.
What if I forget the lyrics on the cultural night?
Keep the lyrics on a small card while practising, and sing for Imran a few times so the song sticks. If you slip on the night, keep going calmly, and the audience will cheer you on.
I've been invited to a second round interview after a very good first one. I'm excited and scared. My name is Ella.
Well done, Ella. A second round means they liked you. It is natural to feel both excited and scared. Do you know who you will meet?
Probably the department head and maybe the founder.
Then expect questions about your goals and how you would fit with the team. Revisit your first interview in your mind and think about what you can add.
In the first round I forgot to ask any questions at the end.
Prepare two or three this time, like what a normal week looks like or how the team works together. Asking shows real interest, and it gives you a chance to know them.
What did I forget to do last time?
Last time you forgot to ask any questions at the end. This time, keep two or three ready, and ask them calmly when the department head or founder invites you to.
I'm a part-time cashier at a small grocery store. I got a customer's change wrong today and I'm upset.
Mistakes with change are common, especially when the shop is busy. What happened after that?
The customer noticed and corrected me. My boss, Mr. Gupta, said it's okay, but I feel silly.
Mr. Gupta's reaction is a good sign. Everyone slips while learning. Slow down a little when handling money, and say the amounts aloud as you count.
Does counting aloud help with the mistake I made with the change?

Yes, saying the amounts aloud helps you catch an error before the customer does. When you give back change, count up from the bill amount so both of you can follow. Ask Mr. Gupta to watch you do it a few times.
A colleague named Imran borrowed my pen drive three weeks ago and hasn't returned it. I need it now.
That is annoying, particularly when you need it. A friendly reminder is fine. Do you work close to him?
We sit two desks apart.
Then stop by his desk and say you need the pen drive back today, and ask if he has it with him. Keep your tone light, so it does not become awkward.
He said it's at home and he'd bring it tomorrow.
That is fair. Remind him again tomorrow morning with a smile if he forgets, and perhaps keep a copy of important files elsewhere in future.
Who borrowed it again?
Imran borrowed your pen drive, and he promised to bring it tomorrow. A quick friendly reminder at his desk in the morning will help him remember.
I'm helping my friend Lucas move to Chennai tomorrow. We'll take the train with a lot of boxes.
Trains can be tricky with many boxes. Plan so that you can lift everything easily. Are they sealed and labelled?
Some are labelled. A few aren't.
Label them all tonight with a marker, writing what is inside and which room it goes to. That will save you both time when you reach Chennai.
The heavy boxes have books. Should I pack them in small boxes?
Yes, books are heavy, so smaller boxes are easier to lift and safer on the train. Do not fill a box to the top with them, and tape the bottoms well.
Good call. Where are we going again?
You are going to Chennai with Lucas, by train. Label every box, keep the small book boxes together near your seats, and make sure you can see them at all times.
I'm finding it hard to wake up for my eight o'clock lectures. I'm Nikhil and I live ten minutes from college.
Eight o'clock lectures are tough for many students. Is it that you sleep late, or that you wake up and fall back asleep?
Both, honestly. I stay up studying and then sleep through my alarm.
Try moving your study time earlier in the evening, and put your phone away at a fixed hour. A regular bedtime helps you wake naturally.
I'll try ten thirty. What about the alarm?
Put it across the room, so you must stand up to switch it off. Some people add a second alarm five minutes later. Ten thirty is a good bedtime to aim for.
I also wanted to ask: is it fine to skip a few lectures?
Missing a few now and then is not the end of the world, but it adds up. Notes and explanations are easy to lose. Try the ten thirty bedtime first, and keep skipping for real emergencies.
What time did I choose for bedtime?
You chose ten thirty, Nikhil. Hold to it for a week, along with the across-the-room alarm, and see whether the eight o'clock lectures feel easier.
My roommate Sarah and I are planning to cook instant noodles in our hostel room, but I'm worried about the rules.
It is wise to check first. Many hostels do not allow cooking in rooms, mainly for safety. Do you know your hostel's rule?
I think there's a rule, but I haven't read it.
Then read the rule sheet or ask the warden politely. If cooking is not allowed, you can use the shared kitchen or the canteen, or eat a ready snack instead.
Sarah says the warden never checks. Should we just do it?
I would not risk it. The rules are there for fire safety, and a small accident can be serious. Check with the warden, and ask about the shared kitchen.
Okay. Who did I want to cook with?
You wanted to cook with your roommate Sarah. Show her the rule sheet or ask the warden together, and then plan a safe place to make your noodles.
I'm Divya and I've been offered a phone interview at nine tomorrow. I live in a noisy neighbourhood.
Noise can distract you and the interviewer. Think of a quiet spot, like a closed room, a parked car or a friend's place.
My cousin Adam's house is quiet. He's at work in the mornings.
That is a good option. Ask Adam if you can use a room at nine, and arrive early so you are settled. A quiet room will help you sound calm.
He said yes. Should I keep notes in front of me?
Yes, a few notes with key points are fine on a phone interview. Keep your CV, a pen and a glass of water nearby. Do not read from a script, though.
What time is it again?
Your phone interview is at nine tomorrow morning. Be at Adam's house a little earlier, test the phone signal, and sit somewhere comfortable and quiet.
I'm a teaching assistant at a small tuition centre. One student, Kabir, keeps talking in class and disturbing others.
That is a common challenge. Before anything else, think about why he talks. He may be bored, confused or just full of energy. What have you tried so far?
I asked him to stop twice, but he starts again within minutes.
Try giving him a small task, like handing out sheets or reading a line aloud. Some children talk less when they feel useful. Praise him when he stays quiet.
Interesting. I'll try giving him a job tomorrow.
Good plan. Keep the job short and clear, and thank him in front of the class when he does it well. Be consistent, and watch whether the talking drops.
What was his name again?
The student's name is Kabir. Tomorrow, hand him a small job like distributing sheets, and notice if he stays calmer once he has something useful to do.
I'm moving to Kochi in a month. I've heard it rains a lot there. I'm Megha, and I'm going for a job.
Kochi does get plenty of rain in the monsoon, so planning ahead will help. Do you have a place to stay yet?
Yes, a room with a family. It's close to my office.
A nearby room is a big plus in rainy weather, since you will not have to travel far. Ask the family where water sometimes collects in the lane.
What should I carry for the rain?
A sturdy umbrella, a light raincoat, and shoes or sandals that dry fast. Carry a small bag cover too, and keep an extra pair of socks at the office.
Good ideas. And where did I say I'm moving?
You are moving to Kochi in a month, for a job. Pack the umbrella, raincoat and fast-drying footwear first, since the rain there can arrive without much warning.
Let me tell you about my first week at college. On day one I got on the wrong bus and ended up in a different town.
Oh no, that must have been a shock. Getting on the wrong bus on the first day is stressful. How did you get back?
A kind conductor told me where to change. I reached college two hours late. The gate guard, Mr. Das, let me in without fuss.
That was lucky, and it sounds like both the conductor and Mr. Das were decent to you. Did you manage to find your class after that?
Yes, a boy named Varun showed me the room. We sat together and became friends. Now which person helped me at the gate?
It was Mr. Das, the gate guard, who let you in without fuss. And Varun showed you the room, so your wrong bus ride gave you two kind helpers and a new friend.
Guess what, I got promoted from trainee to executive today! I'm Sarah and it has been just one year.
That is great news, Sarah. A promotion after one year shows real effort and good work. How are you feeling?
Happy and a little scared. My new manager is going to be Mr. Menon, who I don't know well.
Mixed feelings are normal when a role changes. Try to meet Mr. Menon early and ask what he expects from you in the first month. That gives you a clear picture.
Good idea. I also want to thank the old manager, Ms. Roy. She trained me.
A thank-you to Ms. Roy would be a lovely gesture. Be specific and mention one thing she taught you, so she knows what stayed with you.
I'd say she taught me to double check every report.
Then say exactly that. Telling Ms. Roy that her habit of double checking reports shaped your work is a warm and honest thanks, and she will be proud to hear it.
Who is my new manager going to be?
Your new manager is Mr. Menon. Since you do not know him well, arrange a short chat soon, and mention that Ms. Roy taught you to double check every report.
I'm preparing for an interview at a travel agency. I love maps and I'm good at planning trips for friends.
That is a good fit. Planning trips for friends is real experience, even if it was informal. Can you think of one trip you planned that went well?
Yes, a three day trip to Mysore for six friends, including Adam and Ella.
Great example. Tell it in a few short steps, how you chose places, how you organised the days and how everyone enjoyed it. Mention the number of friends to show you can handle a group.
They might ask what went wrong. Our bus was late.

Be honest and show what you did. Say the bus was late on the Mysore trip, and explain how you changed the plan so that all six friends still saw the main places. That shows you can solve problems calmly.
Tomorrow my parents are visiting my hostel for the first time. I want to show them around, but my room is a mess.
A tidy room will make your parents happy, and it only takes an evening. Start with the bed, desk and floor, since those are what visitors notice first.
My roommate Adam is out of town, so it's my job alone.
Then focus on your side and the shared areas. Sweep the floor, stack books neatly, and put loose clothes in the cupboard. Open the window to let in fresh air.
Good. I'll also show them the mess hall. Should I take them there at lunch?
Lunchtime is a fine choice, since your parents can see how the mess works and eat with you. Ask the warden whether visitors can eat in the mess, and finish the room first, since Adam is away.
I've started a small job at an ice cream parlour. On the first day, the manager, Ms. Lobo, taught me to scoop. It's harder than it looks.
It really is. Scooping takes a bit of wrist technique and practice. How did it go?
The scoops were uneven and one fell on the floor.
That is a common beginner's result. Dip the scoop in warm water, press into the tub and turn your wrist as you lift. Neat scoops come with repetition.
Ms. Lobo said I'd be good in a week. Should I believe her?
Yes, managers usually know how fast a new person improves. Practise carefully, and ask Ms. Lobo for tips whenever the parlour is quiet. A week of effort should show clearly.
I think my colleague Imran is taking credit for my work. Yesterday he presented my chart as his.
That sounds upsetting. Before you decide anything, make sure you have the facts right. Did you share the chart with him, or did he take it from somewhere?
I sent it to the group for feedback. He used it without saying it was mine.
That is a clear situation. You can speak to Imran privately and say that you noticed it, and ask him to credit you next time. Stay calm and factual.
What if he denies it?

Then calmly mention that you sent the chart to the group for feedback, so the date is on record. Tell Imran you only want your work credited. If it keeps happening, tell your manager with the details, not with anger.
Our bus got stuck in a traffic jam in Bangalore and I missed my first day orientation at the new company.
That is unlucky, and many people in big cities have had the same experience. Have you contacted the company?
Yes, I called HR. A lady named Divya said I can join the afternoon session.
That is a relief. Apologise briefly when you arrive and thank Divya for her help. Plan to leave earlier tomorrow, since the traffic may still be heavy.
I'll leave one hour earlier. Who did I speak to at HR?
You spoke to Divya at HR, who offered you the afternoon session. Mention her name when you arrive, so the people at the desk know the plan is already agreed.
Our teacher announced a surprise quiz tomorrow. I'm Lucas and I haven't read the last chapter.
Surprise quizzes are stressful. One evening is enough to cover the main points of one chapter. Do you have your book and notes with you?
Yes. It's the chapter on the human heart.
Read the headings first, then the diagrams, then the summary at the end. Try drawing the heart and labelling the four chambers from memory. That is a good way to test yourself.
I did the drawing but forgot one of the valves.
Look at the diagram again and say the valve names aloud, then draw it a second time. Repeating it a few times fixes the picture in your head.
Okay. Which chapter did I say I was reading?
You said it is the chapter on the human heart. Draw the labelled heart once more before bed, and again in the morning, so the valves are clear for the quiz.
Should I study that chapter again in the morning too?
Yes, a quick ten minute look at the heart diagram and the valve names in the morning will help, since the quiz is tomorrow. Draw the four chambers once more from memory, Lucas.
There is an interview for a bakery assistant job coming up. I have never worked in a bakery but I bake at home with my mother.
Home baking counts as real experience, and it shows you enjoy the work. What do you usually bake?
Mostly cakes and eggless cookies. I'm Shreya, by the way.
Nice to meet you, Shreya. Eggless cookies are useful to mention, since many customers prefer them. Describe your best cake in a sentence or two.
My best is a coffee walnut cake that my neighbours love.
That is a lovely detail. You can say that neighbours ask you to bake your coffee walnut cake, which proves that people enjoy your work.
What should I say about not having formal experience?
Be honest. Say you have baked at home for years and are eager to learn the professional side. Mention your coffee walnut cake and the eggless cookies as examples.
Good. What cake did I say was my best?
You said your best is the coffee walnut cake that your neighbours love. Keep it as the highlight of your answer, Shreya, and offer to bring a small sample if they allow it.
I'm Varun and I help my father in his stationery shop after school. A boy came and asked for a red pen, then argued about the price.
Customers sometimes argue over small things, even a pen that costs very little. What did you do when he started arguing?
I said the price is fixed, and he left without buying.
That was fine, though you could also have been friendly and said the pen has a good quality. Some customers just need a pleasant word to feel respected.
My father said the same. He also said I should smile more.
Your father makes a good point. A smile makes even a fixed price on a red pen sound kinder, Varun, and customers often come back to a shop where they feel welcome.
I'm Divya, and my hostel has a Sunday cleaning duty where each room cleans a corridor section. Our room is cleaning the longest part.
That is a lot of work. Dividing the corridor into smaller parts and sharing tasks will help. How many of you are in the room?
Three of us. Me, Megha and Shreya.
Then each person can take one task, such as sweeping, mopping and clearing the dustbins. Switch tasks every week, so it feels fair to all three of you.
Shreya does not like mopping. What should we do?
Ask her which task she minds least, and give her that one this week. Then rotate fairly. If everyone knows they will swap, nobody has to be stuck with the job they dislike.
Okay. And who are the three of us?
You, Divya, with Megha and Shreya. Plan the rotation on a small paper on the door, so that every Sunday it is clear who sweeps, who mops and who handles the dustbins.
Shreya says she would rather start with sweeping. Is that fine?
That works well, since Shreya dislikes mopping. Put her on sweeping this week and give mopping to whoever minds it least. Rotate next Sunday so Megha and you both get a turn at each task.
My first month at a small design firm is ending. My boss, Ms. Kapoor, asked me to give feedback on how the training went.
That is a thoughtful request, and a good chance to speak honestly. What did you find helpful?
The weekly sessions with Mr. Nair were great. He explained tools slowly.
You can tell Ms. Kapoor that. Naming Mr. Nair's sessions as helpful shows what worked, and it helps her keep that part of the training.
I also wish I had more practice tasks. Is it okay to say that?

Yes, say it politely to Ms. Kapoor. For example, I would learn faster with a few more practice tasks. Mention it after praising Mr. Nair's sessions, since feedback that offers a solution is usually welcomed.
I'm helping my brother Nikhil find a flat in Hyderabad. He works at a bank. We saw three flats today.
That is a busy day, with a lot to take in. How did the three flats compare with each other?
The first was dark but cheap. The second was bright but far from his office. The third had a balcony and was close, but old.
Each has something good. Since Nikhil goes to work daily, a close one saves energy, and a balcony gives him fresh air. Check the old building's water and wiring.
Nikhil likes the third one too. What should we check there?
Look at taps, switches, ceiling corners for damp, and ask neighbours about water and noise. Visit again at a different time of day to see the light and traffic.
We'll go again tomorrow evening. Which flat did we say is old?
It was the third one, the flat with the balcony close to his office. When you visit tomorrow evening, check the old parts carefully, and see how noisy the street gets at that hour.
Should we revisit the second flat too, the bright one, if the third one fails?
Yes, keep the second flat as a backup for Nikhil. It is bright, though far from his office, so check the travel time at office hours before you decide. See the third one first tomorrow evening.
I'm choosing my elective subject next week. I'm torn between psychology and economics. I'm Adam.
Both are interesting. Which one do you imagine yourself reading about on a free evening?
Psychology, I think, but my father says economics is more practical.
It is good to listen to your father, and it is also fine to choose what you enjoy. Interest keeps you going when the subject gets hard.
My friend Ella took psychology last year. Maybe I should ask her about it.
Yes, ask her what the classes are like, how much reading there is and what the exams ask. A friend's honest view is more useful than the course description.
Which two subjects was I choosing between?
You were choosing between psychology and economics. Ask Ella about psychology first, and then, if you want, find a senior who took economics, so you hear both sides.
In my last interview, the panel asked me where I see myself in five years. I gave a vague answer. I'm Ella.
That question is hard for many people. A vague answer is common, so do not worry. Let us prepare a better one. What would you like to be doing?
I'd like to lead a small team in marketing.
Then say that. For example, in five years I hope to have grown in marketing and to be leading a small team. Add what you plan to learn on the way.
I'd learn about customer research and how to manage people.
Perfect. Say that you want to build skills in customer research and in managing people. This shows you have a clear plan without sounding too fixed.
So how would I put it all together?
You could say, in five years I would like to lead a small marketing team. To get there I want to learn customer research and how to manage people, and I hope to learn them here.
That sounds good. What did I want to lead?
You want to lead a small team in marketing. Say it in your own words and with confidence, Ella, and the panel will see that you have a direction.
A few weeks ago I started selling handmade bracelets with my friend Megha at a weekend market. It's slow so far.
Starting a small stall is a good experience, and slow starts are normal. What have you sold so far?
Mostly to people we know. Strangers walk past.
Try placing your best bracelets at the front, and add a small sign with a friendly line. Smiling and greeting people as they pass can also stop them for a look.
Megha says we should add a few cheaper small items.
That is a reasonable idea. Small items such as hair ties or keychains may attract people who want a little gift, and then they may look at the bracelets.
We'll try it next Sunday. Who is my partner at the stall?
Your partner is your friend Megha. Next Sunday, you could set up the small items together at the front, and see which ones people pick up first.
My team's lunch group includes a new guy, Lucas, who doesn't like spicy food, and we always order spicy. What should we do?
That is a thoughtful question. A small change can make Lucas comfortable. Could you order some mild dishes alongside the spicy ones?
Yes, we usually share. I could suggest a mild option too.
Do it casually. You could say, let us add a mild dish for Lucas, and nobody has to feel awkward. Most people are happy to share when they know.
Good. Is it okay to ask him what he likes?
Yes, asking is polite. Say, Lucas, what dishes do you enjoy? Then others can see what works. It also tells him that the group cares about his choices.
Great. Which dish did I say we always order?
You said the group always orders spicy food, not one particular dish. Ask Lucas what mild dishes he likes, and add one of them to the next order for everyone to share.
Lucas is new, so should I tell the others about his dislike before we order?
Better to ask Lucas first and let him decide whether to mention it. If he is fine with it, simply say you would like to add a mild dish, so he does not feel singled out in front of the group.
On my first night in the hostel, I couldn't sleep because of the unfamiliar sounds. I'm Nikhil, a first year student.
That is very common. A new place has new sounds, and your mind stays alert at first. Did anything in particular keep you up?
The ceiling fan clicked and someone was talking loudly in the corridor.
Both are usually temporary. You will get used to the fan within days, and you can ask your floor mates to keep the corridor quiet at night. Earplugs may help for now.
Where should I ask about the fan?
Tell your warden or the caretaker, and mention your room number. A clicking fan often needs a small fix, like tightening a screw or oiling it.
Tomorrow I have an interview at a software company. My cousin Divya works there but I don't want her help to look like a favour.
That is a mature way to think. You can still ask Divya for general guidance, such as what the interview is like, without asking for special treatment.
She told me they ask coding questions and a few about teamwork.
Good, then prepare for both. Practise a couple of coding problems aloud, and think of a teamwork example from college. Explain your reasoning step by step.
My teamwork example is about our robotics project.
That is a fine example. Say what your role was, what challenge the team faced and how you helped solve it. Since Divya told you they ask about teamwork, keep the robotics story short and honest.
I was homesick in my new city until I found a small park near my flat where old men play chess. I'm Adam.
What a nice discovery, Adam. A familiar activity in a new place can make it feel warmer. Do you play chess?
A little. I joined a game with a man named Mr. Pillai and lost badly.
Losing to an experienced player is how most people improve. Mr. Pillai may enjoy having a new opponent, so go back and ask him to show you a trick or two.
I'll go again tomorrow. Do you think they'd mind if I just watch?
Most chess players welcome a quiet watcher, and watching is a good way to learn. Greet them politely, stand a little back, and ask questions during a break.
What was the man's name who beat me?
It was Mr. Pillai, who beat you at the park. When you go tomorrow, you could greet him by name and ask him to explain one move from the game.
Should I take my own chess set when I go back tomorrow?
You do not need to, Adam. The men at the park already play there, so they have boards. Bring a small notebook instead to jot down Mr. Pillai's tips, and ask him to show you one move from your game.
I joined the college cycling club and today we did a ten kilometre ride. I'm Shreya and I'm very tired but happy.
That sounds like a good day. A first group ride is a nice mix of effort and fun. How did your legs feel?
Sore. My friend Lucas rode ahead and waited for me at every turn.
That was kind of Lucas. Riding with someone who waits is helpful when you are new. Drink water, stretch gently and rest tonight.
Should I thank him?
A short thank you is nice. Tell Lucas you appreciated him waiting at every turn, and that it made the ride more fun for you.
I've been working at a fruit stall on holidays. I'm Imran and my uncle owns it. This week he asked me to run it alone for a few hours.
That is a sign that he trusts you. Running a stall alone is a good test. How do you feel about it?
A bit nervous about weighing and counting change.
Practise with your uncle for a short while before he leaves. Ask him to show you the weights and let you handle a few sales with him watching.
He did. I'm okay now. I'll sell mangoes, bananas and guavas.
Good. Arrange the fruit neatly, keep the prices clearly visible, and greet each customer. If someone asks for something you do not know, you can say you will check with your uncle.
Right. What fruits did I list?
You listed mangoes, bananas and guavas. Keep them in separate tidy piles with price cards, and your first hours alone at the stall will go smoothly, Imran.
If a customer wants guavas and I have sold them all, what do I say?
