Say politely that the guavas are finished for today, and suggest the mangoes or bananas you still have, Imran. Tell your uncle afterwards, so he stocks more guavas the next time at the stall.
Our hostel water supply stops at seven in the morning and I always miss my bath. I'm Sarah, and I'm in the girls' block.
That is irritating when you are trying to get ready. Could you shift your routine a little, for example by filling a bucket the night before?
I do that sometimes, but my roommate Megha also uses it.
Then you could each fill your own bucket at night, and use the early water first. A small stool or mug near the tap saves time in the morning.
Maybe I'll wake up at six thirty. Do you think that's enough?

If the water stops at seven, six thirty gives you half an hour, which is enough for most people. Fill your bucket at night anyway, since Megha uses the water too. Set a clear alarm so you are not rushed.
I just finished my first week at an accounts firm. I'm Varun and I was mostly filing papers. It feels boring.
The first week is often about the small tasks. It can feel boring, but filing teaches you where things are and what the firm handles. Did you notice anything interesting in the papers?
I noticed they use a lot of colour tabs. My senior, Mr. Rao, said it was his idea.
That is a clever system, and it sounds like Mr. Rao enjoys organising. Ask him how he chose the colours. Understanding his system helps you find things fast.
I will. Should I also ask for more interesting work?
Not yet in the first week. Do the filing neatly for a couple of weeks, then politely ask Mr. Rao whether you can try something new, such as checking entries.
Okay. What did I say Mr. Rao did?
You said Mr. Rao came up with the colour tab system. Asking him about it is a friendly way to start a talk, and it will also show him that you are paying attention.
Should I ask him on Monday morning, or wait until after lunch?
Monday after lunch may be better, since mornings are usually busy. Ask Mr. Rao about his colour tab system when he looks free, and bring your notebook to write down the colours he uses.
I'm Ella and I just moved to Mysuru. I'm taking a walk each evening to learn the area. Today I found a lovely bakery.
That is a pleasant way to get to know a place. What kind of bakery was it?
A small family one. I bought a fresh bun and the owner, Mrs. Fernandes, told me about the festival next week.
What a friendly welcome. Festivals are a nice way to meet people in a new city. Do you know what kind of festival it is?
A flower and food fair near the palace road. She said it's lively.
That sounds lovely. Go early in the evening when it is cooler and less crowded, and carry a small bag for any flowers or treats you buy.
I might go with a colleague, Adam. Who told me about the fair?
Mrs. Fernandes at the bakery told you about it. Ask Adam if he would like to come along, and you could even stop at her bakery for a bun on the way.
Adam can't make it on that day. Is the fair on any other day?
I cannot check what is on, Ella, but Mrs. Fernandes at the bakery knows the area well. Ask her whether the flower and food fair runs over several days, so Adam can join you another evening.
Tomorrow I interview at a newspaper office as a trainee reporter. I'm Divya and I wrote for my college magazine.
Your magazine work is a real asset. Pick two or three pieces you are proud of, and be ready to describe how you wrote them.
One was about a local potter, Mr. Naidu, whom I interviewed for two hours.
That is a perfect example for a reporter. Explain how you prepared your questions, how you listened, and what you learned about his work. It shows patience and curiosity.
They may ask about deadlines. I once wrote an article overnight.
Mention it, but also say how you plan your time normally, so it does not sound like a habit. Show that you can work under pressure and also prepare ahead.
Should I bring the article?
Yes, bring a clean printed copy of the potter story and one other piece. Keep them in a folder, and offer them only if asked, or at the end of the interview.
Which person did I interview for that piece?
You interviewed Mr. Naidu, the local potter, for two hours. Bring the printed article, and be ready to tell the interviewers what you learned from that long conversation.
I work as a library helper on weekends. A boy asked me for a book on space but we only had one and it was torn.
That is a small problem to solve. Could you offer him another space book or check whether the torn one is still readable?
The torn one is missing its last pages. There is also a children's book about planets.
You could show him the planets book and explain that it covers the same topic in simple language. Also let your supervisor know about the torn book so it can be repaired.
He took the planets book. I told Mr. Thomas about the torn one.
Well done on both counts. The boy found something to read, and Mr. Thomas can now arrange repairs. That is good, careful library work.
I'm making a presentation for my college annual day. I'm Nikhil, and my teacher, Mrs. Verma, gave me the topic of water saving.
That is a useful topic, and easy to connect to everyday life. How long is your slot?
Five minutes. I'm thinking of three simple tips.
Three tips are perfect for five minutes. Make each one practical, such as fixing a leaking tap, closing the tap while brushing and collecting used water for plants.
I like those. Should I also include a story?
A very short real-life example makes the talk memorable. You could mention a household that saved water with small habits, but keep it to a sentence or two.
Okay. Who gave me the topic again?
Mrs. Verma, your teacher, gave you the topic of water saving. When you finish, you could thank her briefly and show her your three tips before the annual day.
Which of the three tips should come first in my talk?
Start with fixing a leaking tap, since everyone can relate to it. Then closing the tap while brushing, and last collecting used water for plants. Show Mrs. Verma this order tomorrow for her opinion.
I'm on the hostel committee this year. I'm Lucas and I'm in charge of organising the freshers' welcome.
Congratulations, Lucas. A welcome event sets the mood for new students. What are you planning?
A small get-together on the terrace with snacks and a few games. About forty people.
That sounds friendly. Forty people need some structure. Keep the games simple, like name tag mixing or a quick quiz, so new students talk to each other.
Good, that helps. We were also thinking of a short talk by the warden, Mrs. Pillai.
A short talk from Mrs. Pillai is useful, since she can explain the rules and who to contact. Ask her to keep it to five minutes, and to share it before the games begin.
Do you think we should have a rain plan?
Yes, definitely. Keep an indoor space, such as the common room, ready for the terrace party. Tell everyone where to go if the weather changes, and keep the snacks covered.
Good point. Who is going to give the talk?
Mrs. Pillai, your warden, will give the short talk. Ask her to speak before the games, and have the common room ready as your backup for the freshers' welcome.
My roommate, Megha, is leaving the hostel next month and I'd miss her. I'm Ella.
That is sad news, Ella. It is hard when a roommate you get along with moves out. Has she told you why she is leaving?
She got a flat closer to her internship. We might end up in separate blocks anyway.
Then it makes sense for her. You can still stay in touch and meet for meals in the mess. Ask the warden early who your next roommate might be.
Good point. Could I ask to pick the new person myself?
You can ask, and some wardens allow it if you name a friend who needs a bed. If you cannot choose, tell the warden what matters to you, like quiet at night, so Megha's replacement suits you.
I've been asked to represent my team at a client meeting next week. My manager, Mr. D'Souza, will be there too.
That is a good sign that he trusts you. Having Mr. D'Souza in the room also means you are not alone. What will you need to talk about?
The progress of our packaging redesign. I'll cover the timeline.
Then prepare a simple timeline with three or four key dates and one line on what is done. Keep your explanation clear so a client with no technical knowledge can follow.
Mr. D'Souza wants me to start with the good news first. Why would he say that?

Starting with good news sets a positive tone and builds trust before you mention delays. So open the timeline with what is already finished on the packaging redesign, then move calmly to what remains.
I'm Lucas. I moved to Coimbatore two weeks ago and found a nice tea shop run by an old man named Mr. Subbu.
That is a lovely find, Lucas. A friendly shop owner can make a new city feel less strange. Do you go there often?
Almost every evening. He remembers my order now.
That is a small sign you belong there. Regular small chats like that are how new places turn into familiar ones, and it takes only a few weeks.
He asked where I'm from and I told him Kerala. He said his wife is from Kerala too.
A nice link between you. You can ask him about her, and what food or festival she misses from home. People love sharing stories like that.
Could be a good conversation. What did he say about her?
He said his wife is from Kerala, just like you. Ask Mr. Subbu what dishes she cooks, and tell him what you miss from Kerala too. It could grow into a real friendship.
I'll ask tomorrow. Remind me of his name so I greet him properly.
His name is Mr. Subbu, the old man who runs your tea shop. Greet him by name tomorrow and mention his wife from Kerala, and he will surely be pleased.
We brought home a puppy yesterday. His name is Biscuit and he cried all night.
Congratulations on Biscuit! The first nights are hard for puppies because everything is new and he misses his mother. A warm blanket near your bed and a quiet, dim room can help him settle.
Should I let him sleep on my bed?
You can, but it is easier to decide now than to change later. Many people start with a small bed beside theirs, so he feels close without learning to demand the big bed.
OK, a bed on the floor then. Where do I put it?
Put it in your bedroom, away from the door and any cold draught. Keep it in the same corner every night so Biscuit learns it is his own place to sleep.
The power went out again in our street. Third time this week.
That is frustrating, especially three times in one week. Do you know if it is a local fault, or is the whole area affected? Neighbours often know first.
Only our lane. My mother says the transformer is old. I have an exam project due tomorrow on my laptop.
Then charge the laptop fully as soon as the power returns, and save your work every few minutes. If it stays off tonight, you could draft the project on paper and type it later.
Good idea. I will write the introduction by hand now. Henry from next door has a torch I can borrow.

Borrowing Henry's torch is a good plan, and a steady light will make handwriting easier. Write the introduction first, since that part usually needs the most careful thinking. You can type it when the power is back.
It has been raining all day and my little sister Tanvi is bored. Any ideas?
A rainy day is perfect for indoor games. You could build a blanket fort, play cards, or draw together. How old is Tanvi? That helps me suggest something she will enjoy.
She is six. She likes animals and drawing.
Then try an animal drawing game. Each of you draws one part of a creature, such as the head, and then swaps papers to add a body. The strange animals you end up with are usually very funny.
Ha, she will love that. What if she wants to keep going for hours?
Then let her. Tanvi could name each creature and make a small zoo from the pages, with signs for each cage. That turns a boring rainy afternoon into a project she is proud of.
My brother and I keep fighting about who washes the dishes. His name is Asif.
That is a common fight. A fair system usually helps more than arguing each night. Do you and Asif have other chores too, or only dishes?
I also sweep the floor, and he takes out the garbage.

So right now you sweep and Asif takes out the garbage, and the dishes are the job neither of you wants. You could take turns with the dishes by the week, so one week they are yours and the next week they are his. Then nobody is stuck with them forever.
That sounds fair. Can you help me say it to him without starting another fight?
Sure. You could say, "Asif, let's take turns with the dishes, one week each, starting this Sunday." Starting with the plan, not the complaint, makes it easier for him to say yes.
I am thinking of adopting a kitten but I live in a small flat on the fourth floor.
A small flat can suit a kitten well, since cats need less space than many dogs. The main things are a safe window or balcony, a scratching post, and a quiet corner to rest.
My balcony has no grill. Is that a problem?
Yes, that matters. Kittens climb and jump, and a fourth floor fall can be dangerous. Fit a strong net or grill on the balcony and the windows before you bring her home.
Fine, I will ask the carpenter this weekend. What else should I buy first?

Start with a litter tray, food and water bowls, a scratching post and a soft bed. Since you plan to fit the balcony net this weekend, buy the supplies after that is done, so the kitten arrives to a safe home.
I want to rearrange my bedroom but it is tiny. Where do I even start?
Start by taking everything out that you do not use. A tiny room feels bigger when the floor is clear. Then think about which big item, the bed or the desk, should be placed first.
The bed is the big one. Right now it is in the middle.
Push it against the longest wall. That frees up the centre of the room and gives you a clear walking path. A bed under the window also lets in more light during the day.
The window wall has a radiator though. Is that okay?
Leave a little gap, about a hand's width, between the bed and the radiator so air can move and the bedding does not get too hot. If that does not fit, use the other long wall instead.
The new neighbours moved in upstairs. They have two small boys who run around a lot.
Kids that age have a lot of energy, so some noise is normal. Has it been bothering you, or are you just curious about the new family?
It bothers me a bit in the evening when I study. The mother is called Natalie and seems very nice.
Since Natalie seems friendly, a polite chat is the best start. Mention it kindly, and ask if the boys could play somewhere quieter during your study hours. Most parents are happy to try.
I never thought of just asking her. When is a good time?
Catch her on the stairs or at the gate when she is not in a rush, maybe on a weekend morning. Smile, welcome Natalie to the building, and then mention the evening noise gently.
My dog Max keeps digging holes in our garden.
Digging is natural for many dogs. It can mean boredom, too much energy, or even trying to cool down. How often does Max get walks and play time?
One short walk each morning. Not much else, I work long hours.
That could be the reason. Max may have too much energy and nothing to do. A longer evening walk or a chew toy to keep him busy while you are away might reduce the digging.
I could take him out after dinner. Would that really help?
It should. A walk after dinner gives Max exercise and company, and a tired dog digs less. Give it a couple of weeks and see if the holes in the garden slow down.
I just got my own flat and I have no idea how to cook anything.
Congratulations on the new flat! Cooking is easy to learn if you start small. What do you like to eat? We can pick a couple of simple dishes to begin with.
I love egg curry and plain rice. Also khichdi when I am sick.
Those are great to start with. Khichdi is the easiest because rice, lentils and a little salt cook together in one pot. Egg curry needs a bit more care with the onion and tomato base.
Okay, I will try the khichdi first this weekend. How long does it take?

With a pressure cooker, khichdi is ready in about twenty minutes, usually after three or four whistles. Wash the rice and lentils first. Once that works, you will feel ready to try the egg curry next.
The rain flooded the road outside our house. Zoya wants to go to school anyway.
If the road is flooded, it is safer to wait. Water can hide holes, and moving vehicles splash a lot. Can you check with the school whether they are open today?
They sent a message that classes are on, but late arrivals are fine.

Then there is no hurry. Wait for the water to go down, since a late arrival is allowed. If the road is still flooded, it may be wiser to keep Zoya home and tell the school. Once it is clear, an adult can walk with her along the higher side.
Good. Can she wear her usual shoes?
For the wet road, rubber boots or slippers that dry quickly are better than leather school shoes. Zoya can carry her usual shoes in a bag and change into them at school.
Our kitten Ruby has started scratching the sofa. Mum is upset.
Kittens scratch to stretch, keep their claws in shape and mark their space, so she is not being naughty. She just needs a better place to do it. Do you have a scratching post for Ruby yet?
No, we only have a small toy mouse.
Then a post is the first thing to buy. Choose a tall, sturdy one, since Ruby will want to stretch fully. Put it right next to the sofa she likes, because cats scratch where they already spend time.
What if she ignores it?
Rub a little dried catnip on the post, or dangle her toy mouse near it so she touches it. Praise her each time she uses it. Most kittens switch within a week or two.
Okay, I will tell Mum the plan. Please remind me what I should put next to the sofa.
The scratching post, set right beside the sofa Ruby has been scratching. Add the catnip or the toy mouse to make it interesting. Your mum should see Ruby choosing the post fairly soon.
There is a power cut and my phone is at 8 percent. What should I do?
Switch to low power mode, lower the screen brightness, and close apps you are not using. Save the last bit of battery for calls that really matter, such as telling family you are fine.
Done. It is also getting dark and I cannot find the candles.
Check the kitchen drawers and the cupboard where you keep pooja items, since people often store candles there. A phone torch uses battery, so use it only briefly while you search.
Found them in the pooja shelf, with matches. Is it safe to light them in the living room?
Yes, if you put each candle in a steady holder on a flat surface, away from curtains, papers and the edge of a table. Never leave them burning when you go to another room.
Thanks. I will keep two on the dining table. Anything else?
Keep a glass of water nearby and put the matches back in the pooja shelf where you found them, so they are easy to find next time. Blow the candles out before you sleep.
Our neighbour Harsh plays loud music every night until midnight.
That sounds tiring. Before anything else, has he ever been told it disturbs you? Some people simply do not realise how far the sound travels through the walls.
No, I have never said anything. I am nervous.
That is understandable. A calm, short conversation is usually the best first step. Say that you like quiet in the evenings and ask if he could lower the volume after ten.
What if he gets angry?
Then stay polite and do not argue. You can say thank you and leave. If the noise continues, the building committee can speak to him, so you do not have to handle it alone.
Right. I will talk to Harsh on Saturday morning when he is relaxed.
Saturday morning is a good choice, since people are calmer then. Keep it short, mention the ten o'clock time, and say please. A friendly tone with Harsh will likely get the best result.
Can you help me make a chore chart for my family? There are four of us.
Happy to. Tell me who is in the family, their ages, and what jobs need doing each week. Then we can share them out so the chart feels fair.
My husband Asif, me, and our kids Isla who is nine and Tanvi who is twelve. Jobs are cooking, dishes, laundry, sweeping, and watering plants.
Here is an idea. Tanvi can handle the dishes and laundry folding, Isla can water the plants and help sweep, and you and Asif share the cooking. That gives each child a job suited to their age.
Isla would rather do dishes than sweeping. Can we change that?
Of course. Swap it so Isla washes the lighter dishes with supervision and Tanvi takes over the sweeping. Children keep a chart longer when they choose some part of it.
Good. And how do we make sure they actually do it?
Pin the chart where everyone sees it and tick off each job at day's end. A small weekend treat, like a movie night, can reward the family. Tanvi and Isla will likely enjoy ticking their own boxes.
My puppy chews my slippers constantly.
That is very normal. Puppies chew when their teeth are growing, and slippers smell like you, which makes them extra interesting. How old is your puppy?
About four months. His name is Cooper.
At four months Cooper is teething, so chewing is how he soothes his gums. Give him safe chew toys, and keep the slippers on a high shelf or in a closed cupboard.
Which toys are good? He ignores most of them.
Try rubber chew toys that can be chilled in the fridge, since the cold feels good on sore gums. A knotted rope can also work. Rotate the toys so they stay interesting for him.
Good tip. I will freeze one tonight. What was his name again, in case I forget?
His name is Cooper. One small change: chill the rubber toy in the fridge rather than freezing it hard, then give it to him this evening when he goes for your slippers.
I am swapping my bed and desk in my room tomorrow. My little brother Henry wants to help.
That sounds like a good team job. Before you move anything, measure the spaces and clear the floor so you do not trip over things. Is Henry old enough to carry things?
He is ten, so I will let him carry pillows and books.
That is a sensible split. Keep the heavy bed and the desk for you and an adult. Henry can carry light things and help you check that nothing is left behind in the corners.
Dad said he will help with the bed. Should we empty the desk drawers first?
Yes, empty the drawers and remove anything on top, so the desk is lighter and nothing breaks. Put the contents in a box and ask Henry to look after it.
Great, so Henry gets the box. Anything to do after we finish?

Once the furniture is in place, sweep the floor, since moving it will have raised dust. Then let Henry put the things from his box back into the drawers himself, so he feels part of the finished room.
I forgot my umbrella and it started pouring while I am at the bus stop.
Move under the shelter if there is one, and stand away from the road edge to avoid splashes from passing vehicles. How far is your home from here?
About twenty minutes by bus. I have a laptop in my bag.
Then protect the laptop first. Put it inside a plastic bag or wrap it in a jacket, and keep the bag close to your body. Water on a laptop can damage it much faster than it can harm you.
I have a plastic bag from the grocery shop. Should I put the whole bag inside it?

You could, if the plastic bag is big enough. If not, put the laptop in the plastic bag, then place that inside your backpack and zip it closed. Keep the backpack close to you while you wait for the bus.
Done. The bus is coming. Please remind me what I should do when I reach home.
Take the laptop out of the plastic bag and check if any damp got in. Dry your backpack and your wet clothes, and leave the laptop open on a table for a while before you switch it on.
My neighbour is going away for a week and asked me to feed her cat. I have never looked after a cat before.
That is kind of you. Cats are usually easy to care for. Ask your neighbour for the feeding times, how much food to give, and where the litter tray and cat food are kept.
She wrote it all on a note. Twice a day, and the cat is called Natalie.
Funny, a cat named Natalie. Twice a day is simple. Fill the water bowl too, and clean the litter tray every day. Talk to her gently and spend a few minutes keeping her company.
Is it okay to let her go out?
Check your neighbour's note about that. If she did not mention it, keep Natalie inside, since an outdoor cat that is not used to you could wander off and get lost.
Good point. She did say indoors only, so that is settled.
Then you are all set. Feed Natalie twice a day, refresh her water, clean the litter tray, and keep the door closed so she stays inside. A week will go by quickly.
I want to hang a few photos in my hallway but I do not want to make holes in the wall.
You could use adhesive strips made for hanging pictures. They hold light frames and come off without marks. Another option is leaning frames on a narrow shelf along the wall.
The frames are quite light. What is the best height to hang them?
A good rule is to hang the centre of each frame at about eye level, roughly 145 to 150 centimetres from the floor. In a hallway, people walk past, so slightly lower can look better.
I have six frames. Should I put them in a straight line?
A single line looks neat in a hallway. You could also try two rows of three. Lay the frames on the floor first and move them around until the pattern pleases you, before you stick any strips.
Nice, I will try the two rows. And what was the first option you mentioned for hanging?
I suggested adhesive hanging strips, which hold light frames and peel off without marks. Since your six frames are light, they should work well for the two rows of three.
We found a tiny kitten near our gate this morning. She looks very thin.
Poor little thing. Offer her a shallow bowl of water and a little kitten food if you have it. Is her mother nearby? Sometimes the mother is only out looking for food.
I watched for an hour. No mother. I named her Mango because of her orange fur.
Mango is a lovely name. If the mother has not come back, the kitten needs warmth and regular food. Put her in a cardboard box with a soft cloth in a quiet spot indoors.
Can I give her milk from the fridge?
Cow's milk can upset a kitten's stomach. Warm water with a little kitten food mashed in is gentler. A pet shop can sell you kitten milk powder, which is made for tiny ones like Mango.
The pet shop is closed today. What do I do until tomorrow?
Keep Mango warm in her box and offer a little plain, boneless cooked chicken mashed with warm water. Tomorrow, buy the kitten milk powder, and since she is so thin, ask a vet to check her.
Last night our whole building lost power for six hours. The lift stopped and my grandfather lives on the sixth floor.
That must have been hard for him. Stairs are tiring at any age. Did he manage to get down, or did he stay in his flat?
He stayed in. My cousin Gauri went up with a torch and food.
That was thoughtful of Gauri. Having a torch and a little company makes a long power cut easier, and she probably made your grandfather feel less alone.
Next time I want him to be better prepared. Any ideas?
Keep a torch, spare batteries, a small water bottle and some dry snacks in one drawer. A power bank for his phone helps too, so he can call you easily if the lift stops again.
Good. Which person did I say went up to help him?
You said your cousin Gauri went up with a torch and some food. If she lives nearby, you could ask her to help set up the emergency drawer for your grandfather.
The monsoon started today and our terrace leaks in one corner.
Leaks are a nuisance, and it is good you noticed early. Put a bucket under the drip, and move anything that can get wet away from that corner. Is it a ceiling inside or the open terrace?
It is a ceiling in the top room. A damp patch is spreading.
A spreading patch means water is getting through the roof. Keep the bucket in place, wipe the drips, and ask a mason or the building's maintenance person to check the terrace soon.
Is there anything I can do myself till then?
You can move furniture and electronics away from the patch, and keep a cloth beside the bucket for splashes. Do not touch any wires or switches near the damp spot.
Ok, I'll move the cupboard. Should I tell my landlord Harsh today?
Yes, tell Harsh today and send a photo of the damp patch so he can see it clearly. The sooner a repair starts, the less damage the ceiling will get from the monsoon.
I am eleven and my mum wants me to do the laundry. I have never done it.
That is a good skill to learn, and it is easy once you know the steps. Does your family use a washing machine, or do you wash clothes by hand?
We have a washing machine. Mum said to separate whites and colours.
Your mum is right. Colours can run and stain white clothes, so wash them in separate loads. Check pockets too, for tissues, coins or pens, which can ruin a whole load.
What do I do after the washing is finished?
Take the clothes out soon, shake each piece, and hang them to dry in an airy place. Wet clothes left in the machine can start to smell. Fold them once they are fully dry.
Ok. Why did you say to check the pockets first?
Because things like tissues fall apart and stick to everything, and a pen can leave ink marks on the whole load. Checking the pockets before you wash saves you and your mum a lot of trouble.
I share a room with my sister Ruby and we fight about space.
Sharing a room is hard, especially when you want privacy. A simple fix is to divide the room clearly, so each of you has a personal zone. Do you have a shelf, or a cupboard, for each person?
One shared cupboard and two beds. Ruby's things end up on my side.
You could put a line of tape or a small bookshelf between the two halves, and give each of you half the cupboard. Once the borders are clear, it is easier to say, that is mine.
She might not agree to a shelf in the middle though.
Then ask Ruby to help plan it, so she has a say. Let her pick her side of the cupboard and where her bed goes. People accept rules more easily when they helped make them.
Fine, I will ask her tonight. What was the idea for dividing the room?
A strip of tape or a small bookshelf between the two halves, plus half the cupboard for each of you. When you talk to Ruby tonight, offer her the choice of which side she wants.
Our neighbour left a big parcel at our door by mistake and now she is away.
You are right to keep it safe. Bring it inside, if it is not too heavy, so it does not get wet or taken. Do you know any other way of reaching her, perhaps a family member nearby?
Her son Max lives two doors down. I have his number.
Then message Max, tell him a parcel came to your door by mistake, and ask if he would like to collect it. That is the easiest way, and it keeps everything friendly.
What should I write exactly?
Something like: Hi Max, a parcel meant for your mother was left at our door. I have kept it inside. Please pick it up when you are free. Short, polite and clear is best.
Perfect. He replied he will come tomorrow evening.
That is settled then. Keep the parcel in a dry place until Max comes. When he arrives, a quick hello and a thank you will be enough to end the matter on a friendly note.
My daughter wants a puppy for her birthday but I am worried I will be the one looking after it.
That is a fair worry. A puppy needs feeding, walks, training and cleaning up, and young children cannot do all of that alone. How old is your daughter?
Eight. Her name is Isla.
At eight, Isla can help with small jobs like filling the water bowl and brushing, but an adult must do most of the care. Talk with her honestly about what a puppy needs each day.
Should I tell her this before the birthday?
Yes, it is better to talk before the puppy arrives. Ask Isla what she thinks she can do daily. If she lists real jobs, she is more likely to keep to them once the puppy comes.
Good. If she says feeding and walking, is that realistic for an eight-year-old?
Feeding is realistic. Walking is only realistic with an adult beside her, since a puppy can pull hard. So Isla could take the feeding job, and the two of you could share the walks.
The kitchen tap at home drips all night and the sound keeps me awake.
That drip is annoying, and it also wastes water. A worn washer inside the tap is the usual cause. Do you know how to turn off the water supply to the tap?
No. My flatmate Zoya says there is a valve under the sink.
Zoya is probably right. Most sinks have a small valve under them. Turn it clockwise to stop the water, then ask a plumber to replace the washer. It is a quick, cheap job for them.
Can I fix it myself by watching a video online?
You can try if you have the right tools and feel confident, but a plumber will do it quickly and safely. For now, just turn the valve off at night to stop the drip and the noise.
Good idea. Where did you say the valve is?
Under the kitchen sink, as Zoya told you. Look for a small tap or lever on the pipe, and turn it clockwise at night. In the morning, turn it back so you can use the tap.
My parrot keeps repeating a phrase my father says when he is angry. It is awkward when guests come.
Parrots copy sounds they hear often, so that is a common problem. The good news is they can learn new phrases too. What does your parrot like, a certain treat or a person?
He loves peanuts and he loves my sister Gauri. His name is Kiwi.
Then Gauri can help. Whenever Kiwi is about to repeat the angry phrase, she could say a friendly one, like hello Kiwi, and give him a peanut. He will connect the new phrase with a reward.
How long will it take?
It varies. Some parrots pick up a new phrase in days, others take weeks. Repeat the same phrase every day, in the same cheerful tone, and be patient with Kiwi.
Okay. Can you remind me who should say the friendly phrase?
Your sister Gauri. She is Kiwi's favourite person, so he is more likely to listen to her. Have her say the new phrase each day and give him a peanut when he copies it.
I have a long train journey today and the forecast says heavy rain.
Heavy rain can delay trains, so give yourself extra time. Pack a light raincoat, a bottle of water and a snack. Do you know if your train stops anywhere for long?
It is a six-hour trip. I will be reading and listening to music.
Then bring a charger or power bank for your phone, and keep your bag covered with a plastic sheet. Download your music before you leave in case the network is poor.
I will. How should I keep my books dry?
Put them in a zip bag or wrap them in a plastic sheet inside your backpack. Even a thin carry bag works. Dry books are worth the small effort when the weather is this wet.
Smart. What should I carry besides books?
Apart from the books, carry the power bank, the raincoat, the water bottle and a snack. Also keep your ticket where you can reach it easily, without opening the bag in the rain.
Quick question, how often should a two-month-old puppy eat?
At that age most puppies eat three or four small meals a day, because their stomachs are tiny. Check the food packet for the amount, and ask your vet if you are unsure about the right portion.
Ours is a Labrador called Bruno. He seems hungry all the time.
Labradors are known for loving food, so Bruno may simply be keen. Stick to the meal times and amounts rather than adding extra snacks, since a Labrador puppy can gain weight quickly.
Is it okay to give him a bit of roti from my plate?
A small piece of plain roti is not harmful, but it should not become a habit. Table scraps can upset his stomach and teach Bruno to beg at every meal.
Fair enough. He sits beside me every dinner and stares.
That stare is hard to resist! Give Bruno something to do instead, like a chew toy on his own mat, while the family eats. After a few days he will learn dinner time is not his snack time.
Good plan. What was the first thing I asked about?
You asked how often a two-month-old puppy should eat, and I said three or four small meals a day. For Bruno, keeping those fixed times will also help with his begging at dinner.
The lights flickered and then everything went dark. Is it okay to keep the fridge closed?
Yes, keep the fridge door shut. A closed fridge keeps food cold for several hours, but each time you open it the cold escapes. Do you know how long the cut will last?
No idea. I have milk and some leftover dal inside.
Milk and cooked food spoil fastest. If the power is out for many hours, use the milk and dal first once it returns, and throw them away if they smell odd or feel warm.
What about the freezer? There is ice cream in it.
A full freezer stays cold longer than a half-empty one. Keep that door shut too, and the ice cream should stay firm for a good while. If it melts completely, do not refreeze it.
The power is back after three hours! Is the dal safe?
Probably, if the fridge door stayed closed and the dal still feels cold and smells normal. If you doubt it, throw it away. The milk is the same, so check that too.
Great, the dal is cold. Will you remind me what to do with the ice cream if it melted?
Do not refreeze it. Once ice cream has melted completely, it is better to throw it away. Since yours stayed in the closed freezer for three hours, it is likely still fine.
I want to invite my neighbours for chai on Sunday. Is that a good idea?
It is a lovely idea. A small chai evening is an easy way to know your neighbours better. How many families live nearby, and do you have space at home for them?
Three families on our floor. I have a small living room.
Then keep it simple. Invite them for an hour in the late afternoon, serve chai and a few biscuits, and perhaps move a couple of chairs from the bedroom so everyone can sit.
One family is Gauri's, she has a baby. Is that a problem?
Not at all, but think about the baby. Keep the room quiet, put small things out of reach, and give Gauri a comfortable seat where she can keep the baby close.
Good point. Should I send a message or knock on their doors?
Knocking on the door is warmer, and it lets you say hello in person. If someone is out, leave a short note with the day and time of the invitation.
I will knock this evening. What should I remember about Gauri?
Remember that Gauri has a baby, so offer her a comfortable seat and keep the room calm and tidy. Keep hot cups of chai well out of the baby's reach.
My room is a mess and I have an hour. How do I clean it fast?
Start with the floor. Pick up clothes, plates and wrappers and sort them into three piles: laundry, rubbish and things that belong elsewhere. A clear floor already changes how the room looks.
I got the floor done. What about my desk?
Gather loose papers into one pile, put pens in a cup, and wipe the surface with a damp cloth. Take away anything that does not belong on a desk, like cups and old notes.
Okay. My bed is next and my sister Zoya says I never make it.
Pull the sheet flat, straighten the pillow, and spread the blanket over the top. It takes a minute and makes the whole room look neat. Zoya may be impressed.
Ha. I finished in forty minutes. I have time left, what next?
With twenty minutes left, sweep or vacuum the floor, then open the window for fresh air. If any time remains, fold the clothes from your laundry pile and put them away.
Good. Who said I never make my bed?
Your sister Zoya said it. So when she sees your made bed and clean floor, she may change her mind. Sweep the floor now and show it off.
I want my room to feel calmer. Any ideas that are cheap?
Start with light and clutter. Open the curtains for daylight, clear the surfaces, and use soft colours where you can, like a plain bedsheet. Which part bothers you most right now?
The messy shelf by my bed. Books everywhere.
Then sort the books by size or by colour and stand them upright, with a small gap at the end so the shelf does not look crowded. Put the ones you read often within easy reach.
What if I still have too many books?
Move the ones you are not reading to a box under the bed or to a lower shelf, and keep only a few on the bedside shelf. Fewer things in view makes a room feel calmer.
My brother Henry says I should paint the walls blue. Is that too much?
Painting is a big step. Blue is a popular choice for calm rooms, but try a small test patch first, and look at it at different times of day before you decide on the whole wall.
Okay, I will test a patch. What did I say bothers me most?
The messy shelf by your bed, with books everywhere. So sort the books first, and then decide with Henry whether the blue paint is still needed.
Our goldfish seems quiet and stays at the bottom of the bowl.
That can mean a few things, such as cold water, a dirty bowl or too little oxygen. When did you last change the water?
About three weeks ago. Her name is Bubbles.
Three weeks is long for a small bowl. Replace a third of the water with fresh water that has stood overnight, so it is not too cold or too chlorinated, and see if Bubbles livens up.
I will do that. Should I feed her more to cheer her up?
No, extra food can make the water dirtier and the problem worse. A small pinch once or twice a day is enough. Watch Bubbles for a day and see if she moves around more.
She is swimming again after the water change.
I am glad Bubbles is better. A clean bowl makes a big difference, so change part of the water every week from now on, and keep the bowl out of direct sun.
Thanks. Can you remind me how much water I should change each time?
About a third of the water in Bubbles' bowl, using water that has stood overnight. Doing that every week should keep her healthy and active, without upsetting her too much.
My cricket match got cancelled because of rain. I am so annoyed.
That is disappointing, especially if you were looking forward to it. Rain stops play in cricket for good reasons, since a wet pitch is unsafe. Was it an important match?
It was our school team's first match of the season.
Then I understand the frustration. The match will probably be rescheduled, so ask your coach for the new date. Meanwhile, you could practise indoors or watch the team's old videos.
Maybe I will do some fitness exercises in my room until they fix a new date.

That is a good use of the free time. Simple exercises like skipping or stretching need very little space, and they will keep you ready for the school team's first match of the season, whenever it is played.
Can you suggest a good place for a plant in my flat? I only get afternoon sun on the east side.
Afternoon sun usually comes from the west, so the sunny side of your flat may face west. Wherever it comes in, a spot near that window is best for most plants. What kind of plant do you have?
A money plant and a small tulsi.
Both do well in bright light without too much direct heat. Keep the tulsi where it gets some direct sun for a few hours, and the money plant a little further from the glass.
The tulsi is really for my grandmother. Her name is Kamala and she loves watering it.
Then Kamala will enjoy caring for it. Place the tulsi somewhere easy for her to reach, so she can water it daily without bending too far or carrying a heavy pot.
My dog gets scared during thunderstorms. What can I do?
Many dogs are frightened by thunder. Stay calm, since dogs notice your mood. Give him a quiet, cosy spot, and close the curtains to dim the flashes. What does your dog do when it thunders?
He shakes and hides under the bed. His name is Rocky.
Let Rocky stay under the bed if that makes him feel safe. Sit near him, speak softly, and play some gentle music or the TV to cover the noise.
Should I give him treats while he is scared?
A treat is fine if he will take it. It can help him link storms with something nice. Do not force him out from under the bed, though, because that may scare Rocky more.
The old man next door, Mr Rao, has not been seen for two days.
That is worth checking. Has anyone in the building spoken to him, or does he have family close by? A friendly knock at the door is a good first step.
I knocked and no one answered. His lights are on.
Try calling his phone if you have the number, or ask other neighbours whether he mentioned travelling. If you still cannot reach him, tell the building security or his family.
I got his daughter's number from the watchman. Should I call her?
Yes, call her and say you are worried because you have not seen Mr Rao for two days and he did not answer the door. She will know what to do next.
My kitten is afraid of the vacuum cleaner. Her name is Pepper.
Many kittens fear loud machines, since the noise and movement are strange. Pepper is not being silly. Where does she go when you start the vacuum?
She hides in the bathroom.
That is a safe choice for her. Try vacuuming when Pepper is in another room with the door shut, and let her come out only when the machine is off and quiet again.
Could I help her get used to it?
Yes, slowly. Place the switched-off vacuum on the floor with a treat nearby, and let her sniff it. Over several days, turn it on briefly at a distance and reward Pepper for staying calm.
I am cooking dinner for the first time for my family tonight. Nervous!
It is normal to feel nervous, but you can do this. What are you planning to make, and who are you cooking for?
Pasta for my parents and my brother Max. Is it hard to cook?
Pasta is one of the easiest dishes. Boil water with a pinch of salt, add the pasta, cook it until soft but a little firm, then drain and mix it with sauce.
Max does not like onions. Can I leave them out?
Of course. You could use tomatoes, garlic and a little cheese for the sauce. Since Max does not like onions, he will probably enjoy a simple tomato pasta more.
Let me tell you about my weekend. On Saturday we cleaned the whole house for my aunt's visit.
That sounds like a busy day. Cleaning a whole house takes real effort. Did everyone in the family help, or did most of the work fall on you?
Everyone helped. My aunt is called Gauri and she is bringing her twin sons on Sunday.
Twin boys will be lively! It is good you cleaned beforehand. Put breakable things on higher shelves, and clear a corner where the twins can play without knocking over anything.
Good point. On Sunday we made a lot of food and played carrom.
Carrom is a great way to spend time with family. The twins will probably enjoy it too, since the game is simple to learn and fun for children.
They did enjoy it! Who was it that visited us again?
Your aunt Gauri visited, along with her twin sons. It sounds like your cleaning, the food and the carrom made the visit a happy one for everyone.
Yes, I think so. I miss them already.
That is a nice feeling, and it means the visit went well. You could ask Gauri to send photos of the twins, or plan the next visit together.
It is pouring and my father is stuck at the railway station.
That must be worrying. Trains often slow down in heavy rain. Has he told you how long he expects to wait?
He says maybe two hours. He did not bring an umbrella.
Then he should wait inside the station building, away from the platform edge. Ask him to keep his phone charged, and perhaps buy tea or a snack from the station stall.
Should I go pick him up in the car?
If the roads near you are flooded or flowing fast, wait. If they are clear and the station is close, it can help, but check first with him. Do not drive through deep water.
The roads near us are fine but the station road is flooded, he says.
Then stay home. Driving into flood water is risky for you and the car. Tell your father to wait at the station until the road clears, and call him to check on him often.
Do kittens need to be vaccinated before going outside?
Yes, kittens normally need a series of vaccines before they go outdoors, since they can catch illnesses from other animals. A vet will tell you which vaccines she needs and when to give them.
She is about nine weeks old and her name is Daisy. We got her last week.
At nine weeks Daisy is probably due for her first shots soon. Book a visit to a vet this week, and bring any papers the previous owner gave you.
Until then, can she play in our garden?
Better to keep Daisy indoors until the vet says it is safe. Other animals may have left germs in the garden. Give her toys and a climbing post inside for now.
We bought an inverter after so many power cuts. How long will it last?
It depends on the size of the battery and what you connect. Lights and fans use little power, while a heater or a geyser can drain it fast. What do you plan to run on it?
Mostly two fans, lights and the router.
That is a light load, so it should last several hours. Check the inverter's manual or ask the shop for the exact time, since it varies with the battery and the model.
Should I plug the fridge into it as well?
Ask the dealer first. A fridge uses more power when the motor starts, and some small inverters cannot handle it. Your fans, lights and router are a safer base load.
Okay. And what were the three things I wanted to run?
You said two fans, the lights and the router. Those are light loads, so your new inverter should be able to run all three for a good number of hours during a cut.
I need a place to study in my bedroom. There is no space for a desk.
You could use a foldable wall desk or a narrow table by the window. Natural light helps studying. How big is the free wall?
About one metre. Ruby, my sister, sleeps in the same room.
A one metre wall fits a small folding desk. Since Ruby shares the room, a desk lamp with a soft light lets you study in the evening without waking her.
That could work. Will she mind the lamp?
A desk lamp points at your table, so it is less bright than the room light. Tell Ruby the plan first, and agree on a time when the lamp goes off so she can sleep.
A boy from our building broke our window with a cricket ball yesterday.
That is annoying, but accidents happen. Is anyone hurt, and did the boy say anything about it?
Nobody is hurt. He ran off, but I know it is Harsh, the boy from the third floor.
Then speak to his parents calmly. Say that the ball broke your window, and ask if they could help share the cost of repairing it. Most parents will understand.
What if they say it was not him?
Stay calm and describe what you saw. Maybe other children who were playing can say what happened. A polite chat with Harsh himself, with his parents present, may also settle it.
I never know what to do with the old newspapers piling up at home.
There are several useful things you can do. You can sell them to the kabadiwala, use them to wrap fragile items or line cupboards, or recycle them. How many do you have?
About two months' worth. They fill a corner of my room.
Two months' worth is a good bundle. Tie them with string and give them to the kabadiwala next time he comes, which also frees the corner in your room.
Can I keep a few for painting? My brother Asif is doing art.
Of course. Old newspaper protects the floor when Asif paints, and children also use it for collage. Keep a small stack for him and hand the rest to the kabadiwala.
We named our puppy Noodle, and my mum thinks it is silly.
Noodle is a cute name! A name only needs to be easy to say and to hear. Does Noodle respond when you call?
A little. She looks up sometimes.
That is a good start. Say her name in a cheerful voice and give a small treat each time she looks at you. Soon Noodle will connect her name with something good.
What if she runs off when I call?

Do not chase her, since that turns it into a game. Crouch down, call her name happily and reward her when she comes. Never call Noodle to scold her. Practise indoors first, then in a safe, closed area.
Okay. What did my mum think of the name?
You said your mum thinks Noodle is silly. But if Noodle looks up when you call, the name is already working, and your mum may come around once she sees that.
My phone charger keeps stopping when I shake the cable. Is the wire broken?
It sounds like the wire inside the cable is damaged near the plug, which is common. A frayed charger can be unsafe, so stop using it if you see bare wires or feel heat.
I see no bare wires but the cable is warm.
A warm cable is a warning sign, so I would stop using it and buy a new one from a trusted shop. Cheap chargers can overheat. Keep the old one away from the bed.
Fine. Can I keep using the plug part?
Plugs often work fine, but check that the pins are straight and the case is not cracked. Pair it with the new cable, and keep both away from beds, curtains and water.
The rainy season always makes our clothes smell damp. Why does that happen?
Damp clothes take longer to dry in humid air, and the moisture lets germs grow, which causes the smell. Do you dry your clothes indoors or outside?
Indoors, on a stand in the balcony.
A balcony helps, but in humid weather they can still stay damp. Place the stand where air moves, space the clothes apart, and run a fan near them to speed up drying.
I also fold them when they are slightly damp. Is that a problem?
Yes, folding clothes that are still damp traps moisture and the smell comes back. Make sure everything is fully dry first. A last press with an iron can also help with the damp smell.
Okay. Where did I say I dry my clothes?
You said you dry them on a stand in the balcony. Moving the stand to a more airy spot there and adding a fan should help the clothes dry faster in the rainy season.
I want to take my dog Luna to the park, but she pulls on the leash.
Pulling is very common. Dogs get excited outside. A simple rule helps: stop walking whenever the leash goes tight, and move again only when it is loose. How old is Luna?
She is one year old. I have a strong harness.
A harness is a good choice. At one year, Luna has lots of energy, so give her a short run or play before the walk, which can make it easier for her to focus.
Should I use treats during the walk?
Yes, small treats work well. Reward Luna when she walks by your side with a loose leash. Keep the treats in your pocket, so she stays close to you.
My friend says kittens should not drink milk. Is she right?
She is mostly right. Many kittens cannot digest cow's milk well, and it can upset their stomach. Water and proper kitten food are better. Do you have a kitten now?
Yes, from my neighbour. Her name is Chai, she is about ten weeks old.
Ten weeks old means Chai can eat soft kitten food and drink water, and she does not need milk. Keep a bowl of fresh water beside her food and change it every day.
She keeps ignoring the water bowl though.
Try placing the bowl away from her food, since cats often prefer water in a separate spot. A wide, shallow bowl can also help, because some kittens do not like their whiskers touching the sides.
I will try that. Which kitten did I say I had?
You said Chai, the ten-week-old kitten from your neighbour. Place her water bowl in a separate spot from her food, and see if that makes her drink.
I am converting the spare room into a study for my daughter Isla.
That is a nice project. A study needs good light, a steady desk and a quiet spot. How old is Isla, and what does she like to do there?
She is thirteen. She reads a lot and does her homework on a laptop.
Then place the desk near a window for daylight, with the chair facing the wall rather than the door, so she is not distracted. Add a bookshelf within arm's reach for her reading.
She wants a beanbag as well. Is there space for both?
If the room is large enough, put the beanbag in a corner away from the desk, so the study area and the reading corner feel separate. If space is tight, choose a smaller beanbag.
The room is quite small. What should I prioritise?
The desk and chair come first, since Isla will use them for homework every day. Add the beanbag only if you can still walk through the room comfortably.
Makes sense. I will measure the room tonight.
Good plan. Measure the walls and note where the window and the door are. Then you can see whether Isla's desk, chair, shelf and beanbag will all fit before you buy anything.
Our power was cut for the whole day because of maintenance. How do I keep my kids busy?
Plan some screen-free fun. Board games, drawing, storytelling or a treasure hunt in the house all work well. How old are your kids?
Natalie is nine and Harsh is five.
Then try a treasure hunt. Hide a few small prizes around the house, and write simple clues for Natalie to read aloud. Harsh can follow and help find them, which keeps both involved.
What about after lunch? They get sleepy.
After lunch, a quiet story time works nicely. Natalie could read to Harsh, or you could tell a story by torchlight in a darkened room. They may even take a nap.
Good. Which of the kids reads aloud?
Natalie, since she is nine and can read the clues and stories. Harsh is five, so he can listen, help hunt for prizes and hold the torch during story time.
We are planning a Diwali get-together for the whole building. I am the one organising.
That sounds lovely and also a lot of work. How many families are expected, and where will it be held?
About fifteen families, in the common area downstairs. I need a plan.
Start with a simple list: the date, the time, who brings what, and who helps set up. Fifteen families can share the load, so ask each one to bring a dish or a decoration.
Good idea. Asif from the second floor offered to handle the lights.
Perfect, then you already have one helper. Make sure Asif uses proper outdoor extension cords and keeps the wires out of walkways, so nobody trips over them.
I will tell him. What about the children? There will be many.
Plan an activity for them, like making diyas or rangoli with chalk, so they stay busy and safe. Ask a couple of parents to supervise the kids while everyone else enjoys the food.
Great. Who did I say was doing the lights?
You said Asif from the second floor offered to handle the lights. Check with him about the extension cords and ask him to set the wires up away from the rangoli and the children's play area.
I spilled tea on the carpet. Help!
Act fast. Blot the stain with a clean cloth, pressing gently without rubbing, which pushes tea deeper. Is it a wool carpet or a synthetic one?
I think it is synthetic. It is cream colour.
For synthetic carpet, mix a little mild dish soap with cool water and dab it onto the stain with a cloth. Work from the outside in, and keep blotting until the tea lifts.
It is better but there is still a faint mark.
Dab again with the soapy water, then rinse by blotting with a cloth dipped in plain water. Leave it to dry fully, as stains often look lighter once the carpet is dry.
My hamster escaped from his cage and I cannot find him.
Do not panic. Hamsters hide in small, dark spaces. Close the doors to the room so he cannot go further, and check behind furniture and in boxes. Does he have a name?
His name is Peanut. I last saw him near the bookshelf.
Look behind and under the bookshelf first, using a torch. Place a few sunflower seeds near it, and keep quiet. Peanut may come out on his own when the house is calm.
What if he does not come out by night?
Hamsters are active at night, so Peanut will likely start moving then. Put his cage on the floor with the door open and a treat inside, and he may walk right back in.
That is smart. I will leave the cage by the bookshelf.
Good idea. Since you last saw Peanut near the bookshelf, the cage there with seeds inside is the best trap. Keep the room quiet and check on him in the morning.
I am training my puppy to sit. He does not get it.
Training takes patience. Hold a small treat above his nose and slowly move it back over his head. As his head goes up, his bottom goes down. What is his name and age?
Teddy, three months.
At three months Teddy can learn, but his attention is short, so practise for only a few minutes at a time. Say sit as his bottom touches the floor, and give a treat straight away.
He keeps jumping up for the treat instead.
Hold the treat closer to his nose and move it slowly. If he jumps, pull your hand back and wait until all four of his paws are on the ground, then try again.
Okay it worked once! Should I do it again and again?
Yes, but keep each try short and happy. Repeat it a few times, praise Teddy, and then stop while he is still keen. Short sessions, several times a day, work best.
Great. What was the puppy's age again?
Teddy is three months old. At that age he learns quickly, but gets tired fast, so keep practising sit in short sessions of a few minutes, a few times each day.
Our flat gets very hot in the afternoon. How can I keep it cooler without an air conditioner?
Keep the curtains closed on the sunny side during the day, and open the windows in the evening when it is cooler. Which direction do your windows face?
West. The afternoon sun comes straight in.
Then thick or light-coloured curtains on the west windows will help a lot. You can also hang a wet cloth over the window for cooling, and keep a fan pointed at it.
Does painting the walls white help?
Light colours reflect more heat than dark colours, so white walls can make a room feel cooler and brighter. It will not solve the problem alone, but it will help along with the curtains.
Fine, curtains first. Which side did I say gets the sun?
You said the west side, where the afternoon sun comes in. Put thick, light-coloured curtains on the west windows first, and keep them closed through the afternoon.
My school bag got completely soaked today and my books are wet.
Oh no. First take everything out and spread the books open so air can reach the pages. Which ones are worst affected?
My maths notebook and the science textbook.
Stand them upright with the pages fanned out, in a room with moving air, such as under a fan. Put a sheet of paper between wet pages if they stick together.
Can I use a hair dryer on the pages?
A hair dryer on low heat, held at a distance, can help, but too much heat makes the paper curl. Letting your maths notebook and science textbook dry slowly in the air is safer.
Okay. I will do that. Anything for the bag itself?
Empty it, wipe the inside with a dry cloth, and leave it open in an airy place to dry. Once your science textbook and maths notebook are dry, put them back in a plastic cover inside the bag.
My kitten bites my hand when we play. Is it normal?
Yes, kittens use their mouths when they play, since they learn by biting and pouncing. It can hurt, though. What is your kitten's name?
Simba. He is three months old.
At three months Simba is still learning bite control. When he bites, stop the game and walk away for a moment. He will learn that biting ends the fun.
Should I use my hand to play at all?
Avoid using your hand as a toy. Use a feather wand or a soft toy instead, so Simba learns to pounce on toys, not on fingers.
I am moving into a hostel room next week. It is small and shared. What should I bring?
Bring only what you really need: bedding, clothes, a few toiletries, a lamp and a small storage box. Small rooms fill up fast, so pack light.
I also want a plant. Is that okay?
A small plant is a nice touch, if the hostel allows it. Pick a hardy one that needs little water, like a snake plant, and put it on a shelf or windowsill where it gets light.
My roommate will be Ruby. Should I talk to her first?
Yes, message Ruby before you arrive. You can share what each of you is bringing, so you do not both pack a kettle or a lamp. It is also a good way to say hello.
I keep forgetting to water the plants. They look sad.
Plants need a regular routine. Link watering to something you already do every day, like brushing your teeth, so it becomes a habit. Which plants do you have?
A few in pots on the balcony, and a tulsi near the door.
Balcony pots can dry out quickly in the sun. Check the soil with a finger each morning, and water when the top feels dry. The tulsi near the door likes regular water too.
Should I water the tulsi at night?
Morning is better, since the plant can use the water during the day and the soil does not stay damp overnight. Evening works as well in hot weather, but avoid wetting the leaves.
Okay. And where did I say the tulsi was kept?
You said the tulsi is near the door, away from the pots on the balcony. Water it in the morning, along with the balcony plants, so it stays healthy.
Can I tell you a story about my day? It involves my puppy.
Go ahead, I would like to hear it. Tell me what happened and how your puppy took part in it.
So this morning I let Pickle out into the yard and he found a muddy puddle. He jumped right in.
Oh dear, Pickle must have had great fun. Puppies love mud. Did he come out looking like a different colour?
He was brown all over, he used to be white. Then he ran into the kitchen and shook himself near my mother.
That is a classic puppy move. Your mother must have been surprised. How did she react to Pickle shaking mud around the kitchen?
She laughed, then made me give him a bath. Pickle hated it.
A bath after a muddy morning is fair, even if he did not enjoy it. Next time, wipe his paws with a towel at the door, so the mud stays outside.
Good tip. What colour was Pickle before the puddle?
He was white before the puddle, and brown all over afterwards. The bath should have made him white again, so Pickle can stay clean if you wipe his paws at the door next time.
We planned a picnic for Sunday but the forecast says rain.
That is a pity. You could still have the picnic, but indoors, or move it to a day with better weather. Who is coming, and where did you plan to go?
My cousins, Gauri and Henry, and we were going to the lake.
Then check the forecast again on Saturday night. If the rain looks heavy, it is safer to postpone the lake visit, because wet grass and wind near water are no fun.
What if we make it an indoor picnic at home?
That could be great. Spread a sheet on the living room floor, bring the food, and play cards or board games. Gauri and Henry will probably enjoy the change.
My neighbour keeps parking his car in front of my gate. This morning I could not get out.
That is really inconvenient. Have you spoken to him about it before, or would this be the first time?
First time. His name is Asif and he is usually friendly.
Since Asif is usually friendly, a polite word is likely enough. Tell him that the car blocks your gate and ask if he could park a little further along.
Should I leave a note on his car instead?
A short, friendly note is fine if he is not at home. Keep the tone polite, like: Hi Asif, your car blocks my gate. Could you please park a bit to the left? Thanks.
I think I will talk to him in person.
That is the better choice. A conversation with Asif will feel friendlier than a note, and he can answer right away. Choose a calm moment, like when he comes back from work.
How do I get my son to clean his room without nagging?
Children respond better to clear, simple expectations than to repeated reminders. How old is your son, and what does he usually say when you ask?
He is ten, Ruby is his sister. He says he will do it later and then never does.
Pick a fixed time, like Saturday morning after breakfast, and make it a routine. A written checklist, such as books, clothes and bed, helps him know exactly what to finish.
Should I reward him?
A small reward can help, like choosing the dinner menu or an extra half hour of play. Praise matters most. Tell him specifically what he did well, like making his bed.
And what about his sister Ruby, should she have the same checklist?
Yes, give Ruby her own checklist suited to her age, so both children have the same system. That keeps it fair, and neither will feel they are doing more than the other.
My cat hisses at our new puppy. Will they ever get along?
They often do, but it takes time. Hissing is normal at the start, since the cat is protecting her space. How long has the puppy been with you?
Three days. The cat is called Mishti and the puppy is Bruno.
Three days is very early. Keep Mishti and Bruno in separate rooms for now, and let them smell each other's blankets. Give Mishti a high shelf where she can feel safe.
When can I let them meet?
When Mishti is calm and eating near the door that separates them. Then let them see each other with Bruno on a leash, and reward both for staying calm. Go slowly.
What happens if Bruno chases her?
Stop the meeting at once and separate them. Chasing frightens Mishti and teaches Bruno a bad habit. Try again later with Bruno on a leash and a treat to distract him.
I will try that. Which animal is the cat again?
The cat is Mishti. She is the one who hissed at Bruno, the new puppy. Keep her high shelf free, so she always has a safe place from him.
I want to buy my first kitten toy. What is safe?
Choose toys that are too big to swallow and have no small parts that can come off. Feather wands, soft balls and crinkle toys are popular. How old is your kitten?
She is eight weeks old. Her name is Pearl.
At eight weeks Pearl needs light, soft toys. A small ball she can bat around is a good choice. Avoid string and ribbon, because kittens can swallow them.
What about a laser pointer?
A laser can frustrate cats, since they can never catch it. If you use one, end the game by letting Pearl pounce on a real toy, so she gets the satisfaction of catching something.
I am hosting a dinner for six people tonight and my kitchen is small.
Small kitchens can manage a dinner with a bit of planning. What are you cooking, and how much can you prepare ahead?
Rajma, rice, a salad and gulab jamun. I made the jamun yesterday.
That is a smart start. Rajma tastes better when made ahead, so cook it this afternoon and just reheat it. Chop the salad vegetables early and keep them in the fridge.
Where do I seat everyone? We have a small table.
Six people at a small table is a squeeze. Push the table against a wall, add a stool or two, or put the food on a counter and let guests eat from plates on their laps.
Good idea. What did I make yesterday?
You made the gulab jamun yesterday. So tonight you only need to warm it a little before serving. Focus on the rajma and the salad now, and you will have plenty of time left.
There was a storm last night and our power is still off. My phone is almost dead.
Storm damage can take hours to fix. Do you have a power bank, or does someone nearby have a generator?
No power bank. My neighbour Zoya might have an inverter.
Ask Zoya if you can charge your phone at her place, even for a short time. Most people are happy to help during an outage, and she may need to charge hers too.
Okay, I will walk over now. Should I take anything for her?
A small thank-you is a kind touch, like biscuits or fruit. Take your charger and cable too, so you do not need to borrow hers.
Done, charging at Zoya's now. She says the power might be back by noon.
Good, then you can stay a little longer and chat. Thank Zoya when you leave. If the power returns by noon, remember to charge your own devices fully at home as well.
I'd like to rearrange my bedroom so it feels like a new room.
A new layout is a cheap way to refresh a room. Start by deciding what you want to change. Is it the bed, the desk, or the whole room?
The whole room. I'm bored of how it looks.
Then sketch the room on paper first, with the door, window and big furniture marked. Try two or three layouts on paper before you move anything heavy.
Good. The door opens inward, so what do I leave free?
Leave a clear arc where the door swings, and keep a path from the door to the bed and the window. Do not place a tall cupboard where the opening door will hit it.
Okay. What if I want the bed under the window?
That works if the window does not open towards the bed. If it does open that way, you may bump your head. Check the arc of the window the same way you checked the door.
Thanks. Which way did I say the door opens?
You said your bedroom door opens inward, so keep a clear arc where it swings. When you sketch the new layout on paper, draw that arc first and place your furniture around it.
I love the smell of rain. Why does the ground smell like that?

That fresh smell comes from a substance made by tiny soil bacteria and some plants. Raindrops hitting dry ground release it into the air, and our noses are very good at detecting it. Do you enjoy rainy days?
Yes, especially at home with chai. My brother Harsh hates it though.
Chai and rain go well together. Some people feel gloomy in wet weather because they miss the sun and their usual outdoor plans. Why does Harsh dislike it?
He cannot play cricket outside.
That is a good reason. If Harsh misses cricket, you could suggest an indoor game, like table cricket with a ball made from paper, or a card game, to keep him busy until the rain stops.
My dad has started cooking on Sundays and my mum is thrilled.
That is wonderful, and a nice way to share the work at home. Does he cook well, or is it a learning process?
He is learning. Last week he burned the rice, ha.
Burned rice is common when you start. A pot with a thick bottom and a lower flame helps. He could also set a timer, so he does not forget it while doing other things.
I will tell him. Anything else he should know?
Tell him to taste as he cooks, and to keep the pot lid slightly open while the rice boils. He should also keep a dish towel nearby, to catch any spills right away.
Good. My sister Isla wants to help him next Sunday.
That will be fun for both of them. Isla can wash the rice and set the timer, which is a handy job, since the timer is exactly what will stop another burned pot of rice.
What is a good way to organise a messy kitchen drawer full of random stuff?
Take everything out first. Sort the items into groups, like cutlery, tools and things that do not belong. Then wipe the empty drawer. What kind of drawer is it?
The one near the stove. It has spoons, lighters, rubber bands and old coupons.
Keep the spoons and lighter in that drawer, since you use them by the stove. Throw away the old coupons and put the rubber bands in a small box or jar.
Where should the lighter go? It feels unsafe near the stove.

Good instinct. Keep the lighter away from the stove's heat, for example on a high shelf or in a closed drawer nearby that children cannot reach. Keep it apart from the loose rubber bands, so it is easy to find.
My puppy has not pooped today and I am a bit worried.
One quiet day is not unusual, but I cannot judge your puppy's health. Has he eaten and drunk normally, and is he playing as usual? If he seems unwell, speak to a vet.
He ate fine and is playful. His name is Oscar, and he is twelve weeks old.
That sounds reassuring. Puppies like Oscar usually go several times a day, so watch the next few hours. Take him outside after meals and after he wakes, since that is when most puppies go.
What if he still does not go by tomorrow?
Then call the vet and ask. They can tell you what to look for. Do not give him any medicine on your own, and keep a note of what and when Oscar eats.
Our building has a generator, but it only runs for two hours at night. How do I plan around that?
Use those two hours wisely. Charge phones and power banks first, then run any appliances you really need. Do you have any special needs, like someone who studies at night?
My daughter Zoya studies at night. She has exams next week.
Then let Zoya use a lamp and a charged laptop during the generator hours, and plan her hardest subjects for then. During the cut, she can revise from notes or a printed sheet with a torch.
Will a small rechargeable lamp be enough?
A good rechargeable lamp can last for several hours and is gentler than a candle. Charge it fully when the generator runs, so Zoya has light for her exam revision after it goes off.
I am painting my bedroom this weekend. Where should I start?
Start by moving furniture to the middle of the room and covering it with old sheets. Tape the edges of the skirting and the window frames. What colour are you painting it?
A soft yellow. The walls are white now.
Soft yellow on white is easy, since it will need only two coats. Paint the ceiling first if you are doing it, then the walls from top to bottom, in smooth strokes.
Should I keep the windows open while painting?
Yes, open the windows for fresh air and let the paint dry well. Do not sleep in the room until the smell goes away, and keep your soft yellow tins closed when you are not using them.
My neighbour's dog barks at me every time I walk past their gate.
That can be unnerving. Dogs often bark to protect their space, not because they dislike you. Does the dog ever come close, or stay behind the gate?
It stays behind the gate. Her name is Coco.
Then Coco is just doing her guard job. Walk calmly past without staring at her, and do not run. Over time, she may learn that you are not a threat.
Could I offer her a treat?
Only if her owner agrees. Some dogs have food allergies, and the owner may not want strangers feeding Coco. Ask them first, or just say hello to the owner instead.
My kitten has started sleeping on my head at night. Is that okay?
It is a sign she trusts you and enjoys your warmth. It can disturb your sleep, though. How old is she, and what is her name?
Her name is Lily, she is five months old.
At five months, Lily is still a young cat full of energy. If she wakes you, give her a play session and a small meal before bedtime, so she is tired when you sleep.
What if she still wants to sleep on me?
Offer Lily a warm bed next to yours, perhaps with a blanket that smells of you. If she persists, gently move her to it each time, and praise her when she stays there.
I will try. What was her age again?
Lily is five months old. She is young and energetic, so a play session before bed and her own warm spot next to yours should help her settle down.
The lift in our building is broken and an elderly neighbour lives on the fifth floor.
That is hard for someone who finds stairs difficult. Has anyone offered help with her shopping or other errands? Small gestures matter a lot in a situation like this.
Not yet. Her name is Mrs Kapoor, she is eighty.
Then you could knock on Mrs Kapoor's door and ask if she needs anything from the market. Many older people appreciate the offer, even if they say no.
What if she is too proud to accept?
Offer it as a favour you are doing anyway, like I am going to the shop, can I get you milk? Mrs Kapoor may find that easier to accept than being asked if she needs help.
That is a good way to put it. I will ask her tomorrow.
Good. When you do, mention that you can bring her groceries up the stairs, and ask what she usually needs. Mrs Kapoor will likely be glad that a neighbour remembered her.
I volunteered to wash the car with my dad on Sunday. Any tips?
Start by rinsing off loose dirt, then use a bucket of soapy water and a soft cloth. Wash from the top down, so dirty water does not run onto clean areas. Do you have car shampoo?
Only dish soap. Is that okay?
Dish soap works for a one-time wash, but it can strip wax from the paint. Ask your dad if he has car shampoo, or buy a small bottle from a shop.
He says he has some in the garage. Should we wash the windows too?
Yes, do the windows last with a clean cloth and plain water, so no soap film is left on the glass. Your dad's car shampoo will be fine for the body of the car.
Great. And what did you say about dish soap?
I said dish soap works for a single wash, but it can strip the wax from the paint. Since your dad already has car shampoo in the garage, use that on Sunday.
My grandmother is coming to stay with us for a month. How can I make her comfortable?
A little preparation goes a long way. Think about her bed, light, bathroom and daily routine. Does she have any difficulties with walking or stairs?
She uses a stick and finds stairs hard. Her name is Savitri.
Then give Savitri a room on the ground floor if you can, and put a firm chair in the room. Keep the path to the bathroom free of rugs and clutter, so she does not trip.
The only free room is upstairs. What do I do?
