If the upstairs room is the only choice, add a sturdy handrail on the stairs and a night light on the landing. Tell Savitri she can rest between steps, and let her go at her own pace.
I have to walk to school in the rain every day this week. Any tips?
A good raincoat or umbrella is the first thing. Wear shoes that can get wet, and carry a spare pair of socks in a plastic bag. How far is school?
About a kilometre. My friend Max walks with me.
A kilometre is not far, and walking with Max makes it more fun. Use a backpack cover, or put your books in a plastic bag inside, so nothing gets wet.
We usually take a shortcut through a field. Is that ok?
In the rain the field may be muddy and slippery, so it is safer to stay on the road. Ask Max to agree to take the longer way, and walk on the side facing traffic.
Fine. Remind me who I walk with?
You walk with your friend Max. Since you are a pair, you can watch out for each other on the road and agree to skip the muddy field shortcut this week.
I am so tired after work. I do not have energy to cook or clean.
That sounds draining. Everyone has days like that. Would it help to simplify things for a few days? What takes up most of your evening?
Cooking dinner and then washing the dishes. I live alone.
Cook a bigger batch on the weekend and freeze portions, so you only reheat on busy nights. For dishes, wash them in one go while a song plays, instead of leaving a pile.
Which meals freeze well?
Dal, rajma, soups and curries freeze well. Rice and rotis can be frozen too. Let them cool, pack them in containers, and label them so you know what is inside.
We are thinking of getting a dog but our neighbours have small children. Is that a problem?
Not necessarily. Many families have dogs near children. The key is a calm, well-trained dog and good manners about barking and gates. What breed are you thinking of?
A beagle. We stay on the ground floor with a small garden.
Beagles are friendly but can be loud when they bark or howl. A garden helps, since a beagle needs a lot of exercise. Train it early to be calm around visitors and children.
Should I tell the neighbours before we get him?
Yes, a friendly word beforehand is thoughtful. Mention that you are getting a beagle and promise to keep the garden gate closed, so the children feel safe near him.
Good. And what did I say about our home?
You said you live on the ground floor with a small garden. That suits a beagle, which needs space to run, but keep the garden gate shut so the neighbours' children are safe.
My rabbit is not eating her hay today.
Rabbits need hay every day, so a refusal can be a warning sign. I cannot diagnose her. How is she otherwise, is she moving about and drinking water?
She is a bit quiet. Her name is Snowy.
Then please contact a vet who treats rabbits today, since problems with eating can get serious in rabbits. Keep Snowy warm and quiet, and offer fresh water until you can go.
Can I give her carrot instead?
Offer a small piece of fresh vegetable if you wish, but hay is her main food and must not be replaced. Tell the vet that Snowy refuses hay and note when she last ate.
I have a question about crate training. Is it cruel?
Not if it is done kindly. Many dogs see a crate as a safe den. It should never be used as punishment, and the dog should not stay in it for too long. Are you thinking of trying it?
Yes, for my puppy Mochi. She is ten weeks old.
At ten weeks Mochi can learn to like a crate. Put a soft blanket and a toy inside, leave the door open at first, and feed her meals near it so it feels like a happy place.
How long can I leave her inside?
At her age, only an hour or two at a time during the day, since young puppies need frequent toilet breaks. At night she may sleep longer, but take her out once if she cries.
She cried a lot the first night. Should I let her out?
Check that she does not need the toilet, then comfort her briefly and put Mochi back. If you let her out each time she cries, she may learn that crying works.
That makes sense. What was her name again?
Her name is Mochi, and she is ten weeks old. Keep the crate a calm, happy place with her blanket and toy, and give her a little time to settle each night.
I want to be ready for the next power cut. What should I keep at home?
A good kit is simple: a torch with spare batteries, a power bank, candles with matches, some bottled water and snacks. Does anyone at home need special items, like medicine?
My father takes tablets and uses a nebuliser. His name is Rajiv.
Then talk to Rajiv's doctor about what to do if the nebuliser cannot be used during a cut. I cannot advise on medicine, but a battery-powered backup is something the doctor may suggest.
Good idea. I will ask the doctor. What else do I need for the kit?
Keep a small radio, a list of emergency numbers, and a charged power bank. Put everything in one box in a place that all of you know, so nobody has to search in the dark.
Okay. Remind me, whose nebuliser should I ask the doctor about?
Your father's. Ask Rajiv's doctor what he should do in a power cut and whether a backup is needed. Keep the answer written down in the emergency box with the other items.
Will do. Thanks for the checklist.
You are welcome. Once the kit is ready, check the torch batteries and the power bank every few months, and make sure Rajiv knows where the emergency box is kept.
My son Henry wants a bunk bed for his room. He shares it with his brother.
Bunk beds save a lot of floor space. Check that the room has enough ceiling height, and that the bed has strong guard rails on the top bunk. How old are the boys?
Henry is nine and Max is six.
Then the younger child, Max, should sleep in the lower bunk, since six is young for a high bed. Henry, at nine, can manage the top, but make sure the ladder is firm.
Henry will want the top. Max will cry.
That is common. You could rotate, but keep Max on the lower bunk for safety. Give him a small reading light and a curtain, so the lower bunk feels like his own special den.
That is a clever idea. Which one did I say is six?
Max is six. He should have the lower bunk with the curtain and the reading light, while Henry, who is nine, takes the top bunk with the guard rails.
I heard cats should not eat chocolate. Is that true?
Yes, chocolate can be harmful to cats and dogs. Keep it well away from your pets. If one has eaten some, call a vet straight away. Do you have a cat?
A kitten, Biscuit. She stole a little piece of my cake just now.
Please call a vet right away and tell them what and how much Biscuit ate. I cannot judge how serious it is, and they can tell you what to do.
The vet says to watch her and she seems fine. Should I stop her from going near the kitchen?
Yes, for now, keep the kitchen door closed and put cakes and sweets out of reach. Biscuit is curious, and kittens will jump on counters if food is there.
I will do that. Which pet ate the cake?
Biscuit, your kitten, ate a little piece of your cake. She seems fine, but keep watching her, close the kitchen door and call the vet again if anything changes.
A neighbour asked me to water her plants while she is away. I said yes but now I feel unsure.
That is a small, kind favour to do for a neighbour. What exactly is it about the job that makes you feel unsure or worried?
I do not know how much water each plant needs. She has about ten pots.
Then ask her for short instructions before she leaves, or send her a message asking. Most people are happy to explain, and it is better to ask now than to guess.
She gave me a note. The ferns need water daily and the cactus only once a week.
That is clear. Give the ferns a little water every morning and the cactus just once a week, as the note says. A watering can makes it easier and tidier.
Right. And which plants need daily water?
The ferns need water every day. The cactus needs it only once a week, so be careful not to overwater it, as that is the most common mistake with cactus plants.
I got caught in the rain without a raincoat and now I am shivering. What should I do?
Get out of the wet clothes as soon as you can and dry yourself with a towel. Then wear dry clothes and have something warm to drink. Are you at home?
Yes. My roommate Gauri is making tea.
That is perfect. Tea and dry clothes will warm you up quickly. Sit somewhere warm with a blanket and rest for a while, and avoid going back out in the rain.
Should I wash my hair now?
If your hair is wet, dry it well with a towel, then use a hair dryer on low heat if you have one. Going to bed with wet hair can make you feel colder.
Okay. I am feeling a bit better now.
I am glad you are feeling better. Drink the tea Gauri made and stay warm. If you start to feel unwell later, rest, and ask someone at home to help.
Thanks. What was my roommate's name?
Your roommate is Gauri. She made the tea that warmed you up, so a thank you would be nice, perhaps with a biscuit.
I want to adopt an older dog from a shelter instead of a puppy. Is that a good idea?
Many people love adopting older dogs. They are often calmer, house-trained and ready to bond. You will need patience as they adjust. Why are you drawn to an older dog?
I work all day and a puppy would be too much. My sister Natalie says adults are easier.
Natalie has a point. A grown dog usually needs fewer toilet breaks and less training than a puppy. Still, any dog needs daily walks and company, so plan your schedule.
How do I choose one at the shelter?
Spend time with a few dogs. Look for one that seems calm with you, and ask the shelter staff about its history and habits. Visit more than once before you decide.
Good advice. What did Natalie say about adult dogs?
Natalie said adult dogs are easier than puppies. That fits what you said about working all day, so an older dog from the shelter could suit your routine better.
I am trying a weekly cleaning schedule. Monday is bathrooms. What should I do for the other days?
Spread the jobs so no day is too heavy. For example: Tuesday kitchen, Wednesday dusting, Thursday floors, Friday laundry and bedding. Does that suit you?
Yes, but I work late on Thursdays.
Then move the floors to Saturday morning, and make Thursday a rest day. That way, you do not have to clean on your busiest night.
Good. What goes on Friday again?
Laundry and bedding go on Friday, with the kitchen on Tuesday and dusting on Wednesday. Floors move to Saturday, since you work late on Thursdays.
I live alone and the flat feels too quiet. How can I make it cosier?
Soft lighting, a rug, a few plants and some music can make a difference. Is there a room that feels the emptiest?
The living room. It has just a sofa and a TV.
Add a warm lamp, a rug and a few cushions to the living room. A small shelf with books or photos gives the room a personal touch.
I love the idea of photos. I have many of my friends Ruby and Asif.
Then print some of them and put them in simple frames on the shelf. Photos of Ruby and Asif will make the room feel full of people you care about.
Great. And what colour lamp should I get?
A lamp with a warm, yellowish light is cosiest. Place it beside the sofa, near the shelf with the photos of Ruby and Asif, for a soft glow in the evenings.
I will look for one this weekend.
Good plan. Take a measurement of the space beside the sofa first, so the lamp fits, and check that the light is warm before you buy it.
My room has no storage at all. Any space-saving tricks?
Use vertical space. Wall shelves, hooks and over-the-door racks add storage without taking floor space. A bed with drawers underneath is also helpful. What do you need to store?
Clothes, mostly, and a lot of shoes.
Add a hanging shoe organiser on the back of the door for the shoes. For clothes, roll them instead of folding to fit more into drawers, and use hooks for jackets.
The door is the only free wall. Can I use both sides?
Yes, but check that the door still closes properly. Use a slim organiser for your shoes on the inside, and a few hooks on the outside, if the door has space.
We are bringing our new kitten home on Friday. How do we prepare the house?
Walk through each room and look for dangers: loose wires, small objects, open windows, and plants that are unsafe for cats. Set up a small room first, with food, water, a litter tray and a bed.
She is called Rani. We have two children and a dog called Bruno.
Then introduce Rani slowly. Keep her in a small room first, away from Bruno, and let the children visit quietly one at a time, so she does not feel overwhelmed.
The kids will want to carry her around all day.
Explain that kittens need lots of sleep. Show the children how to hold Rani gently with two hands and let them sit on the floor to play, which is safer for her.
Good. And how will I introduce the dog?
Let Bruno smell her blanket first, then let them see each other through a gate with Bruno calm and on a leash. Reward both when they stay quiet. Take your time.
Great. What names did I say were in the family?
You mentioned two children, a dog called Bruno and the new kitten, Rani. Keep Rani in her own room first, and introduce Bruno slowly while the children stay calm.
My puppy wees on the carpet even after I take him out. Why?
Puppies have small bladders and are still learning. Also, a carpet that smells of an earlier accident can invite him to go there again. Do you clean the spot well?
Only with water. His name is Ziggy.
Water does not remove the smell. Use a cleaner made for pet odours, because Ziggy can still smell the old spot and will want to use it again.
How often should I take him out?
Every two hours, and right after he eats, drinks, plays or wakes up. Praise Ziggy and give him a treat when he goes outside, so he learns where to go.
The power is out and I was in the middle of cooking dal on the electric stove. What now?
Turn the stove off at the switch, so it does not start suddenly when the power returns. Then check whether the dal is cooked enough to eat. Do you have a gas burner as a backup?
Yes, a small gas stove. The dal is half cooked.
Then move the pot to the gas stove and finish cooking it there. Keep a torch in your other hand if the kitchen is dark, and take care near the flame.
The torch is in my room. Is a phone light okay?
A phone light works for a few minutes, but save your battery. Ask someone at home to hold the torch, or light a candle in a safe spot away from the stove.
My sister Tanvi will hold the torch.
That is a good plan. Tanvi can stand beside you and shine the light on the pot while you stir the dal, and she can hand you the spices.
The dal is done. Where did I say the dal was cooking?
You said it was on the electric stove, and half cooked when the power failed. You moved it to the small gas stove to finish it, with Tanvi holding the torch.
I want to tell you about the power cut we had last night. It was actually fun.
Tell me more. A power cut can be fun if you make the best of it. What did you all do?
We sat on the terrace and my grandfather told us stories about his village. My cousin Zoya brought her guitar.
What a lovely evening. Stories from your grandfather and music from Zoya under the night sky sounds like something you will remember for a long time.
The best part was when he told the story of the tiger near his house.
A tiger story told by a grandfather in the dark must have been thrilling. Did he say it really happened, or was it one of his made-up tales?
He swears it is true! Anyway, we are going to do this every month.
That is a lovely tradition. You could plan a no-screens evening on the terrace, and ask your grandfather for a new story and Zoya to play her guitar each time.
Good. Which of my relatives plays guitar?
Your cousin Zoya plays the guitar. She can bring it along each month, and your grandfather can tell another village story, like the one about the tiger.
Do you know why power cuts happen so often in summer?
I cannot say why it happens in your area, but in general, more people use fans and coolers in summer, and the demand can be higher than the supply. Storms can also damage lines.
That makes sense. We have had cuts every afternoon this week.
Afternoons are the hottest time, so demand peaks then. It might help to plan jobs that need electricity, like washing and ironing, for the morning, when the demand is lower.
I can do the ironing early. Natalie, my wife, does her office calls at home though.
Then Natalie may want a backup for her calls. A phone with a charged power bank, and mobile data she can switch to if the router goes off, can help during the afternoon cuts.
She has a power bank. Who did I say works from home?
Your wife, Natalie, does her office calls from home. With her power bank charged in the morning, and your ironing done early, the afternoon cuts should trouble you less.
Our neighbourhood is getting a new transformer. Will it stop the power cuts?
A new transformer can reduce cuts caused by overload, but I cannot say whether it will fix every problem. Other faults in the lines can still cause outages. Who told you about the transformer?
My neighbour Asif. He heard it from the electricity office.
Then Asif is a good person to ask for details, such as when the work starts. The electricity office can also tell you if there will be a planned shutdown while they install it.
He says the shutdown will be on Saturday morning. What should we do?
Charge your devices on Friday night, store some drinking water, and plan quiet indoor activities. If the work takes all morning, cook breakfast early or make something that needs no power.
Thanks. Who told me about the transformer?
Your neighbour Asif did. He heard it at the electricity office, so you can ask him again for the exact Saturday timing when you charge your devices on Friday.
My puppy keeps barking at night when we put him in the kitchen. His name is Rusty.
Poor Rusty is probably lonely. Puppies are used to sleeping near their mother and siblings. Is there a way to let him sleep closer to your room for the first few weeks?
Maybe. My wife says the kitchen is the right place.
A kitchen can work if it is warm and safe, but if Rusty is barking a lot, try putting his bed in the corridor near your bedroom door. Give him a soft toy and a ticking clock.
A ticking clock? Why?
The soft ticking sounds a little like a heartbeat, which can comfort puppies. A warm water bottle wrapped in a towel works similarly. Neither is magic, but both help Rusty settle.
Okay. We will move him tonight to the corridor.
Good. Place his bed there with the soft toy, and sit with Rusty for a few minutes until he calms down. He may bark for a night or two, but it should improve.
Remind me who is the one who wants him in the kitchen?
Your wife thinks the kitchen is the right place for Rusty. You could explain that it is only for the first few weeks, and then he can move back once he is more settled.
How do I stop my puppy from jumping on guests?
Teach him that jumping gets no attention. When he jumps, turn away and ignore him. When all four paws are on the floor, say hello and give a treat. Ask guests to do the same.
Our guests think it is cute. His name is Pablo.
That is the challenge. If Pablo gets attention for jumping, he will keep doing it. Ask guests kindly to wait until he sits before they pet him.
What if I keep him on a leash when guests arrive?
A leash helps you control him while he learns. Let Pablo sniff the guest calmly, and reward him for sitting, then let him loose when he is calm.
I just saw my kitten Luna sleep with her tongue out. Is that normal?
It is a funny sight but usually harmless. Some cats relax so deeply that their tongue peeks out. How old is Luna?
Four months old.
At four months Luna sleeps a lot, often sixteen hours a day or more, because she is growing fast. A little tongue showing is nothing to worry about unless she seems unwell while awake.
Okay, she is energetic otherwise. Can I take a photo?
Take the photo, but try to avoid using a flash, which can startle her. A quick photo of Luna asleep with her tongue out will be a nice memory.
My kitten Tiger will not use the litter tray anymore.
That can be upsetting. Cats avoid a tray if it is dirty, if the litter changed, or if they feel stressed. Did anything change recently?
We changed the litter brand two days ago.
That may be the reason. Switch back to the old kind, or mix the two for a few days. Cats can be fussy about the feel and smell of their litter.
Fine. Do you think the tray should be moved too?
Only if it sits in a noisy or busy place. Keep it in a quiet corner, away from his food and water. Do not move it too often, or Tiger may get confused.
Okay, I will mix the old and new litter. Should I clean the accidents?
Yes, clean them with a pet-safe cleaner, since a smell left behind can make Tiger return to the same spot. Then keep the tray clean and the litter mixed for a few days.
Alright. What did we change two days ago?
You changed the litter brand two days ago, which may have upset Tiger. Mixing the old litter with the new one for a few days should help him accept the tray again.
We are going on holiday for a week and I am worried about my dog. His name is Sheru.
Many people feel that way. You can leave him with a trusted friend or family member, or use a good boarding place. What does Sheru prefer, a quiet home or a lot of company?
He is shy. He likes quiet and he knows my cousin Henry.
Then Henry sounds like a good choice. Sheru already knows him, and a familiar person in a familiar home can reduce stress. Ask Henry to keep to Sheru's usual meals and walks.
Should I leave Sheru's own bed and toys?
Yes, leave his own bed, toys and blanket with Henry. Familiar smells comfort a dog who is away from you, and Sheru will settle in more easily.
I will also write a feeding note. Who did I say is a good choice?
Your cousin Henry. Sheru already knows him, so he is the best choice. The feeding note, along with Sheru's bed and toys, will help Henry take good care of him.
Thanks, that makes me feel better.
I am glad. Before you go, share the vet's number with Henry, and tell him Sheru's walking times. Then you can enjoy your holiday knowing he is in good hands.
My little cousin wants a pet but her parents say no. She is very sad.
That is hard for her, and for you to watch. Parents often have good reasons, such as space, cost or allergies. How old is she?
She is seven. Her name is Isla.
At seven, Isla may like a pet but cannot look after it alone. Perhaps she could help a friend or neighbour with their pet, or learn about animals through books and visits.
That could work. Our neighbour has two rabbits.
Then Isla could visit the rabbits with a parent's permission, and help feed them under the neighbour's eye. It lets her learn to care for an animal without owning one.
I just rearranged my room and now I cannot sleep because everything feels strange.
That is common. A new layout can feel odd for a few nights, because your mind is used to the old one. What did you change?
I moved the bed to the other wall and now the window is on my left.
It takes a few nights to adjust. Keep your bedside items in the same spots, like your water and lamp, so something stays familiar. Also dim the lights early.
Good tip. What if I still cannot sleep after a week?
If the new bed position still bothers you, you can move it back or try another spot. You rearranged the room to feel better, so choose the layout where you sleep best.
I think I will give it a week. Which side is the window on now?
The window is on your left now, after you moved the bed to the other wall. Keep your water and lamp in their usual places, and give yourself the week to adjust.
I need to rearrange the living room for a party. Any ideas?
Clear the centre so people can move around, and push the sofas against the walls. Put the food table on one side and keep drinks separate to avoid crowding. How many people are coming?
Around twenty. It is my brother Harsh's birthday.
For twenty guests, bring in extra chairs from other rooms and put them along the walls. Keep a clear path to the door, and place decorations at one end, so Harsh's birthday corner feels special.
Where should the cake go?
Put the cake on a small table in the decorated corner, where everyone can gather around Harsh when he cuts it. Keep it away from the door, so people do not bump it.
The kids upstairs bounce a ball in the evenings. My baby sleeps then.
That is frustrating when you are trying to keep a baby asleep. Would you feel comfortable talking to the parents? A calm, friendly word often helps.
I do not even know their names.
You could introduce yourself at the building entrance, and ask their names. Once you have said hello, mention that your baby sleeps in the evening and ask if the ball games could be earlier.
Okay. I met the mother today. Her name is Ruby.
That is a good first step. Since you now know Ruby's name, you could knock on her door in a day or two, and ask kindly about the ball games in the evening.
Good. What was her name again?
Her name is Ruby. When you speak to her, begin with a friendly hello, then explain that your baby sleeps in the evening and ask if the kids could play with the ball earlier.
I want to thank our neighbours for helping during our house move. What can I give?
A small gift or a card with a note is thoughtful. Something simple like sweets, a plant or a home-cooked dish works well. How many neighbours helped?
Three households. The Sharmas, Mr Dutta and Isla's family.
You could make one small box of sweets for each household, with a handwritten note. Name each one, so every neighbour knows you are thanking them personally.
Good. What should I write to Isla's family?
Something short like: Thank you for helping us move. We are so grateful for your kindness and happy to have you as neighbours. Add a line for Isla, such as a hello from us.
I will write that. Which families helped me?
The Sharmas, Mr Dutta and Isla's family helped you move. Give each one a box of sweets with a note, and write a short hello for Isla in her family's note.
I am trying to decide which room in our house should be the family room. We have three options.
Tell me about the options. What does each room look like, and how does your family use the house in the evenings?
One is the big hall at the front, one is the back room near the kitchen, and one is upstairs. We watch TV and play games together.
The back room near the kitchen could be handy, since snacks and tea are close. The front hall is bigger but may be noisy from the street. Upstairs is quieter but far from the kitchen.
My mother Savitri finds stairs hard, so upstairs is not suitable.
Then that settles the upstairs room. Savitri can reach the hall or the back room easily, and either one will let her join the family in the evenings.
Between the two, the hall has better light.
Good light matters for games and for reading. If the street noise is not too loud, the hall may be the better choice. You could try it for a week and see.
Okay. Remind me, who finds stairs hard?
Your mother Savitri finds stairs hard, which is why upstairs is not suitable. The hall has better light and is easy for her to reach, so it looks like a good family room.
Before I move out I want to sell some old furniture. Where do I start?
Take clear photos in good light and note the size, the condition and the price you would like. Then you can show them to friends, neighbours and local groups. What are you selling?
A wooden wardrobe and a study table.
Good items to sell. Wipe them clean, and mention the wood type and any scratches honestly. People appreciate it when you describe things as they are.
How should I decide on a price?
Look at what similar used furniture costs near you, and set a fair price close to that. Be ready for a small negotiation, as most buyers will ask for a discount.
Good. I will ask my friend Max, who just moved house.
Max is a good person to ask, since he may know where people shop for used furniture, or may need a wardrobe and study table himself.
I want to teach my children to fold clothes. Where do I begin?
Start with simple items like towels and T-shirts. Show them step by step, and let them practise. How old are your children?
Zoya is eight and Asif is eleven.
At those ages, Asif can fold most things, while Zoya can start with towels and handkerchiefs. Make it a game, like a race to fold the most towels neatly.
Zoya often gets frustrated when she cannot do it right.
Reassure her that it takes practice. Praise her effort rather than the result, and let her fold small items first, so she gets success quickly.
That should help. And Asif could help her?
Yes, Asif can show Zoya how to do it, which teaches him patience and helps her learn from a big brother. Keep the lessons short and cheerful.
Okay, which of the kids is eleven?
Asif is eleven and Zoya is eight. Asif can fold most clothes and help Zoya learn on towels and handkerchiefs, with a bit of praise from you.
The garbage truck did not come today and our bin is overflowing.
That is unpleasant, especially in warm weather. Can you keep the bin tightly covered, and put extra rubbish in a sealed bag? Is there someone to call about the missed collection?
The society office. I will call them.
Good, call the society office and ask when the truck will come. Meanwhile, tie the bags tightly and keep them in a corner away from the kitchen, so smells and flies stay away.
They said the truck is coming tomorrow. Should I put the bags outside?
Keep them inside until the truck arrives tomorrow, as bags left outside can attract stray animals. Put them out in the morning, just before the collection time.
The rain stopped and now there is a rainbow outside our window.
How lovely. Rainbows appear when sunlight passes through raindrops and splits into colours. Can you see the whole arch or just a part of it?
Just a part, over the big tree. My little brother Harsh is shouting with joy.
That sounds delightful. Children love rainbows. Let Harsh watch it for as long as it lasts, since it will fade soon as the clouds move.
Should we take a photo?
Yes, a quick photo will help you remember it. Try to include the big tree for a nice view, and take a picture of Harsh looking at the rainbow too.
Great idea. Who was shouting with joy again?
Your little brother Harsh. Take that photo of him looking at the rainbow over the big tree, before it fades away, and you will remember how happy he was.
I am hanging curtains in my new bedroom and cannot decide between blue and grey.
Both are calm colours. Blue feels fresh and light, while grey feels modern and quiet. What colour are the walls and bedsheets?
Walls are cream. My bedsheet is white with small blue flowers.
Then blue curtains would match the flowers on your bedsheet and look good with cream walls. Grey would also work but may feel cooler and plainer next to the blue flowers.
My sister Gauri says grey is more stylish.
Style is a matter of taste. Grey can look elegant, but blue will tie in with your bedsheet. Hold small pieces of both fabrics up to the wall in daylight, then choose the one you like.
I will do that. What colour are my walls?
Your walls are cream. Both the blue and the grey would suit them, but blue picks up the flowers on your white bedsheet, so you may prefer it over what Gauri suggested.
My puppy is scared of the stairs. Should I carry him?
For now it is fine to carry a small puppy, since stairs can hurt his joints, but he also needs to learn gradually. How old is he, and what is his name?
Leo, he is four months old and a bit big.
At four months Leo is growing fast. Let him try one or two low steps with a treat at the top, and support him from behind. Do not push him.
What if he panics halfway up?
Stay calm and gently pick him up. Panic can stay in his memory, so end on a happy note and try again later. Do short practice sessions with plenty of treats for Leo.
Do birds need company? I have one budgie and I am at work all day.
Budgies are social birds and can feel lonely. Having two budgies is often recommended. A mirror, toys and a radio can help in the meantime. How long has yours lived with you?
Two years. His name is Tweety.
After two years, Tweety is used to you, but he may still enjoy a companion. Introduce a second budgie slowly, in a separate cage near his, before putting them together.
I will think about it. Meanwhile can I leave the radio on?
A quiet radio or soft music can keep Tweety company during the day. Keep the volume low and avoid loud talk shows, so he is not startled.
Okay. What was the name of my budgie?
Your budgie is called Tweety. A quiet radio is fine while you are at work, and if you decide to get a second bird, introduce it to Tweety slowly.
I just realised my desk is facing a blank wall and I get bored while studying.
A blank wall can feel dull. You could add a pinboard, a small plant or a calendar, so you have something pleasant to look at. Or turn the desk to face the window.
The window is behind the desk. My brother Max says that is better for light.
Max has a point. With the window behind you, daylight falls on your books and you are not squinting into the brightness, so you can keep the desk where it is.
So what should I put on the wall?
A pinboard works well for notes, a timetable and photos. You could also add a small shelf with one plant. Keep the wall simple, so it does not distract you from the work.
Is it okay to leave a kitten alone while I go to college?
A kitten can be left for a few hours if she has food, water, a litter tray and safe toys, but very young kittens need more company. How old is she, and how long will you be away?
She is four months old, her name is Nimbu. I will be out for six hours.
Six hours is long for Nimbu. Ask someone at home to check on her, or leave her in a small, safe room with toys and a warm bed. Spend time playing with her before you leave.
My mum is at home all day. She can look in on her.
That is the best solution. Ask your mum to feed Nimbu at midday and play with her for a few minutes. A kitten feels safer when a familiar person is near.
Good. I will tell her. Remind me how old Nimbu is?
Nimbu is four months old. Tell your mum she should check her food, water and litter tray at midday, and spend a little time with Nimbu while you are at college.
Our street has a new family who speak a different language at home. I want to welcome them.
That is a kind thought. A smile and a simple hello go a long way, whatever language people speak. What are you planning to do?
Maybe bake something and take it to them. My mother Natalie makes a great cake.
A homemade cake is a warm welcome. Just check first whether they have any food restrictions, such as no eggs, so your mother Natalie can make something everyone can eat.
How can I ask them if we do not speak the same language?
Use simple English, gestures and a smile. You could write one or two short sentences, like: Welcome to our street. Do you eat eggs? A younger family member may be able to help translate.
They have a girl my age. Maybe she can help.
That is likely. A girl your age may know some English from school, and it is a good chance to make a new friend on your street.
I will go on Saturday. Who is baking the cake?
Your mother Natalie is baking it. Before Saturday, ask her to wait until you have asked the new girl whether the family eats eggs, so the cake suits them.
I have a netball match tomorrow and my stomach feels funny. I'm Ishita, by the way.
Hi Ishita. That fluttery feeling is very common before a match. It usually means you care about playing well. What position do you play?
Goal attack. I'm scared I'll miss an easy shot in front of everyone.
Everyone misses shots, even the best players. Try to think about the next pass instead of the last miss. A short warm-up shot routine before the game can also settle you.
Okay. Our coach, Mrs Pillai, says the same thing about the next pass.
Then she is giving you good advice. Tomorrow, when you feel nervous, hear her voice in your head and keep your eyes on the next pass.
What was the position I said I play again? I want to tell my mum.
You said goal attack, Ishita. Tell your mum that you play goal attack and that Mrs Pillai taught you to think about the next pass.
My best friend Laila moved to Pune last week and school feels empty without her.
I'm sorry, Laila moving must feel like a big hole in your day. Missing someone you shared everything with is natural. Have you two talked since she left?
Only once on a video call. She was busy unpacking.
That makes sense, a new house takes time. You could send her a short voice note about something funny from school today. It lets her know you're thinking of her without needing a long call.
Maybe I'll tell her about the mango tree where we always ate lunch.
That is a lovely idea. Shared small places like that make a friendship feel close even from far away. She will probably smile when she hears it.
Should I sit under that tree alone tomorrow or is that sad?
It isn't sad. Sitting under the mango tree can feel like keeping a place for Laila. You might also invite a classmate to join you, so the spot is not only about missing her.
I need a birthday gift for my brother Kunal. He's turning ten.
Happy early birthday to Kunal. What does he like doing most? Games, drawing, cricket, building things?
He loves drawing animals and he always runs out of pencils.
Then a nice set of coloured pencils with a sketchbook would be perfect. If you want something extra, add a small book about how to draw animals step by step.
The pencil set sounds good. I only have a small budget though.
That's fine. A simple set of twelve to twenty-four pencils and a plain sketchbook from a local stationery shop can be quite cheap. You could wrap it nicely yourself with newspaper and ribbon.
Which one did you say I should skip, the book or the pencils?
I did not say to skip either one. The pencils and sketchbook are the main gift for Kunal. The animal drawing book was only an optional extra, so skip that one if your budget is tight.
It has been raining all morning and I can't go out to play. Ugh.
Rainy mornings can feel long when you want to be outside. What were you planning to play?
Football with my cousins Aryan and Pari at the park.
That's a shame. While you wait, you could try an indoor game with them if they are close by, like cards or a board game. Or the rain might stop by afternoon and the field will be fun and muddy.
Pari hates mud. She always says her shoes get ruined.
Then she might like an indoor game more. You could ask her to pick one, so she feels included. Aryan could choose the next game.
Which cousin hates mud again? I want to ask her first.
That was Pari. She said her shoes get ruined in the mud, so ask her first whether she would rather play indoors or wait for the park to dry.
I keep going to bed late and then I'm tired in class. I'm Rehan.
Hi Rehan. Tired mornings are no fun, especially when class starts early. What usually keeps you up at night?
Mostly my phone. I tell myself five more minutes and then it is midnight.
That happens to many people. One simple habit is to charge your phone in another room, so it is not in your hand at bedtime. Then you can read a few pages or listen to quiet music.
I like reading. I have a detective book I want to finish.
That's a good bedtime plan. Read just one chapter each night with a small lamp on, and stop when your eyes feel heavy. The detective story will give you something to look forward to.
Which book did I say I want to finish? I want to ask the librarian for the next one.
You said a detective book, Rehan. Ask the librarian if there is a next one in the series, so your one-chapter-a-night plan can keep going after this book.
Everyone in my group went to the canteen without telling me. I feel left out.
That sounds hurtful, and it makes sense that you feel left out. It can sting even when nobody meant it. Do you think they simply forgot, or did it feel on purpose?
I think they forgot. I was in the library returning a book.
That is a likely reason. If they saw you were busy, they may have just gone ahead. You could tell them calmly, "I felt a bit left out today, next time please call me."
I'm Sneha, and I'm shy about saying things like that.
Thank you for telling me, Sneha. Being shy is okay. You can start small, like saying it with a smile or sending a short message before lunch to say you are joining them.
Can you help me explain where I was, so they know I wasn't ignoring them?
You were in the library returning a book, Sneha. You can say, "I was returning a book and missed you all leaving. Please wait for me next time."
Our neighbour uncle George just had a long week and looks worn out. I'd like to do something nice.
That's thoughtful of you. Small things often help most. Do you know what he enjoys, or what might make his week easier?
He likes hot tea and he waters his plants every evening.
You could bring him a cup of tea one evening, or offer to water the plants for a day so he can rest. Both are gentle ways to show you noticed.
I'll water the plants. Should I knock first?
Yes, knock politely and say what you would like to do. Something like, "Uncle, I can water the plants tonight if you want to rest." Then let him decide.
And what was the other nice thing I could do besides plants?
The other idea was bringing uncle George a cup of hot tea, since you said he likes it. You could do the plants and the tea together if he agrees.
Our school relay is on Friday and I'm the last runner. I'm so nervous.
Being the last runner is a big job, and it is normal to feel nervous. It also means your team trusts you. Have you practised the baton pass?
Yes, but I dropped it twice yesterday. My teammate is Amelia.
Dropping it in practice is useful, because you find the problem early. Ask Amelia to practise a slower, steady handover a few times, with a clear word like "now" as the signal.
Good idea. Amelia talks a lot, she'll like having a word.
A shared word keeps both of you calm and focused. Practise it a few times before Friday so it feels automatic when you are tired.
Remind me, which word was I going to use with her?
The word was "now". You and Amelia can use it as the signal for the handover, so on Friday you both know exactly when to pass and take the baton.
Mum's anniversary is coming up and I want to help Dad pick something. My name is Pari.
Hi Pari, what a nice thing to help with. Does your mum have a hobby or something she keeps saying she would like?
She loves gardening. She wanted a bigger pot for her tulsi plant.
A big, pretty clay pot would be a lovely gift because it is something she asked for. You could add a small watering can or a hand-painted label for the tulsi.
Can I paint the label myself? I am not great at painting.
Yes, handmade is special even if it is a little wobbly. Use simple letters and a few leaves. Mum will treasure it because you made it for her.
Wait, what plant was the pot for?
The pot was for her tulsi plant, Pari. You can paint "Tulsi" on the label, with a few small leaves around the letters.
My little sister Sneha won't sleep without a story. I run out of ideas every night.
That is a sweet routine. You do not need a new story each night. Little ones love hearing favourites again. Which stories does Sneha like?
She likes ones with animals, especially a clever fox.

Then you could make a series about a fox. Each night, the fox can have a small adventure, like finding a lost button or helping a bird. It is easy to continue because the main character stays the same.
I like that. I'll call him Chintu the fox.
Chintu is a cute name. You can keep the stories short and calm, with Chintu going back to his den at the end, so Sneha feels sleepy.
What kind of animal did Sneha like again? I forgot already.
Sneha likes animal stories, especially ones with a clever fox. That is why Chintu the fox is a perfect hero for her bedtime stories.
Do you think I should carry an umbrella today? The sky looks grey but there's no rain yet.
I can't see your sky or a forecast, but grey clouds can mean rain later. Carrying a small folding umbrella costs you very little, and it is annoying to get soaked without one.
Right. I'm walking to my tuition class with my friend Ryan, about twenty minutes.
Twenty minutes is long enough for a shower to catch you. Take the umbrella and offer to share it with Ryan if it starts to pour. You will both stay drier.
Ryan always forgets his. He says he hates carrying things.
Then you are the sensible one today. Walking together under your umbrella gives you a chance to chat, and Ryan will be glad you remembered.
I got a lower mark than I expected in my science test and I can't stop thinking about it.
That is disappointing, especially when you worked for it. It is normal to keep replaying it. Do you know which questions took your marks away?
The diagram question. I mixed up the two parts of the flower.
That is a very fixable mistake. Draw the flower again from memory tonight, label each part, and check it against your book. After a few tries, the parts usually stay in your head.
Okay. Can I do it with Aryan? He's good at drawing.
Yes, that would make it more fun. Aryan can sketch, and you can quiz each other on the labels. Teaching someone else is a good way to remember the flower diagram.
A new boy named Kunal joined our class today and sat alone at lunch.
It can be hard to be new, so noticing him matters. Did you get a chance to talk to him?
No, I was too shy. But I want to tomorrow.
Tomorrow, you could simply say hello and ask if he wants to sit with you. A small question like "Do you like cricket?" can start a chat. You do not need to say much.
What if he says no and wants to sit alone?
Then that is okay, and you can just smile and say he is welcome any time. Some people need a day to settle in. Kunal will remember that you were friendly.
I fall asleep fine but wake up at three in the morning and can't go back. Any ideas for a calmer night?
I can only share simple routine tips, not medical advice. A quiet, dark room helps, and so does keeping lights and screens off if you wake. Slow breathing or a few calm thoughts can also help.
I do drink chai at six in the evening. Could that matter?
It might. Tea has caffeine, and for some people an evening cup makes sleep lighter. You could try having it earlier in the afternoon, or switching to warm milk in the evening.
Okay, I'll move the chai to four. Will that be enough?
I can't promise, but it is a gentle change to test for a week. Watch how you sleep once your chai moves to four, and if it still bothers you, you might talk to a doctor.
I want to buy a thank-you gift for my teacher, Mr Rao, but I only have a little money.
A thank-you gift does not need to be expensive. A short handwritten note often means the most. What does Mr Rao enjoy?
He drinks a lot of tea and he is always losing his pens.
Then a nice pen with a note saying thank you could work well, and since he loses pens, a spare one will help. You can add a small tea packet if your money allows.
I'll get the pen and write the note. What should I write?
Keep it simple and true. For example, "Dear Mr Rao, thank you for explaining things so patiently this year. I hope this pen stays with you longer than the others."
My friend Amelia and I had a small fight about who gets to be team captain.
That sounds uncomfortable, especially with a friend. Is it settled now, or are you both still upset?
Still upset. She won't look at me in class.
It sounds like she is hurt too. You could write her a short note or speak to her alone, and say you do not want a game to spoil your friendship. Start with how you feel instead of who was right.
Good. I'll do it at recess. Should I say I'm sorry first?
If you feel you were unkind, then yes, saying sorry first can soften things. You can tell Amelia, "I'm sorry we argued about the captain thing. I miss talking to you."
The heat is terrible where I live. How do people stay comfortable at home without cooling machines?
Many families keep curtains closed in the afternoon, open windows at night, and drink plenty of water or nimbu pani. Light cotton clothes and rest during the hottest hours also help.
My grandmother also puts a wet cloth on the window. Does that work?
Yes, a damp cloth or khus mat on the window can cool the air that comes in as the water dries. It works best when there is a bit of breeze.
Nice. I'll try it with my room window tomorrow afternoon.
Good plan. Keep the cloth wet by sprinkling it every hour or so. Your grandmother's wet window trick is old but clever, so tell her how well it works.
I'm moving to a new school next month. Ishita says it will be fun but I'm not sure.
Moving is a big change, so mixed feelings are completely normal. Ishita sounds supportive. What worries you the most?
Making friends. I am not good at starting conversations.
Many students feel the same. You do not need a big speech. A simple hello, a compliment on a pencil box, or asking where the library is can be enough to start.
I'll try the library question. Maybe I'll ask Ishita to practise with me.
That is a great way to practise. Ask Ishita to pretend to be a new classmate, and say your question out loud a few times until it feels easy.
Can you help me plan a bedtime routine for my little brother Rehan? He's six and gets cranky at night.
Sure. A simple routine helps children feel safe. For a six-year-old, something like dinner, brushing teeth, a quiet story and lights off at the same time each night usually works well.
He hates brushing. He says the paste is too spicy.
Many children dislike strong mint paste. You could look for a mild fruit-flavoured paste made for kids, and let him pick it in the shop. Choosing gives him a small sense of control.
That's smart. And the story part, should I read or let him read?
For a six-year-old like Rehan, you could take turns. You read a page, then he reads or tells what he sees in the picture. It keeps him calm and makes him feel proud.
I saw an old lady struggling with her bags near the bus stop today, and I didn't help. Now I feel bad.
Feeling bad shows you care. It is okay to miss a moment sometimes. Is she someone you might see again?
Probably. She lives near our building.
Then next time, you could greet her and ask, "Aunty, can I carry one bag for you?" Most people appreciate a polite offer, and she can say yes or no.
What if the bus comes and I'm in a hurry?
If you are rushing, a quick offer still counts, or you could help her with the bag to the bus door. You can also help at her building later, since you live near her.
My cousin Pari is moving to another city next week. What can I give her so she remembers me?
A small keepsake works well. A photo of the two of you in a simple frame, or a little notebook where you wrote memories, would be lovely. What does Pari like?
She likes stickers and writing diaries.
Then a diary with a cover you decorate with stickers is perfect. On the first page, you could write a short message so she finds it when she starts writing in her new city.
I'll do that. Should I put my number inside too?
Yes, but ask your parents first about sharing contact details. You could write "Call me whenever you miss home" along with your parents' number so Pari can reach you.
Tomorrow is my first football trial for the school team. I can barely eat.
A first trial is exciting and scary at the same time. Try a light, familiar meal and plenty of water. What position are you hoping for?
Defender. My friend George says I'm quick at stopping attackers.
Then you already have a good start. George's view matters, because he has seen you play. At the trial, stay calm, keep your body between the ball and the goal, and follow the coach's instructions.
What if I make a silly mistake in the first five minutes?
One mistake is small. Coaches watch how you recover, so jog back to your position and keep going. Showing effort and teamwork counts as much as a perfect tackle.
Okay. Last question: should I wear my old boots or buy new ones?
Old boots that fit well are safer, because new ones can rub and hurt your feet. Wear the pair you already trust and check the laces the night before.
Right. Please say again who told me I'm quick?
It was George. He said you are quick at stopping attackers, so remember his words when you step on to the field tomorrow as a defender.
I found out my friend Ryan has a new best friend and I feel jealous.
Jealousy is an honest feeling, and it does not make you a bad friend. It often shows how much you value Ryan. Has anything changed in how you two spend time?
We used to walk home together. Now he walks with a boy called Aryan.
That could feel like losing something. Still, having Aryan as a friend does not mean Ryan likes you less. Friendships can be bigger than two people.
Should I ask to walk with them?
You could. You might say, "Mind if I join you two?" Walking in a group of three can be fun, and you may find Aryan is kind too.
What if they say no?
That would hurt, but it is unlikely from a friend. If it happens, you can ask Ryan to meet you another day, just the two of you, and tell him you miss your walks.
Alright. I'll try it tomorrow.
Good. Say hello to both Ryan and Aryan with a smile, and keep it light. Trying is brave, and you may find the walk home feels friendly again.
Help me find a gift for my grandfather. He just turned seventy and he's a bit hard to shop for.
Happy seventieth to him. Gifts for grandparents are often best when they are useful or personal. What does he spend time on during the day?
He reads the newspaper and sits in the balcony watching birds.
A small pair of binoculars or a simple bird guide would suit him well. Another idea is a comfortable reading cushion for the balcony chair.
He already has binoculars. Maybe the guide.
A bird guide with clear pictures would be a good choice, especially one about birds in India so he can match what he sees. You could add a notebook to jot down what he spots.
Oh, the notebook is nice. He'll write dates in it. Should I write something inside?
Yes. A short note on the first page, such as "For Dadaji's bird list, with love," would make it feel special. He will probably keep it for years.
Perfect. Now what was the first idea you gave, before the guide?
The first idea was a small pair of binoculars, but you said he already has a pair. In the same reply I also mentioned the bird guide and a reading cushion for his balcony chair.
We planned a picnic in the park on Sunday with Laila and her family. The forecast I saw says maybe rain.
A maybe is hard to plan around. Having a backup helps. Is there a covered place nearby, or could you move the picnic to someone's house?
There is a shelter in the park, but it's small.
A small shelter could work for the food and the adults, while children play nearby if the rain is light. You could also bring a plastic sheet to sit on.
Good. Also, the weather might change by Saturday evening.
Then check the forecast again that evening. Decide together with Laila's family whether to go ahead, move indoors, or pick another day.
What should we bring in case it's cold after rain?
Light jackets or shawls, a flask of hot tea or milk, and a dry towel. Wet grass can make the air feel cooler, so a spare pair of socks may also help.
Great. Who did I say is coming with us?
You said Laila and her family are joining you. It might help to send Laila a message tonight so everyone knows the backup plan.
I want to wake up early to study before school but I never manage it. I'm Sneha, a class ten student.
Hi Sneha. Waking early is easier when you go to bed earlier. What time do you usually sleep, and what time do you want to wake?
I sleep at eleven thirty. I want to wake at five thirty.
That's only six hours, which may feel short. You could try moving bedtime to ten thirty first, then waking at six, and slowly shift. Small steps are easier to keep than a big jump.
Six sounds more doable. What should I do right after waking up?
Wash your face, drink some water, and open the window for fresh air. Then start with the subject you find easiest, so the first ten minutes feel like a win.
I think maths is my easiest. Should I do it first?
Yes, start with maths. A familiar, easy subject helps your brain warm up. Then you can move to the harder subject once you feel awake.
Okay. What bedtime did you suggest to begin with, again?
I suggested ten thirty, Sneha, with waking at six. Once that feels normal, you can slowly move toward the five thirty you wanted.
I want to do something kind at school but I don't want attention. Any quiet ideas?
Quiet kindness is lovely. You could leave a small note of thanks on a teacher's desk, or help a classmate pick up scattered books. Do you want ideas for a particular day?
Maybe for our cleaner, Savita didi. She works so hard.
That is thoughtful. You could write her a short thank-you note and leave it with a cup of water or a small treat. Many people who do tiring work rarely hear thanks.
Can I ask my friends Pari and Rehan to sign it too?
Yes, a card signed by friends feels warm. Keep it simple and honest, and let each person write one line of their own.
What should my line be?
Something true and short, like, "Thank you for keeping our school so clean." Savita didi will appreciate that you noticed her daily work.
Nice. Who was I going to give the note to?
You are giving it to Savita didi, the school cleaner. With Pari and Rehan signing it, it will be a quiet but meaningful thank-you.
I feel nervous about reading aloud in assembly next Monday.
Reading in front of the whole school is a big moment, so nerves make sense. What will you be reading?
A short poem about rain. I'm Aryan, by the way.
Nice to meet you, Aryan. A poem about rain is a pleasant choice. Try reading it slowly at home, and pause at the commas so your voice stays steady.
Should I memorise it or hold the paper?
Hold the paper. It gives you comfort, and you will not panic if you forget a line. Just look up once or twice at the audience between verses.
What do I do with my hands?
Hold the paper with both hands near chest level, so they are busy and steady. Take one slow breath before you begin and speak a little slower than normal.
Thanks. Could you tell me the poem topic again so I practise the right one?
You are reading a short poem about rain, Aryan. Practise it a few times this weekend, slowly, with a pause at each comma.
My friend Laila hasn't replied to my message in two days. Did I do something wrong?
Two days of silence can make anyone wonder, but there are many simple reasons. She could be busy, away, or have no phone nearby. What did your message say?
I asked if she wanted to come to my birthday party on the twentieth.
That is a friendly message and unlikely to upset her. She may be checking with her parents first before she answers. You could wait another day.
What if she's ignoring me? Last week we had a small argument.
That detail matters. If you had an argument, she might need time. You could call or meet her in person and say you hope things are okay, and you would love her to come.
Okay. I'll talk to her at school. Should I mention the argument?
Briefly. You could say, "I'm sorry about last week." Then invite her again without pressure, and let her answer in her own time.
So what date was the party, in case she asks?
Your birthday party is on the twentieth. Tell Laila that date when you speak to her, and say you would really like her to be there.
What can I get my mum for Mother's Day that costs very little?
A handmade card with a few honest lines can mean more than anything bought. You could also cook her a simple breakfast or do her chores for a day. What is she like?
She loves flowers but forgets to water them. Also, I'm Ishita.
Thanks, Ishita. Then a small potted plant that needs little care, like a money plant or a hardy succulent, would suit her. Add a card and offer to remind her about watering.
Actually, I think a card and breakfast is better. Plants die at our house.
That is a sweet change of plan. A card plus breakfast for your mum is thoughtful, and you can still pick a single flower from the market to put beside her plate.
Why does it feel so much hotter before the monsoon starts?
Before the rains, the air often becomes heavy with moisture while the sun is still strong. That makes sweat dry slowly, so your body feels hotter and stickier even if the temperature is the same.
Oh. So it's the humidity. Does the wind help then?
Yes, moving air helps sweat dry, so a fan or a breeze makes you feel cooler. Shade and water help too, even if the air is still muggy.
Then I'll sit by the window fan while I study for my exam.
Good idea. Stay hydrated while you study, and take short breaks to wash your face. A steady breeze at your window fan should keep you more comfortable.
Is it okay to nap in the afternoon? My uncle says it makes you lazy.
I can't give medical advice, but many people find a short nap refreshing, especially after lunch. Ten to twenty minutes is often enough. Longer naps can make some people feel groggy.
I'm Pari and I nap for like two hours after school. Then I can't sleep at night.
That sounds like the long nap may push your night sleep later. You could try shortening it to twenty minutes with an alarm, and see if bedtime gets easier.
Hmm, so which did you say was better, a short nap or a long one?
A short one, Pari. About twenty minutes with an alarm. A two-hour nap after school can make falling asleep at night harder.
I feel a bit sad on Sundays, like the weekend is slipping away.
Many people feel that Sunday-evening heaviness. It usually comes from knowing the week is about to start. Does anything in particular make Mondays feel hard?
Mainly the maths class. Mr Sharma gives a surprise quiz every Monday.
Surprise quizzes can make Monday feel tense. You could do a quick, ten-minute revision of maths on Sunday afternoon, so the quiz feels less scary. Then enjoy the rest of your evening.
That makes sense. Should I study on Saturday instead?
Saturday is fine too. Just keep it short and light, and do a quick look again on Sunday. Revising for Mr Sharma's quiz in small bits will feel easier than cramming.
My friend Rehan is always last to be picked for teams, and I think it hurts him.
It likely does, even if he jokes about it. Noticing is the first step. Are you ever a team captain or able to pick?
Sometimes in PE. I could pick him earlier.
That would be a kind and simple thing. Choose him early because he is a good teammate, and say something encouraging. Others may follow your example.
I'll pick him second next time. Do you think he'll notice?
He probably will, and he will likely feel glad. Rehan will remember that you picked him early when it mattered to him.
I'm buying a present for a six-year-old girl named Laila. Any ideas besides toys?
A picture book is a lovely choice, or a small set of crayons and a drawing pad. A simple craft kit, like beads for a bracelet, can be fun as well.
Beads sound fun, but are they safe for little kids?
Small beads can be a choking risk for very young children, so check the age label on the pack and choose big beads with an adult nearby. If unsure, the picture book is a simpler choice.
Then I'll go with the book. She likes dinosaurs.
A dinosaur picture book will suit Laila perfectly. Look for one with big, colourful pictures and short facts so she can enjoy it alone and with you.
Our school trip is on Thursday and I've heard a storm might come. I'm Aryan and I'm worried it'll get cancelled.
That's a fair worry, Aryan. I can't check the forecast, but your teachers will decide based on safety. Do you know where the trip is?
The botanical garden, about an hour away.
For an outdoor visit like that, the school may postpone it if a storm looks serious. You could ask your class teacher if there is a backup date, so you know what to expect.
Good idea. I'll ask Mrs Das tomorrow. If it is cancelled I'll be sad.
That is understandable. If the garden trip is moved, you will still get to go later, and the wait can make it more fun. Asking Mrs Das is a good first step.
I want to invite a few friends for a sleepover but my flat is small. Is that a bad idea?
Not at all. Many small homes host sleepovers happily. Ask your parents first, and keep the group small so everyone has space. How many friends do you have in mind?
Three: Sneha, Kunal and Amelia. Mum says okay.
Great. With four of you, you could spread mattresses on the living room floor. Plan a few games, a simple snack, and a movie or story to keep it relaxed.
One of them, Kunal, snores a lot. Should I warn the others?
You could mention it gently as a joke, so no one is surprised. Maybe place Kunal's mattress a little away from the others, and keep a spare pillow ready.
I read that a warm shower helps people sleep. Is that true?
Many people say a warm shower or bath makes them feel relaxed before bed. I'm not a doctor, but it can be a nice part of a calming routine. Do you have trouble sleeping?
Sometimes. I'm Rehan and I'm always thinking about tomorrow's tests.
That is common, Rehan. A warm wash, then writing tomorrow's tasks in a small notebook, can help your mind put the worries down. Then you can switch off the light.
The notebook idea is good. What should I write exactly?
List just two or three things you need to do tomorrow, like your test subject and what to pack. Once they are on paper, your mind does not need to keep repeating them.
How do I thank the auto driver who found my lost water bottle and returned it?
That was thoughtful of him. A warm thank-you is a good start. If you see him again, you can say it directly and mention how much it helped.
I don't know where he parks. I just remember he was called Bhaiya Ramesh.
Then you might ask other drivers at the stand near where you were picked up. If you cannot find him, you can pass the kindness on by helping someone else with a lost item.
Okay. I'll look for Ramesh bhaiya near the market tomorrow.
Good. If you find Ramesh bhaiya, a smile and a sincere thank you are enough. Mention that the bottle was important to you, and he will feel appreciated.
I'm excited and scared about my dance performance. It's in front of three hundred people.
Excitement and fear often come together. That much energy can help you perform, if you channel it. How long have you been practising?
Two months. My teacher Meera ma'am says I'm ready but my steps in the second song wobble.
Then focus a little extra on that second song. Slow practice, then speed, and a few runs in front of a mirror or family can help. Trust the two months you have put in.
Maybe I can run through it with Meera ma'am once more this week.
That is a smart plan. Ask Meera ma'am to watch the second song closely and point out the wobbly part. A short, focused practice with her will help you feel steady.
I'm choosing between a kite, a skipping rope and a puzzle for my nephew's birthday. He's seven.
All three are good for a seven-year-old. The kite is outdoor fun, the rope is active, and a puzzle is quiet and clever. What is he like?
He's full of energy but he also gets bored fast.
Then the skipping rope or the kite suits him best, because they keep him moving. A puzzle might hold his attention for a short time only.
Kites are great but we live in a flat with no open ground nearby.
Then the skipping rope is the practical choice. It works on a terrace or in a small courtyard, and it is easy to carry.
Good thinking. Let's go with the second one from my list.
That is the skipping rope, since your list was the kite, the skipping rope and the puzzle. It suits your energetic nephew and fits your flat much better than the kite would.
I love the smell after the first rain. Why does that happen?
That smell comes from dry soil and plants releasing oils and tiny compounds into the air when raindrops hit the ground. Many people call it the smell of earth after rain.
Cool. My brother George thinks it comes from the sky.
It is a common idea, but the smell mostly comes from the ground. Raindrops splash and send the scent into the air, which is why you notice it as soon as rain starts.
I'll tell George. He'll want proof.
You could show him by pouring a little water on dry dust or a clay pot and sniffing. The same earthy smell often appears, which supports the explanation.
We'll try it with his old clay pot tonight.
Nice experiment. Pour a little water slowly on the clay, and let George smell it. He may be surprised that the smell comes from the pot, not the sky.
I can't sleep when my little cousin visits because she wakes up very early.
That is tough, since her schedule changes yours. How early does she get up, and does she make noise?
Around five, and she plays loudly. Her name is Amelia and she's four.
Four-year-olds often wake with lots of energy. You could ask your parents if Amelia can play quietly with a few toys in another room first thing, or ask a grown-up to take her out for a walk.
Maybe I can leave a colouring book near her bed so she does that first.
That is a smart idea. Amelia might colour happily for a while. Add a few crayons and a small light so she can start quietly without waking others.
Do you think it will work?
It might, at least for some mornings. Four-year-olds can be unpredictable, but a colouring book near Amelia's bed gives her something calm to do, and gives you a better chance of sleep.
I accidentally broke Pari's pencil box and I'm too scared to tell her.
That is hard, but being honest is the best way to keep a friendship. Was it an accident, and did anyone see?
It was an accident. It fell off the desk when I was looking for my book.
Then you can say exactly that. Telling Pari what happened, and offering to fix it or replace it, shows you respect her. Most friends understand real accidents.
What if she gets angry?
She may feel upset at first, and that is okay. Stay calm, say sorry, and give her time. People often forgive quickly when they see you are honest.
Alright. What should the first sentence be?
You could begin, "Pari, I have to tell you something. I'm really sorry, I broke your pencil box by accident." Then wait and listen to how she feels.
I miss my old school so much. I've been at the new one for two weeks and everything feels strange.
Two weeks is still very early. It is natural to miss familiar faces and places. What do you miss most?
My friend Ryan and our football games at lunch.
Those sound like good memories. You could keep in touch with Ryan, and also look for a lunch-time game at the new school. Football is easy to join if you ask.
I did see boys playing near the gate. Should I just walk up?
Yes, you could ask, "Can I play?" or just stand nearby and join when a pass comes your way. Most groups are happy to have another player.
Okay. I might tell Ryan about it too.
Good idea. Tell Ryan you found a lunch game at your new school, and ask about his. Sharing news keeps your friendship alive while you build new ones.
My grandma lives alone and I'd like to cheer her up. I'm Laila and I'm twelve.
That's a loving thought, Laila. Small, regular things often matter more than big ones. What does your grandma enjoy?
She loves old songs and stitching.
You could call her on a regular day and ask her to sing a favourite song, or ask her to show you a stitched piece she made. Or you could draw her a little card and post it.
I like the card. Could I put a drawing of her garden?
That is perfect, since it is something she knows and loves. Add a few lines about what you remember from the garden, and a message that you are thinking of her.
I'll draw the tulsi and the jasmine. What else should I write?
Under your drawing of the tulsi and jasmine, write that you miss her songs and watching her stitch, and that you look forward to visiting. Short, warm lines will make your grandma smile.
I want to give my best friend something for passing her music exam. What do you think?
What a lovely idea. Something related to music, or a small treat to celebrate? What instrument does she play?
The harmonium. Her name is Sneha.
For Sneha, a small notebook for writing her own songs or a nice cover for her harmonium would be thoughtful. A box of her favourite sweets with a congratulations card also works.
I only have a small budget, so maybe the card and sweets.
That sounds good. A handwritten card saying how proud you are, with her favourite sweets, will make her feel celebrated without costing much.
Which sweet should I pick?
Choose what Sneha likes best, since you know her. If you are unsure, a small box of mixed sweets or her favourite from the local shop will be a safe and happy choice.
Dad says we should leave early tomorrow because of fog. Is fog dangerous?
Fog makes it hard to see far, so drivers need to be careful and go slower. Leaving early is a sensible way to avoid hurrying. Where are you travelling?
To my aunt's house in another town, around three hours.
A three-hour drive in fog can take longer than usual, so leaving early gives you extra time. Your dad will likely use low beam lights and drive slowly. You could carry water and a snack.
I'll pack some biscuits. Should I also bring a book?
A book is a good idea for a long, slow drive. Reading might make some people feel unwell in a moving car, so look out of the window if you feel that way.
Great. Remind me where we are going tomorrow?
You are going to your aunt's house in another town, about three hours away. Pack your biscuits and a book, and leave early with your dad because of the fog.
My exams start next week and I keep staying up late studying. Is it worth it?

Many students feel that pressure. I cannot give medical advice, but most people remember better when they sleep enough. A steady routine often helps more than very late nights. What time do you study till?
Until two in the morning. I'm Kunal and I'm in class eleven.
Hi Kunal. Two in the morning can leave you tired in the exam hall. You could try studying with short breaks and finishing an hour or two earlier, then revising briefly in the morning.
Okay, but I get nervous that I'll forget things if I sleep.
That worry is understandable. Before bed, you could write a short list of key points, then read it again after you wake. Sleep actually helps your brain keep what you learned.
So what time should I stop studying at night?
Try stopping around midnight, Kunal, and write your key-point list before bed. Then revise it in the morning. Adjust by an hour if you need, but keep the time the same each night.
Aryan and I made a plan to go cycling on Saturday. Now my cousin invited me to a movie that day.
That is a tough choice. You had a plan with Aryan first. Which would you enjoy more?
The cycling, honestly, but the movie is a family thing.
Family events can be important, but it is fair to be honest with both. You might ask if the movie is on Saturday only, and offer Aryan a different day for cycling.
The movie is on Saturday afternoon. Cycling was in the morning.
Then you might do both. Cycle with Aryan in the morning, and be back by noon for the movie. Just tell your cousin the time you will arrive.
Great. I'll message Aryan to confirm the morning.
Good plan. Tell Aryan you are free in the morning, and ask him to start early, so you have time to get home and go to the movie with your cousin.
I got the part of a tree in the school play and everyone laughed. I felt silly.
That sounds embarrassing, and it is fine to feel that way. Being a tree is still a real part, and plays need every role. Did they laugh at you or at the idea?
At the idea, I think. Our friend Rehan said it was funny.
Then it may have been friendly teasing, though it can still sting. You could make the tree special by moving gently like wind in the branches, so people clap, not laugh.
I like that. I could add a bird puppet on my arm.
A bird on a branch is a wonderful idea. Ask your drama teacher if it is allowed, and practise the movements slowly so they look smooth.
What was the part I got again, before the bird idea?
You are playing a tree in the school play. With a bird puppet on one arm and gentle swaying, your tree could be the most memorable part.
A girl in my class forgot her tiffin today and I gave her half of mine. Now I'm hungry.
That was a kind thing to do. It is also okay to feel hungry. Do you have anything left for later?
A banana, I think. Her name is Ishita and she was nearly in tears.
Then Ishita was lucky to have you. You could eat the banana at the next break. Maybe suggest to Ishita that she keeps a small snack in her bag for days like this.
Should I tell the teacher what I did?
You do not need to, since kindness does not need credit. But if the teacher asks, it is fine to say you shared lunch. Ishita might like to thank you herself.
Okay. Do you think Ishita will remember it?
People remember small kindnesses when they feel scared or upset. I think Ishita will remember that you shared your tiffin with her when she was nearly in tears.
I have a swimming race on Saturday and I keep imagining myself coming last.
Those pictures in your head can feel real, but they are only guesses. Try imagining a calm, steady swim instead. Is this your first race?
No, my third. I'm Amelia. I came fourth last time.
Fourth is a good result, Amelia. You have already raced twice and know how it feels. This time, you could aim to beat your own time instead of other swimmers.
That makes sense. But my lane is next to the fastest girl, Laila.
That can feel intimidating. But a fast swimmer beside you can also pull you along. Focus on your own lane, your own breathing and your own turns.
What should I do just before the whistle?
Take a few slow breaths, shake out your arms and say one calm word to yourself, like "steady". Keep your eyes on the water in front of you, not on the other lanes.
I'll say steady. Who did you say I should not watch?
You should not watch the other lanes, including Laila's. Keep your eyes on your own lane and say "steady" to yourself until you hear the whistle.
I'd like to surprise my dad with a gift for Father's Day, but I have no idea what he likes.
You probably know more than you think. What does he do on weekends or when he relaxes?
He fixes things around the house. And he drinks black coffee.
Then a small set of useful tools, a sturdy mug for his coffee, or a handy pouch for his screws and nails could be nice. Which seems most like him?
The mug. I'm Rehan, and I want it to say something funny.
Good to know, Rehan. You could find a plain mug and write a funny line with a ceramic marker, like "World's Best Fixer of Everything". Bake it as the instructions say so it lasts.
Is it hard to do? I'm not very artistic.
Not really. Use simple block letters, practise on paper first, and keep the design small. A slightly uneven handwritten line often feels more personal.
Okay. What was the funny line you suggested?
I suggested "World's Best Fixer of Everything", Rehan. It suits a dad who repairs things at home, and the coffee mug will remind him of you each morning.
My grandmother says the old temple tank fills up in the monsoon and the whole village comes to see it.
That sounds like a lovely tradition. A full tank after rain is often a happy sight, and many villages treat it as a celebration. Have you visited it?
Once, when I was little. I'm Pari and I want to go again in July.
July could be a good time, since monsoon rain usually fills such tanks around then. Ask your grandmother when she thinks it will be fullest, because she knows the local pattern.
Will it be safe to stand near the edge?
Stay a few steps back, especially on wet steps, because stone can be slippery. Hold your grandmother's hand and wear shoes with a good grip.
Good. She will want me to bring sweets for the priest.
That is a kind custom. You could pack a small box of laddoos or whatever your grandmother prefers, and offer them politely at the temple.
