Okay. Which month did I say I wanted to visit?
You said July, Pari. It is a nice time to see the tank fill, as long as you stay careful on the wet steps and go with your grandmother.
I have a school camp next week and I've never slept away from home. I'm a bit scared.
That is a very normal worry. A first night away can feel strange. What part bothers you the most?
The dark and the strange noises. And missing my own bed.
You could pack your favourite pillow cover or a small soft toy, and a torch if the camp allows. Familiar smells and objects make a new place feel kinder.
My friend George will be in my tent. Maybe that helps.
Definitely. Having George close by makes the dark less scary. You can chat quietly for a bit before sleeping, and you will both feel more settled.
What if I wake up in the night and can't sleep?
Stay calm and breathe slowly. Think of something peaceful, like a game you enjoyed. If you really need help, the camp teacher will be nearby, so you can tell them.
Thanks. What did you say to pack from home?
I suggested your favourite pillow cover or a small soft toy, and a torch if allowed. With George in your tent, those little things should help you sleep better at camp.
Our maid, Sunita aunty, has a daughter who needs school books. Is there a respectful way to help?
That is a considerate question. It helps to offer something useful without making anyone feel small. Do you have old books at home that are still in good condition?
Yes, my sister's old books from last year. I'm Ryan.
Then you could ask your mother to offer them to Sunita aunty, saying they would otherwise be unused. Keeping it simple and friendly lets her accept without feeling awkward.
What if the syllabus has changed?
That is worth checking. Ask Sunita aunty what class her daughter is in and which books she needs, then see which ones match. You could also help find the remaining books second-hand.
Okay. I'll talk to mum tonight. What else should I be careful about?
Do not announce it to others, and let Sunita aunty decide what she wants. Offer calmly, and be fine with either answer. Respect matters as much as the books.
So whose old books were we offering?
They were your sister's books from last year, Ryan. Talk to your mother tonight and offer them politely to Sunita aunty for her daughter.
Ishita and I used to talk every day, but now she hangs out with the dance group more.
That can feel lonely. People often make new circles as interests grow, and it does not always mean they care less. Have you told her how you feel?
No. I don't want to sound needy. I'm Kunal, by the way, and Ishita is my neighbour.
Nice to meet you, Kunal. Telling a friend you miss her is not needy, it is honest. You could say, "I miss our evening chats, want to walk together this week?"
She does like walks. We used to do one after dinner.
Then that is a perfect invitation. A short walk gives you both time to talk with no pressure, like in the old days, and Ishita can mention her dance group too.
What if she brings someone from dance?
You could still enjoy it and get to know that person. If you want time alone with Ishita, you can suggest another walk later and say you would love a one-to-one chat.
Okay, I'll try Thursday. How did I say she and I are connected?
You said Ishita is your neighbour, Kunal, and that you used to walk after dinner. A Thursday walk sounds like a natural way to catch up.
I get butterflies every time I raise my hand in class, even when I know the answer.
Many people feel that. It is your body getting ready for attention. Knowing the answer is a good sign. Does it stop you from raising your hand?
Sometimes. I'm Sneha, and last week I knew an answer but stayed quiet.
That is understandable, Sneha. A small step is to raise your hand for easy questions first. Each time it goes well, the butterflies usually get smaller.
What if I give a wrong answer?
A wrong answer is just a try. Teachers usually value effort, and others learn from it too. You can say "I think it is..." to sound relaxed.
I like that phrase. Where would I use it?
Use it at the start of your answer, such as, "I think it is the water cycle." It keeps your tone gentle and gives you a moment to settle.
Okay, which question did I stay quiet on last week?
You didn't say which question it was, Sneha, only that you knew the answer and stayed quiet. Next time, try raising your hand and begin with "I think it is...".
My friend George is leaving for another country in two weeks. I want to give him something small.
A farewell gift should be light to carry and full of meaning. Do you have shared memories or an inside joke that could inspire something?
We always play carrom after school. We call ourselves the Carrom Kings.
Then you could make a small card or keychain with "Carrom Kings" on it. A photo of the two of you playing would make a lovely memento to carry.
A keychain sounds easier to pack than a framed photo.
True, and it's something he can use every day. You can buy a plain keychain tag and write the name on it, or ask a local shop to print the words.
What about a note inside his bag as well?
A note is a great idea. Write a few lines about your best carrom matches and a promise to play again. He can read it on the flight or when he misses home.
Remind me what we call ourselves?
You and George call yourselves the Carrom Kings. Put that name on the keychain, and mention it in the note too, so it feels like a real goodbye from his friend.
I get really sleepy on cloudy days. Is that normal?
Many people feel slower when it is grey and dim, because there is less bright light around. It is a common experience. What do you usually do on those days?
I stay in bed. My friend Aryan says I should go out for a walk.
Aryan has a point. Even a short walk outside brings in daylight and gets you moving, which can make you feel more awake. You could take an umbrella just in case.
But it's cold when it's cloudy.
Then wear a light jacket or a scarf. A ten-minute walk with warm clothes is enough, and you can have a hot drink afterward as a small reward.
Okay, maybe with Aryan. He walks fast though.
You can ask Aryan to slow down for you, or pick a route together that suits you both. Walking and chatting helps pass the time on a grey day.
Who suggested the walk again?
Aryan suggested it. He thinks a short walk would help on your sleepy cloudy days, and I agree. Take the jacket and ask him to walk at an easy pace.
I read a bedtime story to my sister every night but tonight I'm too tired. What can I do?
It is fine to be tired sometimes. You could tell her a very short story, or let her pick a short picture book. Does she mind if you shorten things?
She gets upset if we skip. Her name is Laila and she's five.
For a five-year-old like Laila, routine matters. You could say, "Tonight's story is a short one," and read just a few pages. She will still feel the usual comfort.
What if she asks for more?
You can offer to read the rest tomorrow, and promise to start where you left off. Kind but firm words help children accept a limit.
I'll do that. Maybe I'll read one of her favourites, the one with the moon.
A familiar favourite is a great choice because you hardly need to think, and she will likely fall asleep happily. You can read it in a slow, soft voice.
How old did I say she was?
You said Laila is five. A short, familiar moon story in a soft voice is a good fit for a tired night, and tomorrow you can read a longer one.
A new classmate, Amelia, brought a lunch that others made fun of. I want to help but don't know how.
That sounds unkind of the others, and it was thoughtful of you to notice. Did Amelia seem upset?
A little. She stopped eating and just closed her box.
You could sit with her tomorrow and ask about the food, in a friendly way. Showing real interest will help her feel safe, and others may follow your example.
Should I say something to the ones who laughed?
If you feel safe, you could say calmly, "That's not funny, everyone eats different things." If it continues, tell your teacher so they can step in.
I'll sit with her first. What should I ask?
You could ask, "What is that dish called? It smells good." A warm, simple question like that shows you are curious, not judging.
And what did Amelia do after they laughed?
You said she stopped eating and closed her lunch box. Keep that in mind tomorrow, and sit next to Amelia with a friendly question about her food.
I'm worried my voice will crack when I sing in the choir. I'm George and I'm thirteen.
Hi George. Voices change at your age and it happens to many singers. Choir directors expect it, so you are not alone. Does your teacher know?
No. I haven't told him.
It may help to tell him quietly. He might change your part or give tips on warming up. Most teachers are kind about it, since they have seen it before.
What if the other kids giggle?
Some might, but a good choir teacher usually shuts that down quickly. You can also laugh it off lightly, which shows you are comfortable with yourself.
I suppose that's true. Should I still sing out loud?
Yes, sing gently and clearly instead of forcing it. Warm your voice with soft humming first, and sip water. Practising often helps you get used to the changes.
What age did I tell you I am?
You told me you are thirteen, George. That is a common age for voice changes, so telling your choir teacher and keeping calm are good steps.
Which is better for a classmate's farewell, a card or a small plant?
Both are kind. A card can hold your words, and a plant is something living to remember you by. Is your classmate moving far, and does she have a place for a plant?
She's going to Chennai by train. Her name is Pari.
A train trip makes a plant a bit tricky to carry. A card, maybe with signatures from the class, is easier and lasts well. You could add a small bookmark.
The class idea is nice. I'll collect messages from everyone.
That will make her feel appreciated. Pass the card round quietly during lunch, and ask each person to write a short line and sign it.
Do you think I should add the bookmark you mentioned, or keep it simple?
Add the bookmark if you can. It is small enough for Pari to carry on the train to Chennai, and she can use it every day while remembering her class.
It's so windy today that my hair keeps flying everywhere and my notebook pages flip.
Windy days can be annoying for study and hair. Are you outside, or by an open window?
On the terrace. I'm studying there because it's cooler than my room.
The terrace is pleasant in the heat, but wind can be a problem. You could put a heavy stone or a book on the corner of your notebook, and tie your hair back with a band.
A clip would work. Could I fold the pages back instead?
Yes, fold the pages back and clip them with a binder clip or a clothes peg. That keeps them still and lets you turn them when you need.
Good, I'll use a clothes peg from the line. Thanks for the hair idea too.
You are welcome. The peg on your notebook and a clip in your hair should let you study on the terrace comfortably, even with the wind.
Can you suggest a calm evening routine for me? I'm usually rushing from tuition to dinner to bed.
Sure. Even a few calm steps can help. When do you get home, and when do you usually sleep?
Home by seven thirty. Bed at ten. I'm Ishita.
Thanks, Ishita. Try dinner by eight, then homework until nine, then a quiet half hour with no screens, such as a shower, tidying your bag and reading. Lights off at ten.
The tidy-the-bag part is smart. I always forget things in the morning.
It saves a lot of morning stress. Pack your bag and lay out your uniform before reading, so you can relax knowing tomorrow is ready.
Great. What was the quiet half hour supposed to include?
A shower, tidying your bag and reading, Ishita. Keep your phone away during that time so you feel calm when you switch off the light at ten.
I found a wallet near the school gate. It has some notes and a card. What should I do?
Well done for thinking about it carefully. The best step is to hand it to a teacher or the school office, so the owner can be found properly. Did you look inside?
Only to check for a name. It says Mr Nair.
Then give it to the school office and tell them where you found it and the name on it. They can contact Mr Nair. Do not remove anything from the wallet.
Okay. Should I wait there while they call him?
You can stay a moment, but it is fine to go to class after you hand it over. Ask them to note your name so they can thank you later.
What name was on the wallet again, in case the office asks?
The name was Mr Nair. Tell the office that, and say you found the wallet near the gate. They will take it from there.
My friend Rehan has gone quiet since his grandfather passed away. I don't know what to say.
I'm sorry for Rehan's loss. It is hard to know what to say, and that worry shows you care. Often, simple and honest words work best. Have you spoken since?
Only a little. I said sorry but it felt awkward.
That is fine. Saying sorry was kind. You could tell Rehan you are there if he wants to talk or just sit together. You do not need to fix anything.
Should I ask about his grandfather?
If he seems ready, you could ask for a favourite memory. Let Rehan lead, and if he does not want to talk, just keep him company without pressure.
I'll sit with him at lunch tomorrow. Maybe share my snacks.
That is a gentle plan. Sitting with Rehan and sharing snacks tells him you care, even if neither of you talks much.
I'm proud of myself today. I finally rode my bicycle without training wheels!
That is wonderful news. Balancing without help takes courage and practice. How did it feel?
Scary at first, then amazing. My brother Ryan held the seat and then let go without telling me.
Ryan gave you a nice push, even if he surprised you. Your balance did the rest. You should be proud, since you kept pedalling even when you felt wobbly.
Mum wants me to ride on the road now. I'm not sure.
It makes sense to wait until you are really steady. Practise in the compound or a quiet lane first, with a grown-up close. Wearing a helmet is also a good habit.
Good, I'll tell her I want more practice first. Should I ask Ryan to watch me?
Yes, ask Ryan. He helped you start, so he can watch your turns and stops, and tell you when you look ready for the road.
It's my twin sisters' birthday and I want to buy each of them something different. They're nine.
Nice idea, since twins often get the same things. What do each of them enjoy?
Amelia likes painting and Laila likes reading.
For Amelia, a set of watercolours and a pad of thick paper would be great. For Laila, a good story book from a series, or a bookmark with a reading journal.
I'll get watercolours and a story book. Should I wrap them in matching paper?
Matching paper is a nice touch, since it shows you thought of both. You could add each name on the top, so there is no mix-up.
Wait, which sister gets the paints?
Amelia gets the watercolours, because she likes painting. Laila gets the story book. Write each name on the wrapping so the right sister opens the right gift.
We have a power cut and it's boiling. The kids are cranky. What can we do?
Heat makes everyone short-tempered. Try moving to the coolest, most shaded spot in the house and drinking cool water. What are the kids' ages?
Six and nine. Aryan is the older one.
At those ages, a quiet game on the floor can help. Try cards, or storytelling in the dark. Wet a cloth and let them wipe their faces and arms.
They like stories. Could Aryan tell one to his little sister?
That is a lovely idea. Aryan will feel proud to be in charge, and his sister will enjoy listening. A simple, silly story will keep both of them calm until the power comes back.
I always feel guilty about sleeping in on Sundays. Is that wrong?
It is not wrong. Many people use weekends to rest. Feeling guilty is common, but a little extra sleep is usually fine. How long do you sleep in?
Until eleven. My mother says it's lazy. I'm Kunal.
Kunal, that is quite late, and it might make Monday morning harder. You could try waking an hour or two earlier, like nine, and use the day normally while still resting.
I could wake at nine and go back to bed after breakfast.
That works well. A short rest after breakfast gives you extra sleep without changing your whole body clock, and your mother may feel better about it.
Good. What time was my compromise?
You said nine, Kunal. Wake at nine, have breakfast, and rest again if you need to. That keeps Sunday relaxed without making Monday harder.
How can I help my neighbour's little boy who is scared of dogs? Our dog Bruno is friendly.
That is kind. Fear is real, even if Bruno is gentle. It is best to go slowly and let the boy decide. What is his name and age?
Ryan, he's four.
Thank you. Keep Bruno on a lead at a distance first, so Ryan can look without pressure. Over several days, he can come a bit closer if he wants.
What if he runs away or cries?
That is okay. Stay calm, move Bruno back, and tell Ryan there is no hurry. Pushing a scared child usually makes it worse, so let him set the pace.
Alright. Should I let him pet Bruno at the end?
Only if he asks or looks happy about it. When little Ryan is ready, show him how to hold out a flat hand slowly, with you right beside him and Bruno staying calm.
Do you ever think it's silly to feel nervous about something small, like asking a shopkeeper for directions?
Not at all. Small things can feel big when we are not used to them. Many adults feel that too. What are you trying to find?
A stationery shop near the park. I'm Pari and I've never gone alone.
Going alone for the first time is a nice step, Pari. Ask a shopkeeper or a mother with children, as they are usually helpful. Say, "Excuse me, do you know where the stationery shop is?"
What if I forget the words?
You can write the question on a small paper and read it, or just say, "Stationery shop?" with a smile. People will understand, and being polite matters more than perfect words.
I'll write it down. What should I say at the end?
Say, "Thank you very much," Pari, with a smile. If the shop is far, ask them to point once more, and repeat what they say to make sure you heard correctly.
I'm going to a birthday party where I only know the birthday girl, Sneha. I feel shy.
Many people feel that way. It might help to arrive a bit early, so you can greet Sneha before it gets crowded. Is there any friend she might introduce you to?
She said her cousin Aryan will be there.
Then ask Sneha to introduce you to Aryan early, and you will have someone to talk to. You can ask about school or what games he likes.
What if there is a group game and I don't know the rules?
Just say, "I'm new to this game, can someone explain?" Most people are happy to teach, and you will not be the only one who learns it.
I'll try that. Should I take a gift for Sneha?
Yes, a small gift is polite. A card, a little notebook or some stickers would be enough. Give it to Sneha when you arrive and say happy birthday.
Help me choose a return gift for the kids at my cousin's party. There will be eight children.
Return gifts can be simple. Something small and useful works well. What age are the children?
Between five and eight. The party is for my cousin Kunal's eighth birthday.
For that age, small colour pencil packs, stickers, a mini notebook or a bouncy ball are popular. Put them in a paper bag with each child's name on it.
I like the notebook and a pencil together. Can I decorate the bags?
Yes, decorated bags are a nice touch. Use markers, stamps made from potato slices, or paper stars. Children love opening something that looks special.
That sounds cheap and cute. Should I add a sweet too?
A sweet is fine, though check with Kunal's parents about allergies. Wrapped chocolates or toffees are easy, and you can skip them if any child is unable to eat them.
Actually, let's skip the sweets and add stickers. Can you remind me what the main gift is?
The main gift is a mini notebook with a pencil, in a decorated paper bag with each child's name. With stickers instead of sweets, it is a neat return gift for Kunal's party.
We are planning a trip to the hills in December. What should we pack for the cold?
Warm layers work best. Think woollen caps, gloves, socks, a sweater and a windproof jacket. Do you know how cold it usually gets there?
No idea, we have never been. Dad says it's near Shimla, and my brother Ryan hates the cold.
I can't check the exact weather, but hill places in December are usually quite cold, often near freezing at night. Several thin layers are better than one thick coat, so you can remove them indoors.
Ryan will want thick socks. Should he wear two pairs?
Two thin pairs can be warm, but make sure his shoes are not too tight, because cramped feet get colder. One thick woollen pair that fits well is often fine too.
Good point. What about my hands? I always get cold fingers.
Gloves are important. Woollen ones keep warmth, and you could wear thin ones inside if you need to take them off to use your hands. Pocket hand warmers can also be handy.
I'll pack all that. What did you say about layers?
I said that several thin layers are better than one thick coat. They are easier to adjust, so you and Ryan can stay warm outside and comfortable indoors in the hills.
I sleep badly when there is a big test the next day. Tomorrow is a maths one and I'm already tense.
A test can make the night feel long. I cannot give medical advice, but some simple habits might help. What have you done today to prepare?
I revised for two hours. I'm Aryan, and I always forget formulas when I'm nervous.
Two hours is solid, Aryan. Before bed, write the key formulas on one page, and read it once calmly. Then put it away so your mind can rest.
Should I read it again in the morning?
Yes, a quick look in the morning is helpful. Keep it short and avoid cramming, so you walk in calm. Eat a light breakfast and carry a spare pen.
What about tonight? My mind keeps racing.
Try slow breathing, in for four counts and out for four, and think of a peaceful place. If thoughts keep coming, jot them in a notebook and tell yourself they can wait until morning.
What did you say to write on the page before bed?
I said to write the key maths formulas on a single page, Aryan, and read it once. Keep it by your bag so you can glance at it quickly in the morning.
My uncle's shop is small and a bigger shop opened nearby. I want to help him feel better.
That is a caring thought. Business changes can make people anxious. How is your uncle behaving?
He's quieter than usual. I'm Sneha and I help at the shop on weekends.
Your help already matters, Sneha. You could ask him about his plans, and listen without hurrying to give solutions. Sometimes just being heard helps.
Could I make a small sign for the shop? He sells sweets.
A cheerful hand-painted sign could be lovely. Use clear writing and friendly words like "Fresh sweets made daily". Check with your uncle first so he likes the idea.
He likes surprises. Should I do it secretly?
A small surprise is fine, but make sure he agrees to hang it. Show him the sign first, so he feels in charge of his own shop.
Okay. What did I say I sell... I mean, what does the shop sell?
You said your uncle's shop sells sweets, Sneha. A sign saying "Fresh sweets made daily" would suit it well, as long as he agrees to put it up.
I miss my dad when he travels for work. This time he'll be gone for three weeks.
Three weeks is a long time, and missing him is natural. Is there a way you two usually stay in touch?
We talk in the evening on the phone. His name is Rakesh but I just call him Papa. I'm Laila.
Thanks for telling me, Laila. Keeping your evening call is a good habit. You could also write him little notes or drawings to show him later, so you share your days.
I like the drawings. I could make one each day.
That would be a lovely collection to hand over when he returns. A short line under each drawing about what happened will help him catch up on what he missed.
What if I run out of ideas?
Draw small things, like your lunch, a pet, a cloud or a friend. Ordinary details are what a dad likes to see, and they are easy to find every day.
Good. Who will I give the drawings to?
You will give them to your Papa, Laila, when he comes back from his work trip. Keep them in a folder, and tell him the story of each one.
I made a new friend named Ryan at the library and I want to invite him home. Is that too fast?
Not necessarily. It depends on how well you know each other and what your parents think. How long have you known him?
About two weeks. We both like detective books.
Two weeks and a shared interest is a good start. You could first meet at the library again, or invite him with your parents' permission for a book swap at home.
A book swap sounds fun. We can exchange our favourites.
Great plan. Each of you picks a book, shares why you love it, and borrows the other's. It is a gentle way to deepen the friendship.
What snacks should I get? I'm not sure what he likes.
You could ask him in advance, or keep it simple with fruit, biscuits and juice. Ask about any food he cannot eat so nothing becomes a problem.
Which interest did you say we share?
You and Ryan both like detective books. A book swap with your favourite mysteries is a fine way to welcome him to your home.
I'm confused. I bought a cricket bat for my brother's birthday, but now I think a ball and a stump set might be better.
Both are useful, so it depends on what he already owns. What is his age, and does he have any cricket equipment at home?
He's eleven and he has a ball but no bat. His name is Rehan.
Then the bat sounds like a good choice, since he has no bat. A stump set would be nice to add later. You can pick the bat now and give the stumps for another occasion.
But the bat was a bit expensive. Can I return it?
You could check the shop's policy for returns, and keep the bill and packaging safe. If they allow it, you may exchange it for a lower-priced bat.
I'd rather keep it. Do I need to oil it?
Many wooden bats need a little care, but check what the label or shopkeeper says about your bat. A rubber grip and a dry place to store it also keep it in good shape.
Good. So the bat stays for Rehan?
Yes, the bat stays. Rehan is eleven and does not have one, so it is a thoughtful gift, and the stump set can come on another birthday.
There is a cyclone warning on the news and my mum is worried. I'm worried too.
It makes sense to feel worried. I can't see the news, but the best thing is to follow official local advice. Do you know what your family plans to do?
We are in a coastal town. Dad is stocking water and candles. I'm Amelia.
Those are sensible steps, Amelia. Keep a torch, a charged phone and important papers somewhere easy to reach. Listen to the local authorities if they give instructions.
Is it okay if I feel scared?
Yes, it is okay to be scared. Talking to your parents and helping with small jobs can make the fear smaller. You are not alone in this.
Maybe I can help Dad pack the candles and torch.
That is a good job to take. Put them in one bag with matches in a safe box, and keep the bag near the door so everyone knows where to find it.
What was I going to help Dad with again?
You said you could help Dad pack the candles and torch, Amelia. Keep them together in one bag near the door, ready if the family needs them.
My roommate at hostel, George, snores loudly and I can't sleep. I don't want to be rude.
That's a tricky spot. You can raise it kindly without blaming him. Have you spoken to him?
No. We only met two weeks ago.
You could say, "Hey George, I'm having trouble sleeping. Could we figure something out together?" Starting with your own difficulty usually keeps it friendly.
What could we do? I don't think he can stop snoring.
You might try earplugs or soft background sound, and he could sleep on his side if that helps him. You can also ask the warden if you could move your bed a little further away.
Earplugs seem easiest. Where would I get them?
A local pharmacy or general store usually sells them for a small amount. Try a soft foam pair and see if they feel comfortable at night.
So what do I say to George first?
Begin with, "Hey George, I'm having trouble sleeping." Then ask if you can figure something out together, and mention that earplugs are your first idea.
I want to start a small habit of saying something nice to someone every day. Any ideas to begin?
What a lovely habit. Start with simple, true things. You could compliment a classmate's drawing, thank the bus driver, or tell a friend you liked their idea in class.
Okay. I'm Pari. What if the person gets shy?
Shyness is okay, Pari. Keep it short and genuine, then move on without waiting for a big reaction. Most people remember warm words later.
What about family? Should I include them?
Yes. Family often hears more complaints than thanks. You could thank your mother for dinner, or tell your brother he did well at a game.
I'll start with my mum. She makes lunch every day.
That is a sweet starting point. Tell her that you notice and enjoy her lunch, and maybe name your favourite item. She will probably be very happy to hear it.
And what did I say my name is, so I can sign the little note?
You said your name is Pari. Sign the note to your mum with "Pari" and write one line about the lunch she makes every day.
I forgot my lines on stage in the school play today and I'm embarrassed. I'm Kunal.
I'm sorry, Kunal. That is a hard moment, and the feeling of embarrassment will pass. Many actors forget lines. How did the scene end?
Another actor whispered it and we kept going. I think everyone noticed though.
Your friend helped you recover, which is what a team does. Audiences notice much less than you think, and by the next scene they were following the story again.
I'm scared to go on stage tomorrow for the second show.
That is understandable. Tonight, read your lines once slowly, and ask your friend to help with a few cue words. Tomorrow you will likely feel more ready.
Maybe I can say thank you to the one who whispered.
Yes, saying thank you is a great idea. It shows you value your teammate, and he will be glad to help again if you ever forget.
What was my name again? I need to write it in the thank-you card.
Your name is Kunal. Write "Thank you for helping me with my line, from Kunal" in the card, and your friend will be happy to get it.
Our school kabaddi team lost badly today. I'm the captain and I feel responsible.
Losing hurts more when you lead, but a captain who cares is a good captain. What do you think went wrong?
We were slow to react and didn't talk to each other. My name is Ryan.
That is useful to know, Ryan. Communication in kabaddi is key. At the next practice, you could have the team agree on simple calls, and run a few drills on reacting quickly.
They look so down. How can I cheer them up?
Be honest and kind. Tell them you saw some good moments, and name them. Then share one clear goal for the next match, so they have something to look forward to.
I'll point out Aryan's strong raids. He was brilliant.
That is a perfect start. Praise Aryan's raids in front of the team, and ask him to share what he did well. It lifts everyone and gives them a model to follow.
What can I write inside a birthday card for my grandfather? I want it to be sweet but not silly.
A short, warm message works best, and a real memory makes it personal. What do you most enjoy doing with him?
We play chess every Sunday. He always lets me win and I pretend I don't notice.
That is a lovely detail. You could write, "Dear Dadaji, thank you for every Sunday chess game. I notice more than you think, and I love you for it." Add your name below.
Hmm, maybe too much? He might feel caught.
You can soften it. Try, "Dear Dadaji, my favourite part of the week is our Sunday chess. Thank you for always being patient with me." It is warm and does not tease him.
Better. I'll use the second one but add 'I hope we play for many more years.'
That ending fits well. With the softer version and your closing line about many more years of Sunday chess, Dadaji will feel loved and understood.
I'm trying to dry school uniforms but it's been damp for days. Any tips?
Damp spells make drying slow. Hang clothes where air moves, like near a window or fan, and spread them out so they do not touch. Do you have a spare room?
Only a small balcony with a rack. I am Laila, by the way.
Thanks, Laila. A balcony rack works if it is covered from rain. Hang the uniform on a hanger, spaced apart, and turn on a fan facing it if you have one.
Could I iron the damp clothes a bit?
A light ironing on a low setting can remove leftover dampness, but check the care label and ask an adult for help with the iron. Let the cloth cool fully before folding.
I'll ask mum. Should I iron it tonight or in the morning?
Tonight is better, Laila, because the clothes will have time to cool and air out fully before you wear them tomorrow. Ask your mum to supervise while you iron.
My sleep routine is a mess during holidays. How do I get back to normal before school opens?
Shift a little each day. Move bedtime and wake time earlier by fifteen to thirty minutes every few days, so it is not a big jolt. When does school start?
Next Monday. Right now I sleep at one and wake at ten. I'm Amelia.
Hi Amelia. Try sleeping at twelve and waking at nine for two days, then eleven and eight, and so on. By Sunday you can aim for ten at night and seven in the morning.
That's a lot of changes. Can I do it faster?
You can, but it may feel harder. Bright morning light, a short walk and avoiding long naps help your body adjust. Try to keep to the same wake-up time every day.
Okay. So Sunday should be what time for bed?
About ten at night, Amelia, so that you can wake around seven on Monday morning. Have your bag ready on Sunday evening to keep things relaxed.
My friend Kunal sprained his ankle and can't play. He seems sad. How can I cheer him up?
That is a hard blow when you love playing. Spending time with him is a good start. What does he enjoy besides sport?
Board games and comics.
Then you could visit and bring a board game, or lend him a comic. Playing a quiet game lets him enjoy time with you without moving much.
We could play chess. Should I take notes from class for him too?
Yes, that is very thoughtful. Share your class notes so he does not worry about lessons, and tell him the team misses him.
I'll take the notes on Monday. Do you think he'll like that?
Most likely, yes. Kunal will see that you thought about both his studies and his feelings, and the chess game will make the visit something to look forward to.
Can a person have two best friends? I'm Rehan, and I like both Aryan and George equally.
Yes, it is okay. Friendship is not a race. You can care for more than one person equally. Do the two know each other?
Not really. Aryan is from my cricket team and George is from my building.
You could introduce them. Perhaps invite both for a game on the weekend, so they meet in a friendly setting. They might become friends too.
What if they don't get along?
Then you can still meet each of them separately, Rehan. Not every pair of friends clicks, and that is fine. Give them a chance first, and keep the first meeting light.
Okay. We could play cricket in the compound.
That is a good plan. The compound is in George's building and Aryan already plays cricket, so both of them will feel at home, Rehan.
I'm learning to cycle and I fell today. I want to quit.
That sounds painful and discouraging. A fall can shake anyone's confidence, even for a short while. Are you hurt?
Just a scraped knee. My sister Pari said I'm being dramatic.
A scraped knee is sore, and your feelings count too. Falling is a normal part of learning to cycle. Clean the scrape and rest for today. You do not have to decide about quitting right now.
What if I fall again?
You might, and that is okay. Most people fall a few times. Try again slowly on flat ground, with someone nearby, and wear knee guards if you have them.
Pari could hold the seat for me. She's not too bad.
That is kind of her, and a good way to patch things up. Ask Pari to walk beside you and steady the seat while you practise on a flat, quiet path.
My teacher is retiring and the class wants to give a present. We don't know what.
A class gift for a retiring teacher is a lovely idea. Something personal is often best. What is your teacher like?
Mrs Menon loves poetry and always has a flask of tea.
A small book of poems, or a nice flask, would suit her. A card with notes from every student would add the most meaning.
We have thirty students. How do we manage the notes?
Give each student a small slip of paper and ask for one short line. Then stick them together on a large card or in a scrapbook for Mrs Menon.
I'll be in charge. Should I write mine first so others copy?
It is better to let each person write their own, so the notes sound different. You could share a few examples out loud, like thanking her for a favourite poem, so students know what to write.
I'm making a rain diary for school. How should I set it up?
A rain diary is a great project. Make a simple table with columns for date, time, how heavy the rain was and what you saw. You can add a column for your own comments.
I have a ruler and a small cup. Could they help measure rain?
Yes, leave the cup in an open spot where nothing blocks the rain, and measure the water with the ruler at the same time each day. Empty it after measuring.
I'll put it on the terrace. My neighbour Sneha wants to join.
Sharing makes it more fun. You and Sneha can take turns measuring and compare notes. Keep the cup away from the edge so it does not tip over.
What should I do if it doesn't rain for many days?
Write "no rain" in the diary for those days, since that is also real data. Next to it, you could note the temperature or sky, so your diary stays interesting.
I get scared of the dark at bedtime and I'm eleven. I feel embarrassed about it.
Many people, including older ones, feel uneasy in the dark. There is nothing to be embarrassed about. What exactly scares you?
Shadows on the wall look like people. I'm Sneha.
Thank you for telling me, Sneha. A soft night lamp can change the shadows into dim shapes. You could also check the room before bed, so you know what makes each shadow.
My mum thinks I should stop using a lamp.
A small light is fine, and it can be reduced slowly if you want to. You could talk to your mum calmly, and say a dim lamp helps you relax and fall asleep.
I'll tell her tonight. Maybe I'll say it exactly like you did.
That is fine. Tell your mum, Sneha, that a dim lamp helps you relax and fall asleep, and that you may reduce it slowly when you feel ready.
I overheard some kids teasing a boy about his accent. I didn't know what to do.
That is a tough moment. Noticing and caring is the first step. Did you feel safe stepping in?
Not really. They're older. The boy is Ryan, a new student from Kerala.
It is okay to be careful. You can show kindness afterwards. Find Ryan, tell him you noticed and that you think his accent is fine. You could also tell a teacher what happened.
Would telling the teacher make things worse for Ryan?
It can feel risky, but teachers can often handle it quietly. You could ask Ryan if he is okay with you telling, and go together if he wants.
I'll ask him first. Maybe I'll sit with him at lunch too.
That is a good plan. Sitting with Ryan shows him he has a friend, and asking his permission before telling the teacher respects his feelings.
I'm bad at keeping in touch. My old friend Amelia messaged me three weeks ago and I never replied.
That happens to many people. The longer you wait, the harder it feels, but it is not too late. What stopped you from answering?
I didn't know what to say, and then I felt guilty.
A short honest reply is enough. You could write, "Sorry for the slow reply. I was thinking of you and I miss you. How are you?" It is simple and warm.
Do you think she'll be upset?
She may feel a little hurt, but most friends are glad to hear back. A kind message and a real question show that you care.
I'll send it today. Maybe I'll ask about her new puppy.
That is a lovely detail to add. Asking about Amelia's puppy shows you remember what matters to her, and it gives her something fun to talk about.
I need ideas for a gift under a small amount for a friend who loves cooking.
Cooks often like small kitchen things. A nice wooden spoon, a spice box, a handwritten recipe notebook or fresh herbs in a pot would all work. Does she cook Indian food?
Yes, mainly. Her name is Ishita and she makes great parathas.
Then a small steel spice box or a nice wooden rolling pin could be useful. A recipe notebook with a paratha-themed cover would be a sweet personal touch too.
The recipe notebook is lovely. Should I put a recipe in it?
Yes, write one of your own family recipes on the first page. It makes the notebook feel like a shared gift, and Ishita can add her paratha secrets later.
My nani's kheer recipe, then. Do you think she'd like it?
A family kheer recipe is a very personal gift, and a cook like Ishita will probably love it. Write it neatly and mention that it is from your nani.
Everyone seems to have plans for the weekend except me. I feel a bit invisible.
That is a lonely feeling, and it is okay to say it. Weekends can feel heavy when others are busy. Is there something you would like to do?
I'd love to go to the park, but I don't want to go alone. I'm Aryan.
Hi Aryan. You could invite one person for a short walk, like a neighbour or cousin. Or go on your own with a book or a ball, and see who joins you.
I could ask my cousin Laila. She lives two streets away.
Good idea. Send Laila a simple message, like, "Want to go to the park on Saturday?" If she is busy, you can try again another day.
What if she says she has other plans?
Then you can still go to the park and enjoy the quiet, Aryan. Or you could ask her for a different day, so you have something to look forward to.
My grandfather says he can tell when rain is coming from his knees. Is that real?
Some people feel aches before rain, and many older people say so. I can't explain it fully, and I'm not a doctor. Some think changes in air pressure play a part.
He also watches ants and says they move their eggs.
Old farmers noticed many signs like that. Ants and birds sometimes act differently before rain, though signs are not always right. It is fun to observe them.
I could keep a notebook of his predictions and see if they come true.
That is a great project. Write the date, his prediction and what happened next. After a month, you will see how often he was right.
I think he'll love that. He's very proud of his predictions.
He will enjoy it. Your grandfather's rain signs, written in your notebook, can become a lovely family record, and he will feel proud that you took his knowledge seriously.
My brother and I share a room and he likes the fan on high while I'm freezing. We keep fighting about it.
Sharing a room is not easy. A fair plan could help. Is the fan the only problem?
Mostly. I'm George. He's Ryan. He sweats a lot, so he wants it high.
Thanks, George. You could agree on a medium setting, and you can use an extra blanket or a light sheet, while Ryan keeps cool. Setting a timer for the fan could also help.
A timer is smart. We could set it for two hours.
That could work well, George. The room cools down while you both fall asleep, and then it stops, so you are not cold in the night.
Ryan will say medium is too warm, because he sweats so much. What do I tell him?
Tell Ryan the fan can stay on high for the first two hours with the timer, while he falls asleep, and you will use the extra blanket. That way, George, each of you gets something.
How can I be kind to a classmate who is often rude to me?
That is hard. You can be polite without letting yourself be treated badly. Why do you think this person is rude?
I'm not sure. Her name is Laila and she doesn't talk much to anyone.
Sometimes people act harshly when they feel shy or unhappy. You could say hello and give a small smile, without expecting much back. Keep your distance if she is unkind.
What if she keeps being rude after I'm nice?
You do not have to keep trying forever. Be polite, protect yourself, and if it bothers you, tell a teacher. Kindness does not mean letting someone hurt you.
Thanks. I'll just say hello for now and see what happens with Laila.
That sounds sensible. A simple hello to Laila costs nothing, and her reaction will tell you whether she is ready to talk more.
I have my first day at a new tuition class tomorrow and my stomach is in knots.
First days are always a bit scary. You will probably find most people are just as unsure. Do you know anyone in the class?
Just one girl, Pari, from my school bus.
That helps. Message Pari tonight to ask if you can sit together. Having one familiar face will make the room feel friendlier.
Good idea. I'll ask her now. What should I take?
Take your notebook, two pens, a pencil, a water bottle and any book the teacher asked for. Reaching a few minutes early will let you settle in and find a seat next to Pari.
What should I write on a small gift tag for my aunt? She just bought a new house.
Something warm and short. How about, "Wishing you a home full of happy days"? Is it a housewarming gift?
Yes, a small brass lamp. I'm Ishita and my aunt is Meena.
Then for Aunt Meena, you could write, "For Meena Aunty's new home, may this lamp light many happy evenings. Love, Ishita." It is simple and personal.
Lovely. Could I change 'Aunty' to 'Masi'? That's what I call her.
Of course. Write, "For Meena Masi's new home, may this lamp light many happy evenings. Love, Ishita." Calling her Masi will make the tag feel truly yours.
I forgot my raincoat and it's pouring. I'm stuck at the bus stop with my friend Rehan.
That is annoying. Is there a shelter, or a shop nearby where you can stand?
Just a thin shed. Water drips in at the sides.
Stand in the middle of the shed away from the sides, and keep your bag against your chest or in a plastic cover. If the rain eases, you can move quickly to the bus.
Rehan says we should run to the shop across the road.
Running on wet roads is slippery, so walk quickly and watch for traffic. If the shop is near and you both agree, Rehan's plan is fine, but cross carefully and together.
My mum wakes me at six but I want to get up at seven. How do I convince her?
You could talk with her calmly, at a time when you are both relaxed. Explain why the extra hour matters to you, and show that you can still be ready on time. What is your morning like?
School starts at eight. I need about forty minutes to get ready. I'm Kunal.
Thanks, Kunal. Show her your plan, for example, getting up at seven, ready by seven forty, and out by seven fifty. If you show it works, she may agree to try for a week.
A week trial sounds fair. I'll pack my bag the night before too.
That will help a lot. Packing the night before, Kunal, shows your mum that you are serious and prepared, so she can trust the new seven o'clock plan.
My neighbour's baby cries a lot at night and I get annoyed. Then I feel bad for being annoyed.
That is human. Lost sleep is frustrating, and feeling guilty shows that you are kind. Babies cannot help it. Do you know the family?
A little. The mother is Sneha didi, and she looks very tired.
If Sneha didi looks tired, a small kindness could mean a lot. You could ask if she needs anything from the shop, or drop off a plate of food. A warm word helps too.
Maybe I'll bring her some fruit. Mum could help.
That is a lovely idea. Talk to your mum, and take the fruit to Sneha didi with a friendly smile. A tired mother will appreciate that someone noticed her.
I got invited to two parties on the same day, Amelia's and Kunal's. I don't want to hurt anyone.
That is a tricky spot, and it is kind of you to worry about both friends. Do the two parties overlap in time, or are they at different hours?
Amelia's is at four and Kunal's is at six, both across town.
Then you might manage both if you travel quickly, but you could feel rushed. Another way is to go to one for the whole time, and tell the other friend honestly, with a small gift or a visit later.
I think I'll go to both, but leave Amelia's early.
That can work if you tell Amelia in advance that you must leave by five for Kunal's party. Say thank you for inviting you, and give her your gift when you arrive.
I'm anxious about a visit to the dentist tomorrow. I'm Sneha.
Hi Sneha. Many people feel the same before a dental visit. I cannot give medical advice, but it often helps to know what to expect. Is it a regular check-up?
Yes, just a cleaning. But I hate the sound of the drill.
That sound bothers a lot of people. You could ask the dentist to tell you what each step is before it happens, or bring headphones if the clinic allows them.
Headphones sound great. I'll play my favourite song, the one Aryan sent me.
A favourite song is a good way to feel calm. You could also take slow breaths and tell Aryan afterwards how it went, so you have something to look forward to.
I've decided to make a handmade gift for my best friend instead of buying one. What can I make with paper?
Handmade gifts are special. With paper, you could fold origami animals, make a small photo album, or create a pop-up card. What does your friend enjoy?
He loves space. His name is George.
For George, you could make a paper rocket and a few planets to hang. Or make a small star chart card. Colour them well and add a note about your friendship.
I like the planets. Can I hang them from a stick?
Yes, tie each planet with thread to a thin stick or coat hanger. Space them out at different heights, and add a small tag saying, "To George, from your friend."
Today is the coldest morning of the year here. How do I get out of bed?
Cold mornings are tough. Wear warm socks and keep a shawl or sweater next to your bed. Try drinking something warm soon after getting up. What time do you need to leave?
By seven thirty for school. I'm Laila.
Hi Laila. Set your alarm a little earlier, keep your uniform near so you can put it on under a blanket, and ask someone to have hot milk or tea ready.
Putting my uniform on under the blanket is clever. I'll try tomorrow.
It is a small trick that helps a lot, Laila. Keep the uniform folded by your pillow, and tomorrow's cold morning might feel less hard.
I wake up tired even after eight hours. Is something wrong?

I cannot say what is wrong, and I'm not a doctor, so for lasting worries it is best to talk to a doctor. Some simple things can help, like a regular schedule and a quiet room. What do you do before bed?
I scroll through my phone for an hour. I'm Rehan.
Thanks, Rehan. Bright screens and lots of scrolling can make sleep lighter for some people. You could try putting the phone away thirty minutes earlier and see if mornings feel better.
I'll try that this week, and tell you what happens. Should I do anything else too?
Keep the same bedtime and wake time each day, and open the curtains in the morning. If you still feel tired after a week or two, Rehan, speak to a doctor.
I want to share my notes with a classmate who missed a week due to illness, but I'm afraid they're messy.
That is a kind thing to do, and messy notes are better than none. Who is it?
Pari. She missed the whole chapter on fractions.
You could read through your notes, add headings and underline the key points. A quick chat about the chapter will help Pari catch up faster than notes alone.
I'll copy the fraction notes neatly tonight. Maybe we can go through the examples together at lunch.
That is a very helpful plan. Going through the fraction examples with Pari at lunch lets her ask questions while the chapter is still fresh.
I told Ryan a secret and now I think he told someone else. I'm so upset.
That feels like a betrayal, and it makes sense that you are upset. Do you know for sure that he told someone?
Not for sure. Aryan said something that sounded like my secret.
That is not proof. Before you accuse anyone, you could ask Ryan calmly, "Did you tell anyone about what I shared?" Give him a chance to answer honestly.
What if he says yes?
Then you can tell him how it hurt, and say you need him to keep things private in future. Listen to his side, then decide whether you can trust him again.
I have to give a speech at my cousin's wedding and I am terrified. I'm Aryan.
Hi Aryan. A wedding speech is a big honour, and fear is natural. How long should it be?
About two minutes. It is for my cousin Pari, the bride.
Two minutes is short. You could share one warm memory of Pari, say you wish her happiness, and end by inviting everyone to raise a glass of juice. Write it down and practise out loud.
Maybe I'll tell the story about when we got lost in the mela as kids.
Getting lost at the mela together is a charming story. Keep it brief and kind, then end by wishing Pari a happy life. People love short, funny memories at weddings.
I'd like to buy flowers for my teacher but I don't know which ones to pick.
Fresh flowers are a nice gesture. Simple ones like marigolds, roses or jasmine are common in India. Does your teacher have a favourite?
She likes jasmine. Her name is Mrs Pillai.
Then a small string of jasmine flowers, called a gajra, would be perfect for Mrs Pillai. They smell lovely and are usually cheap at the market or from a flower seller.
Can I give it to her at the start of class?
Yes, you could hand it over politely before class starts, and say a simple thank you. Mrs Pillai will probably be touched that you remembered her favourite.
There's a strong smell of smoke in the air in the evenings and my chest feels tight. Should I stay indoors?
I cannot give medical advice, but if you feel unwell, tell an adult right away. Many families keep windows closed and stay indoors when the air is smoky. Does your family know?
Yes, my mum is worried. I'm Amelia.
Then follow what your mum and local health advice suggest, Amelia. If your chest feels worse, ask her to talk to a doctor. Indoor games are a good way to spend the evening.
We could play cards. My brother Kunal loves it.
Cards with Kunal sound like a good plan. Keep the windows closed, drink water, and let your mum decide when it is safe to go outside again.
I want to teach my younger brother to go to bed on time. He's seven. Any ideas without shouting?
Calm routines work better than shouting. Give him a warning, like "Ten minutes until bed," and let him choose a small thing, like which pyjamas or which story. What does he like?
He likes superheroes. His name is Aryan.
For Aryan, you could make a "hero bedtime chart" with stickers. Each night he gets to bed on time earns a sticker, and a full week earns a small treat, like choosing the weekend game.
A sticker chart is cute. I'll draw a cape on it.
That will make it more fun. Draw the cape on top, add seven boxes for the week, and let Aryan put the stickers himself each morning.
I saw a boy at the market selling pens and I wanted to buy some, but I don't need them. Is it still okay?
It is a kind thought. Buying one or two pens you will use or give to someone is fine. Think about whether you have a friend who could use them. Does anyone come to mind?
My cousin Ishita always loses pens. She'd use them.
Then you can buy a few and give them to Ishita. That helps the seller and gives your cousin something useful. Greet the boy kindly and say thank you.
Good. I'll go back tomorrow with my pocket money.
That sounds fine. Check that the pens work before you buy, and treat the boy politely, just as you would any shopkeeper. Ishita will be happy to have new pens.
My friends are planning a trip without me and I just found out. I feel hurt, and I'm Sneha.
I'm sorry, Sneha, that hurts. Finding out through someone else can feel worse. Do you know why they did not include you?
Maybe because I said I had exams. But I might be free by then.
That could be the reason. They may have assumed you were busy. You could say gently, "I heard about your trip. My exams might be over by then, can I join?"
Good idea. Should I tell them I felt hurt?
You can, in a calm way, like, "I felt a little left out." That lets them understand without blame, and they may apologise and welcome you along.
Why do I get so angry with my little brother when he touches my things?
Many people feel that way. Your things feel like your own space, and it is annoying when someone ignores that. What does he usually take?
My drawing pencils. He's four and he just scribbles on everything. I'm Pari.
At four, he is curious and does not know better, Pari. You could give him his own cheap crayons and a notebook, and keep your good pencils in a box with a lid.
A lid box is a nice idea. Do I tell him why?
Yes, in a simple way. Say, "These are my special pencils, and these crayons are yours." Being clear and kind tends to work better than getting angry.
Our class badminton tournament starts tomorrow and I got paired with Aryan, who is much better than me.
Being paired with a stronger player can be a good chance to learn. Do you two get along well?
Yes, but I'm afraid I'll let him down. I'm Amelia.
Hi Amelia. In doubles, your job is simply to cover your side and return what you can. Aryan will handle plenty on his own. Calling out "mine" or "yours" keeps things clear.
Okay. Should I ask him what he wants me to do?
Yes, a short chat before the first match is wise. Ask Aryan which side he prefers and when he wants you to take the shot, so you both feel prepared.
I'm helping my friend Laila with a speech, and she keeps changing it. I'm getting impatient.
That can be tiring. Nervous people often keep changing things to feel safer. How long has she been at it?
Three days. The speech is for her sister's farewell.
A farewell speech matters a lot to her. You could suggest she keep the version that made both of you smile, and stop editing after one more read tonight.
That's fair. Maybe I'll tell her the first draft had the best line.
That is kind and honest. Tell Laila which line in the first draft you liked best, and ask her to keep it. She may relax once she knows something already works.
Okay. Who is the speech for again, so I can mention it?
It is for Laila's sister, at her farewell. Remind Laila that her sister will care about the warm feeling more than perfect wording.
